latestRelease.name: prospero-win v0.2.0
latestRelease.body:
prospero-win v0.2.0 is the biggest update since the first release. 32-bit Windows games now run directly on the PS5's CPU instead of through the translator, Vulkan traffic is batched so DXVK games keep their frame rate, OpenGL games draw through Mesa's Zink, and Windows programs can finally reach the internet by name and over HTTPS.

New to prospero-win? The [v0.1.0 release notes](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/releases/tag/v0.1.0) explain what it is, what you need and how to add your first game.

## Highlights

- **32-bit games run natively.** No more instruction translation for 32-bit games by default; the translator stays available as a per-game option and as an automatic fallback.
- **Vulkan command batching** for 32-bit games, so DXVK and Zink games aren't held back by the cost of switching between the game and the system.
- **OpenGL through Zink.** OpenGL games no longer need a special build of the app; Mesa's Zink ships in the package.
- **Online-ready networking.** Host names resolve through the console's own resolver, and Windows' TLS (schannel) works, with a pinned set of root certificates.
- **Many fixes** found while bringing up GTA San Andreas, GTA IV, Counter-Strike 1.6, Atomic Bomberman, Pizza Tower and larger Windows programs.

## What's new

### 32-bit games on the native CPU

Until now, every 32-bit game ran through prospero-win's x86 translator. In v0.2.0 a 32-bit game runs on the console's CPU in 32-bit mode, through a new WoW64 backend ([#432](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/432)). Games run their own code at full speed; only calls into the system cross over.

- **Works on any firmware.** The native backend needs to register its signal handlers directly with the kernel. It now finds that entry point in libkernel itself instead of relying on one measured firmware build, and checks it before use, including the layout of the kernel's signal frame ([#681](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/681)).
- **Automatic fallback.** If the native backend can't start on a console for any reason, the game now runs on the translator instead of closing ([#677](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/677), thanks to [leolobato](https://github.com/leolobato)).
- **Your choice per game.** `[runtime] cpu = translator` in a game's profile keeps it on the translator. 64-bit games are unaffected; they always ran natively.
- **Stable under load.** A rare timing window could send a game thread back into 32-bit code with the wrong thread state. It showed up as GTA San Andreas closing about two seconds after start, depending on its shader cache ([#683](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/683), [#682](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/issues/682)).

### Vulkan batching and faster graphics

Each call from a game into the system costs a couple of microseconds on the console, and DXVK makes tens of thousands of Vulkan calls per frame. v0.2.0 queues those calls and sends them over in batches, always in order, and only waits where the game needs an answer ([#432](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/432) and the batching work before it).

- **Counter-Strike 1.6 under Zink** went from 2,234 to 24 crossings per frame, with no change in what's drawn, now that descriptor writes are batched too ([#672](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/672), [#674](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/674)).
- **Shader compiles no longer stall other threads.** Pipeline compiles run outside the batch lock, so one long compile no longer freezes the render thread ([#676](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/676)).
- **A real shader cache.** RADV now keeps its compiled shaders between launches, under `/data/prospero-win/cache/radv`. Before, every launch compiled every pipeline again ([#668](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/668)).
- **prospero-win builds of DXVK.** Game recipes can pin a tuned DXVK build. [DXVK 2.6.2-prospero2](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/dxvk/releases/tag/v2.6.2-prospero2) adds cheaper CS-thread work and options used by the GTA San Andreas and GTA IV recipes ([#407](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/407), [#680](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/680)).

### OpenGL games through Zink

OpenGL games now draw through Mesa's Zink on top of Vulkan, on the native CPU with batching. Zink ships inside the app, so OpenGL games work with the regular package; the separate PS5 OpenGL SDK build is gone ([#438](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/438), [#456](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/456)–[#466](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/466)). Existing profiles with `graphics = opengl` switch over on their own.

### Networking

- **Host names resolve.** Windows programs could only reach numeric addresses before. Names now go through the console's own resolver, using its network settings, with bounded timeouts and a short cache for failed lookups ([#384](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/384)).
- **HTTPS through Windows' TLS.** schannel now works on the console, backed by GnuTLS 3.8.13, and crypt32 verifies servers against Mozilla's root store as curl publishes it, pinned at the 2026-09-25 extract ([#388](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/388)).
- **A stable host name.** Programs that look up their own computer name get one that resolves, which ends GTA IV's endless hostname lookups ([#471](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/471)).

Thanks to [heydemoura](https://github.com/heydemoura) for the resolver and TLS work.

### Per-game runtime options

Profiles gain a `[runtime]` section for options that help some games and not others ([docs](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/WINE_PS5_BUILD.md)):

- `cpu = native | translator`: which CPU backend a 32-bit game uses.
- `thread_scheduling = true`: round-robin scheduling and Windows thread priorities ([#420](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/420), [#424](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/424)).
- `shared_input = true` and `fast_clock = true`: faster key-state reads and a calibrated high-resolution clock ([#462](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/462)).

The library also lists up to 32 games now, instead of 16 ([#679](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/679)).

### Fixes

- **Games that load data into shared sections** (GameMaker titles such as Pizza Tower) start instead of failing with `c000007b` ([#678](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/678), thanks to [leolobato](https://github.com/leolobato)).
- **Memory reserved at a fixed address works.** A 64-bit program that reserves memory at an address of its choosing and commits it later (Steam's protection layer does this) faulted on its first write; that memory is now backed like the rest ([#417](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/417)).
- **The right CPU count.** Games now see the 13 CPUs they can actually use instead of 16, so worker pools sized to the CPU count no longer leave threads waiting ([#419](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/419)).
- **Correct floating-point state in exception handlers**, which managed runtimes and `__try`/`__except` code rely on ([#408](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/408)).
- **Memory, CPU-time and folder-change reports work.** Process memory counters, processor times and directory change notifications returned zeros or nothing on the console ([#413](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/413), [#414](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/414), [#415](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/415)).
- **Recommitted memory comes back zeroed**, as Windows promises, even where the console's larger pages hold other data ([#409](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/409)).
- **ShadowMountPlus and similar loaders.** When `/data` is visible but the app isn't elevated, it now asks for elevation instead of failing at startup ([#423](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/423)).
- **Atomic Bomberman** plays: the translator handles the Watcom runtime's instructions, arrow keys arrive as arrow keys, and input no longer stalls the game ([#425](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/425), [#426](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/426), [#428](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/428)).

Thanks to [kvaps](https://github.com/kvaps) for the loader and Atomic Bomberman fixes, and to [inf1nit3](https://github.com/inf1nit3) for the build setup fix ([#658](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/658)).

### Diagnostics

- The app's log is written from its own thread, so verbose logging no longer stalls a game every few seconds ([#669](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/669)).
- Slow system calls are logged with the game's stack, and new per-frame profiles split each frame's time between the game, the system and the GPU driver ([#673](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/673), [#661](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/661), [#662](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/662)).
- `[debug] env` in a profile adds diagnostic variables for one game without rebuilding anything ([#469](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/469)).

## Known limitations

- The native CPU backend has been validated on the maintainer's console. On other firmware it checks itself at startup and falls back to the translator if anything doesn't match, so games keep working either way; reports from other firmware versions are welcome.
- Name lookups use the console's own DNS settings. A console whose network blocks DNS (some setups do, to keep the firmware from updating) won't resolve names for Windows programs either.
- The firmware helper is unchanged from v0.1.1 ([Lapy v0.3.2-experimental](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/releases/tag/v0.3.2-experimental), now pinned in the build).

## Installing or updating

1. Download `prospero-win-v0.2.0.zip` below and unzip it. You get a folder called `PPSA99995`.
2. Upload that folder to `/data/homebrew/` on your PS5 and let your loader register it.
3. New users: follow [Getting started](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) to add your first game.

To update from v0.1.x, replace the whole `PPSA99995` folder. Your games, profiles, prefixes and saves live in `/data/prospero-win` and are kept. Games installed with a recipe that now pins a newer DXVK (GTA San Andreas, GTA IV) pick it up when you run their recipe again.

## Licensing

`THIRD_PARTY.md` in the folder explains which licence covers which file, `LICENSES/` holds the licence texts (now including GnuTLS's and nettle's, and MPL-2.0 for the root certificates), and `SOURCES.txt` names the exact source revision of every part.

## Checking your download

`SHA256SUMS` holds the zip's SHA-256. Check it with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.

**Full changelog:** [v0.1.1...v0.2.0](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0)

repos.name: Vita3K-PS5
repos.description: Experimental PlayStation Vita emulator port for PS5
repos.readme:
# Vita3K for PS5

A port of the [Vita3K](https://github.com/Vita3K/Vita3K) PlayStation Vita emulator to the jailbroken
PlayStation 5, running as a signed title (`PPSA99300`) with its own console front end.

This is a fork. Everything the emulator does — CPU, GXM, modules, the Vulkan renderer — is upstream Vita3K's
work. What is added here is the platform layer that lets it run inside a PS5 title sandbox, and a controller-driven
interface to replace the desktop one.

> **Status: experimental.** Games boot, run and are playable, but several render incorrectly. See
> [Known problems](#known-problems) before you set your expectations. The desktop and Android builds are untouched:
> nothing in this fork changes them.

## What the port adds

**A console front end.** Upstream's desktop interface assumes a mouse and a window manager, so it is replaced by
one built for a controller on a television:

- A game list laid out like the Vita's home screen — glossy bubbles in rows of three, four and three, ten to a page.
- An installer that browses the file system, installs `.vpk`, `.zip`, `.pkg` and firmware `.pup`, and shows overall
  and per-file progress. It can offer a choice of destination, but in practice there is only ever one — see
  [Known problems](#known-problems).
- Game deletion, a settings screen, a splash screen and the Vita's launch chime.

**A platform layer** (`vita3k/platform/`) for the things the console does not provide the way a desktop does:

| Area | What the console needs |
| --- | --- |
| Controller | SDL has no driver for the DualSense here, so `scePad` is read directly |
| Audio | SDL's backends reach no hardware; `sceAudioOut` is used instead |
| File removal | Boost's `remove_all` is refused in the sandbox; a direct `unlinkat` walk replaces it |
| Memory | The kernel protects memory in 16 KiB granules while `sysconf` reports 4096 |
| Power | `sceSystemServicePowerTick`, so a long install is not cut short by the idle timer |

**Controls.** The DualSense stands in for a Vita that has a touchscreen and no second trigger:

| Input | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Touchpad, dragged | Moves an on-screen pointer, drawn over the game |
| Touchpad, clicked | Taps the Vita's screen wherever the pointer is |
| R2 | SELECT — the Create button never reaches a title, and the touchpad click is taken |
| L3 + R3, held | Returns to the game list, rather than to the PS5's home screen |

## Building

Builds from WSL or Linux. You need LLVM 18, CMake 3.28+, Ninja, Perl, and Meson 1.4+ for RADV.

Vulkan comes from RADV on a PS5 winsys, so that has to be built first. Clone
[PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa) and
[PS5_PayloadSDK](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK) side by side, then in `PS5_Vulkan`:

```sh
tools/setup-native-dependencies.sh
tools/build-radv.sh release      # also needs libllvmspirvlib-18-dev libclc-18-dev libclang-18-dev
tools/rebuild-libc.sh
```

Then build the emulator against **that** SDK fork — the upstream ps5-payload-dev SDK lacks `libps5platform` and the
console's `ucontext_t` layout, and will not work:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-ps5 -G Ninja \
    -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/ps5-payload.cmake \
    -DPS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=<PS5_Vulkan>/.deps/native/ps5-payload-sdk \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_LTO=NEVER
ninja -C build-ps5
```

The result is a complete title in `build-ps5/title/PPSA99300/`, already converted and signed.

[`docs/ps5-porting-plan.md`](./docs/ps5-porting-plan.md) covers how each dependency is cross-built and how the
runtime is laid out.

## Running

### Requirements

The **PS5SX2 Helper**, from the releases of [PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2), loaded along with kstuff.
A title starts in a sandbox that can see only its own mounts, so Vita3K asks to be let out and waits for the Helper
to act on it. Without it Vita3K still runs, but its files go to `/download0/Vita3K` inside the title's own sandbox,
where nothing else on the console can reach them — not even FTP — so anything you install is effectively invisible.

[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) to register and launch the title.

### Steps

1. Copy `build-ps5/title/PPSA99300/` to where ShadowMountPlus scans — `/mnt/usb0/PPSA99300/` or
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99300/`. It only registers a title that has `sce_sys/icon0.png`.
2. Add `PPSA99300` to `/data/whitelist.txt`, or the Helper will not answer Vita3K's request.
3. Load kstuff and the PS5SX2 Helper, then launch Vita3K from the home screen.
4. Install the Vita firmware from a `.pup`, then your games, using the installer in the front end. A game folder
   copied straight into `/data/Vita3K/vita/ux0/app/` is picked up without installing.

Commercial games need their licence (`work.bin`) installed alongside them, exactly as on desktop Vita3K. Without it
the game fails to boot and the log says `No klic provided for encrypted App`.

The log is at `/data/Vita3K/logs/vita3k.log`, with the previous run kept beside it as `vita3k.log.previous` —
worth knowing, because returning to the game list restarts the title and would otherwise overwrite the log you
wanted to read.

## Known problems

- **Some games render incorrectly.** Uncharted: Golden Abyss draws most of the frame correctly but with large black
  rectangles and bands of corruption. Under investigation; several fixes are in and have not resolved it.
- **"Rendering: accurate" renders nothing.** The setting switches to shader interlock, which produces a blank screen
  on RADV while the game keeps running and playing audio.
- **"Memory mapping: disabled" crashes.** Leave it on `double buffer`.
- **USB drives are invisible to the running title.** The jailbreak grafts `/data` into the sandbox but does not
  repoint the process root, so `/mnt/usb0` cannot be reached from inside. This is also why the installer never
  actually asks where to put a game: the only destination it can find is console storage, so it stops offering a
  choice and everything lands in `ux0`. The code for choosing is there and will work once a drive can be reached.
- **Installing is slower than on a PC.** Small writes to `/data` are expensive, and a package install writes the
  game twice — once unpacked, once decrypted.

## Settings

The settings screen exposes the levers that matter for diagnosing a misbehaving game. Each takes effect the next
time a game is launched:

| Setting | Why you would change it |
| --- | --- |
| Rendering | `accurate` drops two render-target shortcuts — currently broken, see above |
| Surface write-back | Copies what the GPU drew back into the game's memory; a game that reads its render targets needs it |
| Memory mapping | How the game's memory reaches the GPU |
| Shader compilation | Background compiling leaves not-yet-compiled geometry undrawn for a moment |
| Stick sensitivity | Raise it when a character walks where it should run |
| Touchpad acts as | Which of the Vita's two touch panels the touchpad stands in for |

## License

GPLv2, the same as upstream Vita3K.

## Thanks

To the Vita3K team for the emulator, and to mihawk-99 for PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa and PS5_PayloadSDK, without which
there would be no Vulkan and no toolchain on the console.

To [Swordpdf](https://github.com/Swordpdf) for [PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2) and its Helper payload,
which is what lets a title reach anything outside its own sandbox, and to
[drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor) for [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus).

## Note

The purpose of this emulator is not to enable illegal activity. You can dump games from a Vita with
[NoNpDrm](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/NoNpDrm) or
[FAGDec](https://github.com/CelesteBlue-dev/PSVita-RE-tools/tree/master/FAGDec/build), and get homebrew from
[VitaDB](https://www.rinnegatamante.eu/vitadb/#/).

PlayStation, PlayStation Vita, PlayStation 5 and PlayStation Network are registered trademarks of Sony Interactive
Entertainment Inc. This emulator is not related to or endorsed by Sony, nor derived from confidential materials
belonging to Sony.

repos.readme:
RPCS3
=====

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a fork for the PlayStation 5 (a libretro core in
> [PS5_RetroArch](https://github.com/dmzebro/PS5_RetroArch)), not an official
> RPCS3 build; please do not report its problems to the RPCS3 team.**
>
> **No binaries of this fork are distributed, and none will be: you must compile
> it yourself from source.** RPCS3 is licensed GPL-2.0-only; the PS5 RetroArch
> title it runs in is GPL-3.0-or-later, and the two cannot be distributed
> together as one program. Build the whole title yourself with PS5_RetroArch's
> `tools/build-title.sh` (a development build: leave `PS5_RELEASE_TAG` unset),
> as its README describes under "PlayStation 3 (RPCS3): build it yourself", and
> keep what you build for your own console: do not share, upload or
> redistribute it.
>
> **Piracy is not condoned.** Use only your own PS3 system software
> (`PS3UPDAT.PUP`, from Sony's official update page) and legally obtained
> backups of games you own: discs you dumped yourself, or PSN purchases with
> their own licence files. No games, firmware or keys are provided.

[![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/RPCS3/rpcs3/rpcs3.yml?branch=master&logo=github&label=Actions)](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/actions/workflows/rpcs3.yml)
[![RPCS3 Discord Server](https://img.shields.io/discord/272035812277878785?color=5865F2&label=RPCS3%20Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/rpcs3)

The world's first free and open-source PlayStation 3 emulator/debugger, written in C++ for Windows, Linux, macOS and FreeBSD.

You can find some basic information on our [**website**](https://rpcs3.net/). Game info is being populated on the [**Wiki**](https://wiki.rpcs3.net/).
For discussion about this emulator, PS3 emulation, and game compatibility reports, please visit our [**forums**](https://forums.rpcs3.net) and our [**Discord server**](https://discord.gg/RPCS3).

[**Support the Lead Developers on Patreon**](https://rpcs3.net/patreon)

## Contributing

If you want to help the project but do not code, the best way to help out is to test games and make bug reports. See:
* [Quickstart](https://rpcs3.net/quickstart)

If you want to contribute as a developer, please take a look at the following pages:

* [Coding Style](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/wiki/Coding-Style)
* [Developer Information](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/wiki/Developer-Information)

You should also contact any of the developers in the forums or in the Discord server to learn more about the current state of the emulator.

### AI Use

Use of AI tools for research and reverse engineering purposes is permitted. However, contributors are expected to fully own and understand all code they submit. Any communication with the team — including code, code comments, and GitHub comments — must come from the human contributor, not an AI agent acting autonomously.

We have unfortunately seen a rise in untested and unverified AI-generated slop being submitted to this project. This wastes maintainer time and, in worse cases, such changes get merged and break functionality for all users. Repeated violations will result in a ban from the repository. Please be respectful of everyone's time.

**Pull requests opened by AI agents or automated tools must include a disclosure in the PR description** stating the scope of AI involvement — which parts were AI-generated and what human testing or review was performed prior to submission. PRs that omit this disclosure may be closed without review.

Don't forget to have your graphics driver up to date and to install the [Visual C++ Redistributable Packages for Visual Studio 2022](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/VC_redist.x64.exe) if you are a Windows user.

latestRelease.body:
# A standalone RPCS3 title compiled from the abandoned PS5_RPCS3
# Uses PS5_RetroArch with a single PlayStation 3 core

Put your own PS3 system software and your own game into the RPCS3 title folder (PPSA42674). The full-core RetroArch title stays untouched. The firmware file has to be named `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, and it has to come from Sony's official PS3 system software update page.

1. Copy the firmware into the RPCS3 system folder on the console:

"/data/homebrew/PPSA42674/system/RPCS3/PS3UPDAT.PUP"

The core looks only for that filename. On the first game load it installs the firmware into `system/RPCS3/` and the screen says `Installing firmware`. Leave the title running until that finishes. A later load sees the installed firmware and skips this step.

2. Create a game directory outside `system/`. One place that works is:

"/data/homebrew/PPSA42674/games/"

What you copy depends on the copy you own:

- A disc you dumped yourself is a folder that contains `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`. Copy that whole folder.
- A PSN purchase is a `.pkg` file. Put its `.rap` licence file in the same folder as the `.pkg`. The core copies every `.rap` beside the package into its licence directory when the package installs.

3. On the console, open RPCS3, Choose **Load Core**, Choose **PlayStation 3**, Choose **Load Content**, open `games/`, and select the game.

- For a disc folder, select `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`, or select the game folder itself. A folder with no `EBOOT.BIN` in either of those two places is rejected.
- For a PSN package, select the `.pkg`. The first load installs it, then starts it. The screen shows the install before the game.

4. Start the game only after the firmware install has finished. The first launch of a game also builds its cache, so that start is slow. Later starts use the cache already stored under `system/RPCS3/`.

Do not copy these files into the RetroArch title `/data/homebrew/PPSA99169/`

repos.name: psp5
repos.description: Native PSP port for the ps5 based on PPSSPP
repos.readme:
# PSP5

**A PSP emulator for the PlayStation 5, based on [PPSSPP](https://github.com/hrydgard/ppsspp).**

PPSSPP is the emulator — its interpreter and x86-64 JIT, its HLE of the PSP's
operating system, its Vulkan renderer. PSP5 is that emulator built as a
standalone PS5 homebrew title: it boots to its own console home screen, reads
the games off the memory stick, and runs them. None of PPSSPP's own interface is
shown — not its logo, not its game browser, not its pause menu, and none of its
on-screen messages.

The title installs as **PSP5**; *PSP5* is the project.

The console port itself is not PSP5's work: `patches/ppsspp/ps5-port.patch` is
taken unmodified from PS5_RetroArch, where it is proven on hardware. What PSP5
adds is what a title needs and a libretro core does not.

PPSSPP already runs on the PS5 as a libretro core inside
[PS5_RetroArch](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch). PSP5 is the other
shape of the same work: its own title, with no frontend in front of it — the same
relationship [PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2) has to PS5_RetroArch's
LRPS2 core.

## Using it

Copy `dist/PPSA99131/` to `/mnt/usb0/PPSA99131` on the console and install it
with ShadowMountPlus. Games go on the emulated memory stick, which is inside the
title's own folder:

```
PPSA99131/memstick/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso     # also .cso, .chd, EBOOT.PBP
PPSA99131/memstick/PSP/Cheats/<DISC_ID>.ini     # CWCheat files
PPSA99131/memstick/PSP/Cheats/cheat.db          # the CWCheat database, to import from
PPSA99131/memstick/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/      # a texture pack, with its textures.ini
```

The disc id is shown under the title on the home screen.

### Games on a USB drive

A drive holds the same tree, so the same paths work with `/mnt/usb0/PSP` in
place of `PPSA99131/memstick/PSP`. All eight USB ports and both extended drives
(`/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`, `/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`) are read, and a texture
pack on a drive is used in place of one on the memory stick.

```
/mnt/usb0/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso
/mnt/usb0/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/
```

**This needs folder listing to be unlocked.** A PS5 title can open a file by its
full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games means listing. PSP5 asks
for the unlock at every start, and any one of these answers: **etaHEN** (turn on
*Legacy CMD server* in its toolbox), **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**, or the **PS5SX2
Helper** (add PSP5 to its `/data/whitelist.txt`).

Nothing is escaped here. The console is already running something as root and
PSP5 asks it for the permission; where nothing answers, PSP5 runs from its own
memory stick as before and a drive looks empty. `psp5.log` says which it was.

### RetroAchievements

Sign in from **OPTIONS → System → RetroAchievements** and games award
achievements as you play. The list opens two ways, and looks the same in both:
**R2** on the home screen, for a game before it is played, and **R1 + R3** over a
running game. Left and right filter it — all, locked, unlocked — and the badges
are the real ones.

Reading a game's achievements before it runs means identifying it: the disc
image is hashed on a worker thread, which takes a moment and is why the bar
opens on a wait. Nothing is asked of the server twice.

The account is the player's rather than the game's, so PSP5 keeps the answer in
its own `config/psp5.txt` instead of PPSSPP's `bAchievementsEnable`, which is one
of its per-game settings — a game configured before signing in would otherwise
carry "off" for ever. The login token is PPSSPP's, under `PSP/SYSTEM`.

**Hardcore mode is off by default.** RetroAchievements forbids save states while
it is on, and PPSSPP enforces that by dropping the operation silently — no
message, nothing in the log. It is in the settings for anyone who wants it, and
it says what it costs.

This needs HTTPS, which the console has no system libcurl for. See
**Building** — without it the title still builds and runs, and says so instead of
offering to sign in.

### Texture packs

**Settings → System → Texture replacement** loads a pack from
`memstick/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/`, or from `<drive>/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/`
when a USB drive has one for that game - which is where a pack usually wants to
be. A pack needs a `textures.ini` beside its images, even a bare one - without
it the replacer stays off and says nothing.

**Save new textures** writes what a game draws to
`memstick/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/new/`, named by hash, which is how a pack is
started. A file put back in the folder above under the same name replaces that
texture; there is no need to list it anywhere.

### Controls

On the home screen:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **L1 / R1** | Recent, A–Z, Favorites |
| **Cross** | the game's details: Play, Resume, cheats |
| **Square** | settings for the game under the cursor |
| **Triangle** | keep a game in Favorites |
| **R2** | this game's achievements |
| **OPTIONS** | settings for the title |

*Resume* appears in place of the cheats entry when the game has a save state,
and boots it straight into the newest one.

In the settings, **L1 / R1** turn the page — Picture, Sound, Controls, System —
and left and right change the focused row. *Close PSP5* is at the foot of
System.

#### Moving the buttons

**Settings → Controls → Buttons** opens a panel of its own, listing all twelve
of the PSP's buttons — the four face buttons, both shoulders, Start, Select and
the four directions — and the console button each sits on.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cross** | set the console button |
| **Square** | set a second one |
| **Triangle** | clear the second |
| **Circle** | back |

A PSP button can answer two console buttons, so Select can sit on both the touch
pad and L3, or L on both L1 and L2.

With the prompt open, press the console button you want. Every button is a
binding, so none of them is free to mean "not that one" — the prompt gives up
after five seconds and leaves the row as it was. Binding a button takes it from
wherever it was, and that row is left reading *Not set*; **Reset the buttons**
puts all twelve back.

This changes what a game is sent and nothing else. The home screen and the
in-game menu read the pad directly, so Cross still chooses and Circle still goes
back however the panel is set, and a mapping cannot leave you unable to reach
the row that would undo it.

#### USB controllers

> **Experimental, and not tested on hardware.**

PSP5 can read controllers the console will not pair: **Xbox 360 wired pads**
(XInput), **PS3 USB pads**, a **DualShock 3** or **DualShock 4** on a cable, and
generic USB HID gamepads read through their own report descriptor. One folds
into player one, so it works beside a DualSense or on its own.

It is on by default, because it does nothing at all until a controller the
console ignores is plugged in. **Settings → Controls → USB controllers** turns
it off, and a file called `nousbpad` in the title's folder stops it before it
starts.

Only devices PSP5 can identify are read. A DualSense, a keyboard, a mouse, a hub
and a drive are left alone, and PSP5 does not open the endpoints of a device the
kernel would not name — which is known to take a wired DualSense away from the
whole console until it is powered off. When a pad does not work, `psp5.log` has
a line for every device looked at and why it was taken or left.

In a game:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **L2 + R2** | the menu: cheats, save states, and the way out |
| **R1 + R3** | the achievements for this game |

The triggers are used for the menu because the PSP has no L2 or R2 of its own -
its shoulder buttons are L1 and R1, which a game needs.

### Language

**Settings → System → Language** sets what a game is told the console's language
is, and the language the home screen itself is in: 45 of them, including
Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. Right-to-left languages
read right to left.

Where PPSSPP has a translation PSP5 uses it. The rest of the interface is PSP5's
own and lives in `assets/lang/psp5/<id>.ini`, 78 strings a language, as plain
`English = translation` lines. **Those are machine-made and unread in most of
these languages.** A line that is wrong is one line to fix, and a missing line
falls back to its English.

The fonts carry 3,055 glyphs a face rather than the kit's 113;
`tools/bake-fonts.sh` builds them and `tools/make-strings.py` writes the
translation files.

Arabic is drawn unjoined - there is no shaping - and the screen is not mirrored
for right-to-left languages, only the text.

### Typing

PSP5 draws its own keyboard, with the console's own shortcuts: **Square**
deletes, **Triangle** is a space, **L1 / R1** move the text cursor, **L2**
shifts, **R2** is done, **Circle** gives up.

## What it is made of

| Piece | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| The emulator | [PPSSPP](https://github.com/hrydgard/ppsspp) v1.20.4, pinned, unvendored |
| The console port | `patches/ppsspp/ps5-port.patch`, from PS5_RetroArch |
| The Vulkan driver | [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan)'s RADV, linked statically |
| The home screen | [PS5_VKHomebrewUI](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VKHomebrewUI)'s kit, Aurora Shelf design |
| The platform layer | [PS5_VulkanTemplate](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate)'s `ps5/src/platform.c`, vendored in `src/platform/` (MIT) |
| The SDK | the [PS5_PayloadSDK](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK) fork, for `ps5platform/{exec,shm,heap,fp}.h` |
| HTTPS | PacBrew's libcurl and OpenSSL, cross-built for the console |
| Networking | `console_curl.c`, vendored in `src/net/` from [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/BlackBearReloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) (GPL-3.0-or-later) |
| The unlock request | the protocol of [SwanStationPS5](https://github.com/darkxex/SwanStationPS5)'s `ps5_unlock.c` and [PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2)'s `ProsperoHenJailbreak.cpp` (both GPL-3.0-or-later) |
| USB controllers | the device routes and report decoding of PS5SX2's `ProsperoUsbPad.cpp` and `OrbisUsbPadDecode.h` (GPL-3.0-or-later), narrowed to pads |

PPSSPP is not vendored. `tools/build.sh` fetches the pinned revision and applies
the two patches, so tracking upstream is a rebase of those patches rather than a
merge of a fork.

## Building

The build runs on Linux (or WSL). It needs the **payload SDK fork** — the upstream
SDK has no `ps5platform/` headers, and the port's JIT and guest memory are built on
them.

```bash
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk   # the fork
export PS5_RADV=/path/to/radv-release             # PS5_Vulkan's output
export PS5_VULKAN=/path/to/PS5_Vulkan             # built, for the link

./tools/build-ffmpeg.sh                           # once; slow, and worth it
PSP5_FFMPEG_PREFIX=$PWD/build/ffmpeg ./tools/build.sh
./tools/link-title.sh                             # -> dist/PPSA99131/
```

Building under WSL from a working copy on the Windows filesystem? Build on the
Linux side — object files on `/mnt/c` are far too slow — and set
`PSP5_DIST_MIRROR` so the finished title lands back in the working copy:

```bash
export PSP5_DIST_MIRROR=/mnt/c/Users/<you>/Documents/Repos/psp5/dist
```

It copies only after the title folder is complete, and replaces `eboot.bin`
through a temporary name, so the mirror is never a half-written title.

RetroAchievements needs HTTPS, and the console has no system libcurl.
`tools/link-title.sh` looks for PacBrew's libcurl and the OpenSSL it was built
against under `PSP5_CURL_PREFIX` (default
`/opt/ps5-payload-sdk/target/user/homebrew`). Without them the link says so and
the title is built without HTTPS: everything else works, and PSP5 reports that
signing in is unavailable rather than failing at it.

`tools/build.sh` checks the SDK and RADV before it starts and says which one is
wrong. It also needs zlib to be the one RADV was built with, which it finds beside
`PS5_RADV` by default; `PS5_ZLIB` overrides it.

FFmpeg is a separate script because it is a slow cross-build that never changes,
while `tools/build.sh` is run over and over. Without it `tools/build.sh` still
works and the link says so, but the PSP's video and its Atrac3 audio are missing —
game intros and menu backgrounds included — so a release build has it.

## How it is put together

PPSSPP's platform ports are a `main` plus a graphics context; `SDL/SDLMain.cpp` is
the desktop one. `src/` is the console's:

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `PS5Main.cpp` | the entry point, the `System_*` host contract, pad to PPSSPP input, the loop |
| `PS5VulkanContext.cpp` | PPSSPP's `GraphicsContext` on `VK_KHR_display` — no window system |
| `PS5VulkanLoader.cpp` | the global Vulkan functions, resolved against RADV's own entry point |
| `PS5Audio.cpp` | PPSSPP's `AudioBackend` on the console's 48 kHz output |
| `PS5Paths.cpp` | the title's folders under `/app0`, created 0777 so FTP can reach them |
| `PS5Overlay.cpp` | the in-game menu, drawn over the game |
| `PS5Achievements.cpp` | the achievements bar, over the game, on **R1 + R3** |
| `PS5OverlayDraw.h` | what both of those are drawn with: palette, rounded shapes, toggles |
| `net/PS5HttpRequest.cpp` | PPSSPP's `http::Request` on libcurl |
| `net/console_curl.c` | the console's own socket and resolver calls (vendored) |
| `ui/PS5AuroraLauncher.cpp` | the home screen's own frame loop, borrowing the device |
| `ui/PS5GameLibrary.cpp` | the memory stick's games, and a cover for each |
| `ui/PS5GameArt.cpp` | `ICON0.PNG`, `PIC1.PNG` and `PARAM.SFO`, read out of an ISO or PBP |
| `ui/PS5Cheats.cpp`, `ui/PS5Settings.cpp` | the cheat file, and PPSSPP's configuration |
| `ui/PS5Prefs.cpp` | the few settings that are PSP5's own, in `config/psp5.txt` |
| `ui/PS5GameAchievements.cpp` | a game's achievements, read on the home screen before it is played |
| `ui/PS5Keyboard.cpp` | typing on a controller, with the console's own shortcuts |
| `ui/PS5GameSound.cpp` | the selected game's `SND0.AT3`, under the shelf |
| `ui/kit/aurora.cpp` | PSP5's copy of the kit's Aurora Shelf design |
| `platform/` | klog, splash, pad, audio and the shell exit (vendored, MIT) |

### Decisions worth knowing

**The home screen and the emulator take turns with the device.** The kit's
renderer and PPSSPP's render manager each assume they own the frame loop, so they
cannot both be up: the shelf runs, hands the device back exactly as it found it,
and PPSSPP takes it for the game. Each turn ends in `PS5VulkanContext::ShutdownDraw`.

**The Aurora design is forked, not patched.** The kit's designs read a
`demo::Catalog` that fills itself in its own constructor, so there is no seam to
push real content through — and the kit is a pinned checkout that
`tools/setup-kit.sh` re-fetches, so an edit in place would not survive. PSP5 keeps
its own copy of the one design it ships and drops the kit's from the build.

**None of PPSSPP's interface is drawn.** Four edits in the patch do it: PSP5
hands PPSSPP an `EmuScreen` directly, so neither the logo nor the game browser is
drawn even once; `MainScreen`'s constructor tells PSP5 the game ended, and PSP5
leaves the frame loop before the switch to it takes effect; the pause menu is
compiled out; and `ScreenManager::switchScreenNow` makes a screen switch that
cannot be refused by one already queued.

**PPSSPP's on-screen messages are cut at the view, not at each caller.**
`g_OSD.Show` is called from all over the core - "Game controller connected",
save-state notices, achievement popups - and silencing them one at a time leaves
the next one to surface later. `OnScreenMessagesView::Draw` returns immediately
instead, so a new call site cannot put a toast on screen.

**The home screen pumps the network queue itself.** PPSSPP's request callbacks
only run from `RequestManager::Update`, which `NativeFrame` calls - and
`NativeFrame` only runs while a game is up. The shelf has its own frame loop, so
it calls `PS5_PumpNetwork` each frame; without it a sign-in is posted and waits
for ever.

**The achievements client is built from PSP5's own setting, every start.**
PPSSPP's `bAchievementsEnable` records what the player wants, not that a client
exists, and nothing on the home screen creates one. PSP5 calls
`Achievements::UpdateSettings` unconditionally when its own setting is on, which
builds the client and logs back in from the saved token.

**PPSSPP's per-game settings are not where PSP5's answers live.** Six of them
now: achievements, hardcore mode, cheats, the control mapping, and both texture
replacement switches. Each is marked `CfgFlag::PER_GAME`, which means
`Config::LoadGameConfig` - called from `Load_PSP_ISO` partway through a boot -
overwrites whatever was set at start-up with whatever that game's second ini
happens to hold. A setting changed on the home screen was simply undone on the
way into the game, silently.

So PSP5 keeps its own answers in `config/psp5.txt` and asserts them again at one
anchor in `EmuScreen`, after `LoadGameConfig` has had its say. Anything new that
turns out to be `PER_GAME` belongs there too. It is the single most repeated
trap in this codebase.

**The patches are kept apart.** `ps5-port.patch` is upstream's, unmodified, so it
can be replaced wholesale when PS5_RetroArch's moves. `ps5-standalone.patch` is
PSP5's, generated by `tools/mkpatch.py` — each edit anchored to the text it
replaces, with the reason beside it, so a change in the pinned PPSSPP fails loudly
there rather than applying somewhere unintended.

**Undefined weak symbols are bound to zero explicitly.** Mesa leaves ~6,700
`radv_*` and `annotate_*` dispatch entries undefined on purpose, and the title
converter requires a stub for every entry in `.dynsym`. `--no-dynamic-linker` used
to drop them, but whether it does depends on the host LLVM, so `tools/link-title.sh`
links, collects what is left, binds each with `--defsym`, and links again.

**Flexible memory stays at the console default (448 MiB).** The 1 GiB a title can
ask for in `param.json` is taken out of direct memory, and PSP5's large
allocations — the JIT's code cache, the guest memory arena, the heap, the GPU's
buffers — are all in direct memory already. Raising it would cost 576 MiB of the
pool that actually matters here. `sce_sys/param.json` is where to change it.

**System dialogs are refused, not ignored.** Every `System_MakeRequest` PSP5 does
not implement returns false. A request that is neither answered nor refused leaves
PPSSPP waiting for a callback that never arrives.

`sce_sys/icon0.png` is drawn by `tools/make-icon.py` (512x512, RGB, no alpha, as
the console wants) and `tools/link-title.sh` stages it. Replace either the file or
the script to change it. The wordmark is drawn rather than set in a typeface:
the PSP logo's letters are single-weight strokes that no ordinary face has.

The home screen's sound sets are drawn too. `tools/make-sounds.py` synthesises
`assets/sfx/<set>/<cue>_NN.wav` - nothing sampled, nothing licensed - and the
link stages them beside the kit's two. A set is a folder, so adding one is
adding a folder: PSP5 lists what it finds under `/app0/ui/sfx` and offers them
all in the settings.

## Licence

GPL-3.0-or-later. PPSSPP is GPL-2.0-**or-later**, which permits combining it with
the GPL-3.0-or-later platform layer and RADV build; the combined work is GPL-3.0.
`src/platform/` is MIT, from PS5_VulkanTemplate, and keeps its notice.
`src/ui/volk/` is MIT. `src/ui/kit/aurora.cpp` is forked from PS5_VKHomebrewUI
(GPL-3.0-or-later) and keeps its copyright line. `src/net/console_curl.{c,h}` is
GPL-3.0-or-later, from BlackBearReloaded's ps5-native-app-boilerplate, and keeps
its notice.

## Credits

The hard parts of this are other people's: **Henrik Rydgård** and PPSSPP's
contributors for the emulator this is built on, **mihawk-99** for the PS5 Vulkan
driver, the payload SDK fork, the platform layer, the homebrew UI kit and the
PPSSPP port patch, **BlackBearReloaded** for the console networking in
ps5-native-app-boilerplate, **Swordpdf** for PS5SX2, which is what a standalone
emulator title on this stack looks like and whose USB controller code and
elevation request PSP5 follows, and **darkxex** for SwanStationPS5, whose
`ps5_unlock.c` is the clearest account of how a title asks to be let out of the
sandbox.

The services that answer that request are **etaHEN**, **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**
and the **PS5SX2 Helper**; without one of them running, no title here can list a
folder on a USB drive.

RetroAchievements support is rcheevos, which PPSSPP already carries, pointed at
[retroachievements.org](https://retroachievements.org) — the achievements
themselves are the work of its community.

latestRelease.name: PSP5 v1.000.100
latestRelease.body:
## PSP5 01.000.100

PSP5 now follows the console's language, reads games and texture packs from USB drives, and lets you remap the PSP's buttons.

### Interface language

Choose a language under **Settings → System → Language** and the home screen follows it, not just the emulator. 45 languages are available, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. The font atlases were rebuilt to carry them, growing from 113 glyphs to 3,055 per face. Right-to-left languages are laid out right-to-left.

Where PPSSPP already translates a term, PSP5 uses its translation. The remainder — favourites, the A–Z view, the cheat panel, the save-state slots, the button names and the description under every settings row — are PSP5's own, shipped as 78 strings in 44 languages under `assets/lang/psp5/`.

**These 78 strings are machine-translated and unreviewed in most languages.** Corrections are a one-line edit in `assets/lang/psp5/<id>.ini`: the files are plain `English = translation`, and a missing line falls back to English.

### Games and texture packs on USB drives

PSP5 now reads drives using the same layout as its own memory stick:

```
/mnt/usb0/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso        # also .cso, .chd, EBOOT.PBP
/mnt/usb0/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/         # a texture pack, with its textures.ini
```

All eight USB ports (`/mnt/usb0` … `/mnt/usb7`) and both extended drives (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`) are scanned. A texture pack on a drive takes precedence over one on the memory stick.

**This requires folder listing to be unlocked.** A PS5 app can open a file by its full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games requires listing. PSP5 requests the unlock at every start, and any of these will grant it: **etaHEN** (enable *Legacy CMD server* in its toolbox), **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**, or the **PS5SX2 Helper** (add PSP5 to its `/data/whitelist.txt`).

Without it, PSP5 runs from its own memory stick as before and USB drives appear empty. The reason is recorded in `psp5.log` as `unlock: nothing answered`.

### Button remapping

**Settings → Controls → Buttons** lists all twelve PSP buttons — the four face buttons, both shoulders, Start, Select and the four D-pad directions — with the console button each is mapped to.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cross** | set the button |
| **Square** | set a second button |
| **Triangle** | clear the second |
| **Circle** | back |

Each PSP button can be mapped to **two** console buttons, so Select can sit on both the touch pad and L3, or L on both L1 and L2.

With the prompt open, press the console button you want. Every button is a valid binding, so none is reserved for cancelling — the prompt counts down from five seconds and leaves the row unchanged. Assigning a button removes it from wherever it was previously, leaving that row as *Not set*. **Reset the buttons** restores all twelve.

Fast-forward speed has moved from System to Controls.

### USB controllers (experimental)

PSP5 can read controllers the console ignores: **Xbox 360 wired pads (XInput)**, **PS3 USB pads**, **DualShock 3** and **DualShock 4** over a cable, and generic USB HID gamepads read through their report descriptors. A USB pad is merged into player one, so it works alongside a DualSense or on its own.

**This feature is experimental and has not been tested on hardware.** It is enabled by default because it stays inactive unless a controller the console ignores is connected. To disable it:

- **Settings → Controls → USB controllers → Off**, or
- create a file named `nousbpad` in the title's folder, which prevents it from starting at all.

PSP5 only reads devices it can identify, and never touches a DualSense, keyboard, mouse, hub or storage device. It does not perform blind endpoint probing, which is known to disable a wired DualSense across the whole console until a power cycle.

If a controller does not work, `psp5.log` records every device examined and the reason it was used or skipped.

### Other changes

- Settings gained a fourth page, Controls.
- Fixed: pressing Cross on a button row advanced it to the next button instead of prompting for one.
- Fixed: `??` in place of text throughout the interface in non-Latin languages, affecting Recent, Time Played, Favorites and much else.
- Fixed: the highlight on the selected row of the button list was misaligned with its text.

### Known limitations

- **Arabic letters render unjoined.** Shaping is not implemented; text is readable but not correctly formed.
- **RTL layout is not mirrored** — text reads right to left, but the screen remains laid out left to right.
- **Japanese and Chinese game titles** read from a disc's `PARAM.SFO` still display as `?`.
- Nothing in the interface indicates when folder listing was not unlocked; USB drives simply appear empty.

### Install

Place the `PPSA99131` folder anywhere ShadowMountPlus scans:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Internal | `/data/homebrew/PPSA99131` or `/data/etaHEN/games/PPSA99131` |
| USB | `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99131` … `/mnt/usb7/homebrew/PPSA99131`, the same under `etaHEN/games`, or `/mnt/usb0/PPSA99131` … `/mnt/usb7/PPSA99131` |
| External | `/mnt/ext0/homebrew/PPSA99131` or `/mnt/ext1/homebrew/PPSA99131`, the same under `etaHEN/games`, or `/mnt/ext0/PPSA99131` |

Then install it with ShadowMountPlus. Custom `scanpath=` entries in `/data/shadowmount/config.ini` work as well.

**Updating:** replace the files inside `PPSA99131`; there is no need to uninstall first. Settings, saves and games live on the emulated memory stick in `PPSA99131/memstick/`, so leaving that folder untouched carries them over.

repos.name: PS5_Dusklight
repos.description: Dusklight for PlayStation 5: a homebrew port on RADV (Aurora, Dawn WebGPU, SDL3). Bring your own disc image.
repos.readme:
# Dusklight for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_Dusklight?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_Dusklight)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/releases/latest)
[![Track Dusklight](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/actions/workflows/track-dusklight.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/actions/workflows/track-dusklight.yml)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight), the
reverse-engineered reimplementation of a classic GameCube adventure. It draws
through Dusklight's own renderer ([Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora) on
Dawn's WebGPU) on RADV, Mesa's Vulkan driver, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

It needs a PS5 that already runs homebrew, and a disc image of the game that you
provide. No game data, Nintendo artwork, Sony software or keys are included, here
or in a build.

This is an unofficial port. It is not part of the Dusklight project and is not
supported by it: please do not take PS5 problems to them.

## Status

Tested on one console, on 2026-10-10 and 11, with the GameCube USA disc (GZ2E01).
"Seen" means it ran there and was watched, or read in the console's log; nothing
else is claimed.

| Area | Seen on the console | Not yet verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | Finds the disc image in the title's folder, boots into the game | Exit back to the home screen from the game's own menu |
| Rendering | 3840x2160 on a 59.94 Hz display, several minutes of play with no crash | Frame rate over a long session; 120 Hz; later areas of the game |
| Saving | A memory card file is created, and a save survived closing and restarting the title | |
| Button prompts | The DualSense's symbols on the game's buttons, on the file select and in play: Cross (A), Circle (B), Square (X), Triangle (Y), R1 (Z) | Other prompts (L, R, Start, the D-pad and stick pictures); a changed button mapping; the other regions' discs |
| Input | A DualSense plays the game | Each button of the mapping; rumble; a second controller |
| Sound | | Everything: the driver opens, nobody has confirmed what it sounds like |
| Shader cache | Aurora's pipeline cache opens and is written | That it is reused after a restart |

Known limits:

- **Objects can appear a frame late the first time a scene shows them.** Aurora
  compiles each new render pipeline on a worker thread and skips the draw until
  it is ready, as it does on every platform. They are cached once compiled.
- **Disc images: GameCube `.iso` or `.ciso` only.** Upstream reads RVZ, GCZ, WIA
  and WBFS through a Rust library; this port has its own small reader in its
  place (`ps5/nod/`). Wii discs are not supported.
- **No code mods, no updater, no Discord presence, no network.** They are turned
  off in this build. The mods in Dusklight's `mods/` folder (the randomizer, the
  Luau runtime and the rest) are code mods, so none is bundled, and a mod that
  needs the Luau runtime does not run. An asset-only `.dusk` (textures, files
  that replace the disc's) put in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/mods/` is listed and
  can be switched on in the Mods menu. Online mods cannot be browsed.
- **"Disc not verified" on the menu is expected.** The disc is found, not
  chosen, so it is never hashed; and a `.ciso` leaves out the disc's filler
  data, so its hash could not match the original's anyway.
- **The button symbols follow the default mapping.** The game draws a button as
  a coloured shape with a white letter, each letter a texture of its own; the
  port replaces those five textures with symbols from Kenney's Input Prompts
  (www.kenney.nl, CC0; `ps5/art/kenney/`, cut to size by `ps5/art/make-glyphs.py`,
  shipped in `res/ps5-glyphs/`, loaded as texture replacements named for the
  USA disc's textures), and turns the green tint of the A button blue. They say Cross for A, Circle for B, Square for X,
  Triangle for Y and R1 for Z, which is Dusklight's default mapping: remap the
  buttons and the symbols no longer match. A replacement of your own for the
  same texture wins, and turning texture replacements off in the settings turns
  these off too.
- **Texture packs: loose files or a `.dusk`, `.png` or `.dds`.** Files named the
  way Dolphin names them (`tex1_256x128_e6a4c7be9bf48305_14.dds`) are picked up
  from `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/userdata/TwilitRealm/Dusklight/texture_replacements/`
  and its subfolders, or from the `textures/` folder of a `.dusk`. A `.dds` may
  be uncompressed 32-bit RGBA or BGRA, BC1 (DXT1), BC3 (DXT5), BC5 or BC7, with
  or without mipmaps; this port also takes the sRGB-tagged variants of those,
  which upstream refuses. BC2 (DXT3), BC4, BC6H and ASTC are not loaded, and a
  compressed texture's width and height must be multiples of 4. Seen on the
  console on 2026-10-12 with three test files in the loose folder: BC7 tagged
  sRGB with mipmaps, DXT5, and uncompressed RGBA; a real texture pack has not
  been tried. The game makes that folder at its first start, and from this
  build on opens it to the FTP server at every start: with v0.2.0 an upload
  into it is refused until the folder's permissions are changed.
- **No file dialog.** The disc image is found by where it is, not chosen.

## Install

Download `Dusklight-PS5-vX.Y.Z.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99305`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
Build.) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Unpack the release (or build: the result is the folder `dist/PPSA99305/`).
2. Copy that whole folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/`, so that
   you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/res/          (fonts and the menus' documents)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon, and after two failed tries it skips that
   title until it is restarted.
3. Copy your disc image into the same folder, under any name ending in `.iso` or
   `.ciso`:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/your-disc.iso
   ```

   It has to be there, not elsewhere in `/data`: a title can only see its own
   folder. The game takes the first image it finds and remembers it.
4. Wait a few seconds for "Dusklight" to appear on the home screen, and start it.

Saves and settings are written to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/userdata/`. Copying a
new build over the folder leaves them, and the disc image, alone.

**The disc image.** Dusklight's own terms apply: dump your own copy of the game
([how](https://wiki.dolphin-emu.org/index.php?title=Ripping_Games)). If your dump
is RVZ or another compressed format, convert it to `.iso` with
[Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) or `nodtool` first.

## Build

The build runs on Linux (x86-64 or arm64; on a Mac, in a Linux VM) with Mihawk's
stack beside this repository:

```text
somewhere/
  PS5_Dusklight/     this repository
  PS5_Vulkan/        https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan   (with its RADV release archive built)
  PS5_Mesa/          https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa
  PS5_PayloadSDK/    https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK
```

Set that stack up first, by its own instructions, until `PS5_Vulkan` has
`.deps/native/radv-release/lib/libvulkan_radeon.ps5.a` and
`build/host/ps5-native-tool`. It needs **LLVM 22**: RADV built with an older clang
does not link into a title. Then:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight.git
cd PS5_Dusklight
ps5/tools/build.sh
```

`build.sh` does the rest, and the first run takes a while:

1. checks out Dusklight (`vendor/dusklight`) with Aurora and Borealis, and applies
   `ps5/patches/` to them;
2. fetches Dawn and SDL3 at the revisions Aurora pins into `.deps/`, and patches
   them for the console;
3. installs the payload SDK at this port's pin;
4. configures Dusklight's own CMake build with the SDK's toolchain and
   `ps5/cmake/ps5-game.cmake`, compiles about 3,000 files, links with RADV and
   writes `dist/PPSA99305/`.

Other tools, all in `ps5/tools/`:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy.sh` | Uploads `dist/PPSA99305/` over FTP (the console's address is `PS5_HOST` in `PS5_Vulkan/.env`). It never touches the disc image or `userdata/`. |
| `run.sh` | Launches the title through PS5_Vulkan's control payload and follows its log; symbolises a crash. |
| `package-release.sh VERSION` | Packs `dist/PPSA99305/` as a release zip with `SOURCE.txt`, the revision of every part. Refuses if a disc image or a save is in the folder. |
| `build-triangle.sh` | Builds a one-triangle WebGPU test in the game's place: the first thing to run when Dawn or the driver changes. |
| `vm.sh TOOL` | From macOS, runs one of the above inside a Lima VM named `ps5`. |
| `update-dusklight.sh` | Moves to upstream Dusklight's latest revision and re-applies the patches. |
| `check-patches.sh` | Says whether the Dawn and SDL3 patches apply to what Aurora now pins. |

## Keeping up with Dusklight

`vendor/dusklight` is a submodule at an upstream revision; nothing of Dusklight is
copied or forked here. What the console needs changed in Dusklight, Aurora and
Borealis is three small patches in `ps5/patches/`; Dawn and SDL3 have theirs
there too.

A [scheduled workflow](.github/workflows/track-dusklight.yml) runs
`update-dusklight.sh` every day. If the patches still apply to upstream's newest
revision, it commits that revision, so a fresh clone builds against the latest
Dusklight the patches fit. If one does not, it commits nothing and opens an issue.
It cannot build the game, so a revision it commits is not known to compile or
run: the Status table above is for the revision it was tested at
(`34a144a493`).

## How it works

```text
  Dusklight (the game's code)                     vendor/dusklight
        |
  Aurora ........ GameCube GX, pads, cards, DVD   vendor/dusklight/extern/aurora
        |              |               |
      Dawn           SDL3             nod
   (WebGPU)     ps5/sdl drivers    ps5/nod: .iso and .ciso
        |
  Vulkan: RADV + PS5 winsys, VK_KHR_display       PS5_Mesa, PS5_Vulkan
        |
  PS5 GPU
```

- **Dawn.** The fork Aurora uses already had a console port (Nintendo Switch):
  a Vulkan driver linked into the program and a native-window surface.
  `ps5/patches/dawn.patch` adds the PS5 beside it: RADV's entry point in place of
  a Vulkan library, and the console's one output as a `VK_KHR_display` surface.
- **SDL3.** Threads, time and files are FreeBSD's. `ps5/sdl/` adds a video driver
  (one display, a window that is the screen), an audio driver (AudioOut, 48 kHz
  stereo) and a joystick driver that presents each controller as a DualSense.
- **nod.** Aurora reads discs through nod, a Rust library. There is no Rust
  toolchain for the console, so `ps5/nod/nod.cpp` implements the part of nod's C
  API that is called, for plain and CISO GameCube images.
- **The console's quirks**, each found the hard way and explained where it is
  handled: constructors that ran in reverse (`ps5/tools/cc-init-array.sh`), an
  `lstat` that does not work for a title and other missing libc functions
  (`ps5/src/shims.c`), and where a title may write (`ps5/src/startup.c`).

## Credits

- [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight) by Twilit Realm and its
  contributors, on the [Twilight Princess decompilation](https://github.com/zeldaret/tp).
- [Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora), [Borealis](https://github.com/encounter/borealis),
  [nod](https://github.com/encounter/nod) and the Dawn fork by Luke Street (encounter) and contributors.
- [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa),
  [PS5_PayloadSDK](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK) and the
  [PS5 Vulkan Template](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate) by Mihawk:
  the driver, the platform layer and the tools this is built with.
- [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom.
- Mesa and RADV, Dawn, SDL, and the libraries listed in [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).
- Kenney (www.kenney.nl) for the button symbols, from Input Prompts (CC0).

## Licence

See [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). In short: the port's own files are MIT or Zlib,
one tool is GPL-3.0, and a built title is GPL-3.0 because of what it links. The
game itself is Nintendo's and is not part of this.

latestRelease.name: Dusklight for PlayStation 5 v1.0.0
latestRelease.body:
Version 1.0, with new home-screen art. Built from upstream Dusklight revision `34a144a493`, the latest on its `main`, as v0.3.0 was.

## Changed

- **New home-screen art.** The icon, the background behind the title and the splash while it starts are a new picture in the spirit of the game's own cover: a young swordsman and a black wolf, split by a seam of twilight, over carved stone in silver and sepia. The background and the splash are now the same picture.
- **Version 1.0.** The program is the same as v0.3.0's: upstream Dusklight has nothing newer to take.

## Install or update

1. Unpack `Dusklight-PS5-v1.0.0.zip`. It holds one folder, `PPSA99305`.
2. Copy that folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/`, over the old one if you have an earlier version. Your disc image, saves, settings and texture packs in that folder are left alone.
3. New install only: copy your own GameCube disc image (`.iso` or `.ciso`) into the same folder.
4. Start "Dusklight" from the home screen. If the home screen keeps the old icon, remove the title from the home screen and let ShadowMountPlus add it again: the folder and its data are kept.

No game data is in this download. The [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight#install) has the details.

## Not verified

The new art has not yet been seen on the console's home screen. Sound, the full controller mapping and long sessions remain unconfirmed.

## Source

A built title is under GPL-3.0. `SOURCE.txt` in the zip names the revision of every part it was built from; this port's is `577c762`.

`Dusklight-PS5-v1.0.0.zip` sha256: `343f8829803ecba03e8cf3168f543543771e6511dfec4e6761c60bb6f4ab8e8d`

repos.name: PS5CEMU-HAR
repos.description: Wii U, 3DS, and DS emulation for PS5 homebrew (Cemu + Azahar+ Melon DS)
repos.readme:
PS5CEMU-HAR plays your Wii U, Nintendo 3DS and Nintendo DS games on a jailbroken PS5,
with Cemu, Azahar and melonDS in one launcher made for the TV and the DualSense.

Download 4.0.1 (ZIP, 52.5 MB) · Release notes · Install · Guide · Compatibility · Credits

--- ## What's new in 4.0.1 Fixes for 4.0.0. The details are in the [release notes](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/releases/tag/v4.0.1). - **Network shares work again.** Connecting to an SMB share no longer crashes the app ([#46](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/46), [#49](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/49)), and a share's tab opens in the folder chooser ([#49](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/49)). - **DS sound at the right speed:** no more crackling or too-fast music, and the speed shown is the DS's ([#47](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/47)). - **Back to the library after a game** on more setups: the app tries each place it can start from, and a home screen tile's game says *Quit to the home screen* ([#48](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/48)). - **Artic Base and Artic Setup** ([#45](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/45)): connections time out instead of hanging, a 3DS that closes the connection no longer closes the app, the app starts over cleanly after a failed load, and the errors say what went wrong. Artic Setup says which keys `aes_keys.txt` lacks before it starts, and *Copy logs to USB* includes Azahar's log of the session before. ## What's new in 4.0.0 The biggest update yet. The full list is in the [release notes](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/releases/tag/v4.0.0). - **31 languages: every one the PS5 has.** The launcher, Settings and the in-game menus are translated into 30 new languages, with your games' names in your language too: English (UK and US), German, French (France and Canada), Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Italian, Dutch, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Greek, Turkish, Finnish, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Thai, Vietnamese and Arabic. - **Nintendo DS games** on melonDS, a third system beside the Wii U and the 3DS. - **Your games on the PS5 home screen:** *Add to home screen* gives any game a tile that starts it straight away, and *Remove from home screen* takes it off again. - **Wii U mods** from a USB drive, with a [step-by-step guide](docs/MODS.md). - **Eight themes:** Link Jack, Classic (the original 2.0 launcher, back), Eden, Meyer Oscar and Meyer Oscar Light, Midnight, Phantom and Terminal, or your own. - **Play from your PC or NAS** over the network (SMB or NFS). - **RetroAchievements** for DS games. - **Faster Wii U games:** Breath of the Wild is back near 60 fps at 1440p, and holds 60 more often at 4K. - **Pokémon X, Y, Omega Ruby, Alpha Sapphire, Sun, Moon, Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon** drawn right. - **And more:** your phone's browser as the GamePad's or a handheld's touch screen, Wii U accounts and save backups to USB, updates and DLC found on your drives and installed with one press, AMD FSR 1, settings for each game, buttons that swap, a turbo button, rumble that works, Skylanders Giants, your own launcher music, and a quicker start. ## Features | | Wii U | Nintendo 3DS | Nintendo DS | |---|---|---|---| | **Emulator** | Cemu, x64 recompiler, Vulkan | Azahar, dynarmic recompiler, Vulkan | melonDS, ARM recompiler | | **Plays** | `.wua`, `.wud`, `.wux`, unpacked games | `.3ds`, `.cci`, `.cxi`, `.app`, `.3dsx`, `.elf`, compressed `.z*`, installed `.cia` | `.nds` | | **Picture** | 4K output, 120 Hz, FSR 1, graphic packs | up to 10x resolution, texture filters, layouts, borders | sharp, smooth or square pixels, layouts, borders | | **Extras** | mods, accounts, amiibo, Skylanders portals, updates and DLC | save states, cheats, amiibo, mods, Artic Base | save states, cheats, RetroAchievements | - **One launcher for all three:** box art and game info from GameTDB, search, sorting and favourites, a page for each game, settings for each game, and an in-game menu on every system. - **Made for the DualSense:** every button remappable, motion controls, rumble, the touchpad as the touch screen, and up to four players on the Wii U. - **Updates itself:** a new release installs from inside the app. ## Install 1. **A PS5 that runs homebrew.** Any firmware up to 13.60, with etaHEN, OnionHEN, or an ELF loader on port 9021. See the [firmware and setup guide](docs/HEN-SETUP.md). 2. **Copy the app.** Download the [latest ZIP](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/raw/releases/PS5CEMU-HAR-v4.0.1.zip), extract it and copy the `PPSA99360` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99360`. 3. **Let your HEN in.** etaHEN: add `PPSA99360` to its app jailbreak list. OnionHEN: add `PPSA99360` at the end of `exact_title_ids` in `config.ini`, with no comma after it. Any other: have an ELF loader on port 9021. 4. **Add your games** (below), and start PS5CEMU-HAR from the home screen. The Setup check shows what's ready and what to do about the rest. Updating: the app offers new releases itself. Everything in `/data/ps5cemu` is kept. ## Your games | | Games folder | Also needs | |---|---|---| | **Wii U** | `/data/ps5cemu/games` | disc keys in `/data/ps5cemu/keys.txt` for encrypted `.wud` and `.wux` | | **3DS** | `/data/ps5cemu/azahar/games` | decrypted dumps, or your console's `aes_keys.txt` in `/data/ps5cemu/azahar/sysdata`; `.cia` files install from Settings | | **DS** | `/data/ps5cemu/melonds/games` | nothing: your own BIOS and firmware in `/data/ps5cemu/melonds/bios` are optional | Any other folder, a USB drive or a network share works too: **Settings > Game files** on each system. No games, keys or firmware are included. Use dumps of games and hardware you own. ## Controls | | | |---|---| | **L1 / R1** | Library and Settings | | **Touchpad click** | The next system | | **Cross / Circle** | Play or open / back | | **Options** | A game's menu: game settings, saves, graphic packs, mods, home screen tile | | **Touchpad click + Options** | The in-game menu | | **Touchpad** | The touch screen (GamePad, 3DS and DS) | Every shortcut, the in-game menu and the rest are in the [guide](docs/GUIDE.md). ## Documentation - [Guide](docs/GUIDE.md): the launcher, each system, controls, saves, mods, the remote touch screen and where files are kept - [Firmware and setup](docs/HEN-SETUP.md) · [Mods](docs/MODS.md) · [Compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) - [Building from source](docs/BUILDING.md) · [Driver performance](docs/DRIVER-PERFORMANCE.md) - Problems: **Settings > Diagnostics > Copy logs to USB**, then [open an issue](https://github.com/premohq/PS5CEMU-HAR/issues/new/choose) ## Building `make release` on Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL works) downloads every dependency at its pinned version, builds the three emulators and the launcher, and writes the app to `build/app/PPSA99360` and a ZIP to `dist/`. See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). ## Credits - [Cemu](https://github.com/cemu-project/Cemu) by the Cemu team and contributors (MPL-2.0) - [Azahar](https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar) by the Azahar team and the Citra contributors before them (GPL-2.0-or-later), with dynarmic by MerryMage and contributors - [melonDS](https://github.com/melonDS-emu/melonDS) by Arisotura and the melonDS team (GPL-3.0), with its FreeBIOS replacements - **Mihawk** for RADV on PS5 ([PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa), [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), the payload SDK fork and its platform layer) and the PS5 ports of Azahar and dynarmic ([PS5_Azahar](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Azahar)), with contributions from **mpereiraesaa** - **BlackBearReloaded** for [ProsperoEden](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden), which the launcher's layout, artwork, Eden theme and software renderer build on, and the [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) for the app runtime, packaging and sandbox elevation - **heydemoura** for the [PS5 Forwarder Format](https://github.com/heydemoura/ps5-forwarder-format) the home screen tiles use - **John Törnblom** for the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), and **pacbrew** for their PS5 libraries - [libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2) and [libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs) by Ronnie Sahlberg for the network shares, and [rcheevos](https://github.com/RetroAchievements/rcheevos) by RetroAchievements - **dolphin78** for the remote touch screen's idea and prototype (#38), and **3lmerx503** for the rumble fix (#41) - **Swordpdf** for the etaHEN jailbreak request from PS5SX2 - **Dimok** for the Wii U Homebrew Launcher's background, and the authors of the 3DS Homebrew Launcher, which inspired the 3DS side's - The [Lexend](https://github.com/googlefonts/lexend) authors for the launcher's font (SIL OFL 1.1) - [GameTDB](https://www.gametdb.com/) for box art and game information, and the authors of the [Cemu community graphic packs](https://github.com/cemu-project/cemu_graphic_packs) ## License The app's own code is GPL-3.0-or-later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). Files derived from Cemu keep Cemu's MPL-2.0, as their headers say; Azahar is GPL-2.0-or-later and melonDS GPL-3.0, and the app that includes them is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later.
