repos.readme:
🚀 PS5 FFPFSC PRO

PS5 Game Compression Utility

📥 Download • 📺 YouTube • ☕ Ko-fi

--- ## 📦 About PS5 FFPFSC PRO is a cross-platform GUI for compressing PlayStation 5 game dumps using MkPFS and FFPFSC. The application supports Windows, Linux, and macOS. The goal is simple: make PS5 game compression easy without requiring command-line tools or complicated setup. Whether you're compressing a single game, batch processing multiple titles, or browsing community compatibility reports, everything can be done from one interface. --- ## 🖼️ Screenshots ### Main Window ![PS5 FFPFSC PRO Main Window](screenshots/main-window.png) ### Community Compatibility Database ![Community Database](screenshots/community-database.png) ### Compression Progress ![Compression Progress](screenshots/compression-progress.png) --- ## ✨ Features * Compress PS5 game dumps into .ffpfsc * Supports game folders, .exfat, .ffpkg, .zip, .rar, and .7z * Drag-and-drop support * Batch compression * Multi-image queueing * Compression tuning options * Compression presets (Fast, Balanced, Max Compression, Low RAM) * Automatic update checker * Live RAM meter * Automatic retry on out-of-memory errors * Detailed logs and progress tracking * Per-game output folders * Compact mode * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Community Compatibility Database * APR / AMPR game support --- ## 📂 Supported Inputs * PS5 game folders * `.exfat` images * `.ffpkg` images * `.zip` archives * `.rar` archives * `.7z` archives --- ## 🌐 Community Compatibility Database After a successful compression, you can optionally submit your results to the community database. The database allows users to: * Share compatibility reports * Report Working / Partial / Not Working / Not Tested Yet status * Search by game name * Search by Title ID * View report counts * View ShadowMount version information * Browse compatibility reports directly from the application * Duplicate submission protection * Vote-based reporting system * Submit results directly from the application * Filter by compatibility status * Browse over 5,000+ community compatibility reports Compatibility status is vote-based so one incorrect report cannot override community results. View the live compatibility database: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dgu0p7U2yB_mhcUELz-Wkc7Yhs-avoWLY1Gcm0n5XJw/edit?usp=drive_web&ouid=115958744890792485831 Or access it directly from PS5 FFPFSC PRO. --- ## ⚙️ Compression Tuning Advanced users can fine-tune compression using: * Compression level selection * CPU core selection * Block size selection Available block sizes: * Auto * Auto-Fit * 16384 * 32768 * 65536 Smaller block sizes may improve results for games containing large numbers of small files. Compression Presets * 🚀 Fast * ⚖️ Balanced * 🗜️ Max Compression * 💾 Low RAM Presets automatically configure compression level, CPU cores, and block size. --- ## 🎮 AMPR / APR Support PS5 FFPFSC PRO can detect games that require the AMPR emulator. Features include: * Automatic PlayGo chunk detection * Automatic APR title detection * Automatic AMPR index generation * Dedicated AMPR folder configuration * Compatibility reporting support * Batch mode support --- 📊 Monitoring & Automation * Live RAM meter * Automatic update checking * Windows completion notifications * Automatic retry on memory errors * Real-time progress tracking --- 🎓 User Experience * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Full Help / FAQ section * Detailed logging * Resizable log panel * Compact mode --- ## 🚀 Getting Started 1. Download the latest release. 2. Run `PS5_FFPFSC_PRO.exe` 3. Add a game folder, archive, `.exfat`, or `.ffpkg` image. 4. Select your compression settings. 5. Click **Start**. The application handles the rest. --- ## 🛠️ Common Issues ### Out of Memory Try: * Lowering CPU cores * Lowering compression level * Closing other applications ### Disk Full Ensure sufficient free space exists in both: * Output folder * Temporary folder ### Write Errors Verify that: * Output locations are valid * Drives are writable * Storage devices have enough free space The application provides detailed error messages and recommended fixes whenever possible. --- ## 🙏 Credits ### Compression Backend * MkPFS * Bizkut ### Community Special thanks to everyone testing games, submitting compatibility reports, reporting bugs, and helping improve the project. --- ## 🔗 Links 📺 YouTube https://youtube.com/@KINGDKAK ☕ Ko-fi https://ko-fi.com/KINGDKAK 📥 Releases https://github.com/KINGDKAK/PS5-FFPFSC-PRO/releases --- ## ⚠️ Disclaimer This project is provided as-is. Only use content you legally own and follow all applicable laws in your region. --- ⭐ If you find the project useful, consider starring the repository and contributing compatibility reports to help the community.

latestRelease.body:
One of the biggest updates to PS5 FFPFSC PRO so far, featuring a complete APR/AMPR overhaul, Community Compatibility integration, compression presets, cross-platform support, and major stability improvements.

✨ New Features

🎮 APR / AMPR Support Overhauled

  • ✅ No more checkbox configuration

  • ✅ Auto-detects APR titles using playgo-chunk.dat

  • ✅ Prompts before compression if a title isn't automatically detected

  • ✅ Automatically prompts for AMPR Emu folder setup

  • ✅ Creates fakelib and injects required files automatically

  • ✅ Builds ampr_emu.index automatically using the AMPRIDX3 format

  • ✅ Works in both single-game and batch compression modes

🌐 Community Compatibility Database

  • ✅ Live Google Sheet integration directly inside the app

  • ✅ Search by game name or Title ID

  • ✅ Filter by compatibility status

  • ✅ Vote-based reporting system

  • ✅ Duplicate submission protection

  • ✅ Browse thousands of community reports without leaving the app

🎓 What's New + Feature Tour

  • ✅ Automatic "What's New" dialog after updating

  • ✅ Interactive feature tour

  • ✅ Re-launch anytime from Settings or Help / FAQ

  • ✅ Quickly learn new features after each update

⚡ Compression Presets

One-click profiles:

  • 🚀 Fast

  • ⚖️ Balanced

  • 🗜️ Max Compression

  • 💾 Low RAM

Automatically configures compression level, CPU cores, and block size.

📊 Monitoring & Automation

  • 🧠 Live RAM meter

  • 🔄 Auto update checking

  • 🔁 Automatic retry on out-of-memory errors

  • 🔔 Windows completion notifications

  • 📈 Compression ratio reporting

🛠 Additional Improvements

  • 📂 Per-game output folders

  • 📦 Multi-image queue support

  • ⚙️ Block size selector

  • ❓ Full Help / FAQ tab

  • 📺 Built-in YouTube tutorial links

🐞 Bug Fixes

📈 Progress Bar Fixes

  • Fixed overall progress getting stuck around 97%

  • Corrected stage ordering

  • Outer MkPFS compression now contributes properly to progress calculations

  • Improved ETA accuracy

🎮 APR / AMPR Stability

  • Fixed _poll crash caused by missing ampr_emu attribute

  • Fixed APR prompts not appearing during batch processing

  • Improved handling of history and disk image items

🔧 General Fixes

  • Fixed Python < 3.10 compatibility issues

  • Fixed Unicode arrow crashes on some Windows consoles

  • Fixed false multiple-game detection

  • Fixed startup crashes caused by missing folder paths

  • CPU core slider now supports up to 16 cores

📋 Requirements

  • Python 3.9+

  • customtkinter

  • pillow

  • tkinterdnd2

  • py7zr

  • rarfile

🙏 Thanks to everyone who tested games, submitted compatibility reports, reported bugs, and helped improve PS5 FFPFSC PRO.

repos.readme:
# EmuStore PS5 — prototype 0.4.0

**Projet porté par RomainJ.**

Store natif PS5 en français, utilisable à la manette. Cette version conserve l'interface avec grille des émulateurs, statuts installés/absents/mise à jour et pictogrammes PS5 × ○ △ □.

**Prototype : compatibilité réelle non validée sur console.**

## Télécharger

- [Release v0.4.0](https://github.com/romanocry/EmuStore-PS5/releases/tag/v0.4.0)
- [Archive installable EmuStore-PS5-v0.4.0.zip](https://github.com/romanocry/EmuStore-PS5/releases/download/v0.4.0/EmuStore-PS5-v0.4.0.zip)
- [Empreinte SHA-256](SHA256SUMS.txt)
- [Notes de version et vérifications](RELEASE-v0.4.0.md)

Le ZIP contient le dossier **PPSA97631**, le binaire, le module système, les ressources et les licences.

## Installer ou remplacer le store

1. Fermer EmuStore sur la console.
2. Extraire le ZIP sur le PC.
3. Avec le FTP de l'environnement homebrew, copier le dossier **PPSA97631** entier dans **/data/homebrew/**. Pour remplacer une ancienne version, remplacer uniquement les fichiers de ce dossier.
4. Faire redétecter les applications par ShadowMountPlus, puis lancer EmuStore.
5. Utiliser les commandes affichées à l'écran.

La console doit disposer d'un environnement homebrew adapté, d'un accès Internet et des permissions nécessaires. Les prérequis propres à chaque émulateur restent applicables. Aucun jeu, BIOS ou clé fourni.

## Sources et documentation antérieure

**Les sources exactes de v0.4.0 n'ont pas été récupérées et ne sont pas incluses dans cette publication.**

Les [sources v0.3.1](EmuStore-PS5-v0.3.1-sources.zip) et la [documentation v0.3.1](docs/README-v0.3.1.md) sont conservées pour référence. Elles décrivent la version précédente. Les archives « Source code » automatiques de GitHub reflètent les fichiers du dépôt ; elles ne sont pas les sources du binaire v0.4.0.

## Crédits et licences

- Projet et catalogue : **RomainJ.**
- Développement assisté par OpenAI Codex.
- Base native et renderer : BlackBearReloaded, **GPL-3.0-or-later**.
- Émulateurs et dépendances : leurs auteurs et licences respectifs.

Voir [LICENSE](LICENSE), [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md) et [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

repos.name: ProsperoStore
repos.description: Native PS5 app store for the homebrew catalog at homebrew.page (title PPSA99000)
repos.readme:
ProsperoStore

The native PS5 app store for homebrew.page

Browse, install, update and uninstall PS5 homebrew from your couch, with the controller or a keyboard.

> [!TIP] > **By default, ProsperoStore uses [homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page)**, the community > catalog of PS5 homebrew. Browse it on the web at **[homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page)**, then > install from the console with one button. The catalog is signed, and every download is checked > against it before anything touches your console. > [!IMPORTANT] > **ProsperoStore is an aggregator.** It lists and installs apps; it doesn't build, maintain or > support them. Each app belongs to its own developer. For a bug, a question or a feature request > about an app, go to that app's GitHub repository (the QR code on its page in the store opens its > page on [homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page), which links to the source) and contact its > developer there. Issues here are for the store itself: browsing, installing, updating and > uninstalling.

ProsperoStore is a homebrew app store that runs natively on the PS5. Title ID `PPSA99000`. It is an alpha; the current version is the newest one on the [releases page](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoStore/releases). > [!WARNING] > **ProsperoStore includes an exact-title one-shot helper built from upstream > [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon).** The PS5 jailbreak > environment must provide [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) > ([1.7beta4](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/releases/tag/1.7beta4) or newer > recommended) and a local ELF loader on TCP port 9021. If a resident Lapy service is already running, the store asks > it first; otherwise it sends the packaged helper over that local connection, so no separate Lapy > payload is needed. Installs, updates and uninstalls have run on firmware 6.02 and 12.70. Other > firmware is experimental; the helper refuses runtime layouts it does not know instead of guessing. ## Features - **The whole [homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page) catalog** - Discover shows one app big over shelves (New and updated, Apps, Games, Tools, Coming soon, On this console); each section has its own grid, with search by name or developer and sorting by name, release or update. - **Likes and comments** - switched on in **Settings**, every tile shows the app's likes and comments, Discover gains a **Most liked** shelf, the grids a "Most liked" order, and an app's page its latest comments; see [Likes and comments](#likes-and-comments). - **One-button installs** - Cross on an app's page downloads it, checks it against the signed catalog, unpacks it and puts it in place. A ring, four steps (Download, Verify, Unpack, Finish) and the time left show the progress; Circle cancels, and nothing changes until the end. - **Updates** - apps installed with the store are offered their newer versions (the Updates section, or Update all). A running app is never touched until it is closed. An update replaces the app's whole folder; the previous folder, with anything you had put inside it, is kept in `/data/prosperostore/previous/` (or `prosperostore/previous` on the app's drive) until that app's next update, so files of yours are never lost. Move them back by FTP if you need them. - **Clean uninstalls** - hold the Uninstall button: the app's folder goes and so does its home-screen tile. Its saved data stays. - **Fast file work** - unpacking and removing run in a helper started through the payload loader, which the console does not slow down: Kodi's 2,700 files unpack in about 25 seconds. - **Apps you installed by hand** - an app the catalog lists can be handed over to the store (Manage with ProsperoStore) and is updated from then on. - **Any install location** - the folders ShadowMountPlus scans on the internal drive, an extended drive or a USB drive, chosen in **Settings**. - **It updates itself** - when a newer ProsperoStore is listed, its own page offers it; see [Updating ProsperoStore](#updating-prosperostore). - **Looks and feel** - each app's picture is made from its own icon's colours, with a soft opening animation, background music, interface sounds and springy motion. **Reduce motion** is in **Settings**. - **Keyboard support** - a USB keyboard works as well as the controller; see [Controls](#controls). - **A QR code on every app's page** - opens the app's page on homebrew.page, with its release notes and source. ## Install > [!TIP] > **Use [ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/releases/tag/1.7beta4) > or newer**, especially on newer firmware. It mounts ProsperoStore from the folder (or drive) you > copy it to, and it also mounts `/data` and USB and extended storage drives into the app's > sandbox. Older versions may not register the store or give it access to `/data`, which shows > as "Read only" in the store. 1. Make sure the console runs ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 or newer and a payload loader on port 9021 (see the warning above). 2. Download `PPSA99000.zip` from the release and unzip it. A release ZIP built by the workflow can be checked with `gh attestation verify PPSA99000.zip -R blackbearreloaded/ProsperoStore` (GitHub CLI); this covers releases built by GitHub Actions from now on, not earlier ones. 3. Copy the `PPSA99000` folder into a folder ShadowMountPlus scans, for example `/data/homebrew`, so that `eboot.bin` ends up at `/data/homebrew/PPSA99000/eboot.bin` (not one folder deeper). 4. Wait a few seconds for ShadowMountPlus to add it to the home screen, then open ProsperoStore. > [!NOTE] > **"Can't start the game or app" (CE-107750-0) after copying the folder?** The console only > starts an app whose files are open to every user (permissions `777`), and what copies the files > decides their permissions. Some FTP servers and programs upload them as `755` or `644`. > > - Set `PPSA99000` and everything inside it to `777` with your FTP program (often "File > permissions", applied to subfolders and files), then open the store again. > - To avoid it next time: the [ftpsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv) payload writes > uploads with the right permissions, and in WinSCP a transfer preset with "Set permissions" > `0777` does it for every upload. > - Updates done from inside the store, and apps the store installs, are set to `777` for you. The store keeps its own data in `/data/prosperostore` (settings, cache, install records and logs), outside the app's folder, so updates keep it. ### Updating older ProsperoEden installations For ProsperoEden (`PPSA99008`) installations that still keep personal game files inside `assets/`, Store moves the known legacy folders (`roms`, `keys`, `firmware`, `updates`, `mods`, `ryujinx`, and `save-import`) to `/data/prosperoeden` during an update. Saves and settings are left unchanged. The migration resumes through the update journal if it is interrupted. Store refuses the update before replacing the app if a destination holds files, a custom game-files folder is selected, settings cannot be read safely, or the migration would cross drives. Resolve the reported conflict or move the files to the chosen folder first. An update made with ProsperoStore 1.000.050 or older left those folders in the store's own `prosperostore/previous/PPSA99008/assets`, where ProsperoEden does not look. The next update of ProsperoEden moves them to `/data/prosperoeden` by the same rules, before that previous folder is replaced. If the same folder holds files both there and in the installed app, the update is refused and names both places: keep one of them, then update again. See [migration validation](docs/eden-migration-validation.md) for automated checks, controlled testing on an original/phat PS5 with firmware 4.50, and the reproducible console test harness. ## Controls | Action | Controller | Keyboard | | --- | --- | --- | | Move | D-pad or left stick | Arrows | | Open, install, update | Cross | Enter or Space | | Back, close | Circle | Escape or Backspace | | Previous / next section (they go round) | L1 / R1 | Shift+Tab / Tab, or Page Up / Page Down | | Close ProsperoStore | Hold Circle on the home page | Hold Escape | | Search | Triangle | / or F3 | | Downloads; hold to uninstall on an app's page | Square | Delete or F2 | | Settings | Options | F10 or the Menu key | | Sort | R3 | F5 | | Like or comment, on an app's page | Touchpad | F6 | | To an app's comments and back to the top, on its page | R2 (L2 also goes back) | F7 | ## Updating ProsperoStore When [homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page) lists a newer ProsperoStore, the store asks when it opens: **Update now**, **What's new** (the release notes) or **Skip**. The store's own page (**Settings > ProsperoStore**) offers the update too. It downloads and unpacks like any app; then the store closes, a small helper started through the payload loader puts the new files in place, and a notification says when to open it again. The next start runs the new version. Versions before 1.000.020 show a short notice at the top right instead of the question. Updating from inside the store is the easy way. To update by hand, replace the `PPSA99000` folder with the one from the new release; if the console then says it can't start the app, see the note about permissions under [Install](#install). ## Likes and comments Every app in the catalog has a discussion on GitHub, the same one its page on homebrew.page shows: the replies are the app's comments, and the upvotes of the discussion are its likes. They are on from the first start; **Settings → Show likes and comments** switches them off. While the switch is off the store asks GitHub for nothing and shows none of it. With it on: - every tile shows the app's likes and comments, zero included; - Discover has a **Most liked** shelf, the ten apps with the most likes in order (it is there when some app has a like), and each section's grid can be sorted by "Most liked"; - an app's page shows its likes and comments among its facts, and a **Comments** block after the release notes with the latest ten: who, when and what they wrote. R2 jumps straight to it, and R2 again or L2 goes back to the top; - the Touchpad on an app's page shows a QR code for the app's discussion. Scan it with your phone to like the app or to write a comment there. Both happen on GitHub and need a GitHub account; the store itself never writes anything. The store reads two kinds of file for this, from one address only: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog/comments-data/`, the counts of every app when the catalog is refreshed and one app's comments when its page opens. These files are not part of the signed catalog and decide nothing about what is installed. What they hold is shown as plain text, cut to length, and the only address taken from them is the discussion's, which must be on github.com and is only ever shown as that code. When they can't be read there are simply no likes and comments, and the rest of the store works as before. ## Reporting a problem If the store shows no apps, stays offline or can't install something, switch on **Debug log** in **Settings** (Options button) and repeat what failed. The log starts with what the store found when it opened (the access it was given, the catalog), then records each step it takes: the network requests and every install. The switch stays on the next time the store opens, wherever the store can keep its settings. Send one of these with your report: - a photo of **About**, where the **Debug trace** section lists the steps (scroll for all of it); - the file `/data/prosperostore/debug-trace.txt`, fetched by FTP; - if the store couldn't write to `/data`: `ProsperoStore-debug-trace.txt` on a USB drive that was plugged in before the store was opened. Say which console and firmware you have, your ShadowMountPlus version and your payload loader. The log holds no account details or passwords. Switch **Debug log** off again afterwards: while it is on, the store starts a little slower. ## Custom catalogs **Settings → Development options** has two switches, one for each source: - **Official catalog** - homebrew.page, always signature-checked. On by default. - **Custom catalog** - your own feed. Switching it on asks for its address when none is set. With both on, the custom catalog's apps are added to homebrew.page's and carry a "Custom catalog" mark on their page. Where both list the same title ID, the official app is the one shown, and the store says how many custom apps were hidden. With only the custom catalog on, it replaces the official one, which is what you want to test a new version of an app that is already listed. The store needs one catalog, so the official one can only be switched off while a custom one is in use. **Custom catalog URL** is the HTTPS directory containing the feed, for example `https://example.com/api/v1/`: the API directory, not the website homepage, a GitHub repository URL or `index.json`. **Restore official catalog** goes back to homebrew.page alone. Changes are saved at once and apply when you close and reopen ProsperoStore. **Verify custom catalog signatures** is on by default and uses the official catalog's built-in public keys, so it suits a copy of the signed official feed. For an independently published feed you can turn it off after confirming the warning; the store then labels the catalog **Signatures not checked**. Only do this with a publisher you trust: hashes detect changed downloads, but an unchecked publisher controls both the download address and its expected hash. Custom feeds must implement the [catalog API](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog/blob/main/docs/api.md): schema-3 `manifest.json`, `index.json`, `versions.json`, and `apps/<TITLEID>.json`. The manifest must list the SHA-256 of each API JSON file. `manifest.sig` is required only while signature verification is on. API-file hashes, artifact hashes, ZIP validation, HTTPS certificate checks, and the existing GitHub release download policy remain enforced. Plain HTTP, self-signed TLS certificates, arbitrary JSON lists, and downloads from non-GitHub artifact hosts are not supported. Each API URL and signature mode has its own catalog cache. Re-enabling verification never reuses an unchecked catalog; the official signed catalog retains its saved rollback protection. Signature checks off also disables sequence rollback checks, so development feeds can rebuild with a lower sequence. Store update notices use the selected catalog, and app QR codes use its `page` URLs. ## Roadmap Ideas for what a solid app store should do, in no promised order. Some need changes to the [catalog](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog) as well as to the store. ### Versions and updates - **Install an older version** - pick a past release on an app's page and install it; an app held at a version is left alone by Update all. - **Roll back in one press** - put back the previous version the store already keeps after an update, with the files you had inside it. - **Skip or hold updates** - "don't offer this update" or "never update", for each app. - **What's new before updating** - the release notes for every app in the Updates list, as the store already shows for itself. - **Automatic updates** - optionally update apps when the store opens, all of them or only the ones you mark. ### Finding apps - **Categories and tags** - emulators, media, streaming, utilities, beyond App, Game and Tool. - **Collections** - curated shelves such as "Start here" or "Emulators". - **Screenshots** - pictures of the app on its page. - **Popularity** - download counts, and sorting by them. - **Favourites** - a list kept on the console. - **Search in descriptions** - not only names and developers. ### Trust and safety - **What an app does outside its sandbox** - a short list on its page, from the catalog's scan of each release. - **Firmware and requirements** - which firmware an app was tested on and what it needs (ShadowMountPlus version, Lapy, extra files), checked before installing. - **Report a problem with an app** - a QR code to the app's issue page, with the console's firmware and the app's version filled in. ### Managing what is installed - **Storage view** - the size of each app, the previous versions the store keeps and its caches, with a way to clear each. - **Move an app** - between the console's storage, a USB drive and the extended drive. - **App data** - show where an app keeps its data, and offer to remove it when uninstalling. - **Back up and restore app data** - to a USB drive. - **Repair** - check an installed app against the catalog and reinstall it when it differs. - **Export the installed list** - and install everything again on another console. ### Downloads - **Resume interrupted downloads** - large apps start again from zero today. - **Queue controls** - reorder, pause and retry. - **Install from a USB drive or a local ZIP** - checked against the catalog when the app is listed. - **A notification when a download finishes** - through the PS5's own notifications. ### For developers - **Beta channel** - opt in to an app's pre-releases. - **Install a test build** - from a pull request or an address, in Development options. - latestRelease.body:
Likes and comments arrive in the store, and app names in other languages are drawn properly. **Still an alpha version**: please report problems.

- **Likes and comments.** Every app in the catalog has a discussion on GitHub, the same one its page on homebrew.page shows. The store now shows each app's likes and comments on its tile, and the comments themselves on the app's page. They are refreshed about once an hour.
- **Most liked.** Discover has a **Most liked** shelf, and R3 on a grid adds **Most liked** to the sort orders.
- **Like or comment from your phone.** On an app's page, press the Touchpad for a QR code that opens the app's discussion; liking and commenting need a GitHub account. R2 jumps to the comments and back, L2 returns to the top.
- **A switch for it.** **Options → Settings → Show likes and comments** is on from the first start. Switched off, the store asks GitHub for nothing and shows none of it.
- **App names in other languages.** A name with an accented letter was shown with a question mark in its place ("R?gie5"). Names, authors, descriptions and release notes are now drawn with accented Latin letters, Greek and Cyrillic. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hebrew are not covered yet.
- **Built on ps5-opengl SDK 1.0.2.**

Update from inside the store: it asks when it opens. To install by hand, unzip `PPSA99000.zip` and replace the `PPSA99000` folder. If the console then says it can't start the app (CE-107750-0), see the note under Install in the README.

`SHA256SUMS` lists the ZIP's SHA-256. This release was built by GitHub Actions from the tag.

repos.name: ps4mount
repos.description: Allows for PKG games on USB external devices to mount on jailbroken PS5s without installing on internal storage or PS5 formatted USB storage
repos.readme:
# PS4Mount

> [!CAUTION]
> **PS4Mount is a work in progress. Use it at your own risk.**
>
> On some consoles and firmwares it can still make the system report that its **database is
> corrupted**. When that happens the console rebuilds its database on the next start, games added by
> PS4Mount can disappear from the library until PS4Mount runs again, and you may have to restart the
> console to get out of repeated error prompts. A forced restart can lose data that was not saved yet.
> **Back up your save data** (PS Plus cloud storage or a USB drive) before using PS4Mount, and
> [report any problem](#reporting-problems) with the log.

Play PS4 fake PKGs on a jailbroken PS5 straight from a USB drive, without installing them.

Put the game (and its update) `.pkg` files on a USB drive, plug it in and load `ps4mount.elf`.
PS4Mount finds the packages, adds the games to the home screen and lets you play them from the
drive. Nothing is copied to the console storage, and deleting a game on the console only removes
it from the library: the `.pkg` stays on the drive.

![PS4Mount icon](assets/icon0.png)

## Screenshots

Notifications on the home screen while PS4Mount scans the USB drives:

![Scan notifications on the PS5 home screen](docs/notifications.png)

The web panel, opened from the **Media** tab:

![PS4Mount web panel](docs/web-panel.png)

## Features

- Detects PS4 fake PKGs (game, update and add-ons) in the root of any connected USB drive, or in other
  folders chosen in the settings.
- Adds the games to the home screen with their icon, name and update version.
- Applies updates: put the update `.pkg` next to the game and it is picked up automatically.
- Installs add-ons (DLC), with data or unlock-only. An add-on is matched to its game by title ID, or by
  the add-on IDs the game lists (so add-ons of another region of the same game work too).
- Adds many games in groups, so a drive with dozens of games does not overload the console.
- Games run from the drive; no internal storage is used for the packages.
- Deleting a game from the PS5 removes it from the library only. The `.pkg` is never deleted.
- Notifications while scanning (how many games were found on each drive) and for added and removed
  games.
- A web panel, also available as **PS4Mount** in the **Media** tab, to see the games and add or
  remove them from the library.

## Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with fake PKG support (for example etaHEN with kstuff).
  Any firmware with fake PKG support. From 6.00 the games are registered the usual way (reported
  working on 6.50, tested on 13.20). Below 6.00 that made the console report a corrupted database
  (5.50), so there PS4Mount registers each game on its own (confirmed working on 5.50), and does not
  add games if the firmware lacks that function. The startup notification and the log say which one
  is used.
- An ELF loader listening on port **9021** to send the payload.
- Access to the kernel log: either **klogsrv** running on port 3232, or no other payload reading
  `/dev/klog`. PS4Mount reads the system log to know when a game starts and when a delete is
  confirmed. Without it, games cannot start (see [How it works](#how-it-works)).
- A USB drive formatted as **exFAT**.
- PS4 **fake** PKGs (game, and optionally its update and add-ons). Retail PKGs are not supported.

## Usage

Download `ps4mount.elf` from the [Releases](https://github.com/gasb07/ps4mount/releases) page
(or [build it](#building)).

1. Copy the PS4 game `.pkg` (and its update and add-on `.pkg` files, if you have them) to the **root**
   of the USB drive. The file names do not matter.
2. Plug the drive into the PS5.
3. Send `ps4mount.elf` to the ELF loader (port 9021). Do this after every console boot, or add it to
   the payloads your jailbreak loads automatically.
4. Wait for the notifications:
   - `Scanning usb0 for PS4 games...`
   - `usb0: 2 PS4 game(s) found, 2 new or updated`
   - `Adding 1/2: <game name> (CUSAxxxxx)`
   - `<game name> ready to play`
5. Start the game from the home screen.

On the first run PS4Mount moves every package it uses into a folder per game on the same drive:

```
/ps4/CUSAxxxxx/app.pkg                          game
/ps4/CUSAxxxxx/patch.pkg                        update (optional)
/ps4/CUSAxxxxx/addcont/CUSAyyyyy/<LABEL>/ac.pkg add-on (optional)
```

A game is reported as ready only after its add-ons are installed too. An add-on whose game is not on the
same drive stays where it is and waits: it is moved and installed as soon as its game is on the drive.
The scan notification says how many add-ons are waiting.

Keep this layout. To add more games later, copy their `.pkg` files to the root of the drive again.

### Web panel

Open **PS4Mount** in the **Media** tab, or browse to `http://<PS5 IP>:8770` from any device on
the same network. The panel shows every game found on the connected drives, with its state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Ready | In the library and ready to play |
| Running | The game is open |
| Not in library | Removed from the library; the `.pkg` is still on the drive |
| Adding | Being added to the library |
| Installed on console | A normal installation of this game exists; PS4Mount leaves it alone |
| On another drive | The same game is also on another connected drive, which is the one used |

Buttons:

- **Remove from library**: removes the game from the home screen. The `.pkg` stays on the drive.
- **Move pkgs back**: removes the game from the library and moves its `.pkg` files back to where they
  came from (see [Moving pkgs back](#moving-pkgs-back)).
- **Add to library**: adds a removed game back.
- **Scan for games**: checks the drives now and shows how many games were found on each one.
- **Settings**: see below.
- **Log**: shows the PS4Mount log.
- **Stop**: stops PS4Mount. Its games cannot start until it is loaded again.

### Settings

![PS4Mount settings](docs/settings.png)

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Folders to search for pkgs | `/` | Folders, relative to each drive, where new `.pkg` files are picked up (one per line). `/` is the root. The `ps4` folder cannot be used: it holds the games already moved. |
| Add new games in groups | On | Adds many new games in groups instead of one after the other, which keeps the console stable when a drive has a lot of games. |
| Games per group | 5 | Size of each group (1 to 50). |
| Install add-ons (DLC) | On | Moves and installs add-on `.pkg` files. When off, add-ons are left where they are. |

The settings also have **Move all games back** and **Pick up moved-back pkgs again** (see below).

Settings are saved in `/data/ps4mount/config.txt`.

The panel has no password. Anyone on your local network can open it.

### Removing games

Deleting a game from the PS5 (Options > Delete on the home screen, or Settings > Storage), or using
**Remove from library** in the panel, removes the game from the library and leaves the `.pkg` on the
drive. A removed game comes back
when you reconnect the drive or click **Add to library**.

To delete the game for good, delete its `/ps4/CUSAxxxxx` folder from the drive on a computer.

### Moving pkgs back

PS4Mount records where every `.pkg` came from in `ps4/CUSAxxxxx/origin.txt` on the drive: the folder
(any of the scan folders) and the original file name. **Move pkgs back** on a game, or **Move all games
back** in the settings, undoes the move:

- The game leaves the library (several games are handled in groups, like when adding).
- The game, its update, older updates kept aside and its add-ons go back to their original folder with
  their original name. A folder that no longer exists is created again, and an existing file is never
  replaced: ` (1)` is added to the name.
- `.pkg` files moved by versions before 0.5.0 have no record and go to the drive root as
  `CUSAxxxxx - <game> - game.pkg`, `... - update.pkg` and `... - <add-on label>.pkg`.
- The files PS4Mount created for the game are removed. Folders are only removed when empty, and no
  `.pkg` is ever deleted.

The `.pkg` files moved back stay where they are on the next scans (they are listed in
`/data/ps4mount/restored.txt`). To add them again, use **Pick up moved-back pkgs again** in the
settings. A `.pkg` you move, rename or replace yourself is picked up as usual.

## Good to know

- Load PS4Mount soon after every boot. While it is not running, the console does not see the
  packages and may hide the games; they come back as soon as PS4Mount runs again.
- Do not unplug the drive while a game is running.
- **Two or more drives connected at the same time can make the whole console interface slow** (home
  screen, Control Center, game hubs), with or without PS4Mount: the system checks its storage devices
  more often with each extra drive or partition. A drive with extra partitions (for example a boot
  partition added by a multiboot tool) counts as several. If the interface gets slow, keep one drive
  connected, ideally with a single partition.
- For a game with an update, the library and the PS5's own "installed" notification show the version
  of the game pkg (for example 01.00). The game runs with the update; the web panel shows its version.
- Games already installed the normal way on the console are never touched, and their add-ons on the
  drive are not installed.
- **Close PS4Mount games before putting the console in rest mode.** Rest mode powers the drive off, and a
  game left open cannot read its files from the drive after waking up: it locks up, and closing it can
  hang on the "Closing" screen, which needs a console restart. Games that were not open stay in the
  library and work normally after waking up.
- **Games with more than about 29 add-ons:** while a game runs, the console mounts each of its packages (the game,
  the update and every add-on) with two virtual devices: a PS4 package holds an outer filesystem with the
  real content as a second filesystem inside it. The console has 64 of these devices, so a running game
  can use at most about 30 packages: the game, its update and roughly 29 add-ons. A game with more
  add-ons (for example Civilization VII with 35) starts normally but only sees the first add-ons, in
  alphabetical order of their label. This is a console limit that applies to installed games too; it
  does not limit how many games you can have.
- If a game fails to start right after being added, start it again. The log (panel > **Log**) shows
  what happened.

## Reporting problems

If something does not work, open an issue with the
[bug report form](https://github.com/gasb07/ps4mount/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml). It asks for
what is needed to find the cause:

1. **PS4Mount version**: shown at the top of the web panel and in the startup notification.
2. **PS5 firmware**, the **jailbreak / HEN** and every **payload** you load, with their versions.
3. Whether **klogsrv** is running.
4. **The game**: name and title ID (`CUSAxxxxx`), and whether it has an update and add-ons.
5. **Your drives**: how many are connected, how they are formatted (exFAT) and whether a drive has
   more than one partition.
6. **What happened**: what you did, what you expected, and the exact message or error code shown on
   the console.
7. **The log**: open the web panel, click **Log** and copy the text, or download
   `/data/ps4mount/log.txt` over FTP. Include the part from the moment the problem happened.

Do not attach `.pkg` files or links to them.

## How it works

A PS4 PKG install on the PS5 is mostly a byte copy of the package to `/user/app/<TITLE_ID>/app.pkg`
plus some metadata. PS4Mount skips the copy:

1. It writes the files an install would leave on the console, generated from the package itself:
   `app.json`, `app.pbm`, `app.xml`, `patch.*`, the PlayGo records (`/user/playgo/...`,
   `/system_data/playgo/<TITLE_ID>/pfs.pbm`), the app metadata, and the fake license (`.rif`/`.idx`)
   decrypted from the package.
2. The game files go into an internal folder, `/system_data/ps4mount/app/<TITLE_ID>` (and
   `/system_data/ps4mount/patch/<TITLE_ID>` for an update), where `app.pkg` and `patch.pkg` are
   symbolic links to the packages on the drive. That folder is mounted over `/user/app/<TITLE_ID>`
   (and `/user/patch/<TITLE_ID>`) with `nullfs`. The drive itself is never mounted there.
3. It asks the system to register the title (`sceAppInstUtilAppInstallAll`), which adds it to the
   library and refreshes the home screen. PS4Mount never writes to the system databases itself.
4. A delete from the console can only remove the links, never the packages. While a delete screen
   is open (on the home screen or in Settings > Storage) PS4Mount also unmounts the game folders,
   so the system can remove `/user/app/<TITLE_ID>` without an error.

State and log are kept in `/data/ps4mount/`. The Media tab shortcut is `PMNT00001`
(`/user/app/PMNT00001`).

## Building

Requirements: the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) in `/opt/ps5-payload-sdk`
(or set `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK`), `xxd` and bash.

```sh
./build.sh          # builds build/ps4mount.elf
```

Unit tests (crypto, the generated install files and the `param.sfo` parser) run on the computer, with
no console or SDK:

```sh
bash test/run.sh
```

GitHub Actions runs them before every build.

Optional tools:

```sh
python3 tools/make_icon.py                                 # redraws assets/icon0.png (needs Pillow)
python3 tools/gen_keys.py <LibOrbisPkg>/LibOrbisPkg/Util/Keys.cs   # regenerates src/keys.h
```

### Releases

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) builds every push and pull request with the PS5
Payload SDK release set in `SDK_VERSION`, and keeps `ps4mount.elf` as a build artifact.

To publish a release:

1. Set the new version in `src/main.c` (`#define VERSION "PS4Mount X.Y.Z"`) and commit it.
2. Tag the commit and push the tag:
   ```sh
   git tag vX.Y.Z
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

The workflow checks that the tag matches `VERSION`, builds the payload and creates the GitHub
release with `ps4mount.elf` and its SHA-256 checksum attached.

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.c` | Daemon: drive scan, registration, mounts, klog events, panel actions |
| `src/pkg.c` | PKG reader and fake-key entry decryption |
| `src/build.c` | Generators for the install files (app/patch metadata, PlayGo records, license) |
| `src/db.c` | Library rows (`app.db`, `appinfo.db`) |
| `src/crypto.c` | SHA-256, AES-128-CBC, CRC32C, RSA-2048 |
| `src/web.c`, `web/index.html` | Web panel |
| `test/` | Unit tests (`bash test/run.sh`) |
| `tools/pdb_*_template.bin` | PlayGo record layouts (no title data) |
| `third_party/sqlite/` | SQLite amalgamation |

## Credits

PS4Mount does not contain code copied from other projects except where noted below.

| Project | Author | License | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) | John Törnblom | GPL-3.0-or-later | Toolchain, headers and runtime linked into the payload |
| [LibOrbisPkg](https://github.com/maxton/LibOrbisPkg) | maxton | LGPL-3.0 | Source of the fake PKG key (`PkgDerivedKey3Keyset`, in `src/keys.h`) and reference for the PKG entry encryption, entry IDs and the `playgo-chunk.dat` layout |
| [SQLite](https://sqlite.org) | SQLite authors | Public domain | `third_party/sqlite/` (amalgamation 3.46.1), used to write the library databases |
| [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) | drakmor | GPL-3.0 | Inspiration for auto-mounting games from USB drives and for registering titles with `sceAppInstUtilAppInstallAll` on firmware 12.00+. No code was used. |
| [ps5-app-dumper](https://github.com/EchoStretch/ps5-app-dumper) | EchoStretch | see project | Reference for the Media tab shortcut (`applicationCategoryType` 65536 with `deeplinkUri`). No code was used. |

## License

PS4Mount is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
It links the PS5 Payload SDK runtime (GPL-3.0-or-later). `src/keys.h` carries data published by
LibOrbisPkg under the LGPL-3.0. SQLite is in the public domain.

This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. Only use it with
games you own.

repos.readme:
# DevilutionX for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_DevilutionX?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_DevilutionX)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-see%20LICENSING.md-orange)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew build of [DevilutionX](https://github.com/diasurgical/devilutionX),
the source port of Diablo and Hellfire, as an installed title (`PPSA99308`) with
a controller, a keyboard and a mouse. The game draws its picture in software, as
it always has; SDL3's Vulkan renderer puts it on the screen through RADV, from
the [PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

It needs a PS5 that already runs homebrew, and **your own copy of Diablo**
(`DIABDAT.MPQ`). No game data, Blizzard artwork, Sony software or keys are
included here.

This is an unofficial build. DevilutionX has a PS5 port of its own
(`Packaging/ps5` upstream, launched through websrv); this one is separate and
is not supported by the DevilutionX project: please do not take its problems
to them.

**Free of charge, for non-commercial use.** A built `eboot.bin` links
DevilutionX (Sustainable Use License) with GPL-3.0 parts of the PS5 stack, and
the two licences' conditions do not fit together on one program:
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md) says where that stands.

## Status

Tested on one console (firmware 13.60, a 3840x2160 output) on 2026-10-12, with
the retail `DIABDAT.MPQ`, at DevilutionX `b0a3b7ba`. "Seen" means it ran there
and was looked at through [PS5 DevLoop](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevLoop)
(a virtual controller and the title's own frames) or read in the console's
log; nothing else is claimed. Sound, the keyboard and the mouse were tried by
hand on the same console.

| Area | Seen on the console | Not yet verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | The intro film, the main menu, a new hero, and into Tristram | Hellfire (needs `hellfire.mpq`), the shareware `spawn.mpq` |
| Picture | Fills the screen at 960x540 (the default) and at 1280x720; Settings lists 1080p, 720p, 540p and 480p | 1080p and 480p in play; a 1080p television |
| Controller | Menus (Cross confirms, Circle goes back), walking with the left stick, the inventory, picking an item up, the game menu, the modifier hint overlays | Each button in play; rumble |
| Button prompts | The DualSense's symbols: "△ to use" on a potion, and the bindings in Settings > Padmapping | Every prompt in the game |
| Keyboard and mouse | Both libraries load and open at start-up. Played with a keyboard and a mouse by Gary Riches on the console (2026-10-12) | Each key and button; text entry; the prompts changing to the keyboard's wording |
| Saving | Save Game from the menu; the hero and the save found again after a restart | |
| Settings | Resolution changed and changed back; kept in `userdata/diablo.ini` | Every other option |
| Sound | Listened to by Gary Riches on the console (2026-10-12) | Music, speech and effects each checked against the PC game |
| Exit | Exit Diablo and Quit Game both close the title (exit status 0) | Closing it from the home screen |
| Multiplayer | | Not built: `NONET` is on |

Known limits:

- **The game menu is Options and the touchpad button together.** DevilutionX
  uses Start as a modifier (hold it to see what the other buttons do), and
  opens its menu with Start and Select; the touchpad's click is Select here,
  because the console keeps the Create button for itself.
- **A hero's name is the random one the game offers** unless a keyboard is
  plugged in: the console's on-screen keyboard is not opened.
- **Text from a keyboard is US layout.** The console gives key codes and no
  characters, so the driver makes the characters itself.
- **Assets are loose files** (`assets/`, `mods/`), not `devilutionx.mpq`:
  Ubuntu's `smpq`, which would pack them, aborts on arm64.

## Controls

**Controller.** These are DevilutionX's defaults for a PlayStation pad, read
from its source (`InitPadmapActions` in `Source/diablo.cpp`).

In menus: D-pad or left stick to move, **Cross** to confirm, **Circle** to go
back, **Square** to delete a hero.

In the game:

| Button | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Left stick, D-pad | Walk |
| Right stick | Move the pointer |
| Circle | Main action: attack, talk, and lift or place an item in the inventory |
| Triangle | Second action: pick up from the ground, open chests and doors, use an item in the inventory |
| Square | Cast the active spell |
| Cross | Open the quick spell list to choose the active spell; close a panel |
| L1 / R1 | Drink a health / a mana potion from the belt |
| L2 / R2 | Character sheet / inventory |
| L3 | Automap |
| R3 | Left mouse click at the pointer |

Two buttons change what the others do while held, and the game draws the
choices on screen while you hold them:

| Hold | Then | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Options | D-pad, face buttons | Opens a panel: the icons shown are character, inventory, map, quests, spell book |
| Touchpad button | Face buttons | Sets or casts a spell hotkey (the four empty squares) |
| Touchpad button | L2 / R2 | Quest log / spell book |
| Touchpad button | D-pad | Moves the pointer |
| Touchpad button | L1 or R3 | Left click (L1) / right click (R3); R1 is right click too |
| Options | Touchpad button | **The game menu** (save, options, quit) |

Settings > Padmapping lists every action with its button and changes any of
them.

**Keyboard and mouse** are the PC game's: left click to move and attack, right
click to cast, `I` inventory, `C` character, `Tab` the map, `Esc` the menu,
`1` to `8` the belt. The game switches its prompts between the two by whichever
you touched last: move the mouse and it says "Right click to use", press a
button on the pad and it shows the pad's symbol.

## Install

1. Unpack a [release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/releases)'s zip,
   or build it (below), which fills `dist/PPSA99308/`.
2. Copy the `PPSA99308` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/` on the console
   (`ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy` does it over FTP from a build).
3. Put your `DIABDAT.MPQ` beside `eboot.bin`, in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/`.
   `hellfire.mpq`, `hfmonk.mpq`, `hfmusic.mpq` and `hfvoice.mpq` go there too
   if you have Hellfire.
4. Launch "DevilutionX" from the home screen.

Settings and saves are kept in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/userdata/`.

If the tile does not appear, look in `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`:
ShadowMountPlus registers a folder when it first sees it, tries twice, and
loses its hook into the system when the console wakes from rest mode ("AppInstallAll
hook is no longer installed"). Restarting ShadowMountPlus registers the title.
Deploy the whole folder at once, icon included, so that the first try has
everything.

## Build

On macOS, through the Linux VM the other ports use (`ps5`, in Lima, with
PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa and PS5_PayloadSDK under `~/ps5`):

```bash
git submodule update --init
ps5/tools/vm.sh build      # dist/PPSA99308/
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy     # to the console, over FTP
ps5/tools/vm.sh run        # launch, and follow the console's log until the game quits
```

`gettext` must be installed in the VM (for the translations).

## How it works

- **`vendor/devilutionx`** is upstream at a pinned revision. What the console
  needs changed is `ps5/patches/devilutionx.patch`, applied before each build:
  where settings and saves go, no hardware pointer, and the screenshot hook
  for PS5 DevLoop. After editing the submodule, run
  `git -C vendor/devilutionx diff > ps5/patches/devilutionx.patch`. Upstream's
  files end their lines with CR LF: `ps5/tools/edit-source.py` replaces text
  without rewriting the rest.
- **`ps5/cmake/ps5-game.cmake`** is included by DevilutionX's own CMake build
  right after `project()`. It chooses SDL3, hands the build this port's
  patched SDL tree, sets the console's options (960x540, PlayStation
  prompts, no networking) and replaces the link with PS5_Vulkan's.
- **`ps5/sdl/`** holds SDL3's drivers for the console. The video driver gives
  SDL one display, whose size it asks of `VK_KHR_display`, and a window
  that is the whole screen; SDL's Vulkan renderer draws through RADV. The same
  driver reads the keyboard and the mouse once per event pump and turns them
  into SDL's events.
- **`ps5/src/platform.c`** is the console itself: the log, the pad,
  libSceMouse and libSceKeyboard, the sound output.
- **960x540** is the default because it is a whole number of the screen's
  pixels on both a 4K and a 1080p output, in the screen's shape. The game's
  original 640x480 view is "480p" in Settings.

Things the build had to be told, each with its comment in
`ps5-game.cmake` or `link-title.sh`: Lua looks for a separate maths library
and POSIX's `_setjmp`; SDL3_image builds without PNG support, silently, unless
it is shown the libpng DevilutionX fetched (no screenshots otherwise); zlib is
already inside the RADV archive.

## Test hooks

- `/app0/devloop-shot`: when PS5 DevLoop creates this file the game writes its
  next frame to `userdata/screenshots/` (`ps5loop.py grab --title devilutionx`).
  The picture is the game's own 8-bit frame, with a palette whose alpha is 0:
  drop the transparency before looking at it.
- `/app0/env.txt`: `NAME=value` lines for the environment, read before the
  game starts. `SDL_PS5_DISPLAY=1920x1080` overrides the output size.

## Artwork

The icon and the background were made for this port by Gary Riches with an
image generator: `ps5/art/`, and `ps5/art/make-title-art.sh` turns them into
`ps5/sce_sys/`. Nothing in them is Blizzard's.

latestRelease.name: DevilutionX for PlayStation 5 v0.1.0
latestRelease.body:
The first release: DevilutionX, the source port of Diablo and Hellfire, as a title on the PS5's home screen, played with a controller or a keyboard and mouse. Built from DevilutionX revision `b0a3b7ba`.

## What it does

- **An installed title**, with its own tile and background, not a payload: start "DevilutionX" from the home screen.
- **Controller, keyboard and mouse.** The game changes its prompts to whichever you touched last, and shows the DualSense's own symbols for the pad.
- **Widescreen, sharp.** 960x540 by default, a whole number of the screen's pixels on a 4K or a 1080p television. Settings also offers 1080p, 720p and the original 480p.
- Saves and settings are kept in the title's own folder.

## Install

1. Unpack `DevilutionX-PS5-v0.1.0.zip`. It holds one folder, `PPSA99308`.
2. Copy that folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/`.
3. Copy `DIABDAT.MPQ` from your own copy of Diablo into the same folder, beside `eboot.bin`. For Hellfire, add `hellfire.mpq`, `hfmonk.mpq`, `hfmusic.mpq` and `hfvoice.mpq`.
4. Start "DevilutionX" from the home screen.

No game data is in this download. You need a PS5 that already runs homebrew, with ShadowMountPlus showing the folders in `/data/homebrew`. The [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX#install) has the details, and the [controls](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX#controls).

## Limits

- **The game menu is Options and the touchpad button together.** Options held alone shows a second set of actions.
- **No multiplayer.** Networking is not built.
- **A new hero gets the random name the game offers** unless a keyboard is plugged in: the console's on-screen keyboard is not opened.
- **A keyboard types in US layout.**
- If the tile does not appear after copying, restart ShadowMountPlus: it does not register new titles after the console has woken from rest mode.

## Not verified

Tried on one console (firmware 13.60, a 4K output): menus, a new hero, play in the town, the inventory, the button prompts, saving and loading, resolution changes and quitting were seen through a test rig; sound, the keyboard and the mouse were tried by hand. Hellfire, the shareware data, a 1080p television, long sessions and anything past the town have not been.

## Source and licences

Free of charge, for non-commercial use. This is a modified build of DevilutionX, which is under the Sustainable Use License 1.0; the console's start-up code and platform layer are under GPL-3.0. Those two licences set conditions that do not fit together on one program, and [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSING.md) says where that stands. `SOURCE.txt` in the zip names the revision of every part it was built from; this port's is `f84598f`.

Unofficial: not part of, or supported by, the DevilutionX project. Please do not take PS5 problems to them.

repos.description: An unofficial Moonlight port (game streaming) for PS5
repos.readme:
ProsperoLight

Moonlight game streaming, natively on PlayStation 5.
Stream games and your desktop from a Sunshine-compatible PC to a homebrew-enabled PS5.


Features and fixes in the `main` branch may not be available in the [latest published release](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight/releases). Check the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the release notes before updating. ## Features - **Native PS5 video:** hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC (including HDR10) through VideoDec2 and AGC, with 1080p, 1440p and 4K stream options. - **High-refresh streaming:** 30, 60, 90 and 120 FPS presets, plus Custom 30–120 FPS. Actual performance depends on codec, bitrate and hardware. - **Frame pacing and VRR:** Unpaced, fixed-refresh Paced and adaptive Paced+VRR modes. Current source builds include Low Latency, Balanced and Smooth VRR timing profiles and low-FPS frame repetition. - **PyroWave:** an optional Vulkan GPU decoder with SDR/HDR and 4:2:0/4:4:4 profiles, requiring a compatible Vibepollo/Vibeshine host. - **Controllers and input:** up to four DualSense controllers, supported haptics/adaptive triggers, USB keyboard and mouse, plus on-screen keyboard and controller-driven mouse mode. - **Audio:** selectable stereo or 5.1-channel Opus playback. - **A console-first launcher:** automatic LAN discovery, multiple saved PCs, application artwork, persistent settings, and a UI available in 31 languages. - **Updates and diagnostics:** in-app update support for compatible folder installations, performance overlay, and optional timing/log capture. ## Get started 1. **Prepare your PS5.** You need a console with a compatible homebrew environment and title loader already configured. ProsperoLight does not install or provide an exploit. 2. **Install ProsperoLight.** Get `PPSA99002.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight/releases), extract it, and copy the complete `PPSA99002/` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. Close the app before replacing an older installation; refresh your homebrew loader's title registration. 3. **Start Sunshine** (or a compatible host) on your PC. A wired local network is strongly recommended. 4. **Pair and play.** Open ProsperoLight, select a discovered PC or add its address, and enter the pairing PIN in your host's web interface. Open **Games** and choose an app or Desktop. Press **Touchpad + L1** to end the stream and return to the launcher. Pairings and settings normally remain in `/data/prosperolight` when updating the app. **[Full user guide →](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)** — installation, pairing, updates, controllers, settings and saved data. ## Controls | During streaming | Action | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | | **Touchpad + L1** | Return to ProsperoLight | | **Touchpad + R1** | Toggle performance overlay | | **Touchpad + Square** | Toggle controller/mouse mode | | **Touchpad + Triangle** | Open/close the on-screen keyboard | Touchpad means pressing the touchpad **until it clicks**. See the [complete controls reference](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#controls), including the host Back/Guide shortcuts and multi-controller behavior. ## Video quality and compatibility ### Bitrate limits **H.264/HEVC decoding and PyroWave have different performance characteristics.** In measured native 4K HEVC sessions, bitrates above roughly 80 Mbps at 120 FPS can exceed the PS5 decoder's real-time budget. Increasing bitrate is not always an improvement. PyroWave has different host and network requirements. ### VRR and frame timing VRR support depends on the console, firmware, TV and actual output mode; a successful VideoOut API call does **not** prove physical HDMI VRR or a particular latency improvement. For a starting point, try a wired network, native HEVC, and conservative bitrate before experimenting with higher refresh rates. **[Performance and video guide →](docs/PERFORMANCE_GUIDE.md)** — codec selection, measured bitrate limits, pacing modes and VRR caveats. ## Documentation | For | Start here | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Players** | [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Performance guide](docs/PERFORMANCE_GUIDE.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | | **Advanced users** | [PyroWave](docs/PYROWAVE.md) · [DualSense](docs/DUALSENSE.md) · [Frame pacing tests](docs/PACING_TEST_MATRIX.md) · [Home-screen forwarders](docs/FORWARDER.md) | | **Developers** | [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Testing](docs/TESTING.md) · [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) | | **Maintainers** | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) · [Validation](docs/VALIDATION.md) · [Release packaging](docs/RELEASE_ZIP.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | **Project** | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Roadmap / ideas](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) | ## Build from source See [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) for Linux/WSL prerequisites and reproducible dependencies. Once set up: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive make doctor make check ``` The build produces a complete `dist/PPSA99002/` app directory. For the safe FTP deployment workflow, see [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). ## Support and contributions Found a bug? [Open an issue](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight/issues) with your PS5 firmware, host version, codec/settings and reproduction steps. For stream problems, enable **Diagnostic logs** and attach relevant logs after reviewing [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). Logs can contain local host addresses and app names; review them before sharing. Contributions and testing across different TVs, firmwares and network setups are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). > [!IMPORTANT] > This is an independent homebrew project, not an official Sony, Moonlight or Sunshine product. It requires a compatible homebrew-enabled console and includes no exploits, proprietary Sony SDK, firmware, keys or game assets. Use at your own risk and only with hardware and content you are entitled to use. ## Credits Built with the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom (ps5-payload-dev). Third-party components, authors and licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## License Copyright © 2026 BlackBearReloaded. Licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party components keep their own licenses. Binary releases are built from the tagged source in this repository. ## Disclaimer - **No affiliation.** This is an independent homebrew project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation", "PS5" and related marks are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Moonlight or Sunshine projects. - **No proprietary material.** No Sony SDK, firmware, encryption keys or decrypted system modules are included. - **No warranty.** This project is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, to the extent permitted by law. See sections 15 and 16 of the GPL. - **Use at your own risk.** Running homebrew requires a modified console, which may void its warranty, breach the platform's terms of service, or cause data loss. - **Legal use only.** Use it only with hardware, accounts and content you own. This project does not support or enable piracy. ## AI assistance This project was developed with AI assistance from OpenAI and/or Anthropic tools.

latestRelease.name: ProsperoLight 01.000.110
latestRelease.body:
### Stable: Punktfunk hosts, more box art, no wait before the stream

### New

- **Punktfunk hosts:** the decoder now reserves six pictures by default, so Punktfunk's GameStream stream (five reference frames) decodes on a release build. Before, it showed no picture. Streams from other hosts are unaffected.
- **JPEG and WebP box art:** covers that hosts such as Punktfunk pass through as JPEG or WebP now appear, as PNG covers always did.
- **PyroWave from punktfunk:** punktfunk's PyroWave revision is accepted; its shaders and bitstream code are the same as the supported one.

### Changed

- **No wait before the stream:** the check for a newer version runs on its own. When homebrew.page could not be reached, starting a stream, a home-screen forwarder included, waited about a minute for that check to give up.
- **Box art:** covers over 1 MiB load, and covers already fetched are kept in memory, so scrolling back through a large library does not download them again.
- Built on ps5-opengl SDK 1.0.2.

### Installation / update

Title ID remains `PPSA99002`; saved PCs, settings and pairing are kept. Close the app before updating. Extract `PPSA99002.zip` and copy the complete `PPSA99002/` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. Keep only one installation for this title. `SHA256SUMS` verifies the download.

repos.readme:
# etaHEN - AIO Homebrew enabler

![etaHEN](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN/blob/main/etaHEN-Icon.jpg)

## 🚀 **Support the Project**

If you find this project useful and would like to support its continued development, consider buying me a coffee!
[![GitHub Sponsers](https://www.ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://github.com/sponsors/LightningMods)

## Building from Source

The Source code is provided in the Source code folder under GPLv3 with all the necessary files to build it as required under GPLv3 
However I will not be providing instructions on how to build it since any dev should know how to use cmake 

## Official PS5 exploit website 
- https://tinyurl.com/PS5IPV6 (requires you to manually send the payload but has the best stability)
- https://ps5jb.pages.dev/ (auto loads the payload for you, id recommend the IPV6 exploit over UMTX)

## Recommended self-host exploits
- [Modified IPV6 exploit for etaHEN support](https://github.com/LightningMods/PS5-IPV6-Kernel-Exploit)

## Payload PowerShell Script usage for Windows (send_payload.ps1)

if you haven't already, you will need to either enable script execution globally via 

```
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass
```
in an admin PowerShell window or run the script with this command after replacing the script path

```
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Path\To\send_payload.ps1
```
**Script Usage**

```
.\send_payload.ps1 -Payload "C:\path\to\example.elf" -IP "192.168.xxx.xxx" -Port XXXX
```

**OR**

```
.\send_payload.ps1

cmdlet send_payload.ps1 at command pipeline position 1
Supply values for the following parameters:
(Type !? for Help.)
Payload: C:\path\to\example.elf
IP: 192.168.xxx.xxx
Port: XXXX
```
- Common Ports: SB elfldr 9021, exploit elfldr 9020

## Features
 - ★ etaHEN toolbox (debug settings replacement)
 - Custom etaHEN [Plugins](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN-SDK/tree/main/Plugin_samples)
 - [Toolbox] Install the Homebrew Store on the console
 - [Toolbox] ★Rest Mode Options
 - [Toolbox] Remote Play Menu
 - [Toolbox] Plugin / Payload ELF Menu with auto start options
 - [Toolbox] External HDD Menu
 - [Toolbox] TestKit Menu  
 - [Toolbox] Kstuff menu
 - [Toolbox] Game Overlay Menu
 - [Toolbox] Cheats Menu (WIP)
 - [Toolbox] Controller Shortcuts
 - [Toolbox] PS5 webMAN Games menu
 - [Toolbox] Custom Game Options Menu
 - [Toolbox] Display Title IDs on Home menu
 - [Toolbox] Disable toolbox auto start
 - [Toolbox] Blu-Ray license activation 
 - [Toolbox] Disc auto eject for BD-J and LUA based exploits
 - [Toolbox] etaHEN credits and supporters
 - [Toolbox] Custom debug settings text and icon
 - [Toolbox] Auto open menu after etaHEN loads
 - [Toolbox] a number of different toolbox settings
 - React bundle (all FWs) & Self (only on 2.xx) FTP decryption Support
 - 2 seperate daemons for improved stability and reliability
 - The Util daemon will be auto restarted by the main etaHEN daemon
 - Custom System Software version (custom System info)
 - kstuff for fself and fpkg support 
 - etaHEN log in /data/etaHEN
 - (optional) System-wide controller shortcut to open itemzflow
 - Debug Settings
 - Game Dumper (Intrgrated with Itemzflow)
 - HEN config file for settings
 - Jailbreak IPC call (jailbreaks Homebrew apps)
 - Update blocker (unmounts update partition)
 - *Optional* Illusions cheats/patches [Plugin](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN-SDK/tree/main/Plugin_samples/Illusion_cheats)
 - *Optional* FTP server on port 1337
 - *Optional* /data allowed inside apps sandboxes
 - Klog server on port 9081
 - elf loader on port 9021 (use Johns elfldr)
 - *Optional* PS5Debug
 - Itemzflow intergration
 - *Optional* Discord RPC server on port 8000, click [here](https://github.com/jeroendev-one/ps5-rpc-client) for setup instructions 
 - *Optional* Direct PKG installer V2 service with WebUI on http://PS5_IP:12800
 - *Optional* Direct PKG installer service on port 9090

## etaHEN SDK
make your own custom plugins via the [etaHEN SDK](https://github.com/lightningmods/etaHEN-SDK)
More info [Here](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN-SDK/blob/main/README.md)

## Upcoming features
 - [Toolbox] FPS Counter
 - More userland patches
 - Improved PS5 Game support (itemzflow)
 - More (consider donating)

## etaHEN INI Configuration file 
etaHEN's ini settings file can be found at `/data/etaHEN/config.ini` and can be accessed using the built-in FTP
and is automatically created when you run etaHEN for the first time

| INI Key             | Description                                                 | Default value |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| `PS5Debug`          | 0 = disables PS5Debug (Sistr0) auto load, 1 = enable PS5Debug auto load | 0 (disabled) |
| `FTP`               | 0 = disables etaHEN built-in FTP, 1 = enables it          | 1 (enabled) |
| `discord_rpc`       | 0 = disables Discord RPC server, 1 = enables it           | 0 (disabled) |
| `toolbox_auto_start` | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled                                 | 1 (enabled) |
| `Allow_data_in_sandbox` | 0 = disables /data in an apps sandbox, 1 = enables it | 1 (enabled) |
| `DPI`               | 0 = disables The Direct PKG Installer service, 1 = enables it | 0 (disabled) |
| `DPI_v2`            | 0 = disables DPI version 2, 1 = enables it                | 0 (disabled) |
| `Klog`              | 0 = disables kernel logging, 1 = enables it               | 0 (disabled) |
| `ALLOW_FTP_DEV_ACCESS` | 0 = disables FTP developer access, 1 = enables it      | 0 (disabled) |
| `StartOption`       | 0=None, 1=Home menu, 2=Settings, 3=Toolbox, 4=itemzflow  | 0 (None) |
| `Rest_Mode_Delay_Seconds` | Delay in seconds before patching shellui coming out rest mode | 0 (no delay) |
| `Util_rest_kill`    | 0 = don't kill the util daemon during rest, 1 = Do kill it on rest | 0 (disabled) |
| `Game_rest_kill`    | 0 = don't kill the open game during rest, 1 = Do kill it on rest | 0 (disabled) |
| `disable_toolbox_auto_start_for_rest_mode` | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled | 0 (disabled) |
| `libhijacker_cheats` | 0 = disables libhijacker cheats, 1 = enables it          | 0 (disabled) |
| `launch_itemzflow`  | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables auto launch of itemzflow        | 0 (disabled) |
| `testkit`           | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables testkit mode                    | 0 (disabled) |
| `Display_tids`      | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables display of title IDs            | 0 (disabled) |
| `APP_JB_Debug_Msg`  | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables app jailbreak debug messages    | 0 (disabled) |
| `etaHEN_Game_Options` | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables etaHEN game options           | 1 (enabled) |
| `auto_eject_disc`   | 0 = disabled, 1 = enables automatic disc ejection         | 0 (disabled) |
| `Cheats_shortcut_opt` | Multi-select option for cheats shortcut                 | 0 (CHEATS_SC_OFF) |
| `Toolbox_shortcut_opt` | Multi-select option for toolbox shortcut               | 0 (TOOLBOX_SC_OFF) |
| `Games_shortcut_opt` | Multi-select option for games shortcut                   | 0 (GAMES_SC_OFF) |
| `Kstuff_shortcut_opt` | Multi-select option for kstuff shortcut                | 0 (KSTUFF_SC_OFF) |
| `auto_eject_disc`  | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled        | 0 (disabled) |
| `overlay_ram`           | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled                    | 0 (disabled) |
| `overlay_cpu`      | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled            | 0 (disabled) |
| `overlay_gpu`  | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled    | 0 (disabled) |
| `overlay_ip` | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled           | 1 (enabled) |
| `overlay_kstuff` | 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled           | 1 (enabled) |
| `Overlay_pos` | Multi-select option for game overlay                | 0 (OVERLAY_POS_TOP_LEFT) |

## DPI API details for tool creators 
etaHEN's Direct PKG Installer currently is very simple and is considered a WIP
the service flow is as follows

1. Connect to etaHEN's TCP server via port 9090 (using the PS5s IP)
2. Send a URL to etaHEN in the following json format
```
{ "url" : "http://xxxx" }
```
3. etaHEN will then send back the return value (0 on success)
```
{ "res" : "0" }
```
4. etaHEN will close the client socket after the return json is sent


## Jailbreaking an app (FPKG) using etaHEN (non-whitelist method, Network and Legacy CMD server toolbox setting required)

```
enum Commands : int {
  INVALID_CMD = -1,
  ACTIVE_CMD = 0,
  LAUNCH_CMD,
  PROCLIST_CMD,
  KILL_CMD,
  KILL_APP_CMD,
  JAILBREAK_CMD
};

struct HijackerCommand
{
  int magic = 0xDEADBEEF;
  Commands cmd = INVALID_CMD;
  int PID = -1;
  int ret = -1337;
  char msg1[0x500];
  char msg2[0x500];
};

int HJOpenConnectionforBC() {

  SceNetSockaddrIn address;
  address.sin_len = sizeof(address);
  address.sin_family = AF_INET;
  address.sin_port = sceNetHtons(9028); //command serve port
  memset(address.sin_zero, 0, sizeof(address.sin_zero));
  sceNetInetPton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &address.sin_addr.s_addr);

  int socket = sceNetSocket("IPC_CMD_SERVER", AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
  if (sceNetConnect(socket, (SceNetSockaddr*)&address, sizeof(address)) < 0) {
    close(socket), socket = -1;
  }

  return socket;
}

bool HJJailbreakforBC(int& sock) {

  // send jailbreak IPC command
  HijackerCommand cmd;
  cmd.PID = getpid();
  cmd.cmd = JAILBREAK_CMD;

  if (send(sock, (void*)&cmd, sizeof(cmd), MSG_NOSIGNAL) == -1) {
      puts("failed to send command");
      return false;
  }
  else {
    // get ret val from daemon
    recv(sock, reinterpret_cast<void*>(&cmd), sizeof(cmd), MSG_NOSIGNAL);
    close(sock), sock = -1;
    if (cmd.ret != 0 && cmd.ret != -1337) {
      puts("Jailbreak has failed");
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  return false;
}

int main()
{

     int ret = HJOpenConnectionforBC();
     if (ret < 0) {
         puts("Failed to connect to daemon");
         return -1;
     }
     if (!HJJailbreakforBC(ret))
     {
          puts("Jailbreak failed");
          return -1;
     }

     return 0;
}
```
