repos.name: any-pad
repos.description: bluetooth any pad in PS5
repos.readme: # AnyPad PS5: Free your PS5 from the DualSense **A Bluetooth controller bridge for jailbroken PS5 consoles.** **Un puente de mandos Bluetooth para PS5 con jailbreak.** **[English](#english) · [Español](#español)** · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Italiano](README.it.md) · [Português](README.pt.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-Hant.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) --- # English AnyPad PS5 lets you use controllers from other platforms on your PS5. It connects them through the console's own Bluetooth chip and presents them to the system as virtual DualSense controllers. No USB dongle required. **Version 0.9.5-beta.** Tested on a PS5 fat, firmware 10.01, with a DualShock 4 and an 8BitDo SF30 Pro (Switch mode), in the console menus, in games and in emulators. **Available in twelve languages:** English, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, German, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic. The AnyPad page follows the console language. --- ## About this project AnyPad PS5 started on 3 October 2026 at about 14:20 (Spanish time), the day I published its first version. The idea came from MissionControl, which lets the Nintendo Switch use controllers from other consoles. AnyPad may not have been the first project to use other controllers on the PS5: there were already projects that connected them by USB. But none connected them by Bluetooth, and AnyPad was the first to do it. I had an idea and I carried it out. The goal now is to make AnyPad work with more controllers. If you try it, please send me your log (see "Help us confirm compatibility" below): every log helps. The full source code is published in this repository under GPL-3.0-or-later (see "Open source, and working with an AI" below). If you develop an emulator and would like to integrate AnyPad, you are welcome to do so under that license. Write to me at [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com) if you need help. One known issue remains: if the DualSense is switched off while AnyPad is running, it can stay blinking blue. I hope future projects do not have it. Projects forked from AnyPad, from the code I published, will very probably inherit this issue. It is part of AnyPad's legacy, and a sign that, at least in their Bluetooth part, they are forks of AnyPad. --- ## Open source, and working with an AI From version 0.9.5 the whole source code of AnyPad PS5 is published in this repository, under GPL-3.0-or-later: the Bluetooth host, the controller profiles, the AnyPad page, the tests and the build scripts. It includes a simulator, so a controller can be checked on a computer without a console. What I believe AnyPad really adds, more than the bridge itself, is **its communication system for integrating new controllers with the help of an AI**. While AnyPad is running, its page offers on your local network: - the log, in real time; - a few settings of the Bluetooth connection that can be changed while it runs, without restarting or rebuilding; - the pairing button. An AI assistant that has a terminal on a computer in the same network (for example Claude Code, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI) can follow what AnyPad does while you switch a controller on, propose a change, rebuild the ELF, upload it to the console and check the result in the next run. This is how AnyPad itself has been improved. The file **[AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md)** is a guide written for that assistant: how to connect, what it may and may not touch, how to test a change and how to add support for a new controller. You can give it to the assistant as the first instruction. Please keep in mind: - A chat in a web browser cannot reach your console. The assistant needs a terminal on a computer connected to the same local network as the PS5. AnyPad itself never connects to the internet. - The page has no PIN, as in every version: anyone on your local network can read the log and send commands to AnyPad. Use it only on a network you trust, and stop AnyPad when you finish. - The log contains the Bluetooth addresses of your controllers and the id of your console user. Review it before sharing it. ### Share what you (or your AI) learn If you adapt AnyPad to a controller, with or without an AI, please open an [issue](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/issues) with the controller model, the console firmware, the jailbreak, the AnyPad version, what you changed and why, and the log. If an AI helped you, say so and let it write the explanation: what the controller does differently, what was changed and how it was tested. I will review each proposal and integrate the compatible ones in later versions. A change must keep passing `make test` and must not alter how the DualShock 4 and the 8BitDo connect. ### Build from source You need the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk). ``` make test # host tests, with the Bluetooth simulator make ps5 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # the ELF in dist/ tools/build-elf-docker.sh /path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # or the same, inside a container ``` ### Please mention me If you make your own version of AnyPad, or you include it (or a part of it) in an emulator, a HEN, a payload or any other program, I would be very grateful if you mentioned **elmonomalvad0** and linked this project. The license, GPL-3.0-or-later, already requires you to keep the copyright notices and to distribute your changes under the same license. The mention is a request, not a condition, and it is what makes it worthwhile to keep sharing the work. ### Inside the code | Where | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/host.c` | The Bluetooth Classic host: search, calls, pairing, L2CAP channels, SDP and HID | | `src/le.c` | Bluetooth LE: scanning, pairing with Secure Connections and identity exchange, HID over GATT | | `src/profiles.c` | One profile per family of controllers: ids, how to read its reports, wake-up sequence, rumble and lights | | `src/generic.c`, `maps/` | Any other HID gamepad, read through its own descriptor and an optional mapping file | | `src/hci_usb.c`, `src/usb_desc.c`, `src/evstream.c` | The HCI over USB with the console's Bluetooth chip, which is shared with the system | | `src/ps5_vpad.c` | Creates the virtual DualSense and feeds it | | `src/web.c`, `web/index.html` | The page and its API | | `src/ps5_main.c` | The main loop of the payload | | `tests/` | The Bluetooth simulators (`sim.c`, `sim_le.c`) and all the tests | Adding a controller is, in most cases, adding one profile in `src/profiles.c` and a test with the simulator. [AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md) explains the details. --- ## What is new in 0.9.5 - **Open source:** the whole code is published, with a guide for working with an AI assistant. ## What is new in 0.9 - **More compatible:** more controllers supported, and support for the two Bluetooth chips used in PS5 consoles. - **Bug fixes.** - **New graphical interface** for the AnyPad page. ## What is new in 0.8 ### Faster pairing Pairing is now much faster and more reliable. In our tests the DualShock 4 and the 8BitDo are found in a few seconds and are ready a few seconds later, where earlier versions often needed several attempts. ### More stable - **Smooth response:** controllers react fluidly while you play, without lag. - **Controllers switched on normally** (instead of in pairing mode) are now paired at the first attempt. - **Smarter handling** of controllers that are slow to answer or refuse a step. ### Configure PS For controllers without a usable PS button (Switch Pro, 8BitDo and others), the **Configure PS** button lets you choose **one button or a combination of three** that will act as the PS button. Choose how many, press them on the controller and hold them for one second: AnyPad detects them by itself. The setting is saved for that controller model. DualShock 4 and DualSense controllers have their own PS button, so this option does not appear for them. ### Twelve languages The AnyPad page follows the console language: English, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, German, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic (right to left). Any other language falls back to English. --- ## ⚠️ Important: do not switch off the DualSense while AnyPad is running If the DualSense is switched off while AnyPad is running, it can enter the blinking blue mode and stop working until the console is restarted. So that the console does not switch it off by itself after a while without use, set: **Settings → System → Power Saving → Set Time Until Controllers Turn Off → Don't Turn Off** If you do not switch it off, everything works normally. --- ## ⚠️ Important: choose "Quick Play / Guest" for the external controller When you press PS on an external controller, the console asks who will use it. Choose **Quick Play / Guest**. Your main user keeps the DualSense, and you can go back to it at any time by picking up the DualSense. --- # Controller compatibility | Controller | Status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | ✅ **Verified** | Put it in pairing mode (Share + PS) every time you pair it. | | **8BitDo SF30 Pro (Switch mode)** | ✅ **Verified** | It shows up as a Switch Pro Controller. Use Configure PS for the PS button. | | **GameSir G7 SE** | ✅ **Verified** | | | **Nintendo Switch Pro Controller** | 🧪 **Supported, not tested yet** | Same protocol as the 8BitDo in Switch mode. | | **Xbox controllers** | ✅ **Working (reported by users)** | Users report them working since 0.8. If yours does not connect, please send me your log and its model. | | **Any other Bluetooth HID gamepad** | 🧪 **Generic profile** | May work without a specific profile. | **Controllers we believe are compatible** (supported in the code, not tested on a console yet): DualShock 4 v1, Hori Onyx, Razer Raiju Ultimate, Razer Raiju Tournament Edition, SCUF Vantage 2, Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, Nintendo Switch Online (SNES, N64, Mega Drive / Genesis), GameSir G3s, G4s, G7 Pro, T1s and T2a, Betop 2585N2, Bionik Vulkan, LanShen X1Pro, Xiaomi Mi Controller, Amazon Fire / iPega, iPega 9-series, 8BitDo SN30 Pro for Xbox Cloud Gaming, 8BitDo Ultimate 2.4G, SteelSeries, NVIDIA Shield controller (2017), Razer Serval, PowerA MOGA Hero, MOGA Pro and MOGA Pro 2, Atari VCS Modern controller, Hyperkin Scout, Mocute 050. If you try one of them, please send me your log. The full list, controller by controller, is in [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). --- # How it works AnyPad PS5 runs as a resident payload on a jailbroken PS5. It uses the console's own Bluetooth chip, **sharing it with the system**, to discover and pair controllers, read their input and present them to the PS5 as virtual DualSense controllers. It does **not** modify games, the PS5 firmware or the jailbreak. Your PS5 must already be able to run payloads. --- # How to use 1. **Load AnyPad.** Download `AnyPad-PS5-0.9.5-beta.elf` from [Releases](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/releases) and load it with the payload loader you normally use. 2. **Open the page.** Open **AnyPad** in the console's Media row, or open `http://:8095` from a phone or computer on the same network. 3. **Pair.** Press **Pair**, then put the controller in pairing mode, close to the console. | Controller | Pairing mode | | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | Hold **Share + PS** until the light bar flashes twice | | **8BitDo (Switch mode)** | Hold **Pair** for about 3 seconds, until the lights blink fast | | **Nintendo Switch Pro** | Press the small sync button next to the USB-C port | | **Other controllers** | Follow the manufacturer's instructions | 4. **Choose the user.** When the console asks, choose **Quick Play / Guest**. Several controllers can be used at the same time, together with the DualSense. --- # Every run starts clean AnyPad does not keep paired controllers between runs. Pair your controllers each time you start AnyPad. This avoids old pairings that no longer work and keeps the Bluetooth chip in a known state. If a controller that was switched off reconnects by itself and does not respond, switch it off and pair it again from the page. --- # Stopping AnyPad Always stop it with **Stop AnyPad PS5** on its page, also before running it again and before switching off or restarting the console. The **Exit** button only closes the page. --- # Troubleshooting ### No controller is found 1. Press **Pair** first and put the controller in pairing mode afterwards. 2. Make sure the controller really is in pairing mode (for example, the DualShock 4 light bar must flash twice). 3. If the controller was paired with another device before and still does not show up, reset it (DualShock 4: a paper clip in the small hole next to L2 for about 5 seconds; 8BitDo Pro 2: hold Pair for about 5 seconds) and try again. ### Another controller payload is running Another payload that uses the Bluetooth chip and port 8095 gets in the way. Stop it from its own menu before running AnyPad; AnyPad shows a notice when it detects this. ### The page does not open Check that AnyPad is running, that your phone or computer is on the same network as the PS5, and that you use the console's IP address with port `8095`. --- # Help us confirm compatibility If you can confirm that AnyPad PS5 works (or does not work) with a controller, please send the log (`/data/anypad/anypad.log`) to [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com), with the controller model, the console firmware, the jailbreak and the AnyPad version. This helps a lot. ### Support the project Many people ask me to test other controllers and other console versions. Any help is very welcome to **port this project to PS4** and to **PS5 firmware 13.60**, and to support **more controllers**. I would love to have a console on firmware 13.60 as well as my 10.01. It is not mandatory, but anyone who wants to help the project can do so on my Throne page: **[throne.com/elmonomalvad0](https://throne.com/elmonomalvad0)** --- # Credits AnyPad PS5 is original code. These projects were studied to understand how things work, and their ideas were written anew for AnyPad. Thanks to their authors: - **[FGG-PlayPods](https://github.com/FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods)** (FGGstore): the idea behind the Bluetooth part, sharing the PS5's own Bluetooth chip with the system. - **[MissionControl](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl)** (ndeadly): controller profiles by vendor and model, and the report layouts of many controllers. - **Ghostcontrol** (StonedModder): how to create a virtual DualSense on the PS5 and assign it to a user. - **[SplashDown](https://github.com/seregonwar/SplashDown)** (seregonwar) and **[shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)**: the virtual pad sequence and the pad data layout. - **[HearBridge-PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5)** (X-F1REBALL-X): ideas on handling Bluetooth negotiation. - **[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** (John Törnblom): the toolchain everything is built with. License: GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Author: **elmonomalvad0**, the same author as *sinfiltros* (the original AnyPad PS5 on GitHub). X: [@elmonomalvad0](https://x.com/elmonomalvad0) · Contact: exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com --- # Español AnyPad PS5 te permite usar en tu PS5 mandos de otras plataformas. Los conecta a través del propio chip Bluetooth de la consola y los presenta al sistema como DualSense virtuales. No hace falta ningún adaptador USB. **Versión 0.9.5-beta.** Probada en una PS5 fat, firmware 10.01, con un DualShock 4 y un 8BitDo SF30 Pro (modo Switch), en los menús de la consola, en juegos y en emuladores. **Disponible en doce idiomas:** español, inglés, francés, italiano, portugués, alemán, ruso, chino simplificado, chino tradicional, japonés, coreano y árabe. La página de AnyPad sigue el idioma de la consola. --- ## Sobre este proyecto AnyPad PS5 empezó el 3 de octubre de 2026, hacia las 14:20 (hora de España), el día que publiqué su primera versión. La idea partió de MissionControl, que permite usar en la Nintendo Switch mandos de otras consolas. Quizá AnyPad no fue el primer proyecto para usar otros mandos en la PS5: ya había proyectos que los conectaban por USB. Pero ninguno los conectaba por Bluetooth, y AnyPad fue el primero en hacerlo. Tuve una idea y la llevé a cabo. El objetivo ahora es que AnyPad funcione con más mandos. Si lo pruebas, por favor envíame tu log (mira «Ayúdanos a confirmar la compatibilidad» más abajo): cada log ayuda. El código fuente completo está publicado en este repositorio con licencia GPL-3.0-or-later (mira «Código abierto y trabajo con una IA» más abajo). Si desarrollas un emulador y quieres integrar AnyPad, puedes hacerlo bajo esa licencia. Escríbeme a [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com) si necesitas ayuda. Queda un fallo conocido: si se apaga el DualSense con AnyPad en marcha, puede quedarse en azul parpadeante. Espero que los próximos proyectos no lo tengan. Los que sean forks de AnyPad, del código que publiqué, muy probablemente heredarán ese fallo. Es parte del legado de AnyPad, y una muestra de que, al menos en su parte Bluetooth, son un fork de AnyPad. --- ## Código abierto y trabajo con una IA Desde la versión 0.9.5 todo el código fuente de AnyPad PS5 está publicado en este repositorio, con licencia GPL-3.0-or-later: el anfitrión Bluetooth, los perfiles de mandos, la página de AnyPad, las pruebas y los scripts de compilación. Incluye un simulador, así que se puede comprobar un mando en un ordenador sin consola. Lo que creo que aporta de verdad AnyPad, más que el puente en sí, es **su sistema de comunicación para integrar mandos nuevos con la ayuda de una IA**. Mientras AnyPad está en marcha, su página ofrece en tu red local: - el log, en tiempo real; - algunos ajustes de la conexión Bluetooth que se pueden cambiar en caliente, sin reiniciar ni recompilar; - el botón de emparejar. Un asistente de IA que tenga una terminal en un ordenador de la misma red (por ejemplo Claude Code, Codex CLI o Gemini CLI) puede seguir lo que hace AnyPad mientras enciendes un mando, proponer un cambio, recompilar el ELF, subirlo a la consola y comprobar el resultado en la siguiente ejecución. Así se ha mejorado el propio AnyPad. El archivo **[AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md)** es una guía escrita para ese asistente: cómo conectarse, qué puede y qué no puede tocar, cómo probar un cambio y cómo añadir un mando nuevo. Puedes dársela al asistente como primera instrucción. Ten en cuenta: - Un chat en el navegador no llega a tu consola. El asistente necesita una terminal en un ordenador conectado a la misma red local que la PS5. AnyPad nunca se conecta a internet. - La página no tiene PIN, como en todas las versiones: cualquiera en tu red local puede leer el log y mandar órdenes a AnyPad. Úsalo solo en una red de confianza y detén AnyPad cuando termines. - El log contiene las direcciones Bluetooth de tus mandos y el id de tu usuario de la consola. Revísalo antes de compartirlo. ### Comparte lo que aprendéis (tú y tu IA) Si adaptas AnyPad a un mando, con o sin IA, abre por favor una [incidencia](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/issues) con el modelo del mando, el firmware de la consola, el jailbreak, la versión de AnyPad, qué has cambiado y por qué, y el log. Si te ha ayudado una IA, dilo y deja que escriba ella la explicación: qué hace distinto el mando, qué se cambió y cómo se probó. Revisaré cada propuesta e integraré las compatibles en versiones posteriores. Un cambio debe seguir pasando `make test` y no debe alterar cómo conectan el DualShock 4 y el 8BitDo. ### Compilar desde el código Necesitas el [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk). ``` make test # pruebas en el ordenador, con el simulador Bluetooth make ps5 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/ruta/al/ps5-payload-sdk # el ELF en dist/ tools/build-elf-docker.sh /ruta/al/ps5-payload-sdk # o lo mismo, dentro de un contenedor ``` ### Por favor, menciónome Si haces tu propia versión de AnyPad, o la incluyes (o una parte) en un emulador, un HEN, un payload o cualquier otro programa, te lo agradeceré mucho si mencionas a **elmonomalvad0** y enlazas este proyecto. La licencia, GPL-3.0-or-later, ya exige que conserves los avisos de copyright y que distribuyas tus cambios con la misma licencia. La mención es una petición, no una condición, y es lo que hace que merezca la pena seguir compartiendo el trabajo. ### Dentro del código | Dónde | Qué hace | | --- | --- | | `src/host.c` | El anfitrión Bluetooth Classic: búsqueda, llamadas, emparejado, canales L2CAP, SDP y HID | | `src/le.c` | Bluetooth LE: búsqueda, emparejado con Secure Connections e intercambio de identidad, HID sobre GATT | | `src/profiles.c` | Un perfil por familia de mandos: ids, cómo leer sus informes, secuencia de despertar, vibración y luces | | `src/generic.c`, `maps/` | Cualquier otro mando HID, leído con su propio descriptor y un archivo de mapeo opcional | | `src/hci_usb.c`, `src/usb_desc.c`, `src/evstream.c` | El HCI por USB con el chip Bluetooth de la consola, que se comparte con el sistema | | `src/ps5_vpad.c` | Crea el DualSense virtual y lo alimenta | | `src/web.c`, `web/index.html` | La página y su API | | `src/ps5_main.c` | El bucle principal del payload | | `tests/` | Los simuladores Bluetooth (`sim.c`, `sim_le.c`) y todas las pruebas | Añadir un mando es, en la mayoría de los casos, añadir un perfil en `src/profiles.c` y una prueba con el simulador. [AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md) explica los detalles. --- ## Novedades de la 0.9.5 - **Código abierto:** todo el código está publicado, con una guía para trabajar con un asistente de IA. ## Novedades de la 0.9 - **Más compatible:** admite más mandos y es compatible con los dos chips Bluetooth que llevan las PS5. - **Errores corregidos.** - **Nuevo entorno gráfico** en la página de AnyPad. ## Novedades de la 0.8 ### Emparejado más rápido El emparejado es ahora mucho más rápido y fiable. En nuestras pruebas, el DualShock 4 y el 8BitDo aparecen en pocos segundos y quedan listos pocos segundos después, cuando antes a menudo hacían falta varios intentos. ### Más estable - **Respuesta fluida:** los mandos reaccionan con suavidad mientras juegas, sin lag. - **Mandos encendidos de forma normal** (en vez de en modo emparejamiento): ahora se emparejan al primer intento. - **Tratamiento más inteligente** de los mandos que tardan en responder o rechazan un paso. ### Configurar PS Para los mandos sin un botón PS que funcione (Switch Pro, 8BitDo y otros), el botón **Configurar PS** permite elegir **un botón o una combinación de tres** que hará de botón PS. Eliges cuántos, los pulsas en el mando y los mantienes un segundo: AnyPad los detecta solo. El ajuste se guarda para ese modelo de mando. Los DualShock 4 y los DualSense tienen su propio botón PS, así que esta opción no aparece para ellos. ### Doce idiomas La página de AnyPad sigue el idioma de la consola: español, inglés, francés, italiano, portugués, alemán, ruso, chino simplificado, chino tradicional, japonés, coreano y árabe (de derecha a izquierda). Cualquier otro idioma usa el inglés. --- ## ⚠️ Importante: no apagues el DualSense con AnyPad en marcha Si el DualSense se apaga mientras AnyPad está en marcha, puede entrar en el modo azul parpadeante y no funcionar hasta reiniciar la consola. Para que la consola no lo apague sola tras un rato sin usarlo, configura: **Ajustes → Sistema → Ahorro de energía → Establecer tiempo hasta que se apaguen los mandos → No apagar** Si no lo apagas, todo funciona con normalidad. --- ## ⚠️ Importante: elige «Juego rápido / Invitado» para el mando externo Cuando pulsas PS en un mando externo, la consola pregunta quién lo va a usar. Elige **Juego rápido / Invitado**. Tu usuario principal conserva el DualSense, y puedes volver a él en cualquier momento cogiendo el DualSense. --- # Compatibilidad de mandos | Mando | Estado | Notas | | --- | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | ✅ **Verificado** | Ponlo en modo emparejamiento (Share + PS) cada vez que lo emparejes. | | **8BitDo SF30 Pro (modo Switch)** | ✅ **Verificado** | Aparece como Switch Pro Controller. Usa Configurar PS para el botón PS. | | **GameSir G7 SE** | ✅ **Verificado** | | | **Nintendo Switch Pro Controller** | 🧪 **Soportado, sin probar** | Mismo protocolo que el 8BitDo en modo Switch. | | **Mandos Xbox** | ✅ **Funcionan (según usuarios)** | Varios usuarios confirman que funcionan desde la 0.8. Si el tuyo no conecta, envíame tu log y el modelo. | | **Cualquier otro mando HID Bluetooth** | 🧪 **Perfil genérico** | Puede funcionar sin un perfil específico. | **Mandos que creemos compatibles** (soportados en el código, aún sin probar en una consola): DualShock 4 v1, Hori Onyx, Razer Raiju Ultimate, Razer Raiju Tournament Edition, SCUF Vantage 2, Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, Nintendo Switch Online (SNES, N64, Mega Drive / Genesis), GameSir G3s, G4s, G7 Pro, T1s y T2a, Betop 2585N2, Bionik Vulkan, LanShen X1Pro, Xiaomi Mi Controller, Amazon Fire / iPega, iPega 9-series, 8BitDo SN30 Pro para Xbox Cloud Gaming, 8BitDo Ultimate 2.4G, SteelSeries, mando NVIDIA Shield (2017), Razer Serval, PowerA MOGA Hero, MOGA Pro y MOGA Pro 2, mando Atari VCS Modern, Hyperkin Scout, Mocute 050. Si pruebas alguno, envíame tu log. La lista completa, mando por mando, está en [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). --- # Cómo funciona AnyPad PS5 se ejecuta como un payload residente en una PS5 con jailbreak. Usa el propio chip Bluetooth de la consola, **compartiéndolo con el sistema**, para buscar y emparejar mandos, leer sus botones y presentarlos a la PS5 como DualSense virtuales. **No** modifica juegos, el firmware de la PS5 ni el jailbreak. Tu PS5 ya debe poder ejecutar payloads. --- # Cómo usarlo 1. **Carga AnyPad.** Descarga `AnyPad-PS5-0.9.5-beta.elf` desde [Releases](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/releases) y cárgalo con el cargador de payloads que uses normalmente. 2. **Abre la página.** Abre **AnyPad** en *Contenido multimedia* de la consola, o `http://:8095` desde un móvil o un PC de la misma red. 3. **Empareja.** Pulsa **Emparejar** y después pon el mando en modo emparejamiento, cerca de la consola. | Mando | Modo emparejamiento | | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | Mantén **Share + PS** hasta que la barra de luz haga un doble destello | | **8BitDo (modo Switch)** | Mantén **Pair** unos 3 segundos, hasta que las luces parpadeen rápido | | **Nintendo Switch Pro** | Pulsa el pequeño botón de sincronización junto al puerto USB-C | | **Otros mandos** | Sigue las instrucciones del fabricante | 4. **Elige el usuario.** Cuando la consola lo pregunte, elige **Juego rápido / Invitado**. Se pueden usar varios mandos a la vez, junto con el DualSense. --- # Cada ejecución empieza limpia AnyPad no guarda mandos emparejados entre ejecuciones. Empareja tus mandos cada vez que arranques AnyPad. Así se evitan emparejados antiguos que ya no funcionan y el chip Bluetooth queda en un estado conocido. Si un mando que se apagó se reconecta solo y no responde, apágalo y vuelve a emparejarlo desde la página. --- # Apagar AnyPad Páralo siempre con **Apagar AnyPad PS5** en su página, también antes de volver a ejecutarlo y antes de apagar o reiniciar la consola. El botón **Salir** solo cierra la página. --- # Solución de problemas ### No encuentra ningún mando 1. Pulsa **Emparejar** primero y pon el mando en modo emparejamiento después. 2. Comprueba que el mando está de verdad en modo emparejamiento (por ejemplo, la barra de luz del DualShock 4 debe hacer un doble destello). 3. Si el mando estuvo emparejado antes con otro aparato y sigue sin aparecer, haz un reset (DualShock 4: un clip en el agujero junto a L2 unos 5 segundos; 8BitDo Pro 2: mantén Pair unos 5 segundos) e inténtalo de nuevo. ### Hay otro payload de mandos en marcha Otro payload que use el chip Bluetooth y el puerto 8095 interfiere. Páralo desde su propio menú antes de ejecutar AnyPad; AnyPad avisa en pantalla cuando lo detecta. ### La página no se abre Comprueba que AnyPad está en marcha, que tu móvil o PC está en la misma red que la PS5 y que usas la IP de la consola con el puerto `8095`. --- # Ayúdanos a confirmar la compatibilidad Si puedes confirmar que AnyPad PS5 funciona (o no funciona) con un mando, envía el log (`/data/anypad/anypad.log`) a [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com), con el modelo del mando, el firmware de la consola, el jailbreak y la versión de AnyPad. Esto ayuda mucho. ### Apoya el proyecto Mucha gente me pide que pruebe otros mandos y otras versiones de la consola. Agradecemos cualquier ayuda para poder **portar este proyecto a PS4**, a las versiones **13.60 de PS5** y a **diferentes mandos**. Me encantaría tener una consola con el firmware 13.60 además de la mía, con el 10.01. No es obligatorio, pero quien quiera ayudar al proyecto puede hacerlo desde mi página de Throne: **[throne.com/elmonomalvad0](https://throne.com/elmonomalvad0)** --- # Agradecimientos AnyPad PS5 es código propio. Estos proyectos se estudiaron para entender cómo funcionan las cosas, y sus ideas se escribieron de nuevo para AnyPad. Gracias a sus autores: - **[FGG-PlayPods](https://github.com/FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods)** (FGGstore): la idea de la parte Bluetooth, compartir el propio chip Bluetooth de la PS5 con el sistema. - **[MissionControl](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl)** (ndeadly): los perfiles de mandos por fabricante y modelo, y el formato de los informes de muchos mandos. - **Ghostcontrol** (StonedModder): cómo crear un DualSense virtual en la PS5 y asignarlo a un usuario. - **[SplashDown](https://github.com/seregonwar/SplashDown)** (seregonwar) y **[shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)**: la secuencia del mando virtual y el formato de los datos del mando. - **[HearBridge-PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5)** (X-F1REBALL-X): ideas sobre la negociación Bluetooth. - **[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** (John Törnblom): las herramientas con las que se compila todo. Licencia: GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Autor: **elmonomalvad0**, el mismo autor que *sinfiltros* (el AnyPad PS5 original en GitHub). X: [@elmonomalvad0](https://x.com/elmonomalvad0) · Contacto: exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com

**12 October 2026** · More compatible: more controllers supported, and support for the two Bluetooth chips used in PS5 consoles. Bug fixes and a new graphical interface for the AnyPad page. Please do not switch off the DualSense while AnyPad is running. If you try it with another controller, please send me your log.

**12 de octubre de 2026** · Más compatible: admite más mandos y es compatible con los dos chips Bluetooth que llevan las PS5. Errores corregidos y un nuevo entorno gráfico en la página de AnyPad. Por favor, no apagues el DualSense mientras AnyPad está en marcha. Si lo pruebas con otro mando, envíame tu log.

EN: run the ELF, open AnyPad (Media row), press Pair and then put the controller in pairing mode. Choose Quick Play / Guest when the console asks. Exit with the Stop AnyPad PS5 button.

ES: ejecuta el ELF, abre AnyPad (Contenido multimedia), pulsa Emparejar y después pon el mando en modo emparejamiento. Elige Juego rápido / Invitado cuando la consola lo pregunte. Sal con el botón Apagar AnyPad PS5.

repos.description: A clean and intuitive package manager for PS5
repos.readme:
PKG Manager

A clean and intuitive package manager for PlayStation 5. Browse and install your packages directly from USB drives or over your local network (Samba/SMB), with support for multi-part packages.

| | | |:---:|:---:| | **Select Storage Media**
![Select Storage Media](assets/screenshots/select-storage.webp) | **Package Browser**
![Package Browser](assets/screenshots/all-sources.webp) | | **Package Details & Add-ons**
![Package Details](assets/screenshots/package-details.webp) | **Installation Progress**
![Installation Progress](assets/screenshots/install-screen.webp) | | **Multi-Part Disc Swapping**
![Multi-Part Disc Swapping](assets/screenshots/insert-disc.webp) | **Samba (SMB) Settings**
![Samba Network Shares](assets/screenshots/settings-samba.webp) | ## Features - **Clean Web Interface**: Displays your packages with package titles, icons, and version information. - **USB & Network (Samba/SMB) Support**: Automatically detects packages on connected USB drives, or stream them over your local network from a PC or NAS via Samba shares. - **Direct Install**: Install a local PKG file from another device on your network, such as a PC, directly to the console. - **Multi-Part Packages & Disc Swapping**: Install large packages split across multiple optical discs or USB drives, with on-screen prompts when swapping discs. Ideal for physical backups! - **No Duplicate Storage Needed**: Installs packages directly on the fly without requiring double the storage space for temporary copy files. - **Installed Version Detection**: Checks your console to display installed application versions and prevent duplicate package installs. - **Home Screen Shortcut**: Installs a dedicated shortcut tile to your PS5 home screen for quick and easy access. - **Leftover Cleanup**: Detects and cleans up orphaned files and directories commonly left behind on console storage after a database rebuild. ## Installation ### Recommended: Payload Manager Download and launch PKG Manager from the default repository in [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager). ### Manual ELF Loading Alternatively, download the ELF from [Releases](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager/releases) and load it with elfldr. ## Usage ### Accessing the Interface Once running, open the interface in either of the following ways: - Launch the **PKG Manager** shortcut tile directly from the PS5 home screen. - Open `http://[PS5_IP]:8844` in any web browser on a phone, tablet, or PC connected to the same local network. ### Package Locations When using a USB drive or optical disc, packages are detected in: - The **root** directory of the drive (nested folders in root are not scanned). - The **/pkg/** directory, where nested subdirectories are also scanned (e.g. `/pkg/homebrew/`). ### Network Shares (Samba / SMB) You can configure SMB network shares in **Settings → Samba** to browse and install packages stored on your PC or NAS. Network shares are not refreshed automatically; use the **Rescan** button to update the package catalog after adding new files. For Windows shares without a username or password, see the [Windows 11 guest-sharing FAQ](#how-do-i-connect-to-a-windows-11-share-without-a-password). ### Direct Install From another device on the same network, open the PKG Manager interface and choose **Direct Install**. Select or drop a local `.pkg` file to install it directly on the console. ### Multi-Part Packages If you want to back up large packages onto optical discs (Blu-ray, DVD) or are limited by storage media size, you can split your package into multi-part files using the included tool: ```bash python3 tools/pkg_split.py /path/to/package.pkg -s 23G ``` Multi-part packages can be burned across multiple discs or loaded directly from a USB drive. When installing from discs, the installer will automatically detect inserted media and prompt you with on-screen notifications whenever a disc swap is needed. ## FAQ ### How do I connect to a Windows 11 share without a password? Guest sharing allows other devices on your local network to read shared packages without entering credentials. Configure the following on the **Windows PC hosting the files**: 1. **Enable file sharing & turn off password protection.** Set the PC's network profile to **Private**. Open **Settings → Network & internet → Advanced network settings → Advanced sharing settings**. Under **Private networks**, enable **Network discovery** and **File and printer sharing**. Under **All networks**, turn off **Password protected sharing**. Ensure File and Printer Sharing is allowed through Windows Firewall for the private network. 2. **Share the folder with read access.** Right-click your package folder, open **Properties → Sharing → Advanced Sharing**, enable **Share this folder**, and name it (e.g. `PS5PKG`). In **Permissions**, grant **Everyone → Read**. In the folder's **Security** tab, verify that **Everyone** (or **Users**) has **Read & execute**, **List folder contents**, and **Read** permissions. Share and filesystem permissions both apply. 3. **Add the share in PKG Manager.** In **Settings → Samba**, enter the PC's IP address as **Server**, leave port **445**, and enter `PS5PKG` as **Share**. Leave **Username** and **Password** blank. Use **Test connection**, then save the share. If **Select share** fails, type the share name directly: Windows may block listing shares while allowing access to a known share.
Troubleshooting / If connection fails (Windows 11 24H2, Pro, or Enterprise) Newer Windows 11 releases (such as 24H2) or Pro/Enterprise editions enforce SMB signing and restrict guest logons by default. If the connection fails or returns access denied errors, check the following: #### 1. Enable the built-in Guest account Open **PowerShell as Administrator** and run: ```powershell $guest = Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-501' } $guest | Enable-LocalUser $guest | Select-Object Name ``` #### 2. Permit Guest to log on over the network On Windows editions with Local Security Policy, open `secpol.msc` and navigate to **Local Policies → User Rights Assignment**: * Remove **Guest** from **Deny access to this computer from the network**. * Ensure **Access this computer from the network** includes **Guest** or a group that permits its access. #### 3. Allow unsigned guest sessions and disable encryption Windows guest sessions cannot use SMB signing or encryption. In administrator PowerShell, run: ```powershell # Disable signing requirement for the SMB server: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $false -Force # Verify and disable SMB encryption if enabled: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EncryptData $false -Force Set-SmbShare -Name 'PS5PKG' -EncryptData $false -Force ``` #### Common Failures | Error | What to check | | --- | --- | | Account disabled / `0xC0000072` | Enable the Guest account in step 1 above. | | Logon type not granted / `0xC000015B` | Check the network logon policies in `secpol.msc` (step 2). | | Signing required | Disable the server signing requirement (step 3), or use a Windows account with credentials. | | Access denied / `0xC0000022` | Check guest logon, signing/encryption requirements, and both Share and Security permission lists. | > **Note**: Windows' **Enable insecure guest logons** (`AllowInsecureGuestAuth`) > policy controls Windows acting as an SMB *client*. It does not enable guest > access to shares *hosted* by that PC. References: Microsoft's [Windows file-sharing guide](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/file-sharing-over-a-network-in-windows), [SMB signing requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/smb-signing), [Guest account activation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.localaccounts/enable-localuser), and [network logon deny policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/security-policy-settings/deny-access-to-this-computer-from-the-network). For diagnostic commands and Windows VM test results, see [SMB diagnostics](docs/SMB_DIAGNOSTICS.md).
## Architecture For in-depth technical details regarding the system architecture, range streaming, and installation pipeline, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Credits The following projects were used as foundations or reference for different parts of this project: - [John Törnblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom) - [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) - [LightningMods](https://github.com/LightningMods) - [etaHEN](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN) - [earthonion](https://github.com/earthonion) - [garlic-savemgr](https://github.com/earthonion/garlic-savemgr) - [sahlberg](https://github.com/sahlberg) - [libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2) - Everyone contributing to the PS5 homebrew scene. ## Donations If you'd like to support my work, please check out [DONATE.md](DONATE.md). ## Development For build instructions, test runner details, and deployment scripts, see [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md).

repos.name: pkg-sender
repos.description: PKG Sender — install PS4/PS5 packages over LAN. Pick games on PC, auto-find the console, queue and install. No USB, no manual IP.
repos.readme: # PS4 PS5 PKG Sender **PKG Sender** installs PlayStation games over LAN from your PC: pick games, they queue up and install on the console. No USB juggling, no manual IP typing. PS5 **PKG** games install fine, no FPKG patching needed on your side. Disc images (`.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg`) copy straight to `/data/homebrew`. ## Download Get `PkgSender-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) — self-contained, no .NET needed, no admin needed. On Linux: the `.deb` from the CI workflow installs to `/usr/lib/pkgsender` with a `pkgsender` menu entry; the portable `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.AppImage` run from anywhere. All are self-contained, no .NET needed: ```sh tar -xzf PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz && ./PkgSender ``` > ⚠ **`pkg-receiver.elf` is PS5 ONLY.** PS4 does NOT need any ELF — it uses > Remote Package Installer or GoldHEN (see [Tutorial — PS4](#tutorial--ps4)). > Sending the ELF to a PS4 will not work. | Console | What runs on the console | Shipped where | | ------- | ------------------------ | ------------- | | PS5 | `pkg-receiver.elf` (send once via WebKit, stays listening on `12800`) | attached to the release + inside the PC install folder | | PS4 | **Remote Package Installer** homebrew (port `12800`) **or** GoldHEN with Payload Server on (ports `9090`/`9021`/`9020`) — install either yourself | not shipped, get it from its own release | On first launch the About window opens (support links live there). --- ## Screenshots ![PKG Sender compact view](docs/screenshot-compact.png) ![Sending ASTRO BOT to PS5](docs/screenshot-sending.png) ![Console browser — Images view](docs/screenshot-console-images.png) --- ## Tutorial — PS5 ### 1. Start the receiver on the console 1. Jailbreak your PS5 and send `pkg-receiver.elf` (it ships inside the PC install folder). 2. Wait for the console toast *listening on port 12800*. 3. On first run the receiver also installs a **pkg remote installer** shortcut on the PS5 home screen (Media category, `PKGS12800`). ### 2. Connect PC and console Put the console on the same network as this PC (Wi-Fi or LAN). The console itself needs no internet. See [LAN connection](#lan-connection) below for the direct-cable option. Open PKG Sender — it finds the console by itself (receiver beacon first, LAN sweep as fallback). If the console got a new DHCP address, it asks: *switch to it?* Press **Test** to verify (status dot goes green). ### 3. Install a PKG game 1. Press **Scan drives…** (or **+ Add folder**, or just drag files/folders onto the window), select games, press **Send PKG**. 2. Updates and DLCs stay glued to their base game (exact Title ID — regions stay separate). Click the 🔗 chip on a card to show only that family. 3. Watch the send queue: per-file progress, pause, reorder, retry. Tick **PS4 console** only for PS4 targets (see below) — PS5 queues natively. ### 4. Install from the console browser (no PC walking) 1. In PKG Sender press **Share to console**. The status bar shows the catalog URL (`http://:9898/catalog`). 2. On the PS5, open the **pkg remote installer** home-screen shortcut (or browse to `http://:12800/`). 3. **Games** tab: base games with covers; click one for details, install updates/DLCs individually or everything at once with **Install all**. 4. **Images** tab: disc images with a **Copy to homebrew** button each. Copy progress (percent + speed) shows above the list with **Pause** / **Cancel copy** — works even for copies started from the PC app. 5. The header shows `page X • receiver Y` — if they differ, resend the newest ELF. ### 5. Copy a disc image (PC side) Select `.exfat` / `.ffpkg` / `.ffpfsc` rows and press **Copy images** — they land in `/data/homebrew`. Each copy gets a queue row with live progress; ⏸ pauses the receiver, ✕ cancels it for real (partial file stays for resume). --- ## Tutorial — PS4 > No ELF, no USB, no FTP. The PS4 only needs a jailbreak plus one installer > service (below). PKG Sender pushes an install task to it; the PS4 then > downloads the PKG from your PC over plain HTTP (port `9898`). ### 1. Prepare the console Jailbreak the PS4 and start **one** of these (the app tries them in this order): 1. **Remote Package Installer (RPI)** — install the RPI `.pkg` on the PS4 and run it (serves its API on port `12800`). Easiest path, use this one. Get it from the author: (Releases page). 2. **GoldHEN with Payload Server enabled** — enable it in GoldHEN settings (ports `9090` / `9021` / `9020`). PKG Sender injects its installer payload itself; you install nothing extra. ### 1b. Install speed (measured, same gigabit LAN) | Path | Typical speed | Why | | ---- | ------------- | --- | | RPI (recommended) | ~75 MB/s | RPI's own downloader, 2 parallel 16 MB streams | | GoldHEN | ~50 MB/s | BGFT pulls the manifest pieces strictly one-by-one in 16 MB chunks — a console-side pipeline cap, not your network | Reference points on the same setup: USB install ~100 MB/s, plain LAN file transfer ~100 MB/s, PKG Sender's own HTTP server benchmarks at 2000+ MB/s loopback. So if install speed matters, do not use the GoldHEN path — use RPI. No PC-side tuning raises the GoldHEN path further. ### 2. Connect and test Same network as the PC (see [LAN connection](#lan-connection)). In PKG Sender type the console IP and press **Test** — it reports which mode it found (`RPI` or `GoldHEN`). ### 3. Install a PKG game 1. Drag & drop the `.pkg` file onto the window — it goes **straight to the send queue** (nothing is added to the library). Or scan/add a folder and select games, then press **Send PKG**. 2. Tick **PS4 console** above the queue — PS4 installs go strictly one-by-one (a PS5 queues natively, a PS4 does not). 3. What happens per mode: - **RPI**: the PC sends the file URL to `http://:12800/api/install`; the PS4 downloads and installs it itself. Watch it appear in RPI on the TV. - **GoldHEN**: payload injection over the binloader ports, then the PS4 pulls the PKG from your PC. If the console reports a BGFT error (`0x80990033`), it couldn't reach `http://:9898` — check the firewall rule and that the PC IP in the app is your real LAN address. 4. The queue row stays live until the download finishes; **Resume** continues a stopped one instead of starting over. No FTP is involved on either console — all transfers are plain HTTP from the PC's file server (port `9898`). --- ## LAN connection ### Method 1 — Through a router The easiest option — connect both your PC and console to the same router. ``` PC ─────┐ ├── Router PS5/PS4 ┘ ``` You don't need to configure IP addresses manually. 1. Connect your PC to the router using Ethernet or Wi-Fi. 2. Connect your PS5/PS4 to the same router. 3. Start the receiver (PS5) / RPI-HEN (PS4) on the console. 4. Open PKG Sender — it discovers the console on your local network automatically. ### Method 2 — Direct Ethernet connection PC straight to PS5/PS4 with an Ethernet cable, no router. ``` PC ───────── Ethernet ───────── PS5/PS4 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.2 ``` Because there is no router providing DHCP, you must manually assign an IP address to both devices. **1. Set the PC IP address.** On Windows: Settings → Network & Internet → Ethernet → IP assignment → Edit. Select Manual, enable IPv4, and enter (on Linux, use the IPv4 → Manual tab of your network settings, e.g. NetworkManager): - IP address: `192.168.10.1` - Subnet mask: `255.255.255.0` - Gateway: leave empty - DNS: leave empty **2. Set the console IP address.** Configure the console's Ethernet connection with: - IP address: `192.168.10.2` - Subnet mask: `255.255.255.0` - Gateway: leave empty - DNS: leave empty The important part is that both devices are on the same subnet (`255.255.255.0`). **3. Start the receiver** on the console, then launch PKG Sender on your PC. In the app pick the PC address from the PC box, type the console IP, press **Test**. > ⚠ Do NOT leave a direct cable on automatic IP assignment. Windows or the console may fall back to a `169.254.x.x` address when no DHCP server is available — PKG Sender ignores these automatic link-local addresses on purpose. If the cable is plugged in but nothing is found, this is almost always the cause. --- ## Features - Zero-config networking: auto PC address, console auto-detect with switch prompt, live status dot, re-scan (↻ Detect) button - Library: cover art, Title ID, version, size; filter PS5/PS4, sort name/size, search with in-bar clear (✕) - Add games three ways: **Scan drives…**, **+ Add folder**, or **drag & drop** files/folders onto the window - Family linking: updates and DLCs stay glued to their base game (exact Title ID — regions stay separate); 🔗 chip shows the family, click to filter, click again to go back - Send queue with per-file progress, pause, reorder, retry, clear-done (orphaned rows included) - Image copies with live progress, receiver-side pause, and real cancel (partial kept for resume) - Console browser page (PS5): logo header, 5-column grid, platform badges, details modal, install-all queue, copy progress with pause/cancel - Self-updating: silent check at startup, footer button lights up on new release (off switch in About for offline PCs) - Guide window with setup + troubleshooting, first-run About --- ## Receiver API (PS5) The receiver listens on `http://:12800`. File paths are jailed under `/data/homebrew`. This API is not stable and may change between versions. | Method | Path | Input | Reply | | ------ | ---- | ----- | ----- | | GET | `/api` | — | probe (online check, no action) | | GET | `/api/status` | — | `{"busy":bool,"active":N,"pull":bool,"pullName","pullGot","pullWant","pullPaused":bool}` | | GET | `/api/pc` | — | `{"pc":"1.2.3.4","age":N}` (last PC announce, `age` -1 = never) | | GET | `/api/version` | — | `{"build":"..."}` (compare with the page header) | | GET | `/api/space` | — | `{"free":N,"total":N}` (`/data` bytes) | | GET | `/logo.png`, `/favicon.ico` | — | sender logo PNG | | POST | `/api/install` | `{"packages":[""],"name":"...","icon_url":"..."}` (`name`/`icon_url` optional) | `{"status":"success"}` or `{"status":"fail",...}` | | GET | `/install?url=` | PKG URL as query arg (+`name`, `+icon`) | starts install, plain-text reply | | GET | `/api/files/stat?path=` | remote path | `{"exists":bool,"size":N}` | | POST | `/api/files/pull` | `{"url":"http://pc:9898/pkg/id","path":"/data/homebrew/f.pkg","mode":"overwrite"/"resume"}` | `{"ok":true,"started":true}` + console toast on finish | | POST | `/api/pull/pause` | `{"paused":1/0}` | `{"ok":true,"paused":bool}` | | POST | `/api/pull/cancel` | `{}` | `{"ok":true,"cancelled":true}` (partial stays for resume) | File-explorer endpoints (`/api/fs/*`, Files tab) are temporarily disabled in the receiver. Discovery: the receiver broadcasts `PKGSENDER v1` to UDP `255.255.255.255:12801` every 3 seconds. ## Console library (pkg remote installer, PS5) Browse and install the scanned PC library from the console's own browser — no need to walk back to the PC: 1. In PKG Sender, scan your folders, then press **Share to console**. The status bar shows the catalog URL (`http://:9898/catalog`). While shared, the PC also broadcasts `PKGSENDER-PC :9898` to UDP `255.255.255.255:12802` every 3 seconds, so the console finds it automatically (no manual IP entry). 2. On first run the receiver installs a **pkg remote installer** shortcut on the PS5 home screen (Media category, `PKGS12800`). Open it — or browse to `http://:12800/` manually. 3. **Games tab**: base games only (alphabetical, with covers, sizes and IDs); click a base game for details and its updates/DLCs, each with its own Install button, or **Install all** for the whole family. Search filters by title or Title ID; chips filter PS5/PS4. 4. The **Images** tab shows disc images (exfat/ffpfsc/ffpkg) with a **Copy to homebrew** button each, plus live progress with Pause/Cancel. Published endpoints on the PC file server (`:9898`, CORS-open): | Method | Path | Reply | | ------ | ---- | ----- | | GET | `/catalog` | `[{"id","title","titleId","version","size","sizeText","role","familyKey","platform","format","file","hasIcon"}]` (`role` = Game/Patch/DLC/Image) | | GET | `/icon/{id}` | cover PNG (`image/png`) | | GET | `/pkg/{id}` | file bytes (range-capable, same as pushes use) | --- ## Credits - [ps5-web-file-manager](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager) (GPL-3.0) — the home-screen web-shortcut launcher idea; reimplemented here, no code copied. - [seregonwar/zftpd](https://github.com/seregonwar/zftpd) (MIT) — pointed at PS5 TCP socket-buffer tuning as the fix for slow bulk transfers; our pull-downloader buffering was rewritten from scratch, no code copied. ## Support If you enjoy what I build and want to support my work, you can donate — every bit means a lot. 💙 [☕ برام یه قهوه بخر — coffeebede.com/loopayeh](https://coffeebede.com/loopayeh) *(🇮🇷 برای ایران — حمایت تومانی)* - USDT (BEP-20) *(🌍 بین‌المللی)*: `0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50` ([send via TrustWallet](https://link.trustwallet.com/send?coin=20000714&address=0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50&token_id=0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955)) - More: [loopayeh.github.io](https://loopayeh.github.io/) ## Troubleshooting - **● No receiver (red)** — the elf isn't running on the console. Send it again. On the console page, `page X • receiver Y` mismatch means the same thing. - **○ No network (gray)** — this PC has no active LAN/Wi-Fi. - **Push goes through but download never starts** — allow inbound TCP port 9898: on Windows in Windows Firewall (the installer adds this rule plus UDP 12801 for beacons); on Linux, e.g. `sudo ufw allow 9898/tcp` or `sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=9898/tcp`. - **Console IP keeps changing (DHCP)** — reopen the app or hit Detect; it offers the new address. - **Image cards without covers** — the header bridge needs `pkgviewer.py` next to the installed app (ships since 1.2.5) plus a Python with `mkpfs`; rescan after installing. ## Build from source Needs .NET 8 SDK (+ Inno Setup 6 for the installer): ```bat Build-Release.bat ``` This publishes a self-contained single-file build to `dist\`, copies in `pkg-receiver.elf` + `pkgviewer.py`, and, if `iscc` is available, produces `PkgSender-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe`. The PS5 receiver rebuilds with the ps5-payload-sdk toolchain: ```sh cd payload && make PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ``` On Linux the tar.gz and AppImage artifacts build with .NET 8 SDK only (`DOTNET=/path/to/dotnet ./Build-Release.sh` if the SDK is not on `PATH`): ```sh ./Build-Release.sh ``` This publishes linux-x64 to `dist/` and produces `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `.AppImage` there (the AppImage step downloads `appimagetool` when it is not installed). The `.deb` is built separately by the `Linux .deb` CI workflow. Automated tests (updater version/asset/network logic and the Linux tar.gz self-update contract) run with: ```sh dotnet test tests/coretests/CoreTests.csproj ``` ## How updates work The app checks GitHub releases for a `PkgSender-Setup-*.exe` asset newer than its own version. **Download + Install** fetches it to a temp dir, launches it silent, and exits so Setup can overwrite the running app. On Linux it looks for the `PkgSender-*-linux-x64.tar.gz` asset instead: a portable (tar.gz) install is swapped in place — the new binary lands next to the old one (kept as `PkgSender.old`, removed on next start) and the app restarts itself. The official `.deb` and AppImage installs skip the in-place swap and ask for the usual package/update path.

Linux desktop is now fully covered: alongside the .deb there are portable tar.gz and AppImage builds (also the answer for Arch, see #11), with in-app self-update for tar.gz installs. This release also brings the repo's first automated test suite (39 xUnit tests, now running in CI) plus updater security hardening. iOS gets narrow-phone UI fixes and a build fix; Android is unchanged (still 1.0.1).

repos.name: Playstation-5-Save-Mounter
repos.readme:
# Playstation 5 Save Mounter 2.0.1
Supports all jailbreakable PS5 FWs.  
Mounts PS1, PS2, PSP, PS4 and PS5 game saves.

Use this elf loader: https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr

## Instructions (mouting existing saves)
1) Load elfldr.
2) Load FTP.
3) Open the tool.
4) Enter the IP address of your PS5 and click 'Connect'.
5) Click 'Setup' and select your username.
6) Click 'Get Games' and select your game in the combobox.
7) Click 'Search'.
8) Select the save you want to mount in the combobox.
9) Click 'Mount'.
10) Your save is now mounted and accessible from FTP in `/mnt/pfs/`.
11) After copying or replacing the files, be sure to click 'Unmount'.

** Warning: Don't replace files in `sce_sys` directory, it is unnecessary and will probably corrupt your save**

---

# Credits:
* cow - based on his save mounting research using `sceFs*` internal PS5 functions
* earthonion - for his loading game titles code and save creation from [garlic-savemgr](https://git.etawen.dev/earthonion/garlic-savemgr)

repos.name: savemnt-offset-dumper
repos.description: payload for the PlayStation 5 that resolves a set of firmware-specific offsets
repos.readme:
# savemnt-offset-dumper

payload for the PlayStation 5 that resolves a set of firmware-specific offsets, scans process memory, dumps a process image, and
writes the results to disk. A toast notification reports success or failure. Written to `/data/savemntOffsets/`:

## What it does

On execution it:

1. **Reads the firmware version** via `kernel_get_fw_version()` and decodes it to
   a `MAJOR.MINOR` string.

2. **Finds the `SceShellCore` process** by walking the process list (`sysctl`
   `KERN_PROC`) and matching the command name.

3. **Resolves library exports to RVAs.** For each target module it looks up the
   module handle and map base in a process, then resolves each symbol and records
   its RVA (`addr - mapbase`). Modules and symbols:
   - `libSceSaveData.sprx` — `sceSaveDataMount`, `sceSaveDataUmount`,
     `sceSaveDataDirNameSearch`, `sceSaveDataTransferringMount`,
     `sceSaveDataInitialize3`
   - `libSceUserService.sprx` — `sceUserServiceGetInitialUser`,
     `sceUserServiceGetLoginUserIdList`, `sceUserServiceGetUserName`
   - `libSceLibcInternal.sprx` — `opendir`, `readdir`, `closedir`, `strcpy`,
     `fopen`, `fread`, `fclose`

   Export RVAs are process-independent, so if a module is not mapped into
   `SceShellCore` the payload loads it into its own process
   (`sceKernelLoadStartModule`) and resolves it there — the RVAs are identical.

4. **Scans `SceShellCore` memory for C-strings.** For each needle it reads the
   image in overlapping chunks (`mdbg_copyout`) and reports every NUL-terminated
   match as an RVA relative to the `SceShellCore` map base.

5. **Dumps the `SceShellCore` image.** Writes a flat 32 MiB blob starting at the
   map base, so that **file offset == RVA**. Unmapped pages are zero-filled to
   preserve alignment.

## Output

Written to `/data/savemntOffsets/`:

- `offset.txt` — firmware version, the resolved module bases and export RVAs, and
  the string-scan matches.
- `shellcore.bin` — the flat `SceShellCore` image dump (file offset == RVA).

## Building

Requires the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and `make`.

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
make
```

Produces `savemntdmp.elf`.

## Running

Send the built ELF to a console running a payload loader:

```sh
make PS5_HOST=<console-ip> PS5_PORT=9021 test
```

or load it manually with elfldr / ps5debug-NG. Results land in
`/data/savemntOffsets/`.

## License

GPL-3.0, matching the ps5-payload-sdk.

repos.readme:
# Garlic SaveMgr for PS5

PS5 save decrypt/encrypt/browse with embedded web UI.

## Usage

1. Send `garlic-savemgr.elf` to elfldr
2. Open `http://<ps5-ip>:8082` in your browser on your PC
3. Drag and drop files into the browse tab to add/replace files

## Building

Requires the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk).

```sh
make PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
```
