latestRelease.body:
## Prospero Explorer v1.0

### What is Prospero Explorer

Prospero Explorer is a file explorer for the PS5 console, built on the SharpProspero SDK. It browses and manages the file system, unpacks and builds archives, plays audio and video, views and edits text, views and converts pictures, installs packages from the writable area and from removable devices, launches an installed title, serves the whole file system over the network, opens a web address, and reports what the machine is doing.

### How to install & launch

- Unzip the file ```ProsperoExplorer-v1.zip``` **into a folder** and **move/copy the folder** to ```/homebrew``` on your USB **OR** ```/data/homebrew``` on the console
- Install using [dump_installer](https://github.com/EchoStretch/dump_installer)
- Launch from home screen

### Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Browsing | Listing with sizes and kinds, sorting, hidden names, find within a folder, multiple selection, copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, new folder, new file, properties, checksums |
| Archives | Browse and unpack zip and tar, unpack a lone gzip or zlib stream, build a zip or tar from a selection |
| Media | Audio and video playback with seeking, looping, volume and tags; WAV and VAG play through the decoders when the player will not take them |
| Text | Viewer with line numbers, wrapping, a hex view and a table view for comma- or tab-separated files; editing by line, find, go to line, save and save as |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA and GIF; fit modes, panning and pinch-zoom by touch, rotate, flip, grayscale, invert, brightness, contrast, blur, a screenshot of the view, and conversion between every form that can be written |
| Packages | Finds installable files in the writable area and on removable devices, installs them, reports whether a title is already present, and launches an installed title by its id |
| Network | A file service over the network reaching the whole file system, with optional login, a read-only mode and a root it cannot climb above |
| Web | Opens a web address in the system browser |
| System | Console, users, network, memory, storage and display readings |
| Settings | Every part of the above, kept between runs |

repos.name: Prospero-Multi-Tools
repos.description: PS5 Homebrew Backup Manager & Toolkit for PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita backups.
repos.readme:
# Prospero Multi Tools

A PS5 Backup Toolkit for PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita. Browse backups, inspect and modify metadata, install PS4/PS5 packages, launch PS1/PS2/PSP titles, and more. ## Contents - [Prospero Multi Tools](#prospero-multi-tools) - [Contents](#contents) - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Download](#download) - [Install the app](#install-the-app) - [Set up the emulators](#set-up-the-emulators) - [First run checklist](#first-run-checklist) - [Where installed backups live](#where-installed-backups-live) - [Uninstalling a backup](#uninstalling-a-backup) - [Backup covers and icons](#backup-covers-and-icons) - [What every screen does](#what-every-screen-does) - [Settings you might want to change](#settings-you-might-want-to-change) - [Known limits](#known-limits) ## What you need - A PS5 running a firmware supported by the [`unjail`](https://github.com/SvenGDK/unjail-ps5app-payload)` payload. - The `unjail` payload sent to the console before you open the app. Without it, the app cannot widen its file view past its own sandbox: installs, emulator launches, and every scan of `/data` or a USB drive will refuse. The `unjail` payload is required for every launch. - An USB drive is enough to get started. The app also reads and writes `/data` and `/user` internally once the escalation daemon is running. ## Download Two files are available on the Releases page: - `ProsperoMultiTools.zip` — the homebrew app itself as a signed folder module ready to install on the console. - `EmulatorPack.zip` — the emulator folders and the shared `emulator-resources/`. ## Install the app 1. Unzip `ProsperoMultiTools.zip`. 2. Copy the resulting folder to an USB drive `/homebrew/PPSA99110` or the console's own storage `/data/homebrew/PPSA99110`. 3. Install the homebrew app with [`dump_installer`](https://github.com/EchoStretch/dump_installer) 4. Send the [`unjail`](https://github.com/SvenGDK/unjail-ps5app-payload) payload to the console once per boot before opening the app. ## Set up the emulators The launch paths for PS1, PS2 and PSP backups drive the emulators shipped in `EmulatorPack.zip`. 1. Unpack `EmulatorPack.zip`. 2. Copy the emulator folders you want (`ps1hd`, `psphd`, and any PS2 emulator folders such as `BULLY`, `JAK`, `MANHUNT`, `Siren`, `RotkV1`, ...) onto the console. The primary location is: `/data/homebrew/emulators//` USB alternatives are also accepted: `/mnt/usbN/homebrew/emulators//` (N = 0..7) 3. Copy the whole `emulator-resources/` folder from the same archive to: `/data/homebrew/emulator-resources/` on the console or to an USB drive `/homebrew/emulator-resources` 4. Open the app and check the `Diagnostics` screen. It lists every emulator folder the current install detected under `/data/homebrew/emulators/` and each USB root. ## First run checklist - Open the app. The bottom of the Home screen tells you how many storage locations answered. If it says zero, the escalation daemon has not been sent yet or no USB drive is plugged in. - Open `Diagnostics`. It reports whether the escalation daemon widened the file view, which storage roots are reachable, whether the file broker is answering, and which emulators the current install carries. ## Where installed backups live `/data/homebrew/games//` ## Uninstalling a backup Uninstalling a backup from the console's own home screen removes the shell registration only. The `/data/homebrew/games//` folder is left in place. Remove it by hand from a file manager if you want the disk space back. An automated cleanup step will be added into the app in a later version. ## Backup covers and icons PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita backups carry their icon art inside their own PKG file, so the app reads it directly. PS1 and PS2 backups do not carry that image. The first time a PS1 or PS2 backup is opened, the app fetches its cover from the network and stores it in an on-device cache. This means: - An active internet connection is required the first time a PS1 or PS2 cover is displayed. - Every subsequent open reads from the on-device cache; the network is not touched again for that title. ## What every screen does - `Backup Managers` — one entry per platform (PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP, PS Vita). Each opens a scan of every reachable storage root; the result is a split view with a cover preview on the left and metadata on the right. Selecting a backup opens the detail screen. - `Backup detail` — title, game id, content id, region, category, version, firmware, size, source file or folder, plus the SFO or `param.json` rows. Action buttons: `Launch from folder`, `Install package`, `Launch title`, `Configure and launch` (for the emulator-based platforms), `Copy backup`, `Move backup`, `Delete backup`, `Edit SFO`, `Edit param.json`. - `Emulator launch` — per-title options plus a live launch driver. PS1, PS2 and PSP each have their own option set (render scale, aspect, filters, multitap, disc count, VMC path, and so on). - `PS1 / PS2 Tools` — merge multi-BIN CUE sets into a single BIN, convert PS2 BIN/CUE images to ISO. - `PS5 Tools` — send an ELF payload over TCP, clear the console's error history, read the inserted disc's `param.json`, and probe the well-known homebrew TCP ports (payload, WebSrv, FTP, klog, kernel exploit, PKG installer, and so on). - `Console Utilities` — per-platform SFO / backup folder / PKG inspection for PS3, PS4, PSP and PS Vita. - `Shared Tools -> Shared Utilities` — browse any folder the file view exposes, and view a file's first bytes as a hex dump. - `System -> Settings` — display, behaviour, audio, payload-sender defaults, and a reset button. - `System -> Diagnostics` — the reachability report described above. - `System -> Refresh storage` — re-probes every root without leaving the app. - `System -> Unlock full storage access` — sends the escalation request again if it did not apply at boot. - `Exit` — close the app. ## Settings you might want to change - `Paths -> Start path` sets the folder the file pickers open at. - `Paths -> Backup search path` overrides the default scan set (`/data` plus every USB) with a semicolon-separated list of folders. - `Display -> Text scale` and `Display -> List rows` adjust the reading density. - `Behavior -> Confirm before delete / move` toggles the confirmation dialog for destructive actions. - `Behavior -> Show hidden files` toggles dotfile visibility in the picker. - `Behavior -> System notifications` toggles the top-screen toast messages the shell posts. - `Behavior -> Notification time` sets how long toasts stay on screen. - `Audio -> Play soundtrack when available` toggles the per-title soundtrack playback in `Backup detail`. - `Audio -> Volume` sets the soundtrack playback volume. - `Payload sender -> Host` and `Port` are the defaults `PS5 Tools -> Payload sender` picks up. - `Reset -> Reset all settings to defaults` restores every option above to its shipped default. ## Known limits - `/data` and `/user` are not offered by the file and folder browser yet. Every launch and install path still reaches them correctly through the file broker. - Uninstalling a backup from the console's home screen leaves `/data/homebrew/games//` behind. Remove the folder by hand for now. - The `unjail` payload must be sent again every time the console reboots. - PS1 and PS2 cover art needs an active internet connection the first time each title is displayed.

repos.readme:
SwitchPS5

SwitchPS5 brings a Nintendo Switch-style interface to [ProsperoEden](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden) on PlayStation 5. It combines a familiar HOME screen, software library, settings screens, and multiplayer menu with the underlying ProsperoEden emulation platform. The project focuses on the user interface, navigation, launcher integration, branding, package identity, and update handling. Emulation capabilities and game compatibility depend on the upstream components included in each build. See the release notes for the upstream version, changes, tested features, and known limitations of a particular release ## Features - **Nintendo Switch-inspired interface** — A redesigned launcher based on the Nintendo Switch HOME menu, featuring familiar navigation, animations, artwork, and sounds. - **HOME screen** — A console-style landing screen for browsing and launching games. - **Software library** — Browse installed games through a Switch-inspired library layout. - **System settings** — Access emulator configuration through the customized settings interface. - **Multiplayer menu** — A dedicated interface for ProsperoEden's experimental multiplayer functionality. - **Custom assets** — Switch-inspired icons, backgrounds, fonts, animations, and sound effects. - **ProsperoEden backend** — Uses the upstream emulator's game execution core, graphics renderers, controller support, and compatibility improvements. - **Independent installation** — Installs separately from ProsperoEden, allowing both applications to coexist on the same console. Game compatibility and emulation performance depend on the underlying ProsperoEden version and the individual game. ## Screenshots These launcher previews use placeholder games and profiles. ![Switch-style HOME screen](screenshots/home.png) ![All Software library](screenshots/library.png) ![System Settings](screenshots/settings.png) ![Multiplayer menu](screenshots/multiplayer.png) Some upstream interface features have intentionally been excluded to maintain the SwitchPS5 experience. - **Automatic updates are disabled.** Updating directly through ProsperoEden's built-in updater could replace the custom interface with the original upstream UI. SwitchPS5 must therefore be updated manually. - **Theme support has been removed.** SwitchPS5 uses its own dedicated interface and does not support switching to ProsperoEden's themes. - **The entire ProsperoEden layout has been removed.** SwitchPS5 retains its custom Nintendo Switch-inspired HOME screen, library, settings, and navigation instead of adopting the redesigned upstream launcher. - The PS5 app is named **Switch** and uses title ID **PPSA99009** ## Source Code SwitchPS5 is a modified version of ProsperoEden. The project retains the upstream emulation backend while implementing a separate Nintendo Switch-inspired frontend and application identity. The source includes selected artwork, fonts, motion data, and sounds extracted from decrypted Nintendo Switch firmware. No complete Nintendo Switch firmware, encryption keys, game dumps, or save data are provided with the project. For upstream emulator development, technical documentation, and build information, refer to the [ProsperoEden repository](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden). ## Credits ProsperoEden creator: **[BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden)**.\ Emulator core: [Eden and contributors](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror). SwitchPS5 is an unofficial homebrew project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Nintendo, Sony Interactive Entertainment, or the original emulator developers.\ Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, and all associated trademarks belong to their respective owners.\ This project is intended for lawful use with games and files you own and have obtained legally. Piracy and the distribution of copyrighted game files, firmware, or encryption keys are not supported.\ SwitchPS5 is experimental software provided without warranty. Compatibility, stability, and performance may vary. Use at your own risk.

repos.name: CheatRunner_Patches
repos.description: A community collection of PS4 & PS5 game patches made for CheatRunner.
repos.readme:
# CheatRunner Patches

A community collection of **PS4 & PS5 game patches** made for [CheatRunner](https://github.com/notmaj0r/CheatRunner).

Drop the patch file for your game in, launch it, and enjoy: 60 FPS, resolution patches, and more.

---

## 📥 Getting CheatRunner

These patches are made to work with **CheatRunner**.

You can download it here:
👉 **https://github.com/notmaj0r/CheatRunner**

---

## 📁 Repository structure

| Folder | Platform | File name |
|---|---|---|
| [`xml/`](xml) | PS4 | `CUSAXXXXX.xml` |
| [`xml_prospero/`](xml_prospero) | PS5 | `PPSAXXXXX.xml` |

Each file is named after the game's **Title ID** and can hold one or more patches for that game.

---

## 🚀 How to use

1. Download and set up [CheatRunner](https://github.com/notmaj0r/CheatRunner).
2. Find your game's Title ID (`CUSAXXXXX` for PS4, `PPSAXXXXX` for PS5).
3. Download the matching `.xml` file from the right folder (`xml` or `xml_prospero`).
4. Put it in CheatRunner's patch folder.
5. Launch the game and enable the patch you want.

> ⚠️ Patches are made for a **specific game version** (the `AppVer` field). If your game is on a different update, the patch may not work or may even crash the game.

---

## 🧩 Patch format

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Patch>
    <TitleID>
        <ID>CUSA00021</ID>
    </TitleID>
    <Metadata Title="Watch Dogs"
              Name="60 FPS"
              Note="Enable at game boot."
              Author="maj0r"
              PatchVer="1.0"
              AppVer="01.05"
              AppElf="eboot.bin">
        <PatchList>
            <Line Type="bytes" Address="0x1e3669b" Value="00"/>
        </PatchList>
    </Metadata>
</Patch>
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `Title` | Game name |
| `Name` | Patch name (e.g. `60 FPS`) |
| `Note` | Tips for the user (e.g. when to enable it) |
| `Author` | Credits, in order of contribution (e.g. `maj0r & Player1`) |
| `PatchVer` | Patch version |
| `AppVer` | Game update the patch was made for |
| `AppElf` | Executable that gets patched |

---

## 🤝 Contributing

Contributions are very welcome! Please read the rules below before opening a pull request.

### Pull request rules

1. **Only submit patches that are 100% tested and verified working with CheatRunner.** 
No guesses, no "should work".
2. **Filling out the form below is mandatory** in your pull request description.
3. **When editing an existing patch, never remove or overwrite the author credits, and never change their order** (order of arrival).
   Example: `maj0r & Player1 & Player2`. Add yourself at the end.
4. **When adding or editing a game's Title ID file, don't add yourself as an author unless you contributed at least one patch to that file.**

### Pull request form

Fill out this form in your PR description, using your own game's info.
This is just an example:

```
Game: God of War
Platform: PS4
TITLE ID: CUSAXXXXX
UPDATE: 1.22
Tested working with CheatRunner? Yes!
Tested on PS5? Yes
```

> `Tested working with CheatRunner?` must be **Yes**. PRs that answer anything else will not be merged.

### Checklist before you submit

- [ ] The file is in the right folder (`xml` for PS4, `xml_prospero` for PS5)
- [ ] The file is named after the Title ID
- [ ] `AppVer` matches the game update you tested on
- [ ] Existing authors are kept, in the same order
- [ ] I only added myself as an author if I contributed a patch to the file
- [ ] I tested it with CheatRunner and it works
- [ ] The PR form is filled out

---

## 🙏 Credits

Thanks to everyone who tests and contributes patches.
Authors are credited inside each patch file.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

Use these patches at your own risk.
Only use them with games you legally own.
This repository does not host or distribute any game files.

repos.readme:
Listen to your PS5's audio on your phone, tablet or PC. No Bluetooth or extra hardware, just a browser (or the Android/Windows app) on the same Wi-Fi. HearBridge Browser is a small payload for a jailbroken PS5. It captures the console's audio output and serves it on your local network, together with a player page. Open the page, tap Play, and you hear the game. Full guide with setup, tips and FAQ: https://x-f1reball-x.github.io/HearBridge-Browser/guide/

## Features - **Works in any modern browser**: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, including iPhone and iPad. - **Android app**: finds your console on the network by itself, so you don't have to type the IP. - **Windows app**: a small portable `.exe` that opens the player in its own window. Nothing to install. - **Volume boost up to 500%**, with a soft limiter so it doesn't clip or distort. - **Sound modes**: Normal, Game, Music, Dynamic, Voice and Night. - **Automatic latency**: the Auto buffer learns the lowest delay your device can handle without dropouts. You can also pick Low, Stable or set it by hand. - **Record and export**: record what you hear and save it as WAV, FLAC, MP3 or Opus. - **Device detection**: the page checks what your browser supports, marks the recommended settings and greys out the ones that won't work. - Several people can listen at the same time, each with their own quality setting. ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port **9021**. - A phone, tablet or computer on the same local network as the console. ## Install 1. Download `hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf` from the [Releases](../../releases) page. 2. Send it to the console's ELF loader on port 9021, for example: ``` nc -q0 9021 < hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf ``` or use any payload sender you already have. 3. Wait for the notification on the PS5, then on your device open: ``` http://:8096 ``` Or install `HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0.apk` on Android and pick your console from the list. ### Windows app Download `HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0-windows-x64.exe` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and run it. No install needed. - Needs Windows 10 or 11 (x64) with the WebView2 runtime. It's built into Windows 11 and current Windows 10, so you most likely have it already. - The exe isn't signed, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - If it can't reach the console, type your console's IP in the box and press Retry. It remembers the last IP that worked. The payload keeps running until you stop it or turn off the console. Sending it again replaces the running copy. ## Usage On a phone the page has four tabs. The mini player with the volume slider is always at the bottom. On a tablet or desktop everything is on one screen. **Play**: the big Play button, L/R level meters, and live stats (latency, bitrate, number of listeners). The volume slider goes from 0 to 500%; anything above 100% is boost. **Sound**: pick a sound mode, the stream quality (PCM 48k or 24k, or the lighter μ-law versions for weak Wi-Fi) and the buffer (Auto, Low, Stable or Manual). Your choices are saved per device. **Record**: start and stop a recording, listen to a preview, then export as WAV, FLAC, MP3 or Opus. You can keep the volume as you heard it, set a custom level, or normalize the file. **Info**: connection details, what your device supports, and links. If you prefer a media player, `http://:8096/live.wav` works in VLC or ffplay. ## FAQ **Do I need Bluetooth or any extra hardware?** No. Everything goes over your normal Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. **Does my audio go to the internet?** No. It only works on your local network. The console streams directly to your device and nothing leaves your network. The page doesn't load anything from outside either. **Why no Dolby or DTS?** Browsers can't decode Dolby or DTS streams, so the audio is sent as plain stereo. Set the PS5 audio output to stereo / linear PCM if you hear nothing. **I hear nothing on my iPhone.** Check the silent switch on the side of the phone and the volume buttons. HearBridge asks iOS to play even in silent mode, but some iOS versions still mute the browser when the switch is on. If iOS interrupts the audio (a call, Siri, etc.), tap "Tap to resume audio". **How do I stop it?** Send a POST to `http://:8096/api/stop`, or reboot the console. ## Screenshots
Play Sound Record Info
Tablet
## Building from source ### PS5 payload You need the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and Python 3. ``` export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ./build.sh # PS5 payload -> dist/hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf ./build.sh host # local test server for your PC -> build/hearbridge-browser-host ``` The PS5 build needs `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` set to your sdk folder, with the sdk's LLVM toolchain on your `PATH`. If it isn't set, `build.sh` stops with an error. The host build doesn't need the sdk. The player page (`web/index.html`) and the MP3 encoder are embedded into the ELF by `tools/embed.py`. The host build plays a test tone, so you can work on the page without a console. Use `HB_TEST=program ./build/hearbridge-browser-host` for something closer to real game audio. ### Android app Needs JDK 17+ and the Android SDK. ``` cd android ./gradlew assembleRelease ``` Release signing reads `android/keystore/keystore.properties`. Without it the APK is built unsigned. See [android/README.md](android/README.md). ### Windows app Needs Go 1.24+ and [go-winres](https://github.com/tc-hib/go-winres) (the script installs it if it's missing). Builds from Linux or Windows (Git Bash). ``` cd windows ./build.sh # -> windows/dist/HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0-windows-x64.exe ``` The icon and version info are generated into a `.syso` file during the build. See [windows/README.md](windows/README.md). ## Credits - The audio capture code comes from my earlier project [HearBridge PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5), and the limiter in the page is a port of its `gain.c`. - MP3 export uses [lamejs](https://github.com/zhuker/lamejs) (LGPL-3.0, unmodified, in `vendor/lamejs`). ## Support If you like the project, you can buy me a coffee: - Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/XF1REBALLX - X: [X-F1REBALL-X](https://x.com/XxF1REBALLxX) ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

repos.name: ps5-theme
repos.description: Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles (etaHEN plugin or standalone payload): backgrounds, icons, sounds, fonts and home music as read-only overlays.
repos.readme: # PS5 Themes (ps5-theme) Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles on firmware 13.60 and below, as an [etaHEN](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60) plugin or a standalone payload. Change the home screen's backgrounds, icons, sounds, fonts and home music, keep as many themes as you like, and switch between them from the console, a phone or a computer. The system is never written: every theme is a read-only overlay held in memory, so the console is stock again the moment the plugin stops, and the plugin puts your theme back each time etaHEN starts. ![A theme on the console: its own home background, and Snoopy icons for the Discover tile and two apps](docs/screenshots/console-home.jpg) ![The theme library](docs/screenshots/library.png) Version 1.60. Developed and tested on a PS5 with firmware 13.42, both with etaHEN 2.5B (unified build) and on its own from PS5 Payload Manager. > **About the screenshots.** They were taken from the author's own console. > The test themes in them use Peanuts artwork, and the games shown use their > publishers' artwork; both belong to their rights holders and are not part of > this project. In the manager's screenshots the console's own pictures are > blurred on purpose: system files stay on the console and are never > redistributed. The photos of the console's screen show its interface as it > appears. ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Install](#install) - [Running without etaHEN](#running-without-etahen) - [Your first theme](#your-first-theme) - [Documentation](#documentation): the guides and the technical pages in [`docs/`](docs/) - [Firmware support and known limits](#firmware-support-and-known-limits) - [Removing](#removing) - [Development Approach](#development-approach) - [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) - [Licences and trademarks](#licences-and-trademarks) ## What it does - **Themes tile and web manager.** A **Themes** tile on the home screen opens the manager in the console's browser. The same manager works from any phone or computer on your network at `http://:8095`. - **Build a theme from parts.** Switch on what you want to change and add a file: background, icons, home music, system sounds, fonts, animations, video, textures and other images, the home screen's own tiles and the interface's icons. - **Game and app icons.** Change the icon, background and logo of any installed game or app, homebrew and PlayStation Network artwork included. The Game Library shows them at once, and the home screen after rest mode; games and apps keep starting as before (see [Changing game and app icons safely](docs/challenges.md#changing-game-and-app-icons-safely)). - **Any file, fitted for you.** One image fills every size of an asset. Any audio file is converted to the exact format and loudness of the sound it replaces, including the console's ATRAC9 home music. The browser does this, and the console checks every file again. - **Appearance themes.** Replace the Control Center's bottom panel, the corner piece by the clock and the home screen artwork of the PlayStation, PlayStation 2, 3 and 4 themes, with placement and see-through parts (see [Appearance themes](docs/appearance-themes.md)). - **Fonts.** Replace the text fonts the home screen and Settings draw with, for the home screen only (see [Fonts](docs/fonts.md)). - **Home music editor.** Pick the part of a song to use, an optional loop part, the order they play in, how the joints sound and the loudness, then hear it before you apply it. - **Wake-up sound.** Replace the sound the console plays as it wakes from rest mode (see [The wake-up sound](docs/home-music.md#the-wake-up-sound)). - **Preview pictures.** Each theme's card shows its background, or any picture you choose, so you can tell themes apart at a glance. - **Save and Discard.** Changes are kept as unsaved until you save them, and Discard puts the theme back as it was. - **Clear progress.** Applying shows what the console is doing and how far it has got. - **Library tools.** Duplicate, export to a `.zip`, import a `.zip` or a folder (drag it in), and delete. - **Comes back by itself.** The applied theme is put back every time etaHEN starts the plugin, after a reboot or an update. Only **Restore stock** stops it. - **Never writes the system.** Nothing under `/system` or `/system_ex` is opened for writing, only media files can be themed, and every file is checked against the system file it replaces (see [what the checks cover](docs/how-it-works.md#what-the-checks-cover-and-what-they-dont)). ## Requirements - A PS5 on firmware 13.60 or below, jailbroken, running etaHEN or any jailbreak with the standard ELF loader (see [Running without etaHEN](#running-without-etahen)). Tested on 13.42 with [etaHEN 2.5B unified](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60/releases/tag/v2.5B-unified.1), which covers 11.00 to 13.60 except 11.40. - A phone or computer on the same network is the easiest way to add files. The console's own browser works for applying and switching themes. - To build from source: Docker. Nothing else on the host. ## Install 1. Copy `ps5-theme.plugin` to `/data/etaHEN/plugins/` on the console. 2. Turn on auto-start, so it runs whenever etaHEN runs. Either: - create an empty file `/data/etaHEN/plugins/ps5-theme.plugin.auto_start`, or - turn on auto-start for it in the etaHEN Toolbox plugin list. 3. Start it from the Toolbox, or jailbreak again. On its first start the plugin lists the home screen's own assets (before any theme is mounted), starts the manager on port **8095**, adds the **Themes** tile, and shows a notification with the address to open from a phone or computer. **Updating:** copy the new `.plugin` file over the old one in `/data/etaHEN/plugins/`. Within about 10 seconds the running plugin finds it, starts it through etaHEN's ELF loader and hands over to it. Your theme stays on the screen the whole time, and no Toolbox or restart is needed, which matters after rest mode, when etaHEN's Toolbox is often gone. An open manager page reloads itself with the new version. (This works from 1.23 on: to get 1.23 itself from an older version, restart the console once.) A newer `ps5-theme.elf` or `.plugin` in `/data/ps5-theme/update/` works the same way, with or without etaHEN. **If the manager can't be reached:** start ps5-theme again (from the Toolbox or PS5 Payload Manager). The new copy takes over from the running one even when that one doesn't answer, and keeps your theme. If that doesn't help, start `ps5-theme-stop.elf` from a payload loader or PS5 Payload Manager, then start ps5-theme again. It stops the running copy and leaves your theme on the screen, apart from the games' and apps' pictures until ps5-theme runs again (see [Stopping without a restart](docs/how-it-works.md#stopping-without-a-restart)). No restart is needed in either case. ## Running without etaHEN The plugin doesn't need etaHEN, only a jailbreak: a kernel exploit and the standard PS5 ELF loader (port 9021) that ps5-payload-sdk programs run under. It gets its own privileges, and everything else is its own code. Every release has both files, which contain the same program: - `ps5-theme.elf`: for any ELF loader, such as [PS5 Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager); - `ps5-theme.plugin`: for etaHEN, the same program with etaHEN's header. **With PS5 Payload Manager:** - **Start it:** put `ps5-theme.elf` in a folder under `/data/pldmgr/payloads/` (or import it from USB) and launch it from the manager. It then does everything it does under etaHEN: the web manager, the Themes tile, and putting the selected theme back. - **Start it after every jailbreak:** add it to the manager's autoload list. - **Update it:** replace that `ps5-theme.elf` with the newer one (or put the newer one in `/data/ps5-theme/update/`). Within about 10 seconds the running copy finds it, starts it through the ELF loader and hands over, keeping your theme on the screen. Every build carries its version inside the program, which is how a plain `.elf` is recognised. **Keeping both as a backup:** you can set up `ps5-theme.elf` in Payload Manager and `ps5-theme.plugin` with auto-start in etaHEN at the same time. Only one copy ever runs: when the second one starts, it finds the first, and it exits if it isn't newer or takes over if it is. So whichever way starts first, you get one copy, and the newest one. **What's different without etaHEN:** nothing starts it at boot unless your jailbreak or Payload Manager does. Both ways have been run on a PS5 with 13.42: `ps5-theme.elf` from PS5 Payload Manager, and `ps5-theme.plugin` from etaHEN. If something works differently on your setup, the Activity page says what happened. ## Your first theme 1. Open the **Themes** tile, or `http://:8095` on a phone or computer. 2. Press **New theme**, give it a name and press **Create**. 3. Press **Edit** on its card, switch on **Background** and drop in a picture. Add home music, icons or sounds the same way. The guides to [backgrounds](docs/backgrounds.md) and [home music](docs/home-music.md) go step by step. 4. Press **Save** in the bar at the bottom, then **Apply to console**. 5. Give it a few seconds. The home screen may show the stock look for a moment while it switches. 6. **To hear new home music,** move to a game or app on the home screen that has its own music, so the console switches to that music, then come back. The console keeps playing the music it already had loaded and only picks up the theme's music when it starts the home music again. To change only the music, make a theme with just **Home music**. Everything else stays stock. ## Documentation | Page | What's in it | |---|---| | [Backgrounds](docs/backgrounds.md) | Changing the home screen's backgrounds: a step-by-step guide, where each background is used, what it needs, and how they are made | | [Home music](docs/home-music.md) | Giving the home screen your own music: a step-by-step guide to the music editor, when you hear it, what it needs, and how it is made; and your own [wake-up sound](docs/home-music.md#the-wake-up-sound) | | [Changing game and app icons](docs/games-and-apps.md) | Installed games' and apps' icons, backgrounds and logos; the console's own tiles; interface icons | | [Appearance themes](docs/appearance-themes.md) | The Control Center's panels and the home screen artwork of the PlayStation 1 to 4 themes: a step-by-step guide, what it needs, how it depends on the anniversary assets, and how they are made and stored | | [Fonts](docs/fonts.md) | Replacing the console's text fonts, and which ones the home screen uses | | [A tour of the manager](docs/manager.md) | Every page and control of the web manager | | [How it works, and why](docs/how-it-works.md) | Overlays instead of writing the system, sandbox views, checks, staging, updating and stopping | | [Theme format](docs/theme-format.md) | What a theme folder and its export contain | | [Challenges and how they were solved](docs/challenges.md) | The problems met on the console and their solutions, including [changing game and app icons safely](docs/challenges.md#changing-game-and-app-icons-safely) and [finding the Appearance artwork](docs/challenges.md#the-appearance-themes-artwork) | | [Testing](docs/testing.md) | The automated tests and the [tests on the console](docs/testing.md#tests-on-the-console) | | [Building from source](docs/building.md) | Building the plugin and the tools, and the project layout | | [Security](docs/security.md) | Who can reach the plugin, what protects the system, fuzzing | Links to this page's old sections (from earlier release notes) land here; the table says where each one is now. ## Firmware support and known limits - Built for firmware up to 13.60; tested on 13.42 with etaHEN 2.5B unified. - On other firmware, the asset list, sandbox views and tile registration are all discovered on the console, but they haven't been tried there. If a theme doesn't show, leave and re-enter the home screen, or jailbreak again; the theme is put back at start either way. - New home music is heard only once the console starts its home music again: move to a game or app that has its own music, then come back (see [Home music](docs/home-music.md#when-you-hear-it)). Its position is kept by the console (see [Music that starts part-way through](docs/challenges.md#music-that-starts-part-way-through)). - After rest mode, the plugin covers the new views ShellUI's restarted apps make (see [Stock again after rest mode](docs/challenges.md#stock-again-after-rest-mode)). An app that read its background before the overlay arrived may show stock until it reloads; **Re-apply** brings it back at once. etaHEN's own Toolbox stopping after rest mode is outside this plugin. - Background and icon sorting is by file name. Anything it misses is under **Other images**. - The home screen's layout can't be themed (it is code). Its colours are in the interface's palettes: **Edit colours** changes the widgets, the Control Center, the button hints, the text and the accent (see [Colours](docs/appearance-themes.md#colours)). - The sound when the console is switched on plays before the jailbreak, so a theme can't change it. The sound as it wakes from rest mode can. - Interface pictures: the console reads its resource files when the interface starts, so changed ones show after rest mode or a restart. The numbered test drew nothing beside the **Games** and **Media** tabs on 13.42. Whether the console draws your own picture inside a vector icon hasn't been seen on the console yet. - etaHEN's plugin **Stop** ends the plugin at once: overlays stay until you choose **Restore stock**, start the plugin again, or reboot. ## Removing 1. Choose **Restore stock**. 2. Delete `/data/etaHEN/plugins/ps5-theme.plugin*` and `/data/ps5-theme/`. 3. Delete the **Themes** tile from the home screen. ## Development Approach This project explores AI-assisted development for PS5 homebrew, with an emphasis on practical validation rather than accepting generated code at face value. Claude Code was used to assist with implementation, debugging and iterative improvements. Development was guided by testing on physical PS5 hardware, examining application logs, investigating observed failures and verifying fixes on the console. The project combines hardware testing with host-side automated tests to exercise application behaviour, error handling and recovery scenarios. The aim is to evaluate how AI-assisted development can be used to build a useful console utility while maintaining a focus on reliability, safety and reproducibility. AI assistance does not replace testing or eliminate the need for continued review. Firmware compatibility and known limitations are documented separately. ## Acknowledgements This project stands on the work of people who share what they learn with everyone. My deepest gratitude to each of them. Without their work, their openness and the time they gave freely, none of this would exist. - **etaHEN**, by LightningMods and its contributors, and **[GronedWaffel](https://github.com/GronedWaffel)** for the [11.00–13.60 unified build](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60) this was built and tested on. etaHEN is the foundation everything here runs on: the plugin format, auto-start and the Toolbox card installer, whose approach the Themes tile follows. - **[ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)**, by John Törnblom and contributors: the toolchain, the kernel access and the examples the whole plugin is built with. - **[kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite)**, by EchoStretch, which ships with the etaHEN build this was developed on. - **[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9)**, by Alex Barney (MIT License): the ATRAC9 codebooks and bitstream layout behind the encoder and the plugin's checks, and one of the two reference decoders in the tests. Without it, home music would not have been possible. - **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/)** and its ATRAC9 decoder, the second independent reference in the codec tests. - **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** by drakmor, **[PS5-File-Explorer](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-File-Explorer)** by juma-sayeh and **[onionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN)** by aydencharles, whose home-screen app registration and navigation work etaHEN's Toolbox card builds on, and through it the Themes tile. - **[ps5-webkit-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader)** by itsPLK, which showed that a home-screen app can open a page served by a payload on the console itself. - **[PSDevWiki](https://www.psdevwiki.com/ps5/)** and everyone who documents the PS5 there, in particular `param.json` and its `deeplinkUri`. - **Zstandard and xxHash**, by Yann Collet and the zstd contributors: the format specification (RFC 8878) and the educational decoder that the plugin's decoder follows. - **Microsoft's Direct3D documentation** of the BC7 format, which the texture encoder follows. - **[PS5Themes](https://github.com/MasterPS0/PS5Themes)** by MasterPS0, whose theme packs showed which files hold the home screen's tab icons, tile icons and per-tile backgrounds. - **[PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2)** by Swordpdf and **[ATRACTool-Reloaded](https://github.com/XyLe-GBP/ATRACTool-Reloaded)** by XyLe-GBP, studied while working out how to get music onto the home screen. - Everyone in the PS5 homebrew community who tests, reports and explains: your write-ups and answers made the hard parts possible. ## Licences and trademarks Copyright (C) 2026 Blaze414 - **ps5-theme is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version** (GPL-3.0-or-later). The full text is in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). You may use, study, change and share it; if you share a changed version, it must stay under the same licence with its source available. It comes with no warranty. - Why the GPL: the plugin is built with [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), whose kernel interface is GPL-3.0-or-later (© John Törnblom), so the plugin as built is under the same terms. - The ATRAC9 tables are generated from LibAtrac9, © 2018 Alex Barney, MIT License (`licenses/LibAtrac9.txt`), which allows their use in a GPL project. - No system files are included. The plugin works with the files on your own console, and the stock copies it keeps never leave it. - "PlayStation", "PS5" and "ATRAC" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. or Sony Group Corporation. latestRelease.name: ps5-theme 1.60
latestRelease.body:
Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles on firmware 13.60 and below. Runs as an etaHEN plugin or on its own from any ELF loader. Tested on firmware 13.42, both with etaHEN 2.5B (unified build) and from PS5 Payload Manager.

## Which file?

- **`ps5-theme.plugin`**: for etaHEN. Copy it to `/data/etaHEN/plugins/` and turn on auto-start.
- **`ps5-theme.elf`**: the same program for [PS5 Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) or any ELF loader (port 9021). No etaHEN needed.
- **`ps5-theme-stop.elf`**: only for when the manager can't be reached. Start it from Payload Manager or a payload loader, then start ps5-theme again. It stops the plugin and leaves your theme on the screen. Put it in a folder of its own under `/data/pldmgr/payloads/`.

## Updating

- **From 1.23 or later:** copy the new file over the old one (or put it in `/data/ps5-theme/update/`). Within about 10 seconds the running plugin finds it and hands over, keeping your theme on the screen. No restart needed.
- **From 1.22 or older:** copy the new file and restart the console once.
- If you keep a copy in PS5 Payload Manager, replace that one too, so an old version isn't started from there.

## New in 1.60 (since 1.59)

- **One progress display while a theme is applied.** On the library, the banner shows the apply's progress, with its percentage on the right; the message in the corner no longer covers it. On the other pages the message shows as before.
- **Docs:** a photo of the colours from **Edit colours** on the console, in the [Appearance themes guide](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/blob/main/docs/appearance-themes.md#colours).

Everything in [1.59](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/releases/tag/v1.59) is included.

### Checked

54 end-to-end tests on the host (full and emulated), and a PS5 with 13.42: an apply with the library open, and the update from 1.59 handing over by itself.


repos.name: NX-Controller-Tester
repos.description: Nintendo Switch homebrew (.nro) to test your controllers: Joy-Con, DualShock 3 (PS3), DualShock 4 (PS4), DualSense (PS5) and PS1/PS2 controllers via the SuperBox 3 USB adapter. Buttons, sticks, drift, triggers, battery, rumble.
repos.readme:
# Controller Tester — Nintendo Switch

**Joy-Con · DualShock 3 (PS3) · DualShock 4 (PS4) · DualSense (PS5) · PS1 / PS2 (via SuperBox 3)**

**By Not_eFootballer**

Nintendo Switch homebrew (`.nro`) to test your controllers in real time. It runs from the Homebrew Menu, needs no sysmodule, and changes nothing on the console.

## Features

- **Controller**: every button, the D-pad, the sticks (X/Y values and %), the triggers, the battery, rumble (left, right, both) and the motion sensors.
- **Drift**: stick trails, ×10 center zoom, 3-second resting measurement with a verdict, circularity test.
- **USB**: diagnostics for controllers plugged in over USB.

## Tested controllers

| Controller | Connection |
|---|---|
| Joy-Con | Bluetooth / rail |
| DualShock 3 (PS3) | USB cable |
| DualShock 4 (PS4) | USB cable |
| DualSense (PS5) | USB cable |
| PS1 / PS2 | **SuperBox 3** USB adapter |

### PS1 / PS2 controllers

PlayStation 1 and 2 controllers have no USB port, so you need an adapter. Plug the controller into a **SuperBox 3**, then plug the SuperBox 3 into the Switch (into the dock, or through a USB-C OTG adapter in handheld mode). The app detects it automatically and shows the controller with the PlayStation layout.

### PS3 / PS4 / PS5 controllers

Just plug them in with a USB cable: they work in the app right away, even though the Switch doesn't support them on its own.

## Installation

1. Download `NXControllerTester.nro` from the **Releases**.
2. Copy it to `sd:/switch/NXControllerTester/`.
3. Open the Homebrew Menu (ideally by holding **R** while launching a game) and start **Controller Tester**.

## Controls

Hold **+** (or **−**), then:

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| L / R | Previous / next page |
| Up / Down | Choose the displayed controller |
| A | Full rumble test |
| ← / → | Left / right motor |
| X | Resting drift measurement |
| Y | Reset statistics |
| **B held for 1 s** | **Quit** (or press HOME twice) |

The touchscreen also works for the tabs, the controller list and rumble.

Tested on firmware 21.0.1 with Atmosphère 1.10.1.

repos.name: ps5-captures
repos.description: PS5 homebrew app: send your screenshots and videos to your phone over Wi-Fi with a QR code. No account, no cloud.
repos.readme:
Captures for PS5

Send your PS5 screenshots and videos to your phone over Wi-Fi.
Open the app, scan the QR code, browse and save. No account, no cloud, no cable.

--- ## What it does The PS5 keeps every screenshot and video clip you capture, but getting them onto your phone normally needs the PlayStation App and a PSN connection. **Captures** is a small homebrew app that serves your captures straight from the console to any phone or computer on the same network: - **Scan and go** - the TV shows a big QR code; point your phone's camera at it and the gallery opens in the browser. - **A real gallery** - every screenshot and video, newest first, grouped by day, with the console's own thumbnails. - **Pick a game** - a picker with each game's icon, name and number of captures (PS5 and PS4 titles). - **View and play** - full-screen pictures, videos play right in the browser (with seeking), swipe between them. - **Save one or many** - save a single file, or select several and save them one by one (or as one `.zip`). - **Phone-friendly videos** - clips that some homebrew apps record as WebM are made into MP4 on the PS5 when you save them, so phone galleries take them. - **Nothing to set up** - one button on the PS5 (Circle to close). ## Safe by design - The gallery only runs **while the Captures screen is open**; close the app and it stops. - It only **reads** the capture folders (`/user/av_contents/photo` and `/video`) - nothing on the console is changed or deleted. - It is only reachable from your **local network** (the PS5's own address, port 8090). Nothing goes to the internet. ## Requirements - A **jailbroken PS5** with a payload loader (for example the PS5 Payload Manager / `elfldr` on port 9021). Tested on firmware **13.00**. - **ShadowMountPlus** (or another homebrew registrar) so the installed app gets its home-screen tile. - A phone or computer on the **same network** as the PS5. ## Install 1. Download **`CapturesPS5-v1.2.zip`** from the [Releases](../../releases) page and unzip it to get **`CapturesPS5.elf`**. 2. Send it with your payload loader (Payload Manager, `elfldr`, ...). It installs the app to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99233` and stays running as the app's helper. 3. Open **Captures** from the home screen (if the tile doesn't appear, let ShadowMountPlus rescan or restart the PS5). After a reboot you don't need to send the payload again: when no helper answers, the app sends its own helper to the ELF loader (`elfldr`, port 9021) by itself. ## Use 1. Open **Captures** on the PS5. The TV shows a QR code and the address, e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:8090`. 2. Scan the code with your phone (or type the address in the phone's browser). 3. Browse, tap to view, **Save** to download. **Select** lets you pick several and save them (each as its own file, or all in one `.zip` for a computer). 4. Press **Circle** on the controller to close Captures (the gallery stops with it). **iPhone tip:** press and hold a picture and choose *Save to Photos*. Downloaded videos land in the Files app, from where *Share -> Save Video* puts them in Photos. **WebM videos:** clips recorded while some homebrew apps run are WebM files, which phone galleries refuse. When you save one, the PS5 first makes an MP4 of it (the page shows the progress; usually under a minute) and keeps it in `/data/captures/mp4/`, so saving it again is instant. Only the clips you save are converted. ## What's new - **1.2** - WebM clips are made into MP4 on the PS5 when you save them (FFmpeg + x264 in the helper), with the progress on the phone and the TV; the `.zip` carries the MP4s; several picked files save one by one, so phones keep them as normal files; the "files sent" counter is gone. - **1.1** - downloads are sent as files, so phones save videos instead of opening them in a player; WebM clips are served as their MP4 copy when one is placed in `/data/captures/mp4/`. - **1.0** - first release. ## Build from source Needs Linux (or WSL), the [ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), clang/lld 18, zlib, nasm and curl. First build FFmpeg and x264 for the PS5 (downloads FFmpeg 7.1.5 and a pinned x264 into `deps/`), then the app: ```sh PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk deps/build-deps.sh make PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # -> build/ps5/CapturesPS5.elf ``` How it is built: | Part | Files | What it is | | --- | --- | --- | | The app | `coreorbis/main-captures.cpp` | the QR screen (a native PS5 title, `eboot.bin`) | | The gallery | `coreorbis/orbis-shims/ProsperoCaptures.cpp`, `captures_page.inc` | the web server and the phone page, run by the helper | | The converter | `coreorbis/orbis-shims/ProsperoConvert.cpp`, `deps/build-deps.sh` | WebM -> MP4 (H.264 + AAC) on the PS5 with FFmpeg and x264 | | The helper | `coreorbis/orbis-shims/ProsperoHelper.cpp` | a payload that takes the app out of its sandbox and serves the gallery | | The installer | `installer/installer_main.cpp`, `ProsperoInstall.cpp` | installs the app folder built into the payload | | PS5 layer | `coreorbis/orbis-shims/*` | video, pad, notifications, paths, crash log | ## Credits - **[genplusgxPS5](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/genplusgxPS5)** by MisterTemaki - the PS5 app shell this grew from (video, pad, text, the installer/helper layout and the sandbox escape). - **[PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2)** by swordpdf - the native-title, installer and helper approach that shell follows. - **[ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded)** by BlackBearReloaded - the native app build tools and startup code in `proto/native` (GPL-3.0). - **[ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** - the toolchain and PS5 libraries. - **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org)** (LGPL-2.1+, built with `--enable-gpl`) and **[x264](https://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html)** (GPL-2.0-or-later) - the WebM -> MP4 converter in the helper; `deps/build-deps.sh` fetches and builds the exact sources used. - **[QR Code generator library](https://www.nayuki.io/page/qr-code-generator-library)** by Project Nayuki (MIT). - **[stb_truetype](https://github.com/nothings/stb)** by Sean Barrett (public domain / MIT). - Fonts: **Roboto** (Apache 2.0), **PromptFont** by Yukari "Shinmera" Hafner (SIL OFL), **Font Awesome** brands (SIL OFL) - their licenses are in `frontend/assets/fonts`. Made with the help of an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic). ## License The project as a whole is released under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 or later** (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)), because the app links the GPL-3.0 startup code of ps5-native-app-boilerplate and the helper links FFmpeg (built with `--enable-gpl`) and x264 (GPL-2.0-or-later). The files written for this project and the PS5 layer carry their own MIT notices and may also be used under MIT on their own. *Captures is an unofficial homebrew project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation" and "PS5" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. Use at your own risk.*

repos.name: msx-ps5
repos.description: MSX emulator for the PS5 with a 3D game shelf (blueMSX)
repos.readme:
MSX PS5

An MSX emulator for the PS5, with a 3D game shelf.
blueMSX at its heart; boxes, cartridges and floppies you can turn in your hands.


Cartridges
Blow on the contacts

Floppy disks
Playing
--- ## What it does **MSX PS5** runs MSX, MSX2 and MSX2+ games on a jailbroken PS5 as a home-screen app, through the [blueMSX](http://www.bluemsx.com/) emulator (its [libretro core](https://github.com/libretro/blueMSX-libretro)). - **A 3D shelf** - every game stands on a glossy shelf as its **box**, its **cartridge** or its **floppy disk** (L3 switches the style). Boxes get a spine and a back made from the cover art, with the publisher, year and screenshots. - **Turn it over** - L2 / R2 spin the game in front of you, with clicks in the controller and resistance in the triggers. - **Blow on the cartridge** - swipe up on the touchpad to turn a cartridge to its contacts, then blow into the controller's microphone to clean them, just like back then. - **Box art by itself** - covers, box backs and screenshots are downloaded from [libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails) (Square fetches one again). - **Favorites** - Circle marks a game; the Favorites tab keeps them together. - **Music and sounds** - ten original shelf tunes (ambient, chill, hip-hop, jazz and more) and CC0 sound effects, each with its own volume. - **Playing** - CRT shaders and scanlines, screen size and aspect, save states, rewind (hold L2 + R2), fast forward (hold R2), the sprite limit removed, FM-PAC / MSX-MUSIC sound, controls for all games or for each game. ## Requirements - A **jailbroken PS5** with a payload loader (for example the PS5 Payload Manager / `elfldr` on port 9021). Tested on firmware **13.00**. - **ShadowMountPlus** (or another homebrew registrar) so the installed app gets its home-screen tile. - Your own MSX games (none are included); an internet connection on the PS5 for the box art. ## Install 1. Download **`MSXPS5-v1.0.zip`** from the [Releases](../../releases) page and unzip it. Inside are **`MSXPS5.elf`** (the app) and a **`bios`** folder. 2. Send `MSXPS5.elf` with your payload loader. It installs the app to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99231` and stays running as the app's helper. 3. Open **MSX PS5** once from the home screen (if the tile doesn't appear, let ShadowMountPlus rescan or restart the PS5). The app makes its folders in **`/data/msx`**: `roms`, `bios`, `covers`, `saves`, `states`... 4. Copy the BIOS and your games (below), then open MSX PS5 again. After a reboot you don't need to send the payload again: the app sends its own helper to the ELF loader when none answers. ## Setup ### Copying files to the PS5 Use any way you already have to put files in `/data` on your PS5, for example: - **FTP** - load an FTP server payload on the PS5, then connect from your computer with an FTP client such as FileZilla (host: the PS5's IP address, port: the one the payload shows, usually 2121). - **A web file manager** payload - open its address in your computer's browser and upload from there. ### 1. BIOS (do this first) Copy the **contents** of the zip's `bios` folder (the `Machines` and `Databases` folders) to **`/data/msx/bios`**: ``` /data/msx/bios/Machines/... /data/msx/bios/Databases/... ``` That is enough for **cartridge games**: they run on the free **C-BIOS** that comes with it. **Disk (`.dsk`) and tape (`.cas`) games** need a real MSX BIOS, which can't be shared here. Put the BIOS ROMs you own in the matching machine's folder, `/data/msx/bios/Machines//` (its `config.ini` names the files it needs), or copy the `Machines` folder of a blueMSX installation that has them over the zip's one. Settings > EMULATION > **MSX machine** chooses MSX, MSX2, MSX2+ or MSX turbo R (Auto picks one by the game). ### 2. Games Copy your games to **`/data/msx/roms`** (subfolders are fine): - cartridges: `.rom` `.mx1` `.mx2` - disks: `.dsk` - tapes: `.cas` - any of them inside a `.zip` The shelf lists them by name; games are recognised by their contents, so file names don't have to be exact. ### 3. Covers Box art, box backs and screenshots are **downloaded by themselves** from [libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails) - the PS5 only needs an internet connection. - Settings > LIBRARY > **Download covers** turns it on or off. - On the shelf, **Square** downloads the selected game's cover again. - Downloaded art is kept in `/data/msx/covers`, so it is fetched only once. - **Your own cover:** put a `.png` or `.jpg` with the same name as the game file in **`/data/msx/covers`** (for example `/data/msx/covers/Knightmare.png` for `Knightmare.rom`), or next to the game file. Your own art always wins over a download. ## Controls | On the shelf | | | --- | --- | | Cross | play | | D-pad left / right | browse (L1 / R1: ten at a time) | | D-pad up / down | choose the system / Favorites | | L2 / R2 | turn the game | | L3 | boxes / cartridges / floppies | | Triangle | settings | | Square | download the cover again | | Circle | favorite | | Touchpad | cartridge: swipe up to see its contacts (then blow); floppy: swipe to slide the shutter | | Options | quit | In a game, press **L3 + R3** for the menu (resume, save / load state, reset, settings, back to the game list). Hold **R2** to fast forward and **L2 + R2** to rewind. The MSX joystick and keys are mapped to the PS5 buttons in Settings > CONTROLS, for all games or for one game. **Blowing on a cartridge** uses the controller's built-in microphone, so it has to be on: if the mic button's light is orange, press it once (the bottom line on the screen tells you). ## Updating Send the new `MSXPS5.elf` the same way. Your games, BIOS, covers, settings, saves (`/data/msx/saves`) and save states (`/data/msx/states`) are kept. ## Troubleshooting - **"No games found"** - the games aren't in `/data/msx/roms`, or have an extension the shelf doesn't list. - **A disk or tape game asks for the MSX BIOS** - see [BIOS](#1-bios-do-this-first): those need the real BIOS ROMs. - **No covers** - check the PS5's internet connection and Settings > LIBRARY > Download covers; a few games simply have no art in libretro-thumbnails (add your own). - **The tile isn't on the home screen** - let ShadowMountPlus rescan, or restart the PS5 and send the payload again. - **Something else** - the app writes its log to `/data/msx/logs/boot.log`; please attach it to an [issue](../../issues). ## Build from source Needs Linux (or WSL), the [ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) (v0.42 or newer) and clang/lld 18: ```sh cd ps5 make ps5 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # -> build/ps5/MSXPS5.elf ``` | Part | Where | What it is | | --- | --- | --- | | The emulator | `Src/`, `libretro.c` | blueMSX-libretro, with a few PS5 fixes marked "MSX PS5" | | The app | `ps5/frontend/` | the shelf (`fe_shelf`, `fe_cart3d`, `fe_art`), menus, covers, sound and music | | PS5 layer | `ps5/coreorbis/` | video, pad, microphone, audio, paths, crash log | | Installer / helper | `ps5/installer/`, `ProsperoHelper.cpp` | installs the app and gives it access to `/data` | The upstream core's own documentation is in [README-blueMSX-libretro.md](README-blueMSX-libretro.md). ## Credits - **[blueMSX](http://www.bluemsx.com/)** by Daniel Vik and the blueMSX team, and the **[blueMSX-libretro](https://github.com/libretro/blueMSX-libretro)** core - the emulation. - **[genplusgxPS5](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/genplusgxPS5)** by MisterTemaki - the PS5 front end this grew from (video, pad, text, menus, the installer/helper layout). - **[ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded)** by BlackBearReloaded - the native app build tools and startup code in `ps5/proto/native` (GPL-3.0). - **[ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** - the toolchain and PS5 libraries. - **[C-BIOS](https://cbios.sourceforge.net/)** - the free MSX BIOS (its license is in `system/bluemsx/Machines/*C-BIOS/cbios.txt`). - **[libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails)** - box art and screenshots (downloaded, not included); game facts from blueMSX's msxromdb. - **[Mbed TLS](https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls)** (Apache-2.0) - HTTPS for the downloads. - CRT shaders rewritten from libretro's [slang-shaders](https://github.com/libretro/slang-shaders) - see [ps5/THIRD_PARTY_SHADERS.md](ps5/THIRD_PARTY_SHADERS.md). - Sound effects (CC0): [Kenney](https://kenney.nl) and freesound.org (micropolis, KRAFTWERK2K1, CrimsonGalaxies) - see `ps5/sounds/CREDITS.txt`. The shelf music is original. - Fonts: **Roboto** (Apache 2.0), **PromptFont** by Yukari "Shinmera" Hafner (SIL OFL), **Font Awesome** brands (SIL OFL) - their licenses are in `ps5/frontend/assets/fonts`. Made by **the7mirrors**, with the help of an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic). ## License The project as a whole is released under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 or later** (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)), because the app links the GPL-3.0 startup code of ps5-native-app-boilerplate. The blueMSX sources keep their own license (see [license.txt](license.txt)); the PS5 front end files carry MIT notices; the other components keep the licenses named above. *MSX PS5 is an unofficial homebrew project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or MSX Licensing Corporation. "PlayStation" and "PS5" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.; "MSX" is a trademark of MSX Licensing Corporation. No games or copyrighted BIOS files are included. Use at your own risk.*

repos.name: visor-ps5
repos.description: Mirror a Meta Quest 2 to the TV from a jailbroken PS5 - no PC, nothing to install on the headset
repos.readme:
Visor

Watch your Meta Quest 2 on the TV, straight from a jailbroken PS5.
Português

![Visor home screen](docs/home.png) Visor is a PS5 homebrew that mirrors a Quest 2 headset to the TV. The PS5 talks to the headset directly over Wi-Fi: no PC in the middle and nothing to install on the Quest. - Finds headsets on the network by itself - One eye, cropped to 16:9, instead of the raw double image - Quality presets (resolution, bitrate, frame rate) or manual values, H.264 or H.265 - Live reframing with the D-pad while watching - Home screen shortcut on the PS5 - English and Portuguese ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port 9021 (every current jailbreak has one). Nothing else: no websrv, no Homebrew Launcher. - A Quest 2 in developer mode with ADB over Wi-Fi turned on. This needs a USB cable and a computer once per headset reboot: ``` adb tcpip 5555 ``` - PS5 and headset on the same network. ## Install 1. Download `visor.elf` from the [releases](../../releases). 2. Send it to the PS5 like any other payload, for example: ``` socat -t 99999999 - TCP::9021 < visor.elf ``` 3. A notification says Visor is ready and a **Visor** icon shows up on the home screen. Open it from there. `visor.elf` is a single file: it unpacks itself to `/data/visor`, adds the icon and stays in the background to open the app when the icon is pressed. Like every payload it is gone after a console restart, so send it again after jailbreaking (or add it to your loader's autoload list). The icon and your settings stay. The first time you connect, put the headset on: it asks whether to allow USB debugging. Tick "Always allow". ## Controls | Screen | Button | Action | | --- | --- | --- | | Menus | D-pad / Cross / Circle | Move / select / back | | Watching | Options | Show or hide stats and hints | | Watching | D-pad | Reframe the picture | | Watching | L1 / R1 | Zoom out / in | | Watching | Circle | Stop | Reframing restarts the stream (about a second), because the crop happens on the headset. ## Limits - **No audio.** Capturing it would mute the headset for whoever is wearing it. - **Quest 2 only for now.** Other headsets have different screens, so the eye crop would be off. "Both eyes" in the settings works on anything. - The headset has to be awake (on your head) to stream. - The home screen icon is a web shortcut, so the console opens its browser window first and leaves it in front of Visor. Press Circle once to dismiss it. ## How it works Visor carries a small ADB client. It connects to the headset on port 5555, pushes the [scrcpy](https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy) server, starts it with the chosen crop and quality, and decodes the video stream with FFmpeg into an SDL2 texture. The UI is RmlUi. The app is launched as a regular PS5 application by the homebrew loader from [websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv), built into `visor.elf`. ## Building On Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL works), `sudo bash tools/setup-wsl.sh` installs the compilers and the [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo) toolchain. Then: ``` bash tools/build-ps5.sh # dist/visor.elf bash tools/send-elf.sh dist/visor.elf # send it to the console ``` The log of the last run is `/data/visor/visor.log` on the console. `curl http://:8744/` opens the app without touching the controller. ``` ``` There is also a PC build for working without the console: ``` bash tools/run-coretest.sh # ADB + stream + decode, saves a frame bash tools/uishot.sh out.bmp "down ok" # renders a screen headlessly ``` ## License GPL-3.0. Third-party parts are listed in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

repos.name: PS5-Network-Mounting
repos.readme:
# PS5 Network Mounting

Network Share FUSE Mount Daemon & Prospero Web Interface for PlayStation 5

Mount remote NFS exports and SMB2/SMB3 shares read-only to /hostapp on PS5 homebrew.

--- ## Overview **PS5 Network Mounting** is a native PS5 homebrew payload and daemon that mounts remote network shares directly into the PlayStation 5 filesystem at `/hostapp` using a user-space FUSE adapter. Once mounted, the console and homebrew loaders can browse, read, and execute applications, games, and packages directly over the local network without transferring files to the internal SSD or USB storage. The daemon includes an embedded, high-performance HTTP server serving a modern web control interface designed to match the **ProsperoMgr** user experience and dark visual identity. The interface is accessible from both the **PS5 Web Browser** (`http://127.0.0.1:18080`) and any external browser on the local area network (`http://:18080`). --- ## Key Features - **Console Integration & UX (ProsperoMgr Style):** - **Automatic WebKit Browser Launch:** On loading the ELF payload, the daemon automatically launches the PS5 modal WebKit browser pointing directly to `http://:18080`, giving immediate control on your TV screen without manual URL entry. - **On-Screen PS5 Toast Notifications:** Displays native on-screen toast notifications upon startup showing the payload version and the local network listening URL (`http://:18080`). - **Resilient Network Daemon:** Recovers gracefully if `sceNetInit` or net pools are already initialized by your payload launcher or earlier homebrew. - **Supported Protocols:** - **NFS (v3/v4):** Backed by `libnfs` and a low-latency PS5 FUSE adapter. Connects directly to TrueNAS, Synology, QNAP, or Linux exports. - **SMB2 / SMB3:** Backed by `libsmb2` and a dedicated FUSE adapter with guest and authenticated session support. - *FTP and SFTP are intentionally omitted to focus on high-throughput, kernel-mountable block/file protocols.* - **Kernel & Execution Compatibility:** - Regular files are mapped with executable permissions (`0555`), allowing native PS5 game binaries (`eboot.bin`), PRX shared libraries, and assets to execute seamlessly from `/hostapp`. - Directories are mapped with standard directory permissions (`0755`). - Automatic creation of the `/hostapp` mount target if missing. - **Embedded Web Control Panel (ProsperoMgr Theme):** - Styled to match the dark graphite/navy palette (`#0a0e16`, `#10161f`, `#161e2a`) and blue accents (`#2f8cff`) of ProsperoMgr. - Live mount health indicators with pulsing status pill (`.pmgr-live-dot`). - Fully embedded in the binary via `tools/embed_ui.py` — zero external runtime asset dependencies. - **Hardened HTTP Daemon & API:** - **Network-wide accessibility:** Binds to `0.0.0.0:18080` by default so any PC, phone, or tablet on your LAN can manage mounts. - **Concurrency:** Thread-pool dispatch supporting up to 32 concurrent requests with socket timeouts to prevent stalls. - **Standard JSON Parser:** Built-in RFC 8259 parser (`native/json.hpp`) replacing naive substring search, with validation against malformed payloads and key collisions. - **CSRF & Origin Protection:** Strict checks against cross-origin attacks with required `X-Requested-With: PS5NM` request validation. --- ## Architecture & Layout ``` ├── .github/workflows/ │ ├── ps5-full-nfs-smb-build.yml # Full PS5 target ELF cross-compilation CI │ └── source-checks.yml # Host build, JSON unit tests, smoke tests, FUSE syntax checks ├── docs/ │ ├── API.md # HTTP REST API specification │ ├── BUILD.md # Compilation guide & SDK requirements │ ├── IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md # Protocol & platform implementation details │ ├── NFS_TEST_PLAN.md # Test matrix for NFS exports │ └── THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md # Open-source licenses (libnfs, libsmb2, FUSE) ├── native/ │ ├── json.hpp # Zero-dependency, standards-compliant JSON parser │ ├── main.cpp # HTTP server, REST routing, socket worker threads │ ├── mount_backend.hpp / .cpp # Core mount orchestration & status state machine │ ├── nfs_fuse.hpp / .cpp # NFS FUSE adapter (libnfs) │ ├── smb_fuse.hpp / .cpp # SMB FUSE adapter (libsmb2) │ └── web_assets.hpp # Deterministically generated C++ header of the embedded UI ├── tests/ │ ├── http_smoke.py # Automated HTTP/REST and security test suite │ ├── net_stubs.cpp # Host networking stubs for Linux development │ └── test_json.cpp # JSON parser unit test suite ├── tools/ │ └── embed_ui.py # Compresses and embeds web/index.html into C++ header └── web/ └── index.html # Single-page web UI with ProsperoMgr styling ``` --- ## Quick Start & Usage ### 1. Launching the Payload on PS5 1. Send or run the compiled `ps5nm.elf` using your preferred PS5 payload sender (e.g. Netcat on port `9021` or payload loader). 2. The payload initializes networking (`sceNetInit`), starts the FUSE subsystem, and begins listening on `0.0.0.0:18080`. ### 2. Accessing the Control Panel - **From PS5 Browser:** Navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:18080` - **From PC / Phone / Mac:** Navigate to `http://:18080` ### 3. Mounting Shares - **NFS Share:** - **Server:** `192.168.1.50` - **Port:** `2049` (default) - **Export Path:** `/mnt/dataPool/games` (absolute path as exported on the NAS) - *Tip: Ensure the NFS export allows read permissions and `no_root_squash` or all-squash to a user with read access.* - **SMB Share:** - **Server:** `192.168.1.50` - **Port:** `445` (default) - **Share Name:** `games` or `games/PS5` (do not prefix with slashes) - **Username / Password:** Provide if your SMB server requires authentication, or leave blank for guest access. --- ## REST API Reference The web control panel communicates via JSON endpoints under `/api/v1`: | Endpoint | Method | Description | |---|---|---| | `/api/v1/status` | `GET` | Returns live mount status, active protocol, endpoint, and last error. | | `/api/v1/mount` | `POST` | Validates parameters and mounts the requested NFS or SMB share to `/hostapp`. | | `/api/v1/unmount` | `POST` | Safely detaches the active FUSE filesystem from `/hostapp`. | All `POST` requests require `Content-Type: application/json` and `X-Requested-With: PS5NM`. Detailed request/response schemas can be found in [`docs/API.md`](docs/API.md). --- ## Building ### Building on Host (Linux/macOS for Development & Testing) ```bash # Compile and run JSON unit tests g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Inative tests/test_json.cpp -o /tmp/test_json /tmp/test_json # Compile host binary with network stubs g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Inative \ native/main.cpp native/mount_backend.cpp tests/net_stubs.cpp \ -pthread -o /tmp/ps5nm-host # Run automated HTTP test suite python3 tests/http_smoke.py ``` ### Building the PS5 ELF (Target Build) Target compilation requires the OpenOrbis / Prospero toolchain with ORBISDEV libraries (`libfuse`, `libnfs`, `libsmb2`, `mbedtls`, `zlib`). ```bash export OO_PS4_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/openorbis export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk make PS5NM_WITH_FUSE=1 ``` The automated GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ps5-full-nfs-smb-build.yml`) builds the full production ELF release automatically on push. --- ## Acknowledgments & Credits - **[ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/Sweeney-development/ProsperoMgr):** UI design reference, color palette, and styling system. - **[Itemzflow](https://github.com/LightningMods/Itemzflow):** Reference implementation for PS5 FUSE / NFS integration (`fuse-nfs`). - **[ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/Sweeney-development/ps5-ezremote-client):** SMB client and `libsmb2` reference patterns. - **[libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs):** Client library for NFS. - **[libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2):** Client library for SMB2/SMB3.

latestRelease.body:
## PS5 Network Mounting v1.1.1

### Fixes & Diagnostics in v1.1.1
- **Resilient Startup & Port Retries**: Added 10-attempt socket bind/listen retry loop with detailed klog diagnostics. Detects if port 18080 is already active from a previous execution, triggers WebKit/toast refresh, and exits cleanly.
- **WebKit & Toast Startup Worker**: Decoupled WebKit browser launch and toast notifications into an asynchronous background worker with a 300ms settling pause and multi-attempt retry logic.
- **UserService Initialization**: Explicitly initializes `sceUserService` prior to `sceSystemServiceLaunchWebBrowser`.
- **Dual Toast Delivery**: Supports both plain `sceKernelSendNotificationRequest` and rich `sceNotificationSend` notifications.
- **Kernel Syslog Diagnostics**: Emits `<118>[PS5NM]` diagnostic logs directly to PS5 klog via `sendsyslog`.

### Highlights & Core Capabilities
- **Auto-open WebKit Browser**: On payload launch, automatically opens the PS5 WebKit browser modal pointing directly to the web UI at `http://<PS5-IP>:18080`.
- **On-Screen PS5 Toast Notification**: Displays a ProsperoMgr-style on-screen notification showing the payload version and listening network address and port.
- **Background Daemon**: Resilient network initialization that keeps running smoothly even if `sceNetInit` was already initialized by the payload loader.
- **Full NFS & SMB FUSE Mount**: Support for NFS (v3/v4) and SMB (SMB2/SMB3) network shares mounted to `/hostapp` or designated mount paths.
- **ProsperoMgr-inspired Dark Theme UI**: Full remote control from PS5 browser or PC/phone on the LAN.

### Included Artifacts
- `PS5NetworkMounting.elf`: Full standalone PS5 homebrew payload with NFS and SMB FUSE adapters included.

repos.readme:
# PlayStation Save Decrypters

A collection of custom save-game decrypters and checksum fixers for PS3, PSP, and PS4.

## In your browser

Many of these tools also run as a web page, with no download and no upload:

**https://bucanero.github.io/save-decrypters/**

Pick a game, drop the save in, get it back decrypted — and the same page puts
the edited one back together, checksums included. It is the
[Apollo engine](https://github.com/bucanero/apollo-lib) compiled to WebAssembly
(see [apollo-patcher](https://github.com/bucanero/apollo-patcher)) driving the
`.savepatch` files from
[apollo-patches](https://github.com/bucanero/apollo-patches), so there is one
implementation of each format rather than two.

Every game listed there has been checked against the samples in this
repository: CI applies the patch to a real encrypted save and compares the
result byte-for-byte with the plaintext the C tool below produces. A tool that
stops matching does not get published — see
[`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](.github/workflows/pages.yml). The site
therefore covers fewer games than this repository does; the rest are being
worked through, and the CLI tools here remain the complete set.

The MC4 and ShnExt cheat file tools have their own pages, built from each
tool's `web/` folder (shared code in [`common/web`](common/web)):
[MC4](https://bucanero.github.io/save-decrypters/mc4-cheat-decrypter/web/) and
[ShnExt](https://bucanero.github.io/save-decrypters/shnext-cheat-decrypter/web/).
