repos.name: ps5-dump-forge
repos.description: A toolkit for working with PS5 game dumps. Cross-platform - including the PS5 itself.
repos.readme: Runs on everything (including your PS5) and converts everything: **folder**, **exfat**, **ffpfs**, **ffpfsc**, **pkg**. Can utilize LZ4 compression and unpack archives (**zip**/**7zip**/**rar**). The interface is in **11 languages**. | Platform | Runs on | You get | |---|---|---| | **PS5** | With an ELF loader | The payload (`.elf`); the UI opens in any browser | | **macOS** | 11 or later, Apple Silicon and Intel (one universal zip) | App + CLI | | **Windows** | 10 or 11 on x86-64, 11 on arm64 | App + CLI | | **Linux** | x86-64 or arm64, glibc 2.35+ (e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+) | App (no install, no FUSE) + CLI | ## Features - **Any source to any target**, streamed straight through: no temporary copy, not even the image inside a `.ffpfsc` or a game in an archive. - **Archives as sources**: a `.zip`, `.7z` or `.rar` holding one game is inspected, converted or packed like a folder. - **LZ4 compression**, new experimental way to pack ampr_emu enabled games. - **Library**, to convert and edit dumps. - **Never touches your dump** unless you ask (LZ4 Patch/Unpatch, Inspect's Delete): junk (`.DS_Store`, `._*`, ...) is skipped, not deleted; bad file names are reported up front, never renamed. - **Inspect** a dump or image: cover, title, required firmware, backport firmware (`fakelib/`), embedded DLC, `param.json`, leftover `.part` files. - **Runs on the PS5 itself**: converts on the console's own storage, driven from its browser or any browser on the network. - **Writes onto USB sticks and SD cards** formatted exFAT or FAT32. - **Fast**: (and furious). ## Formats Images are mounted by [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus); the debug FPKG is installed. Every format can be created and read back (an image or `.fpkg` can be extracted to a folder). | Format | Console speed | Size on disk | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `.fpkg` (debug FPKG, saved as `.pkg`) | Native, full speed | 30–60% less, depending on the game | Installs on firmware 11.60 or lower with kstuff + fpkg-enable + ppr-patch. Kraken level (`--kraken`): **Fast** (default), **Balanced** / **Smallest** ≈ 2.6% smaller at ~6× / ~9× the compression time, **Stored** uncompressed (for a console that installs a compressed package but won't start it). Reads packages from this builder and compatible debug builders. | | `.ffpkg` (UFS2) | Full image speed | Equal to the game size | ShadowMountPlus's recommendation. | | `.exfat` (512 B sectors, 64 KiB clusters) | Full image speed | Equal to the game size | For games that only run like external-drive content. | | `.ffpfs` (PFS, uncompressed) | Full image speed | Equal to the game size | Experimental in ShadowMountPlus. ASCII file names only. | | `.ffpfsc` (compressed PFS container) | may stutter | Depends on the compression level, usually 30–60% less | Experimental, always mounted read-only. exFAT (default), UFS2 or PFS inside. zlib level 0–9 (`--level`), default 6. | | Folder | Full drive speed | Equal to the game size | Run as it is by ShadowMountPlus. | ## LZ4 asset packs Experimental, and only for games whose `eboot.bin` imports `libSceAmpr` (AMPR titles). Forge LZ4-compresses a game's assets into `ampr_assets-NNN.pak` volumes that the [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) runtime, installed under `fakelib/`, reads back on the console; the result is a plain game folder, or an image holding one. Everything is in the app's **LZ4** tab: 1. **Trace**: make a plain `.ffpkg`, patch it (**LZ4** → **Trace** → **Patch**), mount it writable (`image_rw=`) with ShadowMountPlus and play one long session. 2. **Download traces**: close the game, wait about a minute, open the console's Forge in a computer's browser and choose **Download traces** on that image (one zip). 3. **Pack** the original dump on the computer: **LZ4** → **Pack/Unpack**, pick the zip under **Traces** and a target (LZ4 packed folder, `.ffpkg`, `.exfat` or `.ffpfs`). Without traces or a profile, Pack falls back to a built-in guess of which files to pack, which is less reliable. ampr_emu 0.4.2.1 is an upstream test build: some games crash when saving. Details, CLI options and caveats: [docs/LZ4.md](docs/LZ4.md). ## Download and run Every release archive on the Releases page holds the app and the `ps5-dump-forge` command-line tool. Nothing to install; the app writes nothing beyond its own WebView data, so keep it in any folder you can write to. ### PS5 (jailbroken, with an ELF loader) - **Load it** with any ELF loader: send `ps5-dump-forge--ps5.elf` to elfldr's port 9021 (`nc -w 3 9021 < ps5-dump-forge--ps5.elf`), or list it in an autoloader's `autoload.txt`. A notification says Dump Forge is launched; open it from its icon. - **Open the UI** from the Dump Forge icon, or in any browser on the same network: `http://:8095`. ### macOS (11 or later) Get `ps5-dump-forge--macos-universal.zip` (Apple Silicon and Intel) and unzip it anywhere. The app is ad-hoc signed only (no Apple Developer ID, not notarized), so macOS blocks the first launch ("PS5 Dump Forge is damaged" or "cannot be opened"). Use **one** of these: 1. **Terminal** (every macOS version), in the folder that holds the app, then double-click it: ```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "PS5 Dump Forge.app" ``` 2. **System Settings.** Double-click the app once and dismiss the warning, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message about PS5 Dump Forge and click **Open Anyway**. ### Windows (10 or 11 on x86-64, 11 on arm64) - x86-64: `ps5-dump-forge--windows-x86-64.zip` uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 11 and most Windows 10 PCs already have. Without it, get `...-windows-x86-64-webview2.zip`: larger, with its own copy of the runtime in a `WebView2` folder. - arm64: `ps5-dump-forge--windows-arm64.zip` (uses the WebView2 Runtime Windows 11 ships). Extract it to a folder you can write to (not Program Files, not a network share): `PS5 Dump Forge.exe` keeps its WebView data in a `data/webview` folder beside itself. The app is unsigned, so SmartScreen may block the first launch: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If WebView2 is missing or broken, the app says what to do instead of showing a blank window. ### Linux (x86-64 or arm64, glibc 2.35 or later, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) Extract `ps5-dump-forge--linux-x86-64.tar.gz` or `...-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (`tar -xzf`) to a folder you can write to and run `./forge.sh`. No FUSE, no install; keep `PS5 Dump Forge.AppDir` next to `forge.sh` (its WebView data goes in a `data/webview` folder beside it). ### Command-line tool Every desktop archive also has `ps5-dump-forge` (`ps5-dump-forge.exe` on Windows): ```sh ./ps5-dump-forge inspect PPSA01234.exfat ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpkg # folder | exfat | ffpkg | ffpfs | ffpfsc | pkg (debug FPKG) ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpfsc --inner exfat # inner: exfat (default) | ffpkg | ffpfs ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpfsc --level 6 # zlib level 0 (store) .. 9 (smallest), default 6 ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to pkg --kraken fast # fast (default) | balanced | smallest | stored ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to exfat --full-verify # check every byte, not a sample ./ps5-dump-forge convert Game.part1.rar --to ffpkg --password-stdin # archive source; password from stdin ``` ## Build Rust (latest stable) and Node.js: ```sh cargo test --workspace --release cd app && npm ci && npm run tauri dev ``` On Linux the app also needs Tauri's WebKitGTK build dependencies (Debian/Ubuntu package names, as CI installs them): ```sh sudo apt-get install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev librsvg2-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev patchelf file ``` The PS5 payload builds in Docker (any macOS or Linux host with Docker and Node) with `ps5/build.sh`; the rest of its commands are in [ps5/README.md](ps5/README.md). See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the layout and the format rules, and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) for the UI design system. ## Thanks Big thanks to **[PhantomPtr](https://github.com/phantomptr)** for **[ps5upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload)**. Its Rust engine is the reference implementation this project learned the PS5 formats from: the FPKG package builder and reader (PFS, PFSC, Kraken, CNT/FIH, PlayGo, debug license), and the exFAT and UFS2 readers. Its crates are vendored here (`vendor/`, v7.0.22). Big thanks to **[drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor)**, author of **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, for the mount side this tool writes for and for help along the way: the image-building scripts (`mkexfat_macos.sh` and friends) whose sizing and layout rules the `.exfat`/`.ffpkg` writers follow, the format guidance in SMP's README and release notes, and ppr-patch, which makes debug `.pkg` installs possible. Thanks again to **[drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor)** for **[ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu)** (GPL-3.0-or-later), the runtime that makes LZ4 asset packs work: its 0.4.2.1 release and trace runtimes are embedded unmodified, with their source archive in `vendor/ampr_emu/`. **[Lazy_AMPR](https://github.com/Nazky/Lazy_AMPR)** by Nazky was the reference for the trace-then-pack workflow (no code taken). The bundled LZ4 (BSD-2-Clause) and HDE64 notices are in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. Credits for other references are in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See `LICENSE`.

latestRelease.name: PS5 Dump Forge v0.1.1
latestRelease.body:
Runs on everything (including your PS5) and converts everything: game folders to `exfat`, `ffpkg`, `ffpfs`,
`ffpfsc`, `zip`, `7z`, `rar` and debug `FPKG` packages, and back again, with experimental `LZ4` asset packs for AMPR games.

| Platform | Download | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PS5** | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-ps5.elf` | Send it to elfldr's port 9021, then open the **Dump Forge** icon or `http://<ps5-ip>:8095` in any browser |
| **macOS** 11+ (Apple Silicon and Intel) | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-macos-universal.zip` | Ad-hoc signed: allow it once on first launch (see README) |
| **Windows** 10/11 x86-64 | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-windows-x86-64.zip` | Uses the system WebView2 |
| **Windows** 10/11 x86-64, offline | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-windows-x86-64-webview2.zip` | Brings its own WebView2 |
| **Windows** 11 arm64 | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-windows-arm64.zip` | Uses the system WebView2 |
| **Linux** x86-64, glibc 2.35+ | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-linux-x86-64.tar.gz` | Extract, then run `./forge.sh` |
| **Linux** arm64, glibc 2.35+ | `ps5-dump-forge-0.1.1-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | Extract, then run `./forge.sh` |

## What's new

- **Clearer job progress**: each job lists its steps (done, current, upcoming), shows the time in the current
  step, and shows speed and time left only where bytes are actually streaming.
- **UI fixes**, many from an audit of the PS5 web UI.
- **New fpkg level: Stored** (`--kraken stored`): an uncompressed package, for a console that installs a
  compressed package but won't start it.

- **Faster**:
  - `.7z` sources decode on several threads: a solid archive went from 143 s to 22 s, a non-solid one from 156 s
    to 42 s.
  - Big `.rar` sources with thousands of files no longer stall before the copy starts (a 7,169-file archive's
    check went from 10+ minutes to 33 s), and folder output reads the next file ahead (57 s → 47 s).
  - Verification overlaps hashing with reading: `.exfat` and `.ffpfs` checks and LZ4 pack/unpack take about
    half the time.

repos.description: PKG Viewer by Loopayeh: view PS3/PS4/PS5 package info and cover art
repos.readme: # PKG Viewer — PS2 / PS3 / PS4 / PS5 / Switch / Wii U / Xbox 360 ![screenshot](screenshot.png) ![trophies](screenshot-trophies.png) **PKG Viewer** shows what's inside a PlayStation or Switch game file without extracting it: cover art, title, Title ID, region, version, and required firmware. Retail (original) PKGs fully supported — including split multi-part sets. Works with `.pkg` packages, PS2/PS3 `.iso` disc images, `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` images, Switch `.nsp` / `.xci` files, Xbox 360 (GOD/STFS/ISO/XEX), Wii U NUS folders, and game folders. ## Download Get `PKGViewer-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` (Windows) or `PKGViewer-macOS-arm64-X.Y.Z.zip` (Apple Silicon) / `PKGViewer-macOS-x86_64-X.Y.Z.zip` (Intel) from [Releases](../../releases) — no Python needed, no admin needed. ## Why the installer ![file icons](screenshot-icons.png) Grab `PKGViewer-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) — no admin needed: - every format gets its own icon (`.pkg` / `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` / `.nsp` / `.xci`) and opens on double-click — no Open With setup - shows up in `Settings → Default apps`, so all six formats go Always in one place - updates itself in place, no reinstall hassle - uninstall wipes everything clean (files, icons, registry) ## Features - Cover art preview (icon0.png, pic0.png, …) with Save / Copy to clipboard — online covers (PlayStation Store, ps2-covers, GameTDB, XboxUnity, Nintendo IDBE), cached offline - Spec card: Title ID, Content ID, version, region, Min. System, SDK, DRM - Latest patch version per game (PS5/PS4) with PKG-vs-latest compare - Files tab: named entries with id + size — single-file Extract with rename, trophy00.trp contents - Trophies tab: decrypted trophy list (name, grade, hidden) with icons, banner art, Save icons export - OFC (Official) / FPKG (Fake) detection + badges for PS4 and PS5 (incl. split parts) - Details tab: curated param.sfo / param.json, Show all for the full dump - Drag & drop: PKG files, exFAT / ffpfsc / ffpkg images, Switch NSP / XCI files, and game folders onto the window - Rename: clean uniform names from PKG info (`Title - TID - vVersion - Region`, e.g. `Elden Ring - PPSA04863 - v1.06 - EU`) — single file via the Rename button (preview + header Undo), or many at once via the Batch button / dropping them all (batch dialog with preview + All/None + revert log); folders are scanned for game files; split multi-part sets stay together; Revert restores original names from any revert log - AMPR / LZ4 asset containers (LIZARD dumps): listed with size in the spec card + Files tab - Copy/paste works in every text field, on any keyboard layout - Self-updating: silent check at startup, header button lights up on new release - CLI mode: `pkgviewer.py --info file.pkg` (also `.nsp` / `.xci`) — batch: `pkgviewer.py --batch-rename folder [--recursive] [--apply]` (dry run without `--apply`) — revert: `pkgviewer.py --revert batch_rename_*.log [--apply]` ## Usage Drag & drop a `.pkg` / `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` / `.nsp` / `.xci` file or a game folder onto the exe or the open window, or use Open. To run from source (needs Python 3 + Pillow + tkinterdnd2 + mkpfs + pytsk3 + cryptography): ```bat PKGViewer.bat ``` ## Supported formats - **PS2 disc images** (`.iso`) — SYSTEM.CNF serial/version/VMODE, file listing - **PS3 packages** (`.pkg`) — retail + debug NPDRM, decrypted listing - **PS3 game folders** — NPDRM and PS3_GAME layouts - **PS4 / PS5 packages** (`.pkg`) — game, DLC, update, retail + split parts - **PS5 disk images** (`.exfat`) — game dumps - **PS5 compressed images** (`.ffpfsc`) — game dumps - **PS5 UFS2 images** (`.ffpkg`) — game dumps (needs pytsk3 from source) - **PS5 app folders** — extracted game folder (incl. LIZARD AMPR/LZ4 dumps) - **Switch packages** (`.nsp`) — game, update, DLC; official title + icon from Control NCA with `prod.keys` (put it next to the exe or in `%APPDATA%\PKGViewer\`), raw file listing without keys; per-NCA type/key info, readable firmware requirement - **Switch gamecard images** (`.xci`) — partition + file listing, cartridge info, title/icon from the secure partition - **Wii U NUS folders** — TMD title/version/contents, official Nintendo icons - **Xbox 360 GOD folders + STFS packages** — title/Media/Title ID, data parts, embedded thumbnail, online XboxUnity covers - **Xbox 360 ISO / extracted folders / XEX** — XDVDFS listing, version/disc from XEX, TU check ## Build from source ```bat pip install pyinstaller pillow python -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean --onefile --windowed --name PKGViewer --icon assets\logo.ico --add-data "assets;assets" --add-data "assets_about.png;." --collect-submodules PIL pkgviewer.py ``` ## Support [☕ برام یه قهوه بخر — coffeebede.com/loopayeh](https://coffeebede.com/loopayeh) *(🇮🇷 برای ایران — حمایت تومانی)* If this tool was useful, you can also support me internationally with USDT (BEP-20 / BNB Smart Chain): `0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50` [Pay via Trust Wallet](https://link.trustwallet.com/send?coin=20000714&address=0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50&token_id=0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955) ## Credits - PS4 extract/build engine: `LibOrbisPkg` by maxton (via PkgEditor). Optional `orbis-pub-gen`/`orbis-pub-chk` (Sony/OpenOrbis SDK tools, user-supplied). - PS5 files are view-only (no extract/build, no outside tools). - `.ffpfsc` / inner-exFAT reading via `mkpfs` library by PSBrew (RenanGBarreto + contributors incl. rdmrocha, drakmor). - `.ffpkg` (UFS) reading via `pytsk3` (Sleuth Kit bindings). - Switch NCA/NACP parsing follows `hactool` (SciresM) layout; decrypt needs user-supplied `prod.keys` (dump it yourself with Lockpick_RCM) — no keys bundled. - Patch-version lookup: prosperopatches.com / orbispatches.com. - PKG Viewer itself (parsing, UI, rename, trophies, Switch support) is original code — no vendored third-party code bundled. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Contact Telegram: [@loopayeh](https://t.me/loopayeh)

repos.name: ps5-library-browser
repos.description: Native PS5 Game Library Browser & Launcher with NFS support, ShadowMountPlus daemon lock, and Itemzflow-inspired UI
repos.readme:
# PS5 Library Browser

A high-performance, native PS5 library manager and game browser inspired by **Itemzflow**, engineered in modern **C++20**.

`ps5-library-browser` provides an intuitive interface for managing local and network-mounted game libraries, inspecting title packages (Base Games, Add-on DLCs, Title Updates), and managing multi-item installation queues with full **ShadowMountPlus** integration.

---

## 🌟 Key Features

### 1. Game, DLC & Update Package Inspector
- **Header & Outside Info**: Displays game title, Title ID (`PPSA` / `CUSA`), cover art, base game size, primary format (`PKG`, `exFAT`, `FFPKG`), and total package footprint.
- **Three Dedicated Section Tabs**: Quick navigation between **Game**, **DLC**, and **Update** package sections.
- **Formatted & Highlighted Package Details**: Displays filename, human-readable size, highlighted file format badges (`[.PKG]`, `[.EXFAT]`, `[.FFPKG]`), version numbers, and live installation status.
- **Per-Item Install Actions**: Install individual base games, specific DLC packages, or individual title updates directly.
- **DLC "Install All" Pipeline**: One-touch batch installation of all DLC add-ons with cumulative progress, item-level status tracking, cancellation, and granular failure reporting.

### 2. Dual-Mode Library Architecture
- **Installed Games Mode**: Instant local launcher for installed applications on the PS5.
- **Library Browser Mode**: Browses local storage (`/hostapp`), custom directories, and remote NFS mounts.
- **ShadowMountPlus Feature Lock**: Browsing remote libraries is gated behind a live health check to the local **ShadowMountPlus** daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`). If the daemon is absent, the user is presented with a clear lock dialog explaining that ShadowMount Plus is required.

### 3. Native Dual-View Carousel & Block Grid
- **Coverflow Carousel**: 3D-styled cover art carousel with real-time scaling, depth ordering, and smooth scrolling.
- **5-Column Block Grid**: High-density library grid view optimized for large game collections.
- **Format Filters & Live Search**: Filter entries instantly by format (`PKG`, `exFAT`, `FFPKG`, `Folder`) or search by title and Title ID.

### 4. DualSense Input & Prompts
- Native mapping for DualSense D-Pad and analog stick navigation with deadzone and auto-repeat support.
- Dynamic contextual button prompt bar (`△ Toggle Mode / Install All DLCs`, `Touchpad View`, `L1/R1 Filter / Tabs`, `□ Inspect`, `✕ Select / Install`, `○ Back`).
- Modal dialogs for connection recovery and lock explanations.

### 5. High-Speed Scanner & Persistent Cached Indexing
- Scans `/hostapp`, local folders, and network mounts.
- Decodes `sce_sys/param.json` categories (`gd` base game, `gp` patch, `ac` DLC) and title ID tags (`PPSA` / `CUSA`).
- Atomic JSON cache engine ensures zero-latency library startup.

---

## 📂 Architecture

```
ps5-library-browser/
├── .github/workflows/ci.yml         # Automated host build & unit test CI workflow
├── CMakeLists.txt                   # Cross-platform CMake configuration
├── include/ps5_library/
│   ├── daemon_client.hpp            # ShadowMountPlus daemon probe & feature gate
│   ├── game_metadata.hpp            # Metadata parser, categories, and models
│   ├── scanner.hpp                  # Recursive multi-source scanner
│   ├── index_cache.hpp              # Atomic persistent cache & query filters
│   ├── input.hpp                    # DualSense pad mapping & prompt model
│   ├── views.hpp                    # Coverflow & Block Grid layout calculations
│   ├── installer.hpp                # Install pipeline, delegates & batch engine
│   ├── inspector.hpp                # Package inspector state, formatting & tabs
│   └── ui_shell.hpp                 # Native UI shell, state machine & dialogs
├── src/
│   ├── daemon_client.cpp            # Socket client & lock manager
│   ├── game_metadata.cpp            # Param parser & Title ID heuristics
│   ├── scanner.cpp                  # Directory scanner & grouping
│   ├── index_cache.cpp              # Atomic cache implementation
│   ├── input.cpp                    # Input processing & repeat timer
│   ├── views.cpp                    # Coverflow & Grid card positioning
│   ├── installer.cpp                # Install task queue & DLC batch execution
│   ├── inspector.cpp                # Package formatting & inspector navigation
│   └── ui_shell.cpp                 # UI shell flow & input routing
├── tests/
│   ├── daemon_client_test.cpp       # Milestone 1 tests
│   ├── scanner_cache_test.cpp       # Milestone 2 tests
│   ├── ui_shell_test.cpp            # Milestone 3 tests
│   ├── inspector_installer_test.cpp # Milestone 4 tests
│   ├── ps5_installer_persistence_test.cpp # PS5 install delegate, persistence & recovery tests
│   └── install_retry_preflight_history_test.cpp # Retry, preflight & searchable history tests
└── README.md
```

---

## 🛠️ Building & Testing

### Prerequisites
- Modern C++20 compiler (`gcc` 10+, `clang` 11+, or MSVC 2019+)
- CMake 3.16+
- POSIX-compatible host or PS5 homebrew SDK environment

### Build Commands
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library-browser.git
cd ps5-library-browser

# Configure and compile
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

# Execute test suite
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

---

## 🛣️ Development Roadmap

- [x] **Milestone 1: Daemon Health Probe & Feature Lock Engine**
  - Socket HTTP client with non-blocking polling and timeout controls
  - Feature gating with mandatory prompt: *"ShadowMount Plus is required to unlock these features"*
  - Automated mock daemon test suite
- [x] **Milestone 2: High-Speed Game Scanner, Metadata Classifier & Atomic Index Cache**
  - Fast traversal of `/hostapp` and mounted paths
  - `sce_sys/param.json` parser classifying Base Games (`gd`), Updates (`gp`), and DLCs (`ac`)
  - Title ID validation (`PPSA`, `CUSA`, `LAPY`, `FAKE`)
  - Atomic JSON v2 cache with PID/timestamp temporary file write and atomic rename
- [x] **Milestone 3: Native Dual-Mode UI Engine & DualSense Navigation**
  - Mode toggle: Installed Games vs Library Browser
  - Gated remote browser requiring ShadowMountPlus daemon
  - Selectable views: Coverflow carousel and 5-column Block Grid
  - Format filters (PKG, exFAT, FFPKG, Folder) and live search
  - Contextual DualSense button prompt bar and input repeat handling
- [x] **Milestone 4: Game/DLC/Update Package Inspector & Multi-Installer**
  - Package Inspector with Game, DLC, and Update section tabs
  - Formatted package metadata with highlighted file extensions (`[.PKG]`, `[.EXFAT]`, `[.FFPKG]`) and human-readable sizes
  - Per-item install triggers for games, DLCs, and updates
  - "Install All DLCs" pipeline with progress callbacks, cancellation, and granular failure recovery
  - **PS5 Package Install Delegate & Capability Model**: Safe runtime probe checking kernel privileges and system service availability (`libSceAppInstUtil`); returns descriptive `UnsupportedPlatform` diagnostics and guidance on non-PS5 hosts
  - **Persistent Install Jobs Across Restarts**: Atomic JSON state tracking (`/tmp/ps5_library_install_jobs.json`) persisting queued/completed jobs; automatically restores `InProgress` tasks as `Interrupted` on restart
  - **Post-Install Library & Inspector Refresh**: Real-time promotion of item confidence and inspector state upon package installation completion
  - **Actionable Recovery Guidance**: Granular troubleshooting steps for every error code (unsupported platform, missing privileges, missing system services, out of storage, corrupted header, interrupted install)
  - **Install Preflight Validation**: Multi-stage verification inspecting file existence, readability, storage capacity against package size (with configurable safety margin), and header signature format (`.pkg` magic `\x7FPKG`/`PKG\0`, `.ffpkg`/`.exfat` header sizes); prevents corrupt package dispatches before calling target install delegates.
  - **Duplicate Prevention & Retry Workflow**: Preflight duplicate detection prevents queueing conflicting installs for already active/queued jobs, while dedicated retry actions preserve original task IDs, prior error codes/messages, retry counters, and timestamps.
  - **Searchable Install History & Diagnostics**: Full job diagnostic history recording submission/completion timestamps, package identifiers, failure reasons, retry provenance, and step-by-step remediation guidance; accessible via the UI Shell history dialog.
  - **CSV & JSON Install History Export**: Export complete diagnostic logs with timestamps, Title IDs, filenames, format, size/byte counts, outcomes, error details, recovery steps, and retry ancestry (`original_task_id`, `original_error_code`, `retry_count`) directly to file or string buffers.
  - **Granular History Filtering & Multi-Key Sorting**: Multi-criteria filtering by install outcome (`Completed`, `Failed`, `Interrupted`, `Cancelled`, `Queued`, `InProgress`), package format (`pkg`, `exfat`, `ffpkg`, `folder`), and ISO 8601 date ranges; sortable ascending or descending by timestamp or package filename.
  - **Retry Confirmation Modal with Live Preflight Verification**: Interactive UI modal surfacing prior failure diagnostics and re-executing live preflight checks to ensure errors are resolved before requeueing.
  - **Per-Check Preflight Summary**: Clear per-check diagnostic breakdown across File Readability, Package Metadata/Header, and Available Storage with safety margins before dispatching to the installer.
  - **Immediate Preflight Re-Check & Changed Results Diffing**: Automatically verifies package readability, format/metadata signatures, and storage capacity immediately before dispatch, detecting and reporting deviations from initial summary snapshots.
  - **Export File Picker & Configurable Filenames**: Interactive modal for selecting destination directories and filenames for CSV/JSON diagnostic logs with real-time feedback and remediation on failure.
  - **Cross-Session Filter & Sort Persistence**: Atomically preserves install history filter options (outcome, format, date ranges, query) and sort preferences across application restarts.
- [x] **Milestone 5: PS5 Payload Packaging & Cross-Compilation Workflow**
  - Dedicated CMake PS5 target (`ps5_library_browser_elf`) producing `ps5-library-browser.elf`
  - Target entrypoint (`src/main.cpp`) with DualSense event loop, headless verification, `/hostapp` default scanning, and daemon health probe
  - Homebrew metadata package manifest (`sce_sys/param.json`)
  - Automated PS5 cross-compilation CI workflow with `pacbrew-repo` and `ps5-payload-sdk` toolchain packaging
  - **Structured Startup Diagnostics**: Comprehensive boot-time health checks covering root scan mount availability, ShadowMountPlus daemon connectivity, network subsystem initialization, and persistence storage writeability.
  - **On-Screen Recovery Guidance**: Active diagnostic issues automatically trigger an interactive UI dialog with step-by-step remediation procedures and live diagnostics re-run capabilities.
  - **Automated Package & ELF Architecture CI Validation**: Dedicated release validator (`tools/validate_release_package.py`) enforcing archive integrity, required metadata (`sce_sys/param.json`), and 64-bit Little-Endian x86_64 ELF execution attributes.
  - **Tag-Triggered GitHub Release Publishing**: Automated release pipeline generating versioned GitHub Releases with verified release archives when a `v*` tag is pushed.

---

## 🚀 Installation & Setup on PS5

### Prerequisites
1. **PlayStation 5 Console**: Running compatible homebrew firmware (e.g. 3.xx–4.xx) with an active ELF loader or payload environment.
2. **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus)**: Installed and running in the background. PS5 Library Browser requires the ShadowMountPlus local daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`) to unlock remote NFS browsing and virtual mounting features.
3. **Network Connection**: PS5 connected to your local network with access to your NFS storage server (e.g., TrueNAS).

---

### Installation Methods

#### Method 1: Payload Injection via Netcat / ELF Loader
1. Download the latest release package (`ps5-library-browser_v*.zip`) from the [Releases](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library-browser/releases) page and extract it.
2. Launch the ELF loader on your PS5 (listening on port `9020` or `9021`).
3. Send `ps5-library-browser.elf` from your computer using `nc` (netcat) or any PS5 payload sender tool:
   ```bash
   # Linux / macOS
   nc -w 3 <PS5_IP_ADDRESS> 9020 < ps5-library-browser.elf

   # Windows (PowerShell with ncat or GUI payload sender)
   ncat -w 3 <PS5_IP_ADDRESS> 9020 < ps5-library-browser.elf
   ```

#### Method 2: Homebrew Directory Installation (FTP / Itemzflow)
1. Extract the release ZIP package containing `ps5-library-browser.elf` and the `sce_sys/` folder.
2. Connect to your PS5 via FTP (e.g., FTPS5 or Itemzflow built-in FTP server).
3. Transfer the extracted files to `/data/homebrew/ps5-library-browser/` or `/hostapp/`.
4. Launch the application from your PS5 homebrew menu (e.g., [Itemzflow](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/Itemzflow) or [ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ProsperoMgr)).

---

### Startup & Controls Guide

On startup, the built-in **Diagnostics Engine** verifies the scan mount, network stack, cache files, and the ShadowMountPlus daemon. If ShadowMountPlus is offline, an on-screen recovery guidance dialog will appear explaining how to launch the daemon to unlock remote features.

| Button | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Square** | Switch Mode: **Installed Games** ⇄ **Library Browser** |
| **Triangle** | Toggle View: **Coverflow Carousel** ⇄ **5-Column Block Grid** |
| **D-Pad / Left Stick** | Navigate Game Cards & Packages |
| **Cross** | Open Game / DLC / Update Inspector & Execute Install |
| **Circle** | Back / Close Dialog / Dismiss Guidance |
| **Options** | Open Filter & Sort History Modal |

---

- **[ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/victor-s-santos/ps5-homebrew-ui)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-homebrew-ui)) — by victor-s-santos. Modern native C++20 UI framework for PlayStation 5 homebrew, providing the architectural foundation for carousel, block-grid views, and controller navigation.
- **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/Shadow-M0unt/ShadowMountPlus)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus)) — Virtual mounting subsystem and background daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`) providing remote NFS/network storage mounting and `sce_sys/param.json` metadata parsing.
- **[RemotePFS](https://github.com/flatz/RemotePFS)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/RemotePFS](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/RemotePFS)) — by flatz & contributors. Remote PFS mounting and network filesystem utilities for PlayStation 5.
- **[ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/G991/ps5-ezremote-client)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-ezremote-client)) — by G991. Remote client utilities and network mounting integrations.

repos.description: Use your gamepad on PS5. Configurable USB and opt-in Bluetooth controllers with a LAN dashboard.
repos.readme:
# LibrePadPS5

Use your favorite gamepad on a jailbroken PS5.

[Download v1.1.3](https://github.com/arwebSE/LibrePadPS5/releases/download/v1.1.3/LibrePadPS5.elf) · [Releases](https://github.com/arwebSE/LibrePadPS5/releases) · [Issues](https://github.com/arwebSE/LibrePadPS5/issues)

## Features

- Supports 1-4 gamepads.
- Wired USB, Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth connections.
- Support for PlayStation, Xbox, Switch and 8BitDo gamepads.
- A dashboard to connect controllers, change button mappings and download logs.

This project is still in early development. Bluetooth starts disabled. USB adapters such as 8BitDo handle their own pairing.

**Tested on PS5 12.60** with a PDP wired controller and an Xbox One controller using Microsoft's wireless adapter. Other setups, including Bluetooth and four-player games, still need testing. See [controller compatibility](docs/CONTROLLERS.md) for details.

**8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2** input is reported working on PS5 13.60 with Xbox Series and PS4 controllers, including games, emulators and homebrew. v1.1.3 includes the working preview's USB fixes and adds automatic controller recovery after logging out of every account. See [setup](docs/SETUP.md#8bitdo-usb-wireless-adapter-2).

## Get started

You'll need a jailbroken PS5 and an ELF loader or Payload Manager.

1. Stop any other controller payloads and leave your extra gamepads unplugged.
2. Download and load `LibrePadPS5.elf`, then open `http://<PS5_IP>:8096/` on your phone or computer. Replace `<PS5_IP>` with your console's IP address.
3. In **Advanced > Input & native controllers**, reserve the profiles used by your DualSense controllers.
4. Connect your gamepad. Select it under **Control gamepad**, click **Reconnect** if needed, and assign it to a separate signed-in PS5 profile.

Use a different profile for each player, with up to four players total including DualSense users. The game must support the number of players you want to use.

For wireless setup, follow the [Xbox Wireless guide](docs/XBOX.md#quick-install-on-windows), [Bluetooth guide](docs/SETUP.md#bluetooth) or [8BitDo Adapter 2 guide](docs/SETUP.md#8bitdo-usb-wireless-adapter-2). Xbox Wireless supports one controller; its setup helper installs the required firmware for you.

Upgrading? Stop the old version before loading the new one. v1.1.3 fixes the startup failure in v1.1.2 and keeps your saved settings.

## Help and customization

- [Setup and troubleshooting](docs/SETUP.md)
- [Controller compatibility and limitations](docs/CONTROLLERS.md)
- [Change button mappings](docs/SETUP.md#controller-profiles--remapping)
- [Build and development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)

Having trouble? In the dashboard, open **Advanced > Logs & support** to download a report. You can [attach it to a GitHub issue](docs/SETUP.md#share-a-diagnostic-report-on-github) if you'd like to help us troubleshoot. Review it before sharing; logs are optional.

## Credits

Shoutout to [thaikhoa](https://github.com/thaikhoa) for testing the 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2 with Xbox Series and PS4 controllers, sharing logs and helping catch bugs.

Shoutout to [MODDED WARFARE](https://www.youtube.com/@MODDEDWARFARE) for covering similar tools and sharing setup instructions with the PlayStation homebrew community.

Built on [OmniPad PS5](https://github.com/diegobarbosaa/OmniPad-PS5), [AnyPad](vendor/anypad/README.md) and [xow](docs/XBOX.md#source-provenance). Thanks to PoorDS4/Ghostcontrol, YetAnotherControllerEnabler and PS5 Payload SDK contributors.

[GPL-3.0 license](LICENSE).

repos.readme:
# ps5-payload-sdk
This is an SDK for developing payloads targeted at exploited PS5s. ELF loaders
known to work include:
- [ps5-payload-elfldr][elfldr]
- [ps5-payload-websrv][websrv]
- [bdj-ipv6-hen][bdj-ipv6-hen]
- [elfloader][elfloader] via [ps5-jar-loader]
- [remote_lua_loader][remote_lua_loader]

Several artifacts in this repository originate from the [PS5SDK][PS5SDK] project.

## Prerequisites
On Debian-flavored operating systems, you can invoke the following commands to
install dependencies used by the SDK.
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade # optional
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo apt-get install bash clang-18 lld-18 wget # required
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo apt-get install socat cmake meson pkg-config python3 python3-pyelftools # optional
```

If you are using Fedora, you can install dependencies as follows (tested with version 41):
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo dnf install bash llvm-devel clang lld wget # required
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo dnf install socat cmake meson pkg-config python3 python3-pyelftools # optional
```

If you are using macOS, you can install them using the [Homebrew Package Manager][macos-brew] (tested with macOS Sequoia):
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ brew install llvm@18 wget # required
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ export LLVM_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm@18/bin/llvm-config # required
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ brew install socat cmake meson python && pip3 install pyelftools # optional
```

## Quick-start
You can download a binary distribution of the SDK from [the latest release page][latest-rel],
then install it to your local storage, e.g,
```console
john@localhost:tmp$ wget https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/latest/download/ps5-payload-sdk.zip
john@localhost:tmp$ sudo unzip -d /opt ps5-payload-sdk.zip
```
Assuming you have all the prerequisites and you are on a POSIX system,
the binary distribution should work regardless of CPU architecture, e.g., x86_64, aarch64.

## Usage
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ make -C samples/hello_world
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ export PS5_HOST=ps5; export PS5_PORT=9021
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ make -C samples/hello_world test
```

## Building the SDK
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo make DESTDIR=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk install
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo -E ./libcxx.sh # fetch, build, and install libcxx
```

## Adding new SCE Libs
If you have decrypted sprx files that you would like to interact with, you can
build stubs for them as follows (Make sure you have already installed the optional dependencies for your OS):
```console
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ ln -s /path/to/sprx/libSceXYZ.sprx sce_stubs/libSceXYZ.sprx
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ make -C sce_stubs stubs
john@localhost:ps5-payload-dev/sdk$ sudo make DESTDIR=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk install
```

## Reporting Bugs
If you encounter problems with the SDK, please [file a github issue][issues].
If you plan on sending pull requests which affect more than a few lines of code,
please file an issue before you start to work on you changes. This will allow us
to discuss the solution properly before you commit time and effort.

## License
Files in the folder include/freebsd are licenced under BSD licences.
Unless otherwhise explicitly stated inside a file, the rest are licensed under
the GPLv3+.

# launchpad
This is a webapp that launches ELF payloads on jailbroken PS5s. It runs in the
console's browser and deploys payloads via [elfldr][elfldr]. A companion payload
(launchpad-install.elf) adds a launcher to the home screen.

## Building
Assuming you have the [ps5-payload-sdk][sdk-ps5] installed on a POSIX machine,
the installer can be compiled using the following two commands:
```console
john@localhost:launchpad$ export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
john@localhost:launchpad$ make
```

## Adding Payloads
Payloads are listed in docs/payloads.json. The display name, description,
source code and args fields are maintained by hand, while releases and
contributors are generated from the GitHub API:
```console
john@localhost:launchpad$ python3 scripts/update-payloads.py
```
A Github workflow runs this script daily, so a new release of a listed payload
shows up on its own.

## Reporting Bugs
If you encounter problems with launchpad, please [file a github issue][issues].
If you plan on sending pull requests which affect more than a few lines of code,
please file an issue before you start to work on you changes. This will allow us
to discuss the solution properly before you commit time and effort.

launchpad is licensed under the GPLv3+.

repos.readme:
# TacHen

**Beta 3 — GoldHEN Plugin Support; 67 exact PS5 firmware profiles from 1.00 to 13.60, including 11.40.**

The original **Beta 1 ELF remains available unchanged**. The separate compatibility ELF adds public offset tables; the added firmware support is **untested on hardware**. Firmware below 11.00 is theoretical compatibility, not a confirmed working claim.

TacHen brings a native controller menu and a console-hosted web interface with layouts for both phones and PCs together for payloads, packages, games, plugins, cheats, saves and file transfers.

## Download and start

1. Download from [Releases](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/releases/latest): **TacHen-compatibility.elf** for the expanded firmware preview, or **TacHen.elf** for the unchanged original Beta 1 (11.00–13.60, excluding 11.40). Choose one ELF.

2. Reboot and jailbreak your PS5. Send the ELF with your payload sender or load it through your existing payload loader.

3. Wait for the startup notification, then hold **L3 + R3** to open TacHen. **Circle** goes back; L3 + R3 closes the menu.

4. For the web interface, open **http://YOUR-PS5-IP:8780** in your phone or PC browser on the same network. The layout automatically adapts to the screen: a mobile layout on phones and a desktop layout on PCs.

TacHen is a post-jailbreak payload, not an exploit. Use a fresh boot when replacing an already-running TacHen build. This release ELF selects its bundled runtime so an older saved update cannot replace the build you just downloaded.

## GoldHEN Plugin Support

Beta 3 introduces a compatibility bridge for GoldHEN plugin process-information and memory operations on PS5. Download **TacHen-compatibility.elf** for this update; the preserved original `TacHen.elf` does not include it. Import your plugin under Plugins, register its matching game/version, and load it once you are in the game.

**Initial compatibility:** the adapter currently recognizes the official Havana 1.2 `rdr3Payload_132.sprx`; a community tester reported it working without errors on PS5 13.42 with RDR2 1.32. Other GoldHEN plugins still need compatible API coverage and validation. See [the plugin compatibility notes](docs/PRX-CONTAINER-COMPATIBILITY.md).

## Features

- **Payloads:** download from a direct link, manage Downloads, load an ELF from console storage or USB, and set startup order/delays. Selecting an ELF in storage checks and loads it without extra confirmation screens.

- **Packages:** install directly from USB or console storage, manage downloaded packages, and receive packages through DPI v2. Local packages are read from their source rather than copied to the internal drive first. Keep the source drive connected until installation finishes.

- **Games:** browse installed and ShadowMount games, launch, mount and unmount, with automatic status refresh.

- **Plugins:** import and register `.plugin` and `.prx` modules for the intended game/version. It is recommended to start plugins only after you are in the game. Module compatibility depends on the plugin and exact game build.

- **Cheats:** import supported JSON, SHN/XML and MC4 files, or download the etaHEN/GoldHEN catalogs. Opening Cheats selects a matching pack for the running title and version; otherwise it opens the normal library. Cheats are enabled individually, never automatically by opening the page.

- **Saved games:** browse saves and export backups to USB or the FTP share.

- **Transfers:** view progress and use a two-pane file browser to copy files and folders between console storage and USB.

- **Display:** FPS and other game telemetry, optional IP display, dashboard title IDs and game versions, plus the dashboard Cheats action.

- **Phone, PC and tools:** a console-hosted website with mobile and desktop layouts, FTP share, and the MCP interface for compatible tools.

The built-in FTP share is on **port 2122**, rooted at `/data/tachen/share`; use `tachen` or `anonymous` with any password on your trusted local network. DPI v2 uses **port 12800** when enabled in Packages.

## Firmware and beta status

The compatibility ELF recognizes these exact versions; versions between listed entries are not implied:

- **1.xx:** 1.00, 1.01, 1.02, 1.05, 1.10, 1.11, 1.12, 1.13, 1.14.
- **2.xx:** 2.00, 2.20, 2.25, 2.26, 2.30, 2.50, 2.70.
- **3.xx:** 3.00, 3.10, 3.20, 3.21.
- **4.xx:** 4.00, 4.02, 4.03, 4.50, 4.51.
- **5.xx:** 5.00, 5.02, 5.10, 5.50.
- **6.xx:** 6.00, 6.02, 6.50.
- **7.xx:** 7.00, 7.01, 7.20, 7.40, 7.60, 7.61.
- **8.xx:** 8.00, 8.20, 8.40, 8.60.
- **9.xx:** 9.00, 9.05, 9.20, 9.40, 9.60.
- **10.xx:** 10.00, 10.01, 10.20, 10.40, 10.60.
- **11.xx:** 11.00, 11.20, 11.40, 11.60.
- **12.xx:** 12.00, 12.02, 12.20, 12.40, 12.60, 12.70.
- **13.xx:** 13.00, 13.20, 13.40, 13.42, 13.60.

**Testing status:** the 53 added profiles, including **11.40** and every listed firmware **below 11.00**, have not been hardware-tested with TacHen. Their public tables cover the required offsets and have been checked against pinned upstream sources. They should theoretically work, but that is not a guarantee that startup, the menu, plugins, packages, saves or every bundled component works on each version. No 14.00+ profile is included.

The original Beta 1 targeted 14 profiles on 11.00–13.60 excluding 11.40. Testers reported no known issues at its release; this was not an exhaustive per-firmware, game or plugin test matrix. **That report does not apply to the new compatibility build.** Original offsets and the published Beta 1 ELF are unchanged.

Compatibility builds keep their update selection in `/data/tachen/updates-compatibility`, separate from Beta 1's `/data/tachen/updates`. Both use the same normal settings and library. Reboot before switching ELFs; do not try to run both at once. Neither ELF performs a jailbreak or creates an exploit entry point for a firmware.

Please report the exact firmware, ELF/build identity, feature, game/version and reproduction steps. Capture instructions are in [the diagnostics guide](docs/SUPPORT-CAPTURES.md). The [firmware notes](docs/FIRMWARE-COMPATIBILITY.md) explain the sources, validation and limitations.


## Build and source

TacHen is GPL-3.0-or-later. Source is available in this repository and in the release source archive. See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for toolchain and dependency inputs. Release assets include checksums, build metadata and a third-party source bundle. Historical engineering notes live in [docs/DEVELOPMENT-NOTES.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT-NOTES.md).

## Credits

Thanks to the community testers and the authors whose work makes this possible: John Törnblom and the PS5 Payload SDK/libelfldr/libNineS contributors; LightningMods, etaHEN and OnionHEN contributors; EchoStretch and the kstuff contributors; Drakmor and ShadowMountPlus contributors; PLK and Payload Manager contributors; GoldHEN and cheat authors; ciss84; and the authors of the bundled open-source libraries.

TacHen's menu and workflows are its own; bundled components and adapted code retain their original authorship and licenses. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for detailed attribution and provenance.

Reboot and jailbreak, load TacHen, then import/register your plugin for its matching game and version. Load plugins after entering the game. Do not load another HEN alongside TacHen.

**Initial compatibility:** the adapter currently recognizes the official Havana 1.2 `rdr3Payload_132.sprx`. A community tester reported it working without errors on PS5 13.42 with RDR2 1.32; this release contains the exact tested ELF. Other GoldHEN plugins are not yet covered by this adapter. [Compatibility details](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/blob/main/docs/PRX-CONTAINER-COMPATIBILITY.md).

The 53 added firmware profiles remain untested with TacHen. Every listed firmware below 11.00 is theoretical compatibility; 11.40 is also untested. See the [exact firmware list and limitations](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/blob/main/docs/FIRMWARE-COMPATIBILITY.md). No new firmware offsets changed in this update.

Hold **L3 + R3** for the menu. The console-hosted website at `http://YOUR-PS5-IP:8780` supports **phones and PCs**. Use one ELF after a fresh jailbreak. TacHen does not provide a jailbreak entry point.

The compatibility bridge is TacHen code, not a redistribution of Havana or the reconstructed GoldHEN implementation.

repos.name: PS5-Log-Collector
repos.description: Portable Windows app for streaming, timestamping, and saving KLOG from jailbroken PS5 consoles over TCP — no  Netcat or extra runtime required.
repos.readme:
# PS5 Log Collector [English](README.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md)

A portable Windows application for collecting KLOG and KStuff/game debug output from a jailbroken PlayStation 5 — without Netcat or command-line tools. ## Highlights - Connects directly to `klog.elf` / `klogsrv` over raw TCP. - Provides a separate Game DEBUG session for [`ps5debug-NG` v1.3.0](https://github.com/OpenSourcereR-dev/ps5debug-NG). - Provides a KStuff Metrics session for metrics-enabled `kstuff.elf` plus `debug-reader.elf`. - Adds an in-app **SM+** workspace for downloading the saved ShadowMountPlus `debug.log`. - Keeps the ELF-loader connection open after upload to capture the payload's stdout/stderr stream. - Detects the foreground game and records structured trap/signal events with thread and register context. - Optionally sends a user-selected ELF payload to an active console loader on port `9021`. - Uses port `3232` by default, with an editable host and port. - Displays incoming KLOG data in a responsive live viewer. - Adds an ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds and the PC time-zone offset to every line. - Saves the complete session from the moment the connection was established. - Clears the visible log view without stopping capture; the complete session remains available to save. - Preserves partial lines when capture is stopped or the remote side disconnects. - Switches between English and Russian without restarting. - Remembers the selected language and last endpoint. - Ships as one self-contained EXE, with no separate .NET installation. - Does not bundle or invoke Netcat or Telnet. Example output: ```text [2026-09-13T22:42:15.123+03:00] kernel: example message ``` ## Requirements - A jailbroken PlayStation 5 capable of running `klog.elf` or a compatible `klogsrv` payload. - Game DEBUG additionally requires `ps5debug-NG` v1.3.0 running on the console. - The PC and console connected to the same local network. - Windows 11 x64 is the primary supported target. - Windows 10 22H2 x64 is best-effort and should be tested with the current release. ## Quick start 1. Download the latest Windows EXE from the [Releases page](../../releases/latest). 2. Start `PS5LogCollector.exe`. 3. Select **KLOG**. 4. Enter the console IP address. 5. Either activate `klog.elf` manually, or choose your ELF file and select **Send to console** while a compatible loader is active on port `9021`. 6. Keep the KLOG port at `3232` unless the payload uses a custom port, then select **Connect**. 7. Use **Stop** to end capture and **Save log** to export the complete session as UTF-8 text. Saving is also available while capture is active. Cancelling the Save dialog does not interrupt the connection or discard the session. ### Game DEBUG — KStuff Metrics 1. Select **DEBUG → KStuff Metrics** and enter the console IP address. 2. Optionally choose the matching metrics-enabled `kstuff.elf` and send it through the loader on port `9021`. 3. Choose `debug-reader.elf` and select **Start metrics capture**. 4. The app sends the reader, closes only the upload direction, and reads its stdout/stderr over the same `9021` connection. 5. Select **Stop capture** before closing the payload, then save the complete session. The reader prints periodic snapshots of kstuff metrics, kstuff message/word logs, syscall statistics, and ioctl-com statistics. The matching kstuff build must expose the shared observation area; the application cannot make an ordinary kstuff build produce these metrics. ### Game DEBUG — Debugger Events Select **Debugger Events** for the existing `ps5debug-NG` workflow: command port `744`, reverse event port `755`, and structured trap/signal packets. This is a separate diagnostic source and is not the same as KStuff Metrics stdout. KStuff Metrics captures the reader payload's stdout/stderr, not ordinary game stdout. Classic application/SDK stdout is expected to require DECI5 TTY and remains a later transport. KLOG, DEBUG, and SM+ run as separate sessions in v0.5.0. ### SM+ — ShadowMountPlus ([API reference](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/blob/1.7/docs/api.md)) 1. Open **SM+** in the left navigation and enter the PS5 IP address. 2. Select **Fetch debug.log**. The app first tries the ShadowMountPlus HTTP API on port `10101`. 3. If the API is unavailable, expand the FTP fallback and use the console FTP port (commonly `1337` or `2121`) and the saved path `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. The FTP user field is intentionally blank by default; fill it only when the console FTP service requires a username. 4. Review the downloaded file, then use **Save log** to write the original text without adding timestamps or other lines. This is a one-shot download of the saved file; live ShadowMountPlus monitoring is intentionally not part of this phase. The HTTP API is normally loopback-only, so ShadowMountPlus must be configured to bind its API to the local network (for example, `api_bind_address=0.0.0.0`). The API has no authentication, so expose it only on a trusted LAN. It may return only the tail when the file is larger than its response limit, and the status bar reports that condition. ## Connection troubleshooting - **Connection refused:** confirm that `klog.elf` is active and listening on the selected port. - **Timed out:** verify the PS5 IP address, local network connectivity, and firewall rules. - **No new messages:** KLOG may be quiet until the console produces new kernel output. - **Connection closed:** restart the payload if necessary, then connect again manually. The application uses the same raw TCP stream as: ```shell nc 3232 ``` Telnet mode is intentionally not implemented because the upstream service exposes a raw socket rather than the Telnet protocol. ## Privacy and safety KLOG and Game DEBUG files can contain device identifiers, game identifiers, thread names, memory addresses, filesystem paths, network details, or other diagnostic information. Review and redact logs before posting them publicly. PS5 Log Collector only connects to the host and ports entered by the user. It does not upload logs, include telemetry, or perform a jailbreak. Payload transfer happens only after the user explicitly chooses a local ELF file and selects **Send to console**. ## Architecture - `src/Ps5LogCollector.Core` — KLOG transport, ShadowMountPlus HTTP/FTP retrieval, same-socket ELF/stdout capture, ps5debug-NG protocol, session lifecycle, event parsing, temporary spool, and full-session export. - `src/Ps5LogCollector` — WPF/Fluent interface, localized resources, Save dialog, and persisted user preferences. - `tests/Ps5LogCollector.Core.Tests` — dependency-free regression suite covering TCP, timestamps, ShadowMount HTTP API parsing, ps5debug-NG framing, event parsing, detach, export, and localization parity. The live text control retains a bounded recent window for UI performance, while the temporary session spool preserves the complete exportable log. ## Disclaimer This is an independent diagnostic utility and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment. “PlayStation” and “PS5” are trademarks of their respective owners. Use the application only with systems and software you are authorized to access.

repos.name: prospack
repos.description: Pack, verify and send PS5 dumps as .ffpfsc, from your PC
repos.readme:
# Prospack Pack, verify and send PS5 game dumps as `.ffpfsc`, from your PC. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/unicxrn/prospack?style=flat-square&color=9b7bff&label=release)](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/unicxrn/prospack/total?style=flat-square&color=3a3a40)](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-3a3a40?style=flat-square)](#download) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/unicxrn/prospack?style=flat-square&color=3a3a40)](LICENSE)
Prospack takes a PS5 game dump, compresses it into a single `.ffpfsc` image on your PC, checks every file in that image against the original, uploads it to your PS5 and gets ShadowMountPlus to mount it. It's the same kind of image Game Compressor makes on the console, built on your PC's CPU instead, so it's a lot quicker. You also send one file that's usually 40 to 60% smaller than the dump, instead of tens of thousands of loose ones. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --- | --- | | **Windows 10 and 11** | [`Prospack-Setup.exe`](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) | | **Linux** | [`.AppImage`](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) for any distro, or the `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu | Python and MkPFS are built in, so there's nothing else to install. Prospack checks for new versions when it starts and can update itself. The Windows installer isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. The checksums for every download are on the release page if you want to verify it first. ## What you need - A jailbroken PS5 with an FTP server running: ftpsrv (port 2121) or etaHEN (port 1337). - ShadowMountPlus running on the PS5. - A game dump: the folder with `sce_sys/` and `eboot.bin` in it, like `PPSA01234-app`. - Enough free space on your PC for the image while it's being written. It can need up to the size of the dump. ## Using it The first time you open Prospack, setup scans your network for the PS5, checks that ShadowMountPlus is there, and asks where to keep images. After that, drag a dump folder onto the window (or press Ctrl+O) and leave it running. Each game goes through four steps: | Step | What happens | | --- | --- | | **Compress** | [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) packs the dump into `.ffpfsc`: an exFAT image inside a compressed PFS container. | | **Verify** | Every file is read back out of the image and compared with the dump, byte for byte. If anything differs, the job stops before it uploads. | | **Upload** | The image goes to `/data/homebrew` under a hidden name and is renamed once it's complete. Interrupted uploads resume, and Prospack won't overwrite an image that's already there. | | **Mount** | Prospack registers the image with ShadowMountPlus and waits for the game to appear. | You can queue as many games as you like. The <kbd>?</kbd> button in the app explains every screen and walks through the common problems. <details> <summary><b>What Prospack changes on your PS5</b></summary> <br> It writes the same settings Game Compressor writes for its own images, and backs up every file on your PC before changing it: | File | Change | | --- | --- | | `/data/homebrew/<TITLE>.ffpfsc` | The image | | `/data/shadowmount/autotune.ini` | `image_sector=<TITLE>.ffpfsc:65536` | | `/data/shadowmount/config.ini` | `image_ro=<TITLE>.exfat` | | `/data/shadowmount/manual.lst` | The image path. Rewriting this file is what makes ShadowMountPlus scan for it. | | `/data/GameCompressor/validations/` | A record that makes Game Compressor show the game as validated, with the space saved. Only if Game Compressor is installed. | Your dump folder is only read. The one exception is an APR Emu game that has no `ampr_emu.index`: MkPFS adds one, because the game needs it. </details> <details> <summary><b>Troubleshooting</b></summary> <br> #### Prospack can't find my PS5 Check the PS5 is on and running its FTP server, and that the PC is on the same network. Guest Wi-Fi and VPNs often keep them apart. You can type the IP in yourself under Settings → Run setup again (the PS5 shows it under Settings → Network). #### Verify failed The image didn't match the dump, so nothing was uploaded. Use **Compress again**. If it keeps failing, copy the dump again; it may be incomplete or on a failing drive. #### ShadowMountPlus couldn't register the game The image is on the PS5, but ShadowMountPlus couldn't add it to the home screen. If the message mentions a lost system hook, that's a ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 (and older) bug after rest mode: update to 1.7beta5 or newer, or restart ShadowMountPlus, then use **Check again**. #### Mount not confirmed The image made it to the PS5, but ShadowMountPlus hadn't mounted it after five minutes. It often turns up a little later. Use **Check again**, or restart ShadowMountPlus. #### "The PS5 already has a different image" Delete or rename the old `<TITLE>.ffpfsc` on the PS5, then retry. #### The game shows up but won't start That's usually a firmware, backport or ShadowMountPlus version issue rather than the image. ShadowMountPlus logs to `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. </details> ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. When you report a bug, the activity log for the game and your ShadowMountPlus version help a lot. To work on Prospack you need Node 22, Rust and Python 3.12: ```bash npm install pip install -r engine/requirements-build.txt && python engine/build.py npm run tauri dev ``` `npm run dev` runs the interface on its own in a browser, with a simulated PS5, which is the quickest way to work on the UI. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the project layout, the tests (which run against a fake PS5, never a real one) and the quirks of the PS5's FTP server. ## Credits Prospack is built on [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) and made to work alongside [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus), [Game Compressor](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-Game-Compressor) and [ftpsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv). Thanks to everyone who works on them. Please only use dumps of games you own. ## License [GPL-3.0](LICENSE)

repos.readme:
# 👑 Padrino Save Vault (PS5 Savegame Manager)

> **Universal Save Data Backup & Restoration System for PlayStation 5**  
> **Firmware Support:** 3.00 to 13.60 (PS5 Fat, Slim & Pro)  
> **Integration:** Compatible with Payload Manager (etaHEN, Relapse, ItemzFlow & Netcat)

---

## 🌟 Overview

**Padrino Save Vault** is a high-performance standalone payload and application designed to safeguard your entire PlayStation 5 gaming progress directly to an external USB Hard Drive / SSD (`/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`).

Whenever a console crashes, panics, or requires a full factory reset, Padrino Save Vault lets you recover and restore every save file, trophy cache, and database entry with zero data loss.

---

## ✨ Features

* 🚀 **Universal Game Support:** Backs up all native PS5 titles (`PPSA`), backwards-compatible PS4 games (`CUSA`), PlayStation Classics (PS1/PS2/PSP), and Homebrew emulators (`RetroArch`).
* 🔑 **Keystone Preservation:** Automatically preserves cryptographic `keystone` signatures to eliminate "Corrupt Save Data" errors upon restoration.
* 🔄 **Smart Account Re-binding:** Injects restored saves directly into the active user profile upon system reinstalls.
* ⚡ **High-Speed Transfer Engine:** 2MB I/O streaming buffers reaching 140+ MB/s over USB 3.2.
* 🎨 **Obsidian & Gold Visual Dashboard:** 1080p cinematic splash loading screen, external drive capacity gauge, and DualSense controller navigation.
* 🔔 **Native Pop-up Notifications:** Real-time on-screen alerts using `sceKernelSendNotificationRequest`.

---

## 📂 Project Structure

```
padrino-save-vault/
├── GUIA_INSTALACION_Y_USO.md    <-- Step-by-step user installation manual
├── README.md                     <-- Technical documentation
├── test_dashboard.py             <-- Local web preview server (port 1455)
├── ui/                           <-- Full graphical dashboard & splash screen
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── style.css
│   ├── app.js
│   └── assets/
│       ├── icon0.png             <-- 512x512 official emblem
│       ├── logo.jpg              <-- High-resolution shield badge
│       └── splash.jpg            <-- 1920x1080 cinematic vault background
└── src/                          <-- C Source engine for PS5 Prospero OS
    ├── main.c                    <-- Entrypoint and execution modes
    ├── vault_engine.c            <-- USB detection, recursive copy & restore engine
    ├── vault_engine.h
    ├── notify.c                  <-- PS5 native on-screen pop-up notifications
    └── notify.h
```

---

## 🌟 Novedades y Características

* 🚀 **Soporte Universal de Juegos:** Respalda partidas de PS5 nativas (`PPSA`), PS4 retrocompatibles (`CUSA`), clásicos (PS1/PS2/PSP) y Homebrew emuladores (`RetroArch`).
* 💾 **Detección Automática de Discos USB:** Escaneo en cascada `/mnt/usb0` a `/mnt/usb7` para discos duros mecánicos y SSD externos en **exFAT o FAT32**.
* 🔑 **Preservación de Keystones:** Respalda las llaves criptográficas para evitar el error de "Datos Dañados" al restaurar.
* 🔄 **Re-inserción Inteligente:** Mapeo automático de cuentas de usuario al restaurar tras formatear la consola o ante un brick.

2. Cópialo en la carpeta `/data/payloads/` de tu consola (o en `/mnt/usb0/payloads/` en tu disco duro externo).
3. Abre **Payload Manager** en tu PS5 (etaHEN / ItemzFlow) y ejecútalo con **X**.

Reads `.pdb` file as raw binary 2. Extracts readable strings 3. Uses Regex pattern matching 4. Detects: * PNG URLs * JSON URLs * PKG URLs * Content IDs 5. Displays results automatically --- # 📂 Supported Extensions | Type | Supported | | ---- | --------- | | PDB | ✅ | | PNG | ✅ | | JSON | ✅ | | PKG | ✅ | --- # 🔍 Search System The built-in search system allows searching inside: * URLs * Content IDs * JSON links * PKG links Press `Enter` after typing. --- # 💾 Export Example ## TXT Export ```txt ==================================== Name / Content ID: JP0741-CUSA25180_00-JINKIT... repos.name: ps5_yt_blocker
repos.description: PS5 YT_Update_Blocker
repos.readme:
# PS5 PKG YT Update Blocker 

Permanently blocks YouTube app updates.

## Installation
1. Run `build.sh`
2. Install `yt_blocker.pkg` 

## Paths
- DB: `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db`
- Backup: `/user/app/YTBLK0001/backup/`
- Log: `/user/app/YTBLK0001/log.txt`
- 


# YT Update Blocker

A simple GUI tool built with PyQt6 to block YouTube app updates on your PS5. This prevents accidental updates that could softlock the app if you connect to the internet unintentionally. The tool modifies the `appinfo.db` file to spoof the version and redirect update checks to a local address.

This project is a GUI wrapper around the core logic from [Gezine's Y2JB repository](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB/). Huge thanks to Gezine for the original `appinfo_editor.py` script—without it, this wouldn't exist!

## Features
- User-friendly GUI for selecting database and backup paths.
- Automatically creates a backup of the original `appinfo.db` file.
- Modifies the YouTube entry in `appinfo.db` to block updates:
  - Sets `CONTENT_VERSION` to `99.999.999` (a fake high version).
  - Sets `VERSION_FILE_URI` to `http://127.0.0.2` (a non-existent local URL).
- Real-time logging in the app window for transparency.
- Menu links to social channels for support and updates.
- Lightweight and easy to use—no advanced coding knowledge required.

## Requirements
- Python 3.6+ (tested on 3.12).
- PyQt6 (install via `pip install pyqt6`).
- SQLite3 (included in Python standard library).
- Access to your PS5 via FTP (e.g., using FileZilla or any FTP client).
- The YouTube PKG must already be installed on your PS5.

**Note:** This tool is for educational and personal use only. Modifying system files can risk database corruption—always follow the steps carefully and reboot if needed.

## Installation
1. Clone or download this repository:
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/sinajet/yt-update-blocker.git
   ```
   (Replace with your actual repo URL if different.)

2. Install dependencies:
   ```
   pip install pyqt6
   ```

3. Ensure the app icons (`app_pics` folder) and `icon.ico` are in the same directory as `yt_blocker.py`.

## Usage
### Important Notes
- If you're using a PS5 backup file version 1.2.1 or higher (from official releases), you can skip this process as updates might already be handled.
- Always close the YouTube app, navigate to Settings, and ensure no packages are installing/updating before replacing files via FTP to avoid corruption.
- If you encounter a database corruption notification after replacement, reboot your PS5.

### Step-by-Step Guide
1. **Retrieve the Database File:**
   - After installing the YouTube PKG on your PS5, connect to your PS5 via FTP.
   - Navigate to `/system_data/priv/mms/` and download `appinfo.db` to your computer.

2. **Run the Tool:**
   - Launch the script:
     ```
     python yt_blocker.py
     ```
   - The GUI window will open.

3. **Select Paths in the GUI:**
   - Click "Path..." next to "appinfo.db Path" and select your downloaded `appinfo.db` file.
   - Click "Path..." next to "Backup Path" and select a folder to save the original backup (e.g., your desktop).
   - Click "Start Process" to modify the file. The log window will show progress and any errors.

4. **Verify Changes:**
   - The tool will create a backup named `appinfo.org.db` in your selected backup folder.
   - It updates the YouTube entry (titleId: 'PPSA01650') to block updates.
   - Check the log for confirmation: It should show updated values and verification.

5. **Replace the File on PS5:**
   - Use FTP to upload the modified `appinfo.db` back to `/system_data/priv/mms/` on your PS5.
   - Overwrite the existing file.

6. **Test and Reboot:**
   - If no corruption notification appears, reboot your PS5.
   - Launch YouTube—it should now be protected from updates even if connected to the internet.

### Troubleshooting
- **Error: Paths are empty!** Ensure both paths are selected before starting.
- **Error: appinfo.db file not found!** Verify the file name and path.
- **Database Corruption:** Follow the notes above—close apps, check settings, and reboot.
- If issues persist, check the console/log output for details.

## Credits
- **Core Logic:** Massive shoutout to [Gezine](https://github.com/Gezine) for the original update-blocking script in [Y2JB](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB/). This project builds directly on that foundation.
- **GUI Implementation:** Developed by SinaJet as an enhanced, user-friendly version.

## About Us
- [Telegram Channel](https://t.me/sinajet) – For updates and support.
- [YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/c/SinaJet) – Tutorials and more.
- [GitHub Page](https://github.com/sinajet) – Check out my other projects.

If you find this useful, star the repo or drop a message—feedback is appreciated! 🚀

Click the preview to open the HEN Cheats Collection website.

[![PS4](https://img.shields.io/badge/PlayStation-4-003791?style=flat-square&logo=playstation&logoColor=white)](https://hencheats.vercel.app/) [![PS5](https://img.shields.io/badge/PlayStation-5-003791?style=flat-square&logo=playstation&logoColor=white)](https://hencheats.vercel.app/) [![Formats](https://img.shields.io/badge/Formats-JSON%20%7C%20MC4%20%7C%20SHN-24292f?style=flat-square)](https://hencheats.vercel.app/) [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-Live-238636?style=flat-square)](https://hencheats.vercel.app/) > **Play Your Way.**
--- ## Looking for cheats for a game? ### Use the website first If you only need cheats for one game, you do **not** need to download the entire repository. **[Open HEN Cheats Collection →](https://hencheats.vercel.app/)** On the website you can: - Search by **game title**, **Title ID** or **cheat creator** - Filter by **PS4**, **PS5** or other supported platforms - Filter by **JSON**, **MC4** and **SHN** - Sort by **Featured**, **Recently added**, **Title A–Z** or **Most versions** - See every available version for a game - See the creator and format of each cheat file - Read file-specific **notes** and **issue warnings** - Download **individual cheat files** directly - Save games to your **Favorites** - Report a problem with a specific cheat file The website is the fastest way to find out whether the collection contains cheats for the **exact game ID and version** you are running.

Browse the cheat database at hencheats.vercel.app

--- ## Want the entire collection? Download the full repository when you want the complete collection for your console or cheat engine. 1. Click the green **Code** button at the top of this repository. 2. Choose **Download ZIP**. **[Download the complete collection as ZIP](https://github.com/TeeKay87/HEN-Cheats-Collection/archive/refs/heads/master.zip)** The downloaded `cheats` folder is ready for **etaHEN**. Download the full collection using the instructions above. 2. FTP into your PlayStation. 3. Run the `.bat` file that matches the cheat engine you want to use. 3. The script creates a `data` folder and places the cheat files in the required structure. 4. FTP into your PlayStation. 5. Copy the generated `data` folder to the same location as the existing `data` folder on your console. 6. Allow matching cheat files to be overwritten. > [!CAUTION] > **Do not delete the existing `data` folder from your PlayStation.** Merge the generated folder into it and overwrite only the matching files. Restart and re-jailbreak the PlayStation after installing the cheats. --- ## Website or GitHub? **Use the website** when you want to search the collection, compare versions, read notes, save favorites
