repos.name: pgo_stub
repos.description: A lightweight replacement module for the PlayGo runtime library on PlayStation 5
repos.readme:
# libScePlayGo Stub

`libScePlayGo` is a lightweight replacement module for the PlayGo runtime library on PlayStation 5 targets.

Current version: **0.5**.

The module provides the common PlayGo entry points expected by titles that query installation state, chunk availability, language masks, optional chunks, and progress. It is designed for environments where the real PlayGo service is not available or not useful, while still letting software continue through its normal PlayGo checks.

## What It Does

- Exports a `libScePlayGo` PRX-compatible interface.
- Reports PlayGo chunks as available and installed.
- Tracks simple open, close, initialization, install speed, language mask, and todo-list state.
- Provides deterministic responses for chunk IDs, progress, ETA, optional chunks, and required disc checks.
- Supports an optional runtime config file to adjust the visible chunk layout and available languages.
- Can optionally write call logs for debugging PlayGo-related behavior.

By default, all languages and the five SDK scenarios are available, and installation is complete. The title must still initialize PlayGo and open a handle.

## Optional Config

At runtime, the module looks for:

```text
/app0/playgo_stub.dat
```

The file is optional. If it is missing, the module falls back to a default package layout with 1000 chunks and enables all languages. Invalid language configuration falls back to all languages without changing the parsed chunk or scenario settings.

Supported format:

```text
1000
5
english_us,russian,english_gb
```

The first line is either a chunk count or a comma-separated list of valid chunk IDs. Counts above 65000 are clamped to 65000; zero, negative, overflowing, or malformed counts fall back to 1000 chunks. Physical lines longer than 65535 bytes or containing NUL bytes are discarded as invalid without shifting subsequent fields.

The second line is an optional scenario count from 0 through 5. A count of N enables scenario IDs 0 through N-1; an explicit 0 disables all scenarios. Missing or invalid scenario configuration enables all five scenarios. Optional-chunk queries report this mask, and requests for unavailable scenarios return `SCE_PLAYGO_ERROR_BAD_SCENARIO_CONFIGURATION`.

The third line is an optional language configuration, expressed as either:

- A 64-bit hexadecimal mask with a required `0x` prefix, for example `0x4080200000000000`.
- A comma-separated list of language names or numeric system-language IDs, for example `english_us,8,english_gb`.

Names are case-insensitive, whitespace around entries is ignored, and names and IDs can be mixed. Numeric IDs from 0 through 47 are accepted and converted with the PlayGo language-bit mapping. A single decimal value is therefore a language ID, while an empty language set must be written as `0x0`.

Supported language names are:

| ID | Name | ID | Name |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 0 | `japanese` | 15 | `norwegian` |
| 1 | `english_us` | 16 | `polish` |
| 2 | `french` | 17 | `portuguese_br` |
| 3 | `spanish` | 18 | `english_gb` |
| 4 | `german` | 19 | `turkish` |
| 5 | `italian` | 20 | `spanish_la` |
| 6 | `dutch` | 21 | `arabic` |
| 7 | `portuguese_pt` | 22 | `french_ca` |
| 8 | `russian` | 23 | `czech` |
| 9 | `korean` | 24 | `hungarian` |
| 10 | `chinese_t` | 25 | `greek` |
| 11 | `chinese_s` | 26 | `romanian` |
| 12 | `finnish` | 27 | `thai` |
| 13 | `swedish` | 28 | `vietnamese` |
| 14 | `danish` | 29 | `indonesian` |

Examples:

```text
250
```

```text
0,1,2,10,20,30
3
0x4080200000000000
```

The same language selection can be written as a mixed list:

```text
0,1,2,10,20,30
3
english_us,8,english_gb
```

## Logging

Logging is disabled by default. When built with logging enabled, the module writes a simple call log to:

```text
/app0/playlgo.log
```

The log is intended to help identify which PlayGo calls a title makes and what the stub returned.

## Build Variants

Two optimized Prospero configurations are available:

- `ReleaseLog` builds with `PLAYGO_ENABLE_LOGGING=1` and writes artifacts to `out/log/`.
- `ReleaseNoLog` builds with `PLAYGO_ENABLE_LOGGING=0` and writes artifacts to `out/nolog/`.

Each configuration produces both `libScePlayGo.prx` and a fake-signed `libScePlayGo.sprx`. The SPRX is generated automatically by `tools/make_fself.py`.

```powershell
msbuild libScePlayGo.sln /p:Configuration=ReleaseLog /p:Platform=Prospero
msbuild libScePlayGo.sln /p:Configuration=ReleaseNoLog /p:Platform=Prospero
```

## Scope

This project is a compatibility stub, not a full PlayGo implementation. It does not download, install, verify, or stream real package data. Its purpose is to satisfy PlayGo API usage with predictable responses so titles can continue running in test, research, or compatibility environments.

### Empty Lists

After successful initialization and opening a valid handle, the stub accepts `numberOfEntries == 0` in these APIs:

- `scePlayGoGetLocus`: returns `SCE_OK` without accessing either array; both arrays may be `NULL`.
- `scePlayGoSetToDoList`: clears the stub's pending list and returns `SCE_OK`; the input array may be `NULL`.
- `scePlayGoGetToDoList`: writes `0` to `outEntries` and returns `SCE_OK`; the output array may be `NULL`. `outEntries` remains required.

This is a compatibility extension, not a claim about original SDK behavior. The local original PS5 PlayGo reference checks pointers before the count and rejects counts outside 1..1000 in these APIs.

Nonempty lists retain pointer, size, and chunk validation. Empty lists still require an initialized library and a valid open handle.

repos.name: ps5-webkit-autoloader-esp32
repos.description: ESP32 firmware: An automated payload loader for exploited PS5 consoles
repos.readme:
# ESP32 PS5 WebKit Autoloader

A compact HTTP/HTTPS host for the PS5 WebKit Autoloader, packaged as 4 MB flash images for ESP32-PICO, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3 boards. All targets use LittleFS and do not require PSRAM.

The web content in `autoloader/` is based on a modified version of the [`ps5-webkit-autoloader`](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader) frontend. Its bundled [`slopkit`](https://github.com/itsPLK/slopkit), [`ps5-unified-autoloader`](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-unified-autoloader/tree/feat/install-webkit-shortcut) components also contain project-specific modifications and therefore do not exactly match upstream.

## Firmware Version Supports

- poops        7.00 - 12.00
- relapse        7.00 - 13.60   (except 9.05 and 11.40)

You could choose to use poops or relapse if your FW supports both methods while caching. It would use Poops by default if you don't choose.

## Usage

1. Plug the ESP32 into the PS5 and turn on the console.
2. Connect the PS5 to the `ESP32_PORTAL` Wi-Fi network using the password `12345678`.
3. Open **Settings → Guide & Tips ... → Guide & Tips → User's Guide**.
4. Wait for the installation and caching process to finish. Do not disconnect the ESP32 while it is still running.
5. On success, Payload Manager opens automatically and a **WebKit Autoloader** shortcut appears in the **Media** section of the home screen.

After a successful installation, the web content is cached on the PS5. On subsequent boots, launch **WebKit Autoloader** directly from the Media section.

A network connection is still **REQUIRED** to complete the `Relapse` exploit process, as the exploit method relies on the PS5 having an active network interface and IP address. Internet access itself is not required. `Poops` method doesn't need that.

If an attempt fails, follow the on-screen instruction to reboot and try again. If the console freezes, crashes, or powers off, turn it back on and retry. Use this project at your own risk.

## Requirements

- Arduino CLI
- Arduino ESP32 core 2.0.11
- ~~Arduino ESP8266 core 3.1.2 (required for `make 8266`)~~

Install the Arduino CLI and required core:

```sh
./install-deps.sh
```

## Build

```sh
make
```

The default ESP32-S2/S3/C3/PICO firmware leaves native USB disconnected, so the board only draws power from its USB connection. Build the separate debug variant to enable USB CDC/Serial-JTAG output:

```sh
make debug
```

Debug firmware is written to `build/debug/`. For the ESP32-S2 alone, use `make debug-s2`. To timestamp every serial line from 00:00:00, run `python serial_timestamp.py COM4 115200` (requires pyserial).

DNS resolves `manuals.playstation.net`, `ena.net.playstation.net` and `www.msftconnecttest.com` to the ESP32; other names receive NXDOMAIN. The build creates a modified copy of Arduino ESP32 2.0.11's DNSServer under ignored `build/` using `prepare-dns-library.py`. That library retains its [upstream LGPL-2.1 license](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/2.0.11/LICENSE.md).

The build copies `autoloader/` to a temporary `data/` directory, compresses the web assets, and creates:

- `build/pico/esp32-arduino.pico.merged.bin`: Intended to support generic ESP32-PICO series boards.
- `build/s2/esp32-arduino.s2.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-S2 series boards.
- `build/s3/esp32-arduino.s3.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-S3 series boards.
- `build/c3/esp32-arduino.c3.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-C3 series boards.

Use `make pico`, `make s2`, `make s3`, `make c3`~~, `make 8266`~~, or `make clean` to build an individual target or clean generated files. ~~The ESP-12F target uses the Generic ESP8266 4 MB / 3 MB LittleFS layout and produces `build/8266/esp8266-arduino.esp12f.merged.bin`.~~

## Manifest updates

ESP32 serves `.appcache`, `.manifest`, and `.cache` files over HTTP and HTTPS
with a random 16-digit hexadecimal `# VERSION` comment generated once per boot
and HTTP no-cache headers. Resource lists are preserved; the generated version
is not written to flash. Manifests remain uncompressed in LittleFS.

## Credits

- [itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader)
- [itsPLK/ps5-unified-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-unified-autoloader)
- [jordyidk/slopkit](https://github.com/jordyidk/slopkit)
- [ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit](https://github.com/ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit)

Credit also belongs to all projects, researchers, and developers referenced by these upstream projects.

## License

Original ESP32 firmware and build code in this repository is MIT licensed. Modified upstream code, bundled payloads, and other third-party material retain their respective upstream terms; see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

repos.readme:
# aria2 for PS5

This fork builds aria2 as a PS5 ELF payload. See the [upstream README](README.rst) and the [PS5 build guide](ps5/README.md).

## PS5 changes

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Build | `Makefile.ps5` uses the PS5 SDK, SDK SQLite3/libssh2, static c-ares, and static OpenSSL with its legacy provider built in. |
| Startup | The ELF uses `/data/aria2/aria2.conf` without elfldr arguments, creates `/data/aria2`, names the process `aria2.elf`, and allows one instance through `/data/aria2/aria2.lock`. A duplicate launch shows an already-running notification. |
| Configuration | Active entries in `ps5/aria2.conf.in` are embedded as defaults. An existing config file overrides them; explicit command-line options take precedence. |
| Interface | The RPC listener serves embedded AriaNg at `/` and `/index.html`; `/jsonrpc` remains the RPC endpoint. Startup installs a Media shortcut for `http://localhost:6800/` using AriaNg's icon and shows a PS5 notification. AriaNg page navigation keeps the browser URL and history unchanged, so Back can leave the browser directly. PS5 browsers display the interface at 150% zoom. |

## Default configuration

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| RPC | Enabled on all interfaces, port `6800`, `/jsonrpc`, any origin allowed, maximum request size `2M`; no authentication or TLS. |
| Process | `daemon=false`; one instance per `/data/aria2/aria2.lock`. |
| Downloads | `dir=/data/aria2/downloads`, `continue=true`, `file-allocation=prealloc`, `auto-save-interval=60`. |
| Connections | 5 concurrent downloads, 5 connections per server, 10 splits with a minimum size of `10M`. |
| Speed limits | Download and upload limits are `0` (unlimited). |
| Session | Load and save `/data/aria2/aria2.session`; save every 10 seconds and on exit. The ELF creates an empty file if needed. |
| Console | `show-console-readout=false`, `console-log-level=notice`. |
| DHT state | `/data/aria2/dht.dat` and `/data/aria2/dht6.dat`. |
| Logging | `/data/aria2/aria2.log`, level `notice`. |
| Network and DNS | `disable-ipv6=true`, `async-dns=true`, `async-dns-server=192.168.1.1`. |
| HTTPS | `check-certificate=false`; CA file `/data/aria2/ca-bundle.crt`. The compile-time CA path is `/system/common/cert/CA_LIST.cer`. |
| Config file | `/data/aria2/aria2.conf` is optional; embedded defaults work without it. |

To verify HTTPS certificates, set `check-certificate=true` in the config file and provide a usable CA bundle. Change `async-dns-server` if `192.168.1.1` is unreachable.

## Build and run

```sh
make -f Makefile.ps5
nc PS5_IP 9021 < ps5-build/aria2.elf
```

| Output | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ps5-build/aria2.elf` | Send directly to elfldr; no console-side ELF copy is needed. |
| `ps5-build/aria2/aria2.conf` | Optional: copy to `/data/aria2/aria2.conf` to change defaults. |
| `ps5-build/aria2/ca-bundle.crt` | Optional: copy to `/data/aria2/ca-bundle.crt` for certificate verification. |

AriaNg: `http://PS5_IP:6800/` · RPC: `http://PS5_IP:6800/jsonrpc` · PS5 Media shortcut: `AriaNg` (requires the payload to be running; fixed to port `6800`).

## Credits

| Project | Use |
| --- | --- |
| [aria2](https://github.com/aria2/aria2) | Upstream source. |
| [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) | Toolchain and PS5 libraries. |
| [elfldr](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr) | Payload loader and transfer protocol. |
| [ftpsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv) | Reference for process naming and PS5 notifications. |
| [PS5 Web File Manager](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager) | Reference for installing a PS5 Media web shortcut. |
| [AriaNg](https://github.com/mayswind/AriaNg) | Embedded web interface. |
| [c-ares](https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares) | Asynchronous DNS. |
| [OpenSSL](https://github.com/openssl/openssl) | TLS and cryptography. |
| [libssh2](https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2), [SQLite](https://sqlite.org/src/) | Libraries supplied by the PS5 SDK. |
| [curl CA Extract](https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html) | Mozilla CA bundle packaged with the build. |

## License

The aria2 source and PS5 modifications are distributed under GPL-2.0-or-later. Some upstream source files also carry an OpenSSL linking exception; see their headers and `LICENSE.OpenSSL`. Third-party components retain their own terms.

repos.name: PkgToolBox
repos.description: Toolbox for analyzing and editing pkg application files for psp,ps3, ps4 and ps5, includes the most useful functions you might need.
repos.readme:
**A cross-platform toolbox for inspecting, extracting, modifying, and analyzing PlayStation PKG files.**
[![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/seregonwar/PkgToolBox?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/total.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/seregonwar/PkgToolBox?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/stargazers) [![Forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/seregonwar/PkgToolBox?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/network/members) [![Repository Views](https://hits.sh/github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox.svg?label=views)](https://hits.sh/github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/)
--- ## About **PkgToolBox** is a desktop application for working with PlayStation PKG files. It provides a unified graphical interface for inspecting package metadata, browsing internal files, extracting and modifying content, working with trophies, analyzing package structures, and performing other PKG-related operations. PkgToolBox supports package formats used across **PSP, PS3, PS4, and PS5**, although some platform-specific features may still be experimental or under development. --- ## Features - **PKG Information** Inspect package metadata and obtain detailed information about PKG files. - **GP4 / GP5 Project Workspace** Open PS4 `.gp4` and PS5 `.gp5` publishing projects, validate mapped paths, inspect `param.sfo` / `param.json`, preview source assets, and export the resolved project files. GP5 supports both flat and recursive layouts. - **Standalone File Inspection** Drop or open any local file to preview it and use the integrated text/hex inspection flow without first loading a package. - **File Explorer** Navigate the internal structure of a PKG without extracting the entire package. - **File Extraction** Extract individual files or dump the contents of a package. - **Hex Reader & Editor** Inspect and modify files directly in hexadecimal format. - **Text Reader & Editor** View and edit supported text-based files. - **File Management** Manage and delete files contained inside supported packages. - **Trophy Management** Load, unpack, inspect, and manage PlayStation trophy files. - **Trophy Creator** Create custom trophy sets with configurable icons, descriptions, and achievements. - **Wallpaper Management** Inspect, extract, and modify wallpapers and background assets included in packages. - **Encryption-aware extraction** Extract plaintext metadata safely and identify protected entries without producing corrupt output. - **PFS Analysis** Inspect PS4 PFS/PFSC container geometry with the built-in dependency-free engine. - **PARAM.SFO and image metadata** Parse all SFO keys and inspect PNG/DDS dimensions directly in the application. - **Cross-platform Support** PkgToolBox can run on Windows, Linux, and macOS. --- ## Screenshot
--- ## Requirements ### Development - **Python 3.13+** - **PySide6** - **PyInstaller** - Dependencies listed in `requirements.txt` > [!IMPORTANT] > Use **PyInstaller** when packaging the application. Alternative packaging tools such as `cx_Freeze` may not preserve all of the behavior required by PkgToolBox. PkgToolBox does not require shadPKG, OpenOrbis command-line tools, or bundled platform-specific executables. Protected PS4 PFS payload decryption is reported as unsupported until the internal key pipeline is fully validated; clear-text PKG metadata remains browsable and extractable. --- ## Installation ### 1. Clone the repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox.git cd PkgToolBox ``` ### 2. Install the dependencies ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 3. Run PkgToolBox ```bash python main.py ``` --- ## Usage Launch the application and open a PKG, GP4/GP5 project, or standalone file from the same source picker. Any of them can also be dropped onto the window. Depending on the package type and platform, PkgToolBox provides tools for: * browsing package contents; * extracting individual files; * performing full package dumps; * inspecting package metadata; * modifying supported package information; * viewing and editing files with the integrated hex editor; * viewing and editing text files; * managing trophy files; * analyzing PFS structures; * performing supported package-specific operations. For publishing projects, PkgToolBox resolves mapped paths, shows missing files without hiding them, and keeps the project read-only while allowing available content to be browsed, previewed, and exported. --- ## Roadmap ### Completed #### PKG Analysis & Navigation * [x] Advanced internal PKG file explorer * [x] Detailed package information parsing * [x] Improved hexadecimal value analysis * [x] PS3 retail and debug PKG support * [x] PSP PKG support * [x] Initial PS5 PKG support * [x] PS5 GP5 project loading (flat and rootdir layouts) * [x] PS4 GP4 project loading and standalone file workspaces #### Trophy Support * [x] PS4 `.trp` trophy support * [x] PS5 `.ucp` trophy support #### PFS Support * [x] ShadPKG integration * [x] PS4 PFS extraction * [x] PFS information viewer #### Platform Support * [x] Windows support * [x] Linux support * [x] macOS support #### Stability * [x] Improved error handling * [x] Improved application stability * [x] General bug fixes and code improvements ### In Progress / Planned #### PKG Support * [ ] Extended PS5 PKG support * [ ] Advanced PKG splitting * [ ] Improved FPKG update handling * [ ] Native PkgToolBox implementation for PS4 and PS5 #### PKG Rebuild * [ ] Extract, modify, and rebuild supported PKG files * [ ] Recompute required digests and package metadata where applicable #### File Decryption * [ ] `.ESFM` file decryption --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. If you want to improve PkgToolBox, you can: * 🐛 [Report a bug](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/issues) * 💡 [Request a feature](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/issues) * 🔧 [Open a Pull Request](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/pulls) * 💬 Contact me on [X / Twitter](https://x.com/SeregonWar) PkgToolBox is primarily developed and maintained by a single developer, so bug reports, testing, documentation improvements, and code contributions are greatly appreciated. --- ## Acknowledgements PkgToolBox includes or builds upon work from other members of the PlayStation development community. * **[Sinajet](https://github.com/sinajet/)** Creator of [PS5-Game-Info](https://github.com/sinajet/PS5-Game-Info), used by PkgToolBox to analyze `eboot.bin` files extracted from packages and assist with package identification. * **[HoppersPS4](https://github.com/HoppersPS4)** Creator of the C++ version of [Waste_Ur_Time](https://github.com/HoppersPS4/Waste_Ur_Time), which was rewritten and integrated into the `PS4_Passcode_Bruteforcer.py` module. * **[zecoxao/gengp4-src](https://github.com/zecoxao/gengp4-src)**, **[zecoxao/gengp5-src](https://github.com/zecoxao/gengp5-src)** and **[SvenGDK/LibProsperoPKG](https://github.com/SvenGDK/LibProsperoPKG)** Public publishing-project schema and model references used to validate PkgToolBox's independent Python implementation of GP4/GP5 loading. * **[SvenGDK/SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero)** Reference for the broader PS5 development and packaging workflow that the consolidated workspace is designed to complement. If your work is used by PkgToolBox and is missing from this section, please contact me on [X](https://x.com/SeregonWar). --- ## Support Development PkgToolBox has been actively developed and maintained for several years. If you use the project and would like to support its continued development, maintenance, testing, and future features, donations are greatly appreciated.
---
**Made with ❤️ for the PlayStation homebrew community** [Releases](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/releases) • [Issues](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/issues) • [Pull Requests](https://github.com/seregonwar/PkgToolBox/pulls) • [Support](https://www.seregonwar.com/donations)

repos.name: PSXTERM
repos.description: Remote interactive terminal environment for exploited PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 systems.
repos.readme:
# PSXTerm

Remote interactive terminal environment for exploited **PlayStation 4** and
**PlayStation 5** systems.

```
PC / Mac / Linux terminal          PS4 / PS5
        psxterm  <host>            psxtermd (payload)
             |                          |
             |        TCP :2323         |
             +-------- PTTY/1 ----------+
                                        |
                                   session tty
                                  (FreeBSDPTY or
                                     PipeTTY)
                                        |
                                      psh
                                        |
                       +----------------+----------------+
                       |                                 |
                 built-in commands               external CLI ELFs
             (help, pwd, cd, ls, cat, ...)     (/data/psxterm/bin/*)
```

PSXTerm does **not** require Bash, OpenSSH or any desktop userspace on the
console. It ships its own minimal shell, `psh`, and its own framed protocol,
`PTTY/1`.

## Status

Terminology follows the project's strict rules:

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| PTTY/1 protocol (framing, validation, partial IO) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| psxtermd server (poll loop, sessions, timeouts, limits) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| `psh` shell + builtins | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Host client (raw mode, resize, terminal restore, batch mode) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Ratatui workspace client (console profiles, tabs/splits, flash actions, English/Italian) | IMPLEMENTED, WINDOWS + LINUX HOST TESTED; PS4/PS5 HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED |
| FreeBSDPTY backend (host POSIX ptmx) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| PipeTTY fallback | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| External execution (host fork/exec) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| FreeBSDPTY backend (raw /dev/ptmx + TIOCGPTN) | IMPLEMENTED, BUILD FOR PS4/PS5, HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED |
| External execution on PS4/PS5 (elfldr-style) | IMPLEMENTED, BUILDS FOR PS4/PS5, HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED |
| PS4/PS5 filesystem preparation | IMPLEMENTED, BUILDS FOR PS4/PS5, HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED |
| Structured diagnostics + spawn stages | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| `psxterm doctor` (local and remote, `--json`) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Capability negotiation (`PTTY_MSG_CAPS`) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Backpressure bounds (input + output queues) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Persistent sessions (detach / attach / resume, bounded scrollback) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| File transfer (push / pull / install, atomic uploads) | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED |
| Runtime layout, environment and package metadata | IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED; updated runtime sources compile for PS4/PS5, HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED |
| Challenge-response authentication | NOT IMPLEMENTED (shared token only) |
| psh history / completion / cursor editing | NOT IMPLEMENTED |
| psh pipelines and redirection | NOT IMPLEMENTED |
| Job control (jobs/fg/bg) | NOT IMPLEMENTED |
| Hardware bring-up guide | WRITTEN ([docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md](docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md)) |
| CI: host build/tests, ASan/UBSan, PS4/PS5 SDK payload jobs | IMPLEMENTED |
| Client on Windows | Ratatui client IMPLEMENTED, HOST TESTED; C client remains POSIX-only |
| Authentication | Architecture + shared-token mode IMPLEMENTED; disabled by default (insecure development mode) |

The PS4/PS5 builds produce payload ELFs with the official
[ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and
[ps4-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps4-payload-dev/sdk) SDKs. PS5 bring-up
has reached physical hardware, with partial results recorded in
[docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md](docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md); PS4 hardware validation
remains pending. Do not read "builds" as "works".

## Layout

```
include/psxterm/   public headers (protocol, server, session, tty, process, shell, platform)
core/              protocol, server, session, tty abstraction, process abstraction
shell/             psh: parser, environment, command registry, builtins/
platform/host/     host backend (Linux/macOS): POSIX PTY, fork/exec
platform/ps4/      PS4 backend: raw ptmx, elfldr-style spawn, fs prep
platform/ps5/      PS5 backend: raw ptmx, elfldr-style spawn, fs prep
client/            psxterm host client
client/tui/        portable Rust/Ratatui console workspace + flash CLI
tools/             psxterm-ttyprobe, cli_test
tests/             host unit tests (CTest) and tests/integration (Python)
```

## Building

The native Windows/Linux/macOS workspace client is built separately:

```console
cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path client/tui/Cargo.toml
cargo run --release --manifest-path client/tui/Cargo.toml -- --lang it
```

See [the workspace client guide](docs/CLIENT_TUI.md) for console profiles,
multiple terminals, flash commands, localization and shortcuts.

Host (development, Linux/macOS/WSL):

```console
cmake -S . -B build-host -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build-host -j
ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure
python3 tests/integration/test_e2e.py --build build-host
```

PS5 / PS4 payloads, using a payload SDK installation:

```console
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
cmake -S . -B build-ps5 -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK/toolchain/prospero.cmake
cmake --build build-ps5 -j
# -> build-ps5/psxtermd  build-ps5/psxterm-ttyprobe  build-ps5/cli_test.elf

export PS4_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps4-payload-sdk
cmake -S . -B build-ps4 -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$PS4_PAYLOAD_SDK/toolchain/orbis.cmake
cmake --build build-ps4 -j
```

## Running

On the console (payload), after loading `psxtermd` with an ELF loader:

```console
psxtermd                       # port 2323, authentication disabled (insecure)
psxtermd -p 2323 --token SECRET
psxtermd --max-sessions 4 --handshake-timeout 5000 --idle-timeout 600000
psxtermd --tty auto|pty|pipe   # force a tty backend (debugging)
psxtermd --doctor [--json]     # local diagnostics, no client needed
```

From the PC:

```console
psxterm 192.168.1.50                    # interactive session
psxterm 192.168.1.50 -p 2323 -t SECRET
psxterm 192.168.1.50 -e "uname"         # run one command, exit with its status
psxterm doctor 192.168.1.50             # remote diagnostics
psxterm doctor --json 192.168.1.50      # machine-readable report
psxterm sessions 192.168.1.50           # list sessions (running/detached)
psxterm attach 192.168.1.50 3 --resume <token>
psxterm push 192.168.1.50 ./tool.elf /data/psxterm/bin/tool.elf
psxterm pull 192.168.1.50 /data/psxterm/log.txt ./log.txt
psxterm install 192.168.1.50 ./tool.elf  # -> /data/psxterm/bin/tool.elf
```

Inside a session, **Ctrl+]** detaches: the shell, its cwd, environment and
foreground process keep running, output is buffered in a bounded scrollback
(oldest bytes dropped, reported on reattach), and `attach --resume` resumes it
with the session's resume token. A dropped connection behaves like a detach;
`--no-persist` restores destroy-on-disconnect.

`doctor` pings the daemon, then reports platform, filesystem, TTY, session and
process-execution checks, running the controlled `cli_test` target through the
real spawn backend. Exit codes: `0` ready, `1` ready with warnings, `2` not
ready, `64` invalid client usage. See
[docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md](docs/HARDWARE_BRINGUP.md) for the full console
bring-up sequence and failure triage.

### psh

Built-ins: `help pwd cd ls cat clear env export unset uname whoami ps exit`.
`ls` provides adaptive columns, bright file colours, aligned long listings and
`LS_COLORS` customisation. All built-ins have `--help`; see
[terminal output and verification](docs/TERMINAL_OUTPUT.md) for supported
options, palette settings and test scope.
Anything else is resolved through `PATH` (default `/data/psxterm/bin`, with an
implicit `.elf` suffix on consoles) and executed as an external ELF on the
session tty.

External commands receive the runtime home, temporary and XDG directories,
certificate paths and a runtime-first `PATH`. See
[docs/RUNTIME.md](docs/RUNTIME.md) for the layout, metadata lifecycle and
validation status.

### TTY capability probe

```console
psxterm-ttyprobe
```

It opens `/dev/ptmx`, calls `TIOCGPTN`, opens the corresponding `/dev/pts/<n>`,
checks termios, window-size ioctls and `isatty()`, and performs a master/slave
roundtrip. Exit status 0 means FreeBSDPTY is usable; 1 means only the PipeTTY
fallback is available. On consoles this is the runtime check that decides
whether `FreeBSDPTY` is enabled - headers alone prove nothing.

## Protocol

`PTTY/1` is a small framed protocol: a fixed 16-byte little-endian header
(magic `PTTY`, version, type, flags, session id, payload length) followed by an
optional payload of at most 64 KiB. Frames are validated (magic, version,
length, session id) and parsed field by field - no struct casting over
network buffers. Messages: `HELLO HELLO_ACK OPEN OPEN_OK CLOSE STDIN STDOUT
STDERR RESIZE SIGNAL EXEC EXIT PING PONG`. See `include/psxterm/protocol.h`.

## Security

Authentication is **disabled by default** and that is clearly logged as
insecure development mode. Use `--token` for a shared-secret handshake. Never
expose the daemon to untrusted networks while authentication is disabled.

## Testing

* 9 host unit suites via CTest (protocol, parser, env, registry, session,
  tty, shell, diagnostics, runtime).
* 50 host integration tests driving a real daemon with an independent Python
  implementation of PTTY/1, covering malformed input, authentication, session
  limits, resize, signals, multi-session isolation, large inherited environments,
  timeouts, the doctor
  command (human, JSON, busy session, client binary), capabilities,
  backpressure floods with bounded-RSS assertions, detach/attach/resume with
  scrollback truncation, file transfer (roundtrip, atomicity, path safety,
  client binary), runtime metadata JSON escaping and restart preservation,
  manifest failure reporting and a disconnect/fd-leak stress loop.
  Four output matrices cover all built-ins, 95 exact GNU `ls` comparisons,
  13 GNU `cat` comparisons and colours/Unicode at six terminal widths.
* The host PipeTTY stdio matrix checks live `fgets`, binary `fread`, output
  after stdin EOF, separate stdout/stderr channels, the real client, session
  reuse, descriptor cleanup and detached stderr. See
  [docs/STDIO_HOST.md](docs/STDIO_HOST.md) for the scope and console limitation.
* `cli_test` is the controlled external-execution target (argv, environment,
  `isatty`, window size, stdin, stdout/stderr, exit code 7).

## Contributing and development builds

Use the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for client/host checks and translation
changes. Issue forms cover bugs, console crashes, features, documentation, and
localization. See [CI and nightly downloads](docs/CI.md) for desktop and PS4/PS5 development
builds, supported platforms, commit metadata, and SHA-256 checksums.

## License

GPLv3. The PS4/PS5 process backends follow the minimal concepts of the
GPLv3 [ps4/ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev) ELF loaders.

repos.name: PS5CLEAN
repos.description: This tool helps you
repos.readme:
PS5CLEAN

A little fan-powered fun for your PS5.
By YAHBALLON · v1.0.0.6 · (AI-assisted)

## What is PS5CLEAN? PS5CLEAN is a native PS5 homebrew **fun app** with a sci-fi dashboard and timed fan pulses. The idea is simple: let the fan alternate between high and low cooling, in the hope that the changing airflow might loosen a little dust inside the console. **That is the hope, not a proven cleaning effect.** PS5CLEAN is an experimental project, not a replacement for physical cleaning or maintenance. ## Dashboard ![PS5CLEAN dashboard](screenshots/dashboard.png) *Rendered from the actual app UI. This preview is not connected to a console, so live readings are blank.* ## Features - Blue glass dashboard with a rotating fan and an original center emblem. - Four animated cyan light segments around the fan. - Ten-minute cycle by default, with selectable duration and pulse interval. - Live CPU temperature, measured fan duty and a scrolling duty graph. - Start / Stop controls and automatic restoration of the original cooling target. - Direct temperature-target control with kstuff; etaHEN is not required. ## How the pulses work Press **Start Cleaning** to begin. The first half of each pulse interval requests high cooling using a **20 C** temperature target. The second half requests low cooling using a **60 C** target. The cycle repeats until the selected duration ends or you press Stop. The displayed request range is **100% to 0%**, but these are control requests: the console's automatic fan regulation determines the actual speed. **A physically stopped fan is not guaranteed.** The dashboard displays measured duty separately. The app does not stop simply because measured duty takes longer to reach maximum. Stop, completion, loss of app heartbeat, owner exit, device errors or invalid/over-limit temperature restore the original temperature target. Other fan-control apps should be closed while PS5CLEAN is running. ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and access to the fan device. - A loader capable of mounting native homebrew folders, such as ShadowMount Plus. - A localhost ELF loader on **port 9021** to start the included `fan-service.elf`, or manual loading of that service. Fan control has been tested on **firmware 5.10**. Compatibility with every firmware or console model is not established. ## Installation 1. Download the app ZIP from the release assets. 2. Extract the complete **PPSA99338** folder into your homebrew directory, for example `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99338`. 3. Register or mount it through your loader, then launch PS5CLEAN. 4. Select your duration and pulse interval in Settings, then press Start Cleaning. **Title ID:** `PPSA99338` · **Content version:** `01.000.006` ## Controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | L1 / R1 | Switch Cleaning, Settings and About | | Left / Right | Select Start or Stop; change a selected setting | | Up / Down | Select a settings row | | X | Activate the selected button or setting | | Circle | Return to Cleaning, stop an active cycle, or exit while idle | | Options | Stop and exit | ## Build from source Build on Linux or WSL with Clang and the dependencies required by the included build scripts. The scripts fetch pinned public SDK dependencies; generated files are kept in `build/`, `dist/` and `.deps/`. ```sh make USE_CCACHE=0 BUILD_JOBS=4 app ``` Outputs: - `dist/PPSA99338/` - installable app folder. - `dist/PPSA99338.zip` - packaged app. The fan helper listens only on localhost port **7341** and checks the calling app title. Settings are stored in `/data/PS5CLEAN/settings.ini`. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** - PS5CLEAN project. - [BlackBearReloaded / ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) - UI renderer and native boilerplate. - [drakmor / fan_target](https://github.com/drakmor/fan_target) - fan interface reference. - Inter and Montserrat font licenses are included under `assets/fonts/`. - Artwork and development were AI-assisted; artwork notes are included in the source. Distributed under **GPL-3.0**. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# ⚡ AtmoxJB — Private Research & FPKG HEN > *If you found this repository, you weren't meant to stumble here. Consider yourself lucky.* > As a prize for looking in the shadows: **your PS5 jailbreak experience is about to be entirely different.** --- ### 👁️ What is AtmoxJB? **AtmoxJB** is a private, lightweight Homebrew Enabler (HEN) engineered specifically to run unsigned code with zero overhead, bypass arbitrary kernel checks, and deliver full FPKG support across PlayStation 5 firmware up to **11.60**, experimental **12.xx** (as well as legacy PS4 FPKG backports). Unlike conventional loaders, AtmoxJB is tuned for: - 🚀 **Ultra-Fast Execution:** Stripped of redundant bloat, minimal payload latency. - ⚡ **Native Kraken Decompression Acceleration:** Seamless unpacking and streaming of compressed assets for both PS5 (≤ 11.60, experimental 12.xx) and PS4 packages. - 🛡️ **Flexible PPR Architecture:** Plaintext **Package Process Request (PPR)** interception can either be bundled directly into the standalone ELF binary or decoupled into a split modular payload stage. - 🔗 **Silent In-Memory Presence:** Custom detection tags (`atmxlb`, in-memory footprint guards) preventing kernel clobbering and collision crashes. --- ### 🧩 Execution Chain Architecture AtmoxJB operates in post-kernel exploitation space. You must chain it sequentially with your userland and kernel exploit pipeline: ``` [ Userland Exploit ] (WebKit / BD-J / Lua / Y2JB) │ ▼ [ Kernel Exploit ] (IPv6 / UMTX / (Re)Lapse) │ ▼ [ AtmoxJB (HEN) ] (atmox_0.8.elf / AtmoxJB_0.8.elf) │ ├──> Kernel Patching & Entitlement Spoofing ├──> Kraken Hardware Decompression Hooks └──> Plaintext PPR Interception │ ▼ [ ShadowMount+ ] (shadowmountplus.elf — by Drakmor) └──> Virtual FS Mapping (exFAT / Lizard / ffpfsc Game Backups) ``` > [!NOTE] > **Storage & Mounted Game Backups:** > To run mounted virtual backups (such as **exFAT**, **Lizard**, and **ffpfsc** formats), pair AtmoxJB with **ShadowMount+** (alpha/beta builds by Drakmor). Send AtmoxJB first, allow 1–2 seconds for kernel hooks to register, then trigger ShadowMount+. --- ### 📦 Included Research Tooling This is **not** a public distribution repository. For obvious reasons, the core source code remains reserved for our private scene group. However, for those researchers fortunate enough to discover this branch, selected backend research components, hooks, relays, and deployment scripts are provided in this tree: | File / Component | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | `atmox_0.8.elf` / `AtmoxJB_0.8.elf` | Latest compiled AtmoxJB 0.8 payload | | `send_atmox_chain.py` | 1-Click sequential socket launcher (AtmoxJB + ShadowMount+) | | `build_atmox_sm_combo.py` | Self-contained ELF relay injector (V3 payload combo) | | `relay_stub.c` / `send_sm_relay.S` | In-process execution relay stubs | | `combo_hook.c` / `combo_hook.S` | SceShellCore interception & hook routines | | `mount_helper_standalone.c` | Standalone mount helper and FW spoofing module | --- ### 🚀 Quick Start (Chain Dispatch) ```bash # Dispatch the AtmoxJB + ShadowMount+ combo chain python send_atmox_chain.py 192.168.1.100 9020 ``` --- ### 🤝 Acknowledgments & Credits AtmoxJB stands on the shoulders of scene pioneers: - **EchoStretch** — For the invaluable PS5 SDK, tooling, and relentless scene contributions. - **Drakmor** — For **ShadowMount+** and breakthrough virtual filesystem mounting architectures. - **sleirsgoevy** — For foundation research and early PS5 exploit engineering. - **The PS5 Underground Scene** — To everyone pushing the boundaries of console research and sharing ideas in the dark. ---

repos.readme:
# prospero-win sender: source and how it works

This zip is the source of the sender: the Windows app that takes a PC game
(a zip or a folder) and puts it on a jailbroken PS5 running prospero-win,
with its settings worked out automatically. It is taken from the
`sender-gui` branch of the fork at commit `e8adee0` (v4.27).

Binaries are not included (the sender .exe, the prebuilt base prefix zip,
Wine Mono, `wowprospero.dll`, the D3D12 proxy DLLs, `pwexec*.exe`, the
Steamworks stub DLL). Each one is rebuilt from the source here with the
scripts listed below. Nothing here is a game, key or firmware.

## What is in the zip

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/pw_gui.py` | The Windows window (Python Tk). Packaged into the .exe. |
| `tools/pw_quick.py` | The core: finds the game's program, works out its settings, builds its prefix, sends it. Also has a command-line mode. |
| `tools/pw_autoconfig.py` | Engine detection (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, LÖVE, Electron, .NET, XNA, Java) and the per-engine rules for exe, graphics and arguments. |
| `tools/pw_prefix.py` | Talks to the console over FTP, and the prefix/profile file format it uses. |
| `tools/pw_install.py` | Installs games on a Linux PC with the pinned Wine. The sender uses only its pinned DXVK release lookup and download (`dxvk_release`, `fetch`); the rest is for the library side. |
| `tools/pw_base_prefix.py` | Makes the base prefix zip (a Wine prefix made once with the pinned host Wine). |
| `tools/presets/` | Controller presets (`*.input`): mouse, gamepad, warcraft3, goldsrc, pinball. Copied to the console by name. |
| `tools/d3d12_proxy/` | Source of the Direct3D 12 proxy `d3d12.dll` and `d3d12core` stand-ins (feature level capped at 11_0, reports 16 GB RAM). |
| `tools/pwexec/` | `pwexec.c`, the in-process launcher loader (built as `pwexec32.exe` and `pwexec64.exe`). |
| `wine/wowprospero/` | The WoW64 CPU backend source (`cpu.c`, `legacy_ops.h`, ...), built to `wowprospero.dll`. `legacy_ops.h` emulates the x86 instructions the console's 32-bit translator refuses. |
| `tools/build_*.sh`, `tools/media/` | Build scripts for the pieces the sender bundles: host Wine, the media (FFmpeg-backed Media Foundation) layer, Wine Mono, the Steamworks stub, the CPU backend. |
| `tools/sender-licenses/` | License texts and `NOTICES.txt` for everything bundled. |
| `tests/test_pw_quick.py`, `test_pw_autoconfig.py`, `test_pw_prefix.py`, `test_pw_install.py` | The Python tests for the sender. Run: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_pw_quick.py tests/test_pw_autoconfig.py tests/test_pw_prefix.py` |
| `docs/SENDING_GAMES.md`, `docs/VIDEO_DECODING.md` | User docs for sending games, and the notes on video decoding on the console. |
| `.github/workflows/sender.yml` | CI: runs the tests, builds the Windows .exe with PyInstaller. |

## The big picture

The console cannot do the hard parts of a Windows install. It cannot start a
second process, and `wineboot` (which makes a Wine prefix) is off there. So
the sender does the work on the PC and sends the result:

1. A **base prefix** is made once on a PC with the pinned Wine and shipped as
   a zip. It holds only Wine's own files: `system32`, the registry, the
   stand-in fonts, and the media decoders. It is the same for every game.
2. For each game, the sender copies the game's files into the console's copy
   of that base prefix, at `C:\Games\<slug>`, and writes a profile
   (`profiles/<slug>.profile`) that tells the console app what to run.
3. Anything the game needs beyond the game's own files (DXVK, the D3D12
   proxy, Wine Mono, the translator DLL, the loader, registry entries) is
   added beside the game or in the prefix as "stand-ins".
4. Everything goes over FTP to the console (4 connections, `FTP_LANES`), and
   a record of each file already sent lets an interrupted send resume.

The whole sender is a pipeline of these stages. Each one is a function you
can read on its own.

### Stage 1: read the game (`Source`, `pe_info`, `find_executables`)

`Source` reads a zip or a folder without unpacking it. `pe_info` reads a PE
header and its import table, which says the architecture (32 or 64 bit),
whether the program is a GUI, and which DLLs it imports. `find_executables`
lists every `.exe`, scores it (bigger is likelier, top folder is likelier, a
name that matches the game counts for more, a name like `setup`, `crash`,
`patch` counts against it, a program that imports a graphics library counts
for it), and sorts them, best first.

### Stage 2: work out the settings (`autoconfigure`, `guess_graphics`, `launch_pair`, `configured`)

- **Engine**: `pw_autoconfig.py` looks for each engine's files (Unity's
  `UnityPlayer.dll`, Godot's `.pck`, RPG Maker's `Game.rgss`, and so on) and
  returns a `Plan`: which exe to start, which graphics mode, which arguments
  and environment variables. Unreal starts the shipping exe, not the
  launcher. Godot Compatibility games get Vulkan.
- **Graphics**: `guess_graphics` reads the imports of the game's exe and of
  the game's own DLLs (engines load their renderers from DLLs). Direct3D 8
  to 11 means DXVK; OpenGL means `opengl`; otherwise `gdi`. A game that only
  imports Direct3D 12 gets the vkd3d-proton route (`d3d12`), with the proxy.
- **Launcher pairs**: some games are started through a launcher that hands
  off to the real game (Red Alert 2's `RA2.exe` starts `Game.exe`). The
  console cannot start the second program, so `launch_pair` finds the
  (game, launcher) pair in the same folder. The program that imports a
  graphics library is the game. A sibling that draws nothing, is windowed,
  has the same architecture, and is not a tool (setup, patcher, crash
  handler) is the launcher. Either one may be the exe the user picked. When
  a launcher is found, the profile starts `pwexec` with the launcher as its
  first argument.
- **Game**: `configured` assembles a `Game` (a dataclass) from all this, plus
  the environment that `suggest_environment` reads from the game folder.
  `Game.check()` validates it, and `Game.profile()` writes the profile text.

### Stage 3: build the prefix contents (`Sender.items`, `stand_ins`, `environment`, `reg_entries`)

- `Sender.items` lists the game's files as `Item`s, skipping the junk that
  the Windows file system adds (`__MACOSX`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`).
- `stand_ins` returns the extra files the game needs:
  - Direct3D 12 games: the proxy `d3d12.dll` and `d3d12core.dll`, beside the
    exe, plus the vkd3d-proton DLLs.
  - Launcher games: `pwexec32.exe` or `pwexec64.exe`, beside the launcher.
  - Steamworks.NET stub, when the exe names it and the folder lacks it (a
    GOG Stardew Valley build needs it to start under Mono).
  - The translator DLL `wowprospero.dll`, which is bundled, unless the
    console's own app copy is used (`fetch_app_cpu_dll`).
- `reg_entries` reads any `.reg` file in the game folder (for example an
  exported registry key with a CD key). `apply_reg` merges it into the
  prefix's `system.reg` and `user.reg` (for 32-bit games it also copies to
  `Wow6432Node`). The format conversion is in `parse_reg`, `merge_reg`,
  and `reg_text`.
- `environment` builds the Wine environment (for example
  `PW_FAKE_RAM_GB=16` for the D3D12 route) and writes it into `user.reg`.

### Stage 4: send (`Sender.send`, `send_files`, `update_settings`)

- `Sender.send` makes the game's prefix folder on the console (a copy of the
  base prefix, plus the game files) and sends the files. It skips a file
  that already exists at the same size. The state record lets a resend skip
  finished files, and an interrupted send carries on from where it stopped.
  If the game is already on the console, the GUI asks whether to replace it
  (send everything, keeping saves) or to update settings only.
- `send_files` runs the file transfer across the FTP lanes (`each`, `lane`).
  `retrying` reconnects and retries a step (six tries) when the connection
  drops. `CountingReader` and `Progress` feed the speed and the progress bar.
- `update_settings` is the quick path: it rewrites the profile and the
  registry entries, the environment, the stand-ins and the controller preset
  in seconds, and keeps the game's files and saves. Use it after changing a
  setting, or to pick up a new `wowprospero.dll` or loader for a game that
  is already sent.
- `put_mono` sends Wine Mono once to `/data/prospero-win/shared`, for .NET
  Framework and XNA games. `put_preset` copies a controller preset by name
  when the console lacks it. `put_profile` writes the profile.

### Stage 5: the window (`pw_gui.py`)

- The window runs `pw_quick` on a background thread and passes progress and
  status back through a queue (`self.events`), so the window stays
  responsive. A Cancel button stops the transfer; the next Send carries on.
- It fills its fields from `pw_quick.suggest` and `pw_quick.configured`
  when a game is chosen, and lets the user change the exe, the graphics
  mode, the arguments, the environment, the controller preset, and the
  desktop size.
- Other buttons: install or update the prospero-win app from a release zip
  (`install_app`), the Payloads box (sends `.elf` or `.bin` files to the
  console's port 9021 in order, `send_payloads`), and Get logs
  (`fetch_logs` zips `/data/prospero-win/logs` and the profiles beside the
  .exe).
- The `π` in the corner is a small easter egg: Ctrl+Shift+left-click opens
  a link in the default browser.

### Stage 6: the console side (not in this zip)

The sender writes files the console app reads. The app itself, prospero-win
(upstream `mpereiraesaa/prospero-win`, tag v0.1.1), runs Wine on the PS5 with
RADV Vulkan and DXVK, and has an IA-32 translator for 32-bit code. The
sender's replacement translator (`wine/wowprospero`) and loader (`pwexec`) are
built against app 0.1.1. If the app is updated, check them again.

## Build the pieces

The sender .exe is PyInstaller on Windows:

    pyinstaller --noconfirm --onefile --windowed --name prospero-win-sender \
      --paths tools --exclude-module yaml \
      --add-data "tools/presets;presets" --add-data "tools/stubs;stubs" \
      --add-data "tools/d3d12;d3d12" --add-data "tools/cpu;cpu" \
      --add-data "tools/pwexec;pwexec" tools/pw_gui.py

Those `--add-data` folders hold the built binaries:

- `tools/stubs/Steamworks.NET.dll`: `tools/build_steamworks.sh`
- `tools/d3d12/`: `tools/d3d12_proxy/build.sh` (plus vkd3d-proton 3.0.1 DLLs)
- `tools/cpu/wowprospero.dll`: `tools/build_wowprospero.sh`
- `tools/pwexec/pwexec{32,64}.exe`: `tools/pwexec/build.sh` (MinGW)
- Wine Mono zip: `tools/build_mono.sh`
- Base prefix zip: `tools/pw_base_prefix.py` with `tools/build_host_wine.sh`
  (and `tools/build_media.sh` for the media decoders)

## Running the tests

    python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_pw_quick.py tests/test_pw_autoconfig.py \
      tests/test_pw_prefix.py tests/test_pw_install.py

The tests cover the settings rules (engine detection, graphics choice,
launcher pairing), the registry merge, the profile text, and the send
bookkeeping. They don't need a console. Real games have to be checked on the
PS5.

## Known limits

- The console has about 546 MB of RAM reported, and single reservations above
  about 4 GB fail. D3D12 games report 16 GB through the proxy.
- Windows fonts are stand-ins (Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, MS Gothic).
- MIDI and DirectInput gamepads don't work on the console.
- The 32-bit translator covers every x86 instruction the app's translator
  refuses except 3DNow! and 16-bit addressing.
- A game whose exe has no relocation data and needs a fixed address may fail
  in the loader. Relocatable games work.
- The sender targets prospero-win app 0.1.1. A different app version may
  break the translator DLL and the loader.

## Licenses

Everything the sender bundles is open source. `tools/sender-licenses/NOTICES.txt`
lists each piece and where its source is. The sender itself is LGPL-2.1-or-later.

repos.readme:
# PS5 Notify (Android)

**Estado: beta.** PS5 Notify reenvía a la PS5 las notificaciones de las aplicaciones que selecciones en el móvil. La app recibe las notificaciones en tiempo real y, además, puede volver a consultar periódicamente las notificaciones que Android mantiene activas.

## Configuración

1. Instala el APK generado por GitHub Actions: pestaña **Actions** -> último **Build APK** -> **Artifacts** -> `ps5-notify-apk`.
2. Transfiere el archivo `notify-bridge.elf` a la PS5 usando el método de transferencia disponible en tu configuración.
3. Abre **Payload Manager** en la PS5, selecciona `notify-bridge.elf` y ejecútalo como payload. El bridge debe estar ejecutándose para que la PS5 reciba los mensajes.
4. En PS5 Notify, introduce la IP de la PS5 y el puerto del receptor. El puerto predeterminado es `9055`.
5. El token predeterminado es `ps5notify`. No lo cambies: debe coincidir con el token del `notify-bridge.elf`. El campo aparece bloqueado en la app.
6. Pulsa **Conceder acceso a notificaciones** y autoriza PS5 Notify en los ajustes de Android.
7. Selecciona las aplicaciones que quieras reenviar y guarda la configuración.
8. Usa **Guardar y enviar notificación de prueba** para comprobar la conexión.

Si reinicias la PS5 o vuelves a cargar el entorno de payloads, ejecuta otra vez `notify-bridge.elf` desde Payload Manager antes de usar la app.

## Recepción y comprobación

La recepción en tiempo real se mantiene activa. El intervalo adicional permite revisar de nuevo las notificaciones activas, con un mínimo de 1 minuto y un valor predeterminado de 2 minutos. Puedes cambiarlo desde **Verificar también cada (minutos)**; el nuevo intervalo se aplica al guardar.

Después de conceder el permiso, Android mantiene el servicio de notificaciones aunque la pantalla esté apagada o estés usando otra app, así que puedes dejar el móvil bloqueado mientras juegas. El teléfono debe permanecer encendido, con PS5 Notify instalada, el permiso habilitado y conexión a la misma red que la PS5. Apagar el móvil por completo o forzar la detención de la app impedirá recibir notificaciones.

La opción **Mostrar el contenido del mensaje en la TV** está desactivada por defecto para proteger la privacidad.

repos.readme:
A native PS5 front end for Pegasus DL, made for the couch and a controller.

--- One clean page per game. See what every link is before you press it. Manage your files. Let Pegasus do the downloading. [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Credits](#credits) · [Features](#features) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Guides](#guides) · [Controls](#controls) · [Privacy](#privacy) · [License](#license)
| What Wings is | What Wings is not | |---|---| | A PS5 app (title ID `PPSA99178`) that is a front end & performance patcher for a **Pegasus DL** on the same console, through its local API at `127.0.0.1:6970`. | Not Pegasus DL, not affiliated with its author, and not a replacement for it. Pegasus does the downloading, installing and extracting. | | A better way to browse what Pegasus already knows: games grouped one per tile, links explained, files managed with a controller. | Not a source of games. Wings ships **no catalogues, no sources and no download links**. Only play and use games you legally own and are permitted to install. | | Free software, GPL-3.0-or-later, built on the TV app of Orbit Store. | Not Orbit Store. The only part of Orbit's backend in Wings is its small self-update helper, adapted for Wings (see [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md)). | > **Use it responsibly.** Wings is a front end: it ships no catalogues, sources or links. Use it only with content you own or have permission to download, the same as Pegasus DL asks. > > Wings never bundles or redistributes Pegasus DL, and does nothing if it is already running. If it is not running, the waiting screen offers three choices straight away: load it once, turn on Auto-Load, or load it yourself. Only when you choose, Wings downloads the author's official release from its own release page on github.com, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes, and sends it to the payload loader on this console (`127.0.0.1:9021`). It never sends while Pegasus answers and never writes into any payload manager's folder. See [Pegasus auto-load](docs/guides/pegasus-autoload.md). ## Screenshots > **Only download and install games you own.** Use Wings with your own backups and archives, or with content you have the right to download and install. Wings ships no games, catalogues, sources or links.

The games pictured are free and open-source games, shown with their own openly licensed art ([credits](app/host/fixtures/ART-CREDITS.md)); the pictures are rendered from a stand-in back-end, not a real catalogue. They show what Wings looks like, not where to get games: again, only download and install from your own archives or sources you are permitted to use. ## Credits Wings exists because of other people's work. Thank you. - **Orbit Store**, by **saawant12**: the TV app Wings began as, and the design language that made a controller-first PS5 app feel right. [orbit-store-ps5](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5) - **Pegasus DL**, by the developer(s) at [pegasus-ps5](https://github.com/pegasus-ps5/pegasus-dl): the download manager Wings is a front end for. - **PS5Upload**, by **phantomptr**: a great development environment while building and testing Wings. [ps5upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload) - **ShadowMountPlus**, by **drakmor**: mounts and registers the app and your games. [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) - **kstuff** ([ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/kstuff)) and **kstuff-lite** (by **EchoStretch**, [kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite)). - **BlackBearReloaded**: the PS5 UI kit, boilerplate and tooling (`ps5-homebrew-ui`, `ps5-native-app-boilerplate`, `ps5-opengl`). - **ps5-payload-dev** (SDK and ports) and **SvenGDK** ([SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero)). - Popularity data: **IGDB.com**, **Steam** and **Wikimedia** (see [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md)). Libraries, fonts and versions are listed in full in [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). If something you wrote is missing or wrong there, please open an issue. ## Features - **One game, one page.** The same game from several sources is merged into one tile. Its page groups what is available into Base, Update and DLC, then by release, with every mirror shown as a card. - **Know the link before you press it.** A card shows the host, region, the firmware it needs (and the lowest firmware a back-port runs on), format (exFAT, FPKG, PKG), version and how it will download. Where a link points at a known wrapper page, Wings takes the host from the link's name instead. - **A "Best" pick that explains itself.** A link that needs a newer firmware than yours is never Best while anything else exists. Then: native `.pkg`, debrid, automatic providers, browser capture; then firmware fit, region, format, fewer parts, known size, newest version, source order. The card says why, for example `Debrid · USA · 12.xx · exFAT · 1 file`. See [Link types and what Best means](docs/guides/link-types.md). - **Multi-part archives as one card**, with a warning when a numbered set has gaps, and a **Download all parts** action that asks first and can be stopped with Circle after the part in flight. - **Filters that fit the data.** On a game page: firmware ("Runs on my firmware"), region, format, host, source, single file only, no browser needed. The Store grid has its own filters and a "Single file only" switch. The sort of mirrors inside a release can be Best, newest, fewest parts or host. - **Search like the PlayStation one.** Triangle opens a search box with an on-screen keyboard, results update as you type, recent searches are kept as chips. The touchpad slides over the keys and a click types. - **A Files tab built for a controller.** One list from `/` with drive chips and a breadcrumb, multi-select, copy, move, rename, delete, extract, install `.pkg`, a "Where to?" destination browser, an operations list with a visible way to cancel. - **Archive passwords.** When an archive asks for a password Wings tries six well-known public passwords one at a time before it asks you. See [Archive passwords](docs/guides/archive-passwords.md). - **Everything Pegasus does, in one place.** Downloads queue, Library (installed games and APR Emu), Sources, Logs, and Settings split into **Wings** (kept on the console by Wings) and **Pegasus DL** (changes Pegasus, labelled as such). - **Cover art.** Store posters are downloaded over HTTPS by Wings itself and cached on the console (up to 96 MiB). **On by default**; turn it off in Settings. - **Optional popularity.** Sort by most popular or highest rated, and show a score and rating on tiles, from a small public data file. **On by default**; turn it off in Settings. See [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md). - **Tile details setting.** Store tiles show their link tier and regions Always, On focus (default) or Never. - **Choose where art comes from.** Settings > Wings > Art sources: cover icons from the catalogue (default) or from Prosperopatches (each title's PS5 icon), and the wide picture behind a game's page from every source (default) or from Prosperopatches only (the PS5's own background). - **Updates itself, on your say-so.** Wings checks this project's latest release when it starts and tells you if a newer one exists. You can download it from Settings > Wings > Updates; Wings verifies it (size, SHA-256 and the image itself) and installs it only after you confirm, keeping the old file until the new one is in place. Where the console does not allow the swap, it shows the exact steps. See [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md). ## Install **You need** a PS5 that can run homebrew, with: - **kstuff**, so a fake-signed app starts, and - **ShadowMountPlus**, so the package mounts and its tile appears. This is the same setup Orbit Store asks for. Pegasus DL must be running on the console when you open Wings. 1. Download `PPSA99178.ffpkg` from the [latest release](https://github.com/LaRazaDelSol/wings-app/releases/latest). 2. Check the file. On Windows, in PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\PPSA99178.ffpkg -Algorithm SHA256`. The value must equal the SHA-256 shown on the release page (case does not matter). If it does not, download again. VirusTotal scans: [PPSA99178.ffpkg](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/7597dc7c53f4174302af89aafa1d049745564c0b8f76433b6fade88e4a05105d) · [PPSA99178-Alternative.zip](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/f14f05763f85e9863a8d9b63c0b4ce0c48344cc68b7fa8e2e17026aec84b610e) 3. Copy the file to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (FTP or your usual file transfer). Check that the size on the console equals the size on the release page. 4. Wait about ten seconds. ShadowMountPlus registers it and a **Wings** tile appears in the Games row. 5. Open **Wings**. Wings 0.1.3 and newer update themselves: when a new version is out, Wings offers it and does Download and Install for you; then close Wings and open it again (see [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md)). By hand: replace the file, remove the staged copies ShadowMountPlus made, then close Wings and open it again. To remove Wings, close it, delete `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` (or the folder `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178/`), and restart the jailbreak chain so the tile disappears. Optionally delete `/data/wings/` (diagnostics and a copy of the settings) and `/data/wings-helper/` (the update helper's download). Pegasus DL and its downloads are not touched. Wings writes only to its own folders: `/download0/wings/` (cover cache, settings, diagnostics, bad-link marks, inside the title's storage) and `/data/wings/` (diagnostics and a copy of the settings, so you can read them in the file manager). When you install an update, its helper also writes `/data/wings-helper/` and replaces `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` (keeping the old one as `.old`). ## Quick start 1. Start Pegasus DL on the console and wait until its web UI answers. 2. Open Wings. A pill at the top right says "Connecting", then "Pegasus DL" with its version. If it says **Waiting for Pegasus DL**, Wings keeps trying; start Pegasus. 3. **Store**: tiles for your catalogue, one per game. Triangle searches, Options opens utilities, and the sort and filter button sits in the grid header. 4. Cross on a tile opens its page. The **Best** card is on top; Cross downloads it. Pegasus takes over: watch it in **Downloads**. 5. When it finishes, **Library** shows installed games and **Files** shows where things are. 6. First-run settings worth a look: Settings, **Wings** group, **Link ranking** (your firmware, region and format, so Best fits your console) and **Cover art** / **Popularity data** (both on by default). More detail: [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md). ## Guides | Guide | | |---|---| | [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md) | Tabs, first run, settings to set once | | [Finding and downloading a game](docs/guides/finding-and-downloading.md) | Search, filters, game page, queue | | [Link types and what Best means](docs/guides/link-types.md) | Colours, tiers, the ranking order | | [The Files tab](docs/guides/files-tab.md) | Browse, select, copy, move, extract, install, cancel | | [Archive passwords](docs/guides/archive-passwords.md) | The auto-try, the prompt, "choose what to keep" | | [After a download: ShadowMount scan](docs/guides/after-install-scan.md) | Why a new game waits for Wings to close, and the banner | | [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md) | How Wings tells you about a new release, and how to install it | | [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md) | What is fetched, from where, how to stop it | | [Troubleshooting and FAQ](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md) | Waiting for Pegasus, covers, "extraction failed", diagnostics | ## Controls | Button | In lists and grids | In the keyboard | |---|---|---| | Cross | Open / confirm | Type the key | | Circle | Back / up | Cancel (keeps your old search) | | Square | Favourite a game; select a file | Delete | | Triangle | Search; actions menu in Files | Space (shows the text in a password field) | | Options | Utilities (Store), Filters (game page), Operations (Files) | Run the search | | L1 / R1 | Switch tab | Move the cursor | | R2 | | Run the search | | L2 | | Shift | | R3 / L3 | | Symbols / Clear | | Touchpad | Swipe to scroll or switch tab; click to filter in Files | Slide over the keys, click to type | On a download in Downloads, Cross opens its actions (resume, retry, enter a password, choose what to keep). In Files, while an operation runs, Square cancels it and Triangle opens its destination. ## Privacy Wings has no account, no telemetry that this project operates, and no analytics. To the best of the source tree, the console connects to: | When | To | Why | |---|---|---| | Always | `127.0.0.1:6970` (Pegasus DL on the same console) | Everything Wings shows and does goes through it. | | Cover art **on** (default) | Cloudflare `1.1.1.1` and Google `8.8.8.8` over HTTPS (DNS-over-HTTPS) | Looking up cover servers. They see the host names, for example `image.api.playstation.com`. | | Cover art **on** | The cover servers named in your catalogue's poster URLs, over HTTPS | Downloading the images. Those servers see the console's IP address. | | Only when you press Check, or at most every 6 hours while Settings > Pegasus DL is open (needs Cover art on) | `api.github.com` (the author's release list, one small file) | Showing the latest official Pegasus DL version. GitHub sees the console's IP address. | | Only when you press Download and confirm | `github.com`, then GitHub's `objects.githubusercontent.com` | The official `Pegasus-dl.elf` (about 20 MB), checked against GitHub's SHA-256 before it is saved. Nothing else is accepted. | | Popularity **on** (default) | `larazadelsol.github.io` (GitHub Pages), one file, at most once per 24 hours and once after Wings is updated | Scores and ratings, keyed by title ID. GitHub sees the console's IP address. The file has no user data and Wings sends no identifier beyond a fixed `WingsTV/0.1` User-Agent. | | Known-problem notes or the featured carousel **on** (default) | `larazadelsol.github.io`, two more small files (`notes.v1.json`, `curated.v1.json`), on the same schedule | A short note on games known not to download, and the list of featured games, keyed by title ID. Same User-Agent, no user data. Turn them off in Settings > Wings > Store extras. | | Popularity **on** and Cover art **on**: game-page pictures | The hosts named in the popularity data: `cdn.prosperopatches.com`, `images.igdb.com`, `cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com` (HTTPS) | The 16:9 picture behind a game's page, fetched when you open the page and, ahead of time, for the one game your cursor rests on for half a second (at most one every 6 seconds). Those servers see the console's IP address and the picture asked for. Art sources > *Prosperopatches only* limits this to the first host. | | Art sources set to **Prosperopatches** (off by default; needs Cover art on) | `cdn.prosperopatches.com` over HTTPS | Cover icons and game-page backgrounds, for the titles the popularity data lists there. Prosperopatches sees the console's IP address and the image asked for. | | Update check **on** (default; needs Cover art on) | `api.github.com` (the latest release of this project, one small file), when Wings starts and then at most every 6 hours | Telling you when a newer Wings exists. GitHub sees the console's IP address and the same fixed User-Agent. Turn it off in Settings > Wings > Updates. | | Only when you press Download on the update page | `127.0.0.1:9021` (the payload loader on this console), then the update helper on `127.0.0.1:9178`, which downloads from `github.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` and `objects.githubusercontent.com` | The new Wings package (about 55 MB) and its `.sha256` file, checked before it is kept. GitHub sees the console's IP address. | | Only when you choose **Open TorBox website** | The PS5 browser opens `torbox.app`, through Pegasus DL | Checking what TorBox is preparing for you. Wings itself sends nothing to TorBox. | Turn **Cover art** off and Popularity (which needs it) stops too: Wings then makes **no internet connection at all**. Pegasus DL has its own network behaviour (sources, debrid, downloads); that is Pegasus, not Wings. Details: [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md). The diagnostics report (`/data/wings/diagnostics.txt`) contains no tokens or links and is meant to be safe to share. The title log (`app.log`) can contain Pegasus log lines; read it before posting. ## Build from source From the repository root, inside WSL with Docker: `bash tools/build-wings-wsl.sh` (add `WITH_TEST=1` for the host unit tests and `WITH_PREVIEW=1` for the PNG preview). See [docs/build.md](docs/build.md). The core library (`core/`) builds with any C++17 compiler; see [core/README.md](core/README.md). ## License Wings is free software under the **GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version**, the same license as the Orbit Store TV app it is built on. See [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). It comes with no warranty. Pegasus DL is not part of this project and is not covered by this license.

latestRelease.name: Wings v.0.1.3
latestRelease.body:
## Wings 0.1.3

### Wings updates itself

From now on you never copy files to update Wings. When a new version is out, Wings tells you when it starts and opens an update page with four steps:

1. **Check** - finds the new version.
2. **Download** - downloads it and checks it against the published SHA-256, with progress and Cancel.
3. **Install** - puts it in place in a few seconds. Your current version is kept until the new one runs, so nothing is lost if something goes wrong.
4. **Restart Wings** - close Wings and open it again. That's it.

A small helper inside Wings does the file work (the app itself may not write to `/data/homebrew/`). It only talks to Wings on the console itself, only downloads this project's official package from GitHub, and quits by itself when done. Details: `docs/guides/updating.md`.

### Downloads

- **Dropped downloads reconnect by themselves.** At high speeds some debrid hosts cut connections; Wings now restarts the download automatically (up to 3 tries without progress, more as long as data keeps flowing) and shows "Reconnecting in 8 s (try 2 of 3)". Real errors (file removed, disk full) are never retried. Switch: Settings > Pegasus DL > Auto-reconnect dropped downloads.
- **Circle cancels any waiting screen at once.** "Asking Pegasus DL...", checking a link, Download all parts, loading Pegasus: Circle goes back right away, and a request that answers late changes nothing.
- **.pkg links download fast, then install.** "PKG to PS5" links now go through Pegasus DL's fast download, then install, instead of the PS5's slower downloader. The .pkg is deleted after it installs (Settings > Pegasus DL > Keep PKG files after install). If the fast path is not available, Wings falls back to the PS5's downloader.

### Links

- **Bad links are remembered.** When a link fails for good (file removed, wrong file, broken archive, password never works), Wings marks it on your console and Best stops picking it. The card says "Failed for you on 14 Oct: file removed". Press **Triangle** on a link card to mark or clear one yourself; Settings > Wings lists them. Marks stay on your console and expire after 60 days.

### TorBox

- When TorBox is still preparing a file on its server, Wings now says so and asks again every 30 seconds (Circle stops it) instead of failing.
- **Open TorBox website**: Settings > Pegasus DL > TorBox opens your TorBox dashboard in the PS5 browser.

**Update from 0.1.2 (this one time by hand):** replace `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` with the new file, remove the staged copies ShadowMountPlus made of the old one, close Wings and open it again. After this, Wings updates itself.

**You need:** a jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and ShadowMountPlus, and Pegasus DL (tested with 1.11.0).

Not affiliated with Pegasus DL, Orbit Store or Sony. GPL-3.0-or-later, built on the Orbit Store TV app. Please report bugs with `/data/wings/diagnostics.txt` attached (no tokens or links in it).
