repos.readme:
## PS5GBC

**Game Boy and Game Boy Color Emulator on your PS5, with the original PS5SX2 cover-flow interface.** **v1 — by YAHBALLON** · **App ID: PPSA99210** A GB/GBC-only port based on PS5GBA and mGBA 0.10.5. The GBA core is disabled in this build. ## Features - `.gb` and `.gbc` ROMs only; ZIP containers may contain exactly one GB/GBC ROM. `.gba` files are rejected. - Native 160×144 video, approximately 59.7275 FPS, and stereo output resampled to 48 kHz. - Local, USB and NFS loading; cached library, rescan/reset and recent-first ordering. - Native Vulkan output up to 4K, ORIGINAL / HD SMOOTH / ENHANCED presets, scaling and color settings. - Separate SRAM, RTC battery data and one save-state slot per ROM. - Configurable DualSense buttons, state/menu shortcuts and fast forward. - Yellow handheld logo and GB/GBC Libretro covers with R2 refresh. ## Install and games Download the app ZIP from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5GBC/releases) when available. GitHub's source archives contain source code and must be built first. Extract the **PPSA99210** folder into `/data/homebrew/` or your usual compatible homebrew launcher location. Keep `eboot.bin`, `sce_module/libc.prx`, `sce_sys/`, `lapy.elf` and `lapy-manifest.json` together. ~~~text /data/PS5GBC/games/ /data/PS5GBC/roms/ /data/homebrew/PS5GBC/games/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99210/games/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBC/games/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBC/roms/ ~~~ USB0–7 and recursive subfolders are supported. Configure an NFS share in All games settings, for example `nfs://192.168.1.10/GBC`, then restart. ZIPs must contain one `.gb` or `.gbc`; multi-ROM, encrypted and ZIP64 archives are unsupported. Persistent files live under `/data/PS5GBC/`: battery data in `saves/*.sav` and `saves/*.rtc`, states in `states/`, settings in `gs.ini` and `settings/`, covers/cache in their own folders, and startup output in `logs/boot.log`. Fallback: `/download0/PS5GBC/`. Keep this data when replacing app files. ## Controls | DualSense | GB/GBC | | --- | --- | | Cross / Circle | A / B | | D-pad | Directions | | Options / Create | Start / Select | | Touchpad click | Return to library | | L2 held | Fast forward, muted audio | | L3 + R3 + Up / Down | Save / load state | Square opens settings on the shelf. L1/R1 selects This game / All games; L2/R2 switches Settings / Controls. Button assignments are configurable. R2 on the shelf refreshes the selected cover. Emergency exit: hold L1 + R1 + touchpad for two seconds. ## Graphics and BIOS The copied smooth defaults are **4K / 4K ENHANCED / Stretch / Integer Scaling on / VSync off**. Existing explicit choices take precedence. Stretch takes precedence over integer sizing; use Original for the native **10:9** aspect ratio. Resolution/VSync need an app restart; VSync-off requires immediate presentation support from the driver. The independent edge-aware shader enhances presentation; internal GB/GBC resolution stays 160×144. No HD sprite replacement or platform JIT is used. mGBA detects the appropriate Game Boy model. An external BIOS is optional: `bios/gb_bios.bin` for DMG or `bios/gbc_bios.bin` for GBC. BIOS skipping is enabled by default. No BIOS or commercial ROM is included. ## Covers On-demand artwork uses the Libretro [Game Boy](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy/Named_Boxarts/) and [Game Boy Color](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy%20Color/Named_Boxarts/) collections. Filename/title/region matching uses a bundled 3,160-name index; successful downloads are cached. No-Intro-style names work best. Local PNG/JPEG covers can be placed in `covers/` using the ROM filename without its extension or displayed serial. ## Build and tests ~~~sh PS5GBC_DEPS=/path/to/prepared/ps5-build bash gbc/tools/build.sh python3 gbc/tools/test.py ~~~ See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) and [TESTING.md](TESTING.md). First PS5 console validation is pending. Host tests execute original GB/GBC homebrew, verify real video/audio, input, SRAM/state/RTC support, ZIP loading and Vulkan rendering. Camera, motion sensors, multiplayer and general firmware compatibility are not established. ## Credits and license YAHBALLON / Globaleliteee; Spyros and the PS5SX2/PS5SNES frontend contributors; mGBA contributors; PS5 Vulkan/native tooling, Lapy, Libretro thumbnails and dependency authors. Frontend/integration: GPL-3.0-or-later. mGBA: MPL-2.0. See [COPYING.GPLv3](COPYING.GPLv3) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). This port adds a minimal libretro framebuffer-pointer reset on deinit and a GB-only declaration compatibility header; both are included in the source.

repos.readme:
# PS5GBA

**Game Boy Advance games on your PS5, with the original PS5SX2 cover-flow interface.** **v2 — by YAHBALLON** · **App ID: PPSA99209** PS5GBA is a native PS5 homebrew Game Boy Advance emulator using **mGBA 0.10.5**. It reuses the working PS5SNES frontend while keeping the PS5SX2 shelf, animated game cases, cover glow, reflections, menu sounds and settings panel. The integration and upstream components retain their respective licenses. **Release status:** the v2 build requires a console retest. This repository contains source; installable application ZIPs must be built and attached separately to a GitHub release. See [RELEASE_NOTES.md](RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [TESTING.md](TESTING.md). ## Features A native Vulkan interface with the supplied blue Game Boy Advance launcher logo. - Play **`.gba` ROMs** from internal storage, USB or an **NFSv3 share**. - Load ZIP archives containing **one GBA ROM**, decompressed directly into RAM. - Native GBA emulation at **240 × 160**, approximately **59.7275 FPS**. - Display output up to **3840 × 2160**, with 1080p selection and display-dependent fallback. - **ORIGINAL**, **4K HD SMOOTH** and **4K ENHANCED** graphics modes. - Aspect-ratio, stretch and integer scaling, plus adjustable sharpness, contrast and color boost. - Automatic Libretro GBA box-art downloads, local cover support and **R2 cover refresh**. - Cached game library, visible loading progress, library reset/rescan and recent-first ordering. - Battery-backed saves and **one save-state slot per ROM**. - Configurable GBA buttons and save/load/menu shortcuts, globally or per game. - Fast forward with muted game audio. - Controller-operated NFS URL keyboard and a QR web settings page. - Bounded cover streaming for large libraries, with downloaded covers cached on disk. - Built-in BIOS fallback; an optional user-provided GBA BIOS is supported. ## Install 1. Download the **application ZIP** from the release assets and extract it. 2. Copy the complete **PPSA99209** folder to: ~~~text /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/ ~~~ 3. Launch it with your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. Keep every packaged file, including `sce_module/libc.prx`, `lapy.elf`, `lapy-manifest.json` and `sce_sys/icon0.png`. Games, saves and settings live separately in `/data/PS5GBA/`. For an update, replace the application files and restart the app. Preserve the data folder. Refresh the launcher if it still shows the old icon. The filesystem helper is restricted to this app's title ID. If filesystem access is unavailable, the helper may require the local ELF loader on port **9021**. A normal retail PS5 cannot run this homebrew app. ## Add games ### Internal storage ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/games/ ~~~ These folders are also supported: ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/roms/ /data/homebrew/PS5GBA/games/ /data/homebrew/PS5GBA/roms/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/games/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/roms/ /data/GBA/ ~~~ ### USB ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBA/games/ ~~~ USB0 through USB7 are supported. Alternative folders include: ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBA/roms/ /mnt/usb0/PS5GBA/games/ /mnt/usb0/PS5GBA/roms/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99209/games/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99209/roms/ /mnt/usb0/GBA/ ~~~ Subfolders are scanned up to five levels deep. Games found in these folders are presented in one library. ### NFS Open **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → NFS URL**. Example: ~~~text nfs://192.168.1.10/GBA ~~~ Save the URL and restart PS5GBA. URLs can also be entered in `/data/PS5GBA/nfs.txt`, one share per line. The app connects directly to the server. ROMs are read into RAM when launched; no PS5 kernel mount is required. Clear saved URLs in All games settings when a share is no longer needed. ### ZIP support Use **one `.gba` image per ZIP**. Stored and Deflate compression are supported. - Maximum ROM size: **32 MiB**. - Maximum ZIP/file size: **64 MiB**. - Encrypted, multi-ROM and ZIP64 archives are not supported. - A ZIP containing an entire ROM collection must be unpacked into individual ROMs or individual game ZIPs on your server. ## Graphics settings Open **Square → Settings → Graphics**. Choose **All games** for global defaults or **This game** for an override. | Setting | v2 default | | --- | --- | | Output resolution | **4K** | | Graphics mode | **4K ENHANCED** | | Scaling | **Stretch** | | Integer scaling | **On** | | VSync | **Off** | | Adaptive sharpness | 25% | | Color boost | 15% | | Contrast | 105% | | Display color correction | Off | | FPS counter | Off | These five main defaults match a configuration reported to run smoothly on PS5. Existing explicitly saved choices are preserved. **Stretch takes precedence over integer sizing.** Integer scaling becomes effective when using the original 3:2 aspect ratio. Resolution and VSync are global startup settings and require an app restart. Other graphics choices apply when the next game starts. VSync-off requires an immediate presentation mode from the Vulkan driver; if unavailable, the app logs the FIFO fallback. ### Graphics modes | Mode | Presentation | | --- | --- | | ORIGINAL | Nearest-neighbor pixels, original colors and no sharpening. | | 4K HD SMOOTH | Independent edge-aware pixel-art filtering with diagonal interpolation. | | 4K ENHANCED | Edge-aware filtering with restrained color boost, contrast and adaptive sharpening. | 4K describes the **output framebuffer**. GBA emulation and original artwork remain **240 × 160**; filters do not create newly drawn HD sprites. The edge-aware shader is independently implemented. Experimental high-resolution mGBA OpenGL rendering is not enabled. ## Controls ### Game shelf | Action | Default | | --- | --- | | Browse games | D-pad / left stick, left and right | | Start game | Cross | | Open settings | Square | | Refresh selected cover | R2 | | This game / All games | L1 / R1 in settings | | Settings / Controls tab | L2 / R2 in settings | ### In game | GBA action | Default controller button | | --- | --- | | A | Cross | | B | Circle | | L | L1 | | R | R1 | | Start | Options | | Select | Create | | Directions | D-pad; left stick also enabled by default | | Emulator shortcut | Default | | --- | --- | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return to shelf | Touchpad click | | Fast forward | Hold L2; game audio is muted | ### Customize your buttons Open **Square → R2 / Controls** to view and edit assignments. - Choose **All games** for global defaults or **This game** for an override. - Left/right or Cross cycles an assignment. - Fast forward has a configurable held-button assignment. - Each save/load/menu shortcut has up to three button fields. **None** skips a field; all None disables the shortcut. - Settings save immediately and apply when the next game is started. - Save/load shortcuts trigger once per press and consume their bound game inputs. - Holding **L1 + R1 + touchpad click for two seconds** remains an emergency route back to the shelf. Saving a new state overwrites that ROM's previous state slot. Battery saves are written periodically and when returning to the menu. Content-derived save names avoid collisions between similarly named games. Incompatible or unreadable existing battery saves are preserved rather than silently replaced. ## Library cache and recent games The first successful scan creates a local index. Subsequent starts reuse the NFS index while checking local/USB folders for changes. Offline server detection is bounded so local games remain available. After changing games on an NFS share, choose: **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → Rescan game library** Then restart PS5GBA. Library reset and NFS URL removal are also available in All games settings. Changing the share configuration selects a separate cache. The loading bar indicates activity while the total directory size is unknown, with live game and entry counts. Under **Library**, choose **Recent games first** to show recently launched games at the front after restarting. The last played game is also remembered for selection. This is library ordering, not a separate recent-games screen. ## Covers Automatic box art uses the [Libretro GBA Named_Boxarts collection](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy%20Advance/Named_Boxarts/). The app includes a **5,959-filename index**, with exact filename and normalized title/region matching. No-Intro-style ROM/ZIP names work best. Matching handles common accents, such as Pokémon, and ignores bracketed tags during normalized lookup. Images are downloaded on demand; the artwork itself is not bundled. Press **R2** on the shelf to refresh the selected cover. The previous image is retained if the refresh fails. For a custom cover: ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/covers/Game Name (USA).png ~~~ Match the game filename without its extension, or use its displayed GBA serial. PNG and JPEG are supported. Only nearby artwork is kept live; downloaded covers remain cached on disk. Successful cached covers are reused. The v2 negative-lookup cache is separate from the previous cover source so old failed lookups do not block the new collection. ## BIOS A proprietary BIOS is **not required** for normal use: mGBA provides a built-in fallback. If you have your own GBA BIOS, place it at: ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/bios/gba_bios.bin ~~~ No BIOS is included in the release. BIOS skipping is enabled by default in the current runtime. ## App data and logs | Content | Location | | --- | --- | | Games | `/data/PS5GBA/games/` or `/data/PS5GBA/roms/` | | Battery saves | `/data/PS5GBA/saves/` | | Save states | `/data/PS5GBA/states/` | | Optional BIOS | `/data/PS5GBA/bios/gba_bios.bin` | | Global settings | `/data/PS5GBA/gs.ini` | | Per-game settings | `/data/PS5GBA/settings/` | | Recent games | `/data/PS5GBA/recent-games.txt` | | Custom covers | `/data/PS5GBA/covers/` | | Library, cover and shader caches | `/data/PS5GBA/cache/` | | Boot log | `/data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log` | | Cover download errors | `/data/PS5GBA/logs/cover-download.log` | | NFS URLs | `/data/PS5GBA/nfs.txt` | If `/data` is unavailable, the app uses `/download0/PS5GBA/` as its fallback data folder. The QR settings page listens on **port 8844** and can provide logs. Routine mGBA BIOS/DMA DEBUG and INFO traces are suppressed in v2 to avoid continuous disk writes during gameplay. Core warnings and errors remain available. ## Build from source See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for the dependency layout and build instructions, and [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for release preparation. ~~~sh PS5GBA_DEPS=/path/to/prepared/ps5-build bash gba/tools/build.sh ~~~ The active adapter/runtime is in **`gba/src/`**, the upstream core is in **`gba/third_party/mgba/`**, and the native interface uses **`ps5/frontend/`** directly. The GBA build does not compile a SNES or PS2 emulator core. The required PS5 SDK/Vulkan/network dependencies are prepared externally, as in the PS5SNES build. Run the host regression suite with: ~~~sh python3 gba/tools/test.py ~~~ ## Current limits and testing - One active player in the current integration. - One save-state slot per ROM; states are tied to the core/version. Keep battery saves for portability. - Tilt, gyro, solar-sensor controls and multiplayer are not exposed. - No separate in-game pause overlay or folder-tree browser; touchpad returns to the shelf and subfolders are scanned recursively. - General firmware compatibility and sustained PS5 GPU performance across games have not been established. - A user tested GBA games on PS5 and reported smooth gameplay after selecting the configuration now used as the v2 defaults. The new v2 build still needs a console retest. - Historical host test reports describe real ARM execution, 240 × 160 video, audio, GBA timing, controller input, SRAM/state persistence, ZIP loading, settings, audio resampling and actual Vulkan rendering through 4K. - Pokémon Emerald and the German Smaragd-Edition cover matches were checked against live, valid PNG downloads. - See [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for the remaining console checklist, including Flash/EEPROM and RTC cartridges. - No commercial ROMs, proprietary BIOS files or console keys are included. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** — project customization and supplied logo. - **Spyros and PCSX2 contributors** — original PS5SX2 interface and shared frontend. - [mGBA contributors](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) — Game Boy Advance emulation; **MPL-2.0**. - [mihawk-99 / PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) — native Vulkan driver and runtime work. - [BlackBearReloaded / ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) — native startup and packaging tooling. - [Lapy filesystem helper](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon) — restricted filesystem helper. - [Libretro thumbnails](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/) — box-art collection. - Libnfs, libcurl, OpenSSL, zlib, zstd, libpsl and the bundled font/library authors. SkyEmu was a presentation reference; no SkyEmu code was incorporated. The edge/color shader is independently implemented. PS5GBA integration code is **GPL-3.0-or-later**. Upstream components retain their own licenses and notices. See [COPYING.GPLv3](COPYING.GPLv3), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and the included license files. ## v2 by YAHBALLON (AI-assisted) Adds automatic Libretro GBA covers with normalized title/region matching, local caching and R2 refresh. Changes the default graphics configuration to **4K / 4K ENHANCED / Stretch / Integer Scaling on / VSync off**, based on the user's successful console configuration. Suppresses repeated core BIOS/DMA traces while retaining warnings and errors. Existing explicit settings and saves are retained. Earlier native builds, cover checks and host core tests were reported as passing; these have not been rerun for this checkout, and the updated release still needs console testing.

# PS5SNES

PS5SNES is a standalone PS5 homebrew emulator using the **bsnes-mercury balanced** core and the original PS5SX2 cover-flow interface. It is a separate project with its own application ID (`PPSA99205`) and data directory (`/data/PS5SNES`). Development and documentation were **AI-assisted**. ## Latest update - Local and USB folders are scanned at startup even when a library cache exists. - Offline IPv4 NAS checks avoid long startup retries and preserve local games. - Empty-library hints use the correct PS5SNES folders and disappear when games are present. - Press **R2** on the shelf to refresh the selected game's cover. The existing image is retained if downloading fails. - The [SNES cover repository](https://github.com/Globaleliteee/Gaming_Console_Covers_Art_Repository/tree/main/covers/nintendo/SNES) supplies an index of **723 filenames**. Matching handles case, region, revision/language tags and common title punctuation, with libretro-thumbnails fallback. - Earlier failed cover lookups are retried with the new cover-cache namespace. - Menu branding is **v6 by YAHBALLON**. The v6 repository URLs and image decoding were tested on the host. Validate the new cover behavior on your PS5; compatibility across all ROM naming variants is not guaranteed. The SNES core remains bsnes-mercury balanced. ## Features - Animated game shelf with a charcoal and violet SNES theme. - Cartridge formats: `.sfc`, `.smc`, `.swc`, `.fig`, including common 512-byte copier headers. - Single-ROM ZIP loading in memory, with Stored or Deflate compression. - Games from internal storage, USB and directly configured NFSv3 shares. - Fast cached game library and a loading screen with scan progress. - Battery saves, save/load states and configurable controller buttons and shortcuts. - Native-clock stereo audio converted continuously to the PS5's 48 kHz audio output. - Cover support and a local settings page accessible from a phone or computer. ## Installation Use the application ZIP from a release. Copy its complete `PPSA99205` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99205/` and launch it through your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. Keep the included modules, filesystem helper and `sce_sys` files together. The source archive is for development; it does not contain an installable executable. Place games in `/data/PS5SNES/games/`, or on USB in `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5SNES/games/`. USB0 through USB7 are supported. Additional USB folders and full installation details are in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). For NFS, open **All games → Settings → Network**, enter your export URL (for example `nfs://192.168.0.87/SNES`), save and restart the app. Use **Rescan game library** after changing the files on a share. The example URL is not an automatically configured server. Configuration, saves, covers, cache and logs live under `/data/PS5SNES/`. The app uses `/download0/PS5SNES/` as a fallback when necessary. The local web settings page uses port **8844**. ## Default controls | SNES / action | DualSense | | --- | --- | | A / B | Circle / Cross | | X / Y | Triangle / Square | | L / R | L1 / R1 | | Start | Options | | Select | Touchpad click / Create | | Directions | D-pad / left stick | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return to game shelf | L1 + R1 + Touchpad click | Open **Square → R2 / Controls** to customize buttons globally or per game. The menu combination also provides a two-second emergency hold after remapping. There is one save-state slot per ROM. ## Building from source See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for the dependency layout and public upstream projects. The console build requires Linux/WSL, Clang/LLD 18 and a prepared public PS5 SDK, PS5_Vulkan, libnfs and HTTPS dependency environment. ```bash PS5SNES_DEPS=/path/to/prepared/deps bash snes/tools/build.sh ``` Output: `snes/build-shelf/PS5SNES-v6-Repository-Covers-by-YAHBALLON.zip`. The inherited root PCSX2 CMake project is not the PS5SNES app build entry point. Use the script above. Prepared binary dependencies are not included in this source archive; a complete fresh-machine dependency bootstrap is not provided. Run the host integration test on Linux/WSL with Clang 18, Make and host zlib development headers: ```bash python3 snes/tools/test.py ``` The test generates original LoROM and SPC700 code and checks real emulation, video, audio, controller inputs, battery saves, save states, ZIP loading, copier headers and PAL timing. No commercial ROM or Nintendo firmware is supplied. The build also verifies native memory parameters and signed executable integrity. For a reproducible source ZIP and checksum verification, see [GITHUB_UPDATE.md](GITHUB_UPDATE.md). ## Scope and compatibility Normal SNES cartridges and one active player are exposed. Enhancement-chip HLE is used where supported. Super Game Boy, Satellaview, Sufami Turbo, MSU-1 external data and light guns are not integrated into this frontend. Automated testing was performed on the host. Successful PS5 operation has been reported by the user; compatibility and performance across all games have not been exhaustively tested. ## Project layout | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `snes/src/` | SNES frontend integration, storage, controller mapping and runtime | | `snes/tools/` | Console build, memory checks and host tests | | `snes/third_party/bsnes-mercury/` | Vendored, pinned SNES core | | `snes/sce_sys/` | App metadata and launcher icon | | `snes/assets/` | Supplied original logo | | `ps5/frontend/` | Original PS5SX2 shelf and settings interface | | `ps5/proto/native/` | Native application tooling | ## Credits and licenses - **YAHBALLON** — customization and supplied logo. - **Spyros and PCSX2 contributors** — original PS5SX2 frontend and scaffold. - **bsnes-mercury / Libretro contributors** — SNES emulation core. - **mihawk-99, BlackBearReloaded, Lapy and supporting library contributors** — PS5 graphics, SDK, native tooling and filesystem support. Integration code is GPL-3.0-or-later. Preserve the original component notices and license texts when redistributing. See [COPYING.GPLv3](COPYING.GPLv3) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). This project is not affiliated with Nintendo, Sony or the upstream projects.

repos.readme:
# PS5N64

PS5N64 is a native PS5 homebrew Nintendo 64 emulator using the **ParaLLEl N64 / Mupen64Plus core**. It keeps the original PS5SX2-style shelf, animated game cases, cover glow, reflections, menu sounds and settings panel, with a Nintendo 64 backend. The current renderer is **Angrylion** at native internal resolution. ## Features A green, charcoal and gray Nintendo 64-inspired theme with the supplied launcher logo. - Play **`.z64`**, **`.v64`** and **`.n64`** Nintendo 64 ROMs. - Play ZIP archives containing **one supported N64 ROM**, decompressed directly into RAM. - Load games from internal storage, USB or an **NFSv3 share**. - Automatic Nintendo 64 box-art downloads and custom local covers. - Original animated PS5SX2-style cover-flow game shelf. - Cached NFS game library for fast repeat launches. - Fresh local and USB scanning on startup. - Battery-backed saves and **Controller Pak saves**. - **One save-state slot per ROM**. - Native analog-stick input. - Right-stick C-button controls. - Configurable digital buttons and emulator shortcuts. - Global and per-game controller configurations. - Stereo audio at **48 kHz**. - Audio prebuffering, short underrun fades and bounded queue latency. - Fast bounded IPv4 offline-server detection for configured NFS servers. - Controller-operated NFS configuration. - Local web settings. - Bounded cover streaming for large libraries. - No Nintendo boot firmware required. - No executable-memory JIT is used. ## Install 1. Download **`PS5N64-v7-Audio-Fix-modded-by-YAHBALLON.zip`** from the release assets and extract it. 2. Copy/install the complete **`PPSA99206`** application folder using your compatible PS5 homebrew environment. The application folder should be: ```text /data/homebrew/PPSA99206/ ``` 3. Launch PS5N64 with your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. Keep every packaged application file. Your existing games, saves, settings, covers and cache live separately under: ```text /data/PS5N64/ ``` For an update, replace the application files and restart PS5N64. Refresh your homebrew launcher if it still displays the old icon or application information. A normal retail PS5 cannot run this homebrew application without a compatible homebrew environment. ## Add games ### Internal storage ```text /data/PS5N64/games/ ``` ### USB Primary folder: ```text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5N64/games/ ``` USB0 through USB7 are supported. These alternative folders are also scanned: ```text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5N64/roms/ /mnt/usb0/PS5N64/games/ /mnt/usb0/N64/ ``` Local and USB locations are freshly scanned when PS5N64 starts, even when an existing library cache is present. ### NFS Open the **All games** settings and configure your NFS URL. Example: ```text nfs://192.168.0.87/N64 ``` This address is only a configuration example and is not a tested public export. PS5N64 connects directly to the configured **NFSv3** server. NFS game listings use a local cache so that the application does not need to perform a full network scan on every startup. A bounded IPv4 availability check is used so an offline NAS does not stall startup for an excessive amount of time. If the configured NFS server is unavailable, cached NFS games and available local games can remain visible. Configuration, cache, saves and logs are stored under: ```text /data/PS5N64/ ``` If `/data` is unavailable, PS5N64 can use: ```text /download0/PS5N64/ ``` as a writable fallback. ### ZIP support A ZIP archive must contain exactly **one supported Nintendo 64 ROM**. Supported ROM extensions inside ZIP archives: ```text .z64 .v64 .n64 ``` Stored and Deflate ZIP compression are supported. Multi-ROM archives should be unpacked into individual ROM files or individual game ZIP archives. ## Default controls ### Game shelf | Action | Default | | --- | --- | | Browse games | D-pad / left stick, left and right | | Start game | Cross | | Open settings | Square | | This game / All games | L1 / R1 in settings | | Settings / Controls tab | L2 / R2 in settings | ### In game | N64 action | Default DualSense control | | --- | --- | | Analog stick | Left stick | | C directions | Right stick | | A | Cross | | B | Square | | C Up | Triangle | | C Down | Circle | | Z | L2 | | L | L1 | | R | R1 | | Start | Options | | D-pad | D-pad | ### Emulator shortcuts | Emulator shortcut | Default combination | | --- | --- | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return to shelf | L1 + R1 + Touchpad click | ## Customize your buttons Digital buttons and emulator shortcuts can be configured globally or per game. - Choose **All games** for global defaults. - Choose **This game** for a per-game override. - Analog movement uses the DualSense left stick. - N64 C directions use the right stick by default. - Save and load-state shortcuts can be remapped. - The menu/exit shortcut can be remapped. - A **two-second emergency hold** remains available for returning to the game shelf. - Settings apply when the game is launched again. One active controller is currently exposed by the PS5 frontend. Saving a new state overwrites that ROM's previous state slot. Battery-backed cartridge saves and Controller Pak data are stored separately from the application files. ## Library cache PS5N64 maintains a cached game library for configured NFS shares. Local and USB folders are scanned freshly at startup, even if an existing library cache is available. This allows newly added or removed local games to appear without requiring a full NFS rescan. Cached NFS entries help reduce startup delays and allow previously indexed network titles to remain visible when an IPv4 NAS is temporarily offline. ### Reset library Open: **All games → Settings → Reset library** Use this after major changes to your library or when you want PS5N64 to rebuild its cached game information. Restart PS5N64 after resetting the library. ROMs and save files are **not deleted**. ### Clear NFS configuration Open: **All games → Settings → Clear all NFS URLs** This removes the configured NFS addresses. Restart PS5N64 after using this action. Your ROMs and save files are retained. ## Covers Automatic box-art downloads use the Nintendo 64 filename index from: https://github.com/Globaleliteee/Gaming_Console_Covers_Art_Repository/tree/main/covers/nintendo/N64 The current repository contains an index of **801 Nintendo 64 front covers**. Cover matching uses the ROM filename and understands title and region information. Additional ROM revision or language tags do not prevent a valid match. Existing failed cover lookups are retried after this update. A **libretro-thumbnails fallback** is also available when an appropriate primary cover is not found. For best results, use clean ROM filenames with recognizable game titles and region tags. Downloaded artwork remains cached locally. Only a bounded amount of nearby artwork is kept active in memory while browsing large libraries. ## Audio PS5N64 outputs stereo audio at: ```text 48000 Hz ``` v7 introduces additional audio handling intended to reduce crackling caused by short emulation stalls. This includes: - Audio prebuffering. - Short underrun fades. - Recovery after short stalls. - Bounded audio queue latency. Audio cannot compensate for sustained slow emulation. If emulation remains below full speed for an extended period, audio interruptions or crackling can still occur. ## Renderer and performance The current PS5N64 build uses: - **ParaLLEl N64 / Mupen64Plus** - Cached interpreter - HLE RSP - **Angrylion software rendering** - Native **1x internal rendering resolution** - 4K PS5 display output The PS5 can output the application at 4K, but the Nintendo 64 scene itself is currently rendered internally at native resolution and then presented by the frontend. **ParaLLEl-RDP upscaling is not currently integrated.** **Gopher64 is not currently integrated.** No executable-memory JIT is enabled in this build. Performance varies between games. Full-speed playback is **not guaranteed** and commercial-game compatibility still requires additional testing on real PS5 hardware. ## Current limits - One active controller is currently exposed. - Multiplayer is not exposed by the current frontend. - 64DD is not exposed. - Transfer Pak is not exposed. - VRU is not exposed. - Rumble is not exposed. - ParaLLEl-RDP upscaling is not integrated. - Gopher64 is not integrated. - The current renderer is Angrylion at 1x internal resolution. - No executable-memory JIT is enabled. - General firmware compatibility has not been established. - Performance varies by game. - Full-speed playback is not guaranteed. - Sustained slow emulation can interrupt audio. - Broader real-console testing is still required. - No copyrighted ROMs, Nintendo firmware or console keys are included. ## Latest changes ### v7 — by YAHBALLON - Interface is now **English regardless of the PS5 console language**. - Local and USB folders receive a fresh scan even when a library cache already exists. - Added fast bounded IPv4 offline-NAS detection. - Cached NFS games remain available when the configured network server is unavailable. - Local games remain available when an NFS server is offline. - Added **Reset library** to the All games settings. - Added **Clear all NFS URLs** to the All games settings. - ROMs and saves are retained when using these reset actions. - Added audio prebuffering. - Added audio underrun recovery. - Added short underrun fades to reduce audible crackling from temporary stalls. - Added bounded audio queue latency. - Menu version label updated to: ```text v7 by YAHBALLON ``` ## App data and logs PS5N64 stores application data separately from the installed application. Primary data folder: ```text /data/PS5N64/ ``` Writable fallback: ```text /download0/PS5N64/ ``` Typical content includes: | Content | Location | | --- | --- | | Games | `/data/PS5N64/games/` | | Saves and states | `/data/PS5N64/saves/` | | Settings | `/data/PS5N64/` | | Covers | `/data/PS5N64/covers/` | | Library cache | `/data/PS5N64/cache/` | | Logs | `/data/PS5N64/logs/` | Exact files may vary between builds. ## Build from source Prepare the required dependencies and run: ```bash PS5N64_DEPS=/path/to/prepared/deps bash n64/tools/build.sh ``` The build uses the existing public PS5 development environment together with components including: - PS5 SDK/toolchain - PS5_Vulkan - libnfs - Static HTTPS dependencies - ParaLLEl N64 / Mupen64Plus components - Angrylion renderer Core objects and frontend objects are built outside their source directories. The current emulator configuration uses a cached interpreter, HLE RSP and Angrylion software rendering. No executable-memory JIT is enabled. ## Host tests On Linux with **Clang 18**, run: ```bash python3 n64/tools/test.py ``` The supplied host test uses original test code and does **not** contain commercial Nintendo games or Nintendo boot firmware. The test generates original MIPS cartridge code and validates: - ROM startup. - Framebuffer output. - Audio DMA. - Analog input. - C-button input. - Battery-backed saves. - Save-state roundtrip. - Loading a second ROM. Passing the host tests does not guarantee compatibility or full performance on real PS5 hardware. Real-console testing remains necessary. ## Development notes PS5N64 is based on the PS5SNES/PS5SX2-style frontend structure but uses a separate Nintendo 64 emulator backend. The original project scaffold and frontend components are retained where useful while Nintendo 64 emulation is handled through the N64 core. Development and source modifications were **AI-assisted**. AI-assisted development does not replace hardware validation, compatibility testing or review of the upstream emulator implementations. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** — project customization, integration and supplied assets. - **Spyros and PCSX2 contributors** — original PS5SX2 interface and project scaffold. - **ParaLLEl N64 / Mupen64Plus contributors** — Nintendo 64 emulation. - **Angrylion contributors** — Nintendo 64 software rendering. - **Libretro contributors** — emulator ecosystem and supporting components. - [mihawk-99 / PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) — native Vulkan driver and runtime work. - [Globaleliteee / Gaming Console Covers Art Repository](https://github.com/Globaleliteee/Gaming_Console_Covers_Art_Repository) — Nintendo 64 cover-art index. - libnfs and the bundled networking/library authors. - All additional third-party component authors and contributors. When redistributing PS5N64, preserve the upstream notices and included GPL/component licenses. Upstream components retain their original licenses. Source modifications were AI-assisted. ## Disclaimer PS5N64 is an independent homebrew project. It is **not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by Nintendo, Sony Interactive Entertainment, PCSX2, Mupen64Plus, ParaLLEl N64 or their respective contributors**. "PlayStation", "PS5", "Nintendo", "Nintendo 64" and related names and trademarks belong to their respective owners. Game names, artwork and other copyrighted material belong to their respective owners. No copyrighted commercial ROMs, Nintendo firmware or console keys are distributed with PS5N64. Please use your own legally obtained games.

# PS5NES

PS5NES is a native PS5 homebrew NES emulator using **FCEUmm**. It keeps the PS5SX2 shelf, animated game cases, cover glow, reflections, menu sounds and settings panel, with a NES backend. **NES games on your PS5, with the original PS5SX2 cover-flow interface.** **v1.0.0.9 — by YAHBALLON** · **App ID: PPSA99204** ## Features A red, charcoal and gray NES-inspired theme with the supplied controller-style launcher logo. - Play **iNES / NES 2.0** ROMs and **UNIF** images. - Load games from internal storage, USB or an **NFSv3 share**. - Play ZIP archives containing **one NES ROM**, decompressed directly into RAM. - Automatic NES box-art downloads and custom local covers. - A cached game library for fast repeat launches, with a loading screen for discovery. - Battery-backed saves and **one save-state slot per ROM**. - Configurable NES buttons and save/load/menu shortcuts, globally or per game. - A controller-operated NFS URL keyboard and a QR web settings page. - Bounded cover streaming for large libraries. - No PS2 BIOS required. ## Interface preview ![NES red theme](docs/images/nes-red-shelf.png) Host-rendered preview with demo titles. The app keeps the original PS5SX2 shelf layout. ## Install 1. Download the **application ZIP** from the release assets and extract it. 2. Copy the complete **PPSA99204** folder to: ~~~text /data/homebrew/PPSA99204/ ~~~ 3. Launch it with your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. Keep every packaged file, including sce_module/libc.prx, lapy.elf, lapy-manifest.json and sce_sys/icon0.png. Your existing games, saves and settings live separately in /data/PS5NES/. For an update, replace the application files and restart the app. Refresh the launcher if it still shows the old icon. The filesystem helper is restricted to this app's title ID. If filesystem access is unavailable, it needs the local ELF loader on port **9021**. A normal retail PS5 cannot run this homebrew app. ## Add games ### Internal storage ~~~text /data/PS5NES/games/ /data/homebrew/PS5NES/games/ /data/homebrew/PS5NES/roms/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99204/roms/ ~~~ ### USB ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5NES/games/ ~~~ USB0 through USB7 are supported. These alternative folders are also scanned: ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5NES/roms/ /mnt/usb0/PS5NES/games/ /mnt/usb0/NES/ ~~~ Subfolders are scanned up to five levels deep. Internal ROM detection also handles mounts that deny file metadata. ### NFS Open **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → NFS URL**. Example: ~~~text nfs://192.168.1.10/NES ~~~ Save the URL and restart PS5NES. The same configuration can be entered in /data/PS5NES/nfs.txt, one URL per line, with up to four shares. The app connects directly to the server. ROMs are read into RAM when launched; no PS5 kernel mount is required. ### ZIP support Use **one .nes, .unf or .unif image per ZIP**. Stored and Deflate compression are supported. - Maximum ROM size: **32 MiB** - Maximum ZIP/file size: **64 MiB** - Encrypted, multi-ROM and ZIP64 archives are not supported. - A ZIP containing an entire ROM collection must be unpacked into individual ROMs or individual game ZIPs on your server. ## Controls ### Game shelf | Action | Default | | --- | --- | | Browse games | D-pad / left stick, left and right | | Start game | Cross | | Open settings | Square | | This game / All games | L1 / R1 in settings | | Settings / Controls tab | L2 / R2 in settings | ### In game | NES action | Default controller button | | --- | --- | | A | Cross | | B | Circle | | Start | Options | | Select | Touchpad click or Create | | Directions | D-pad; left stick also enabled by default | | Emulator shortcut | Default combination | | --- | --- | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return to shelf | L1 + R1 + touchpad click | ### Customize your buttons Open **Square → R2 / Controls** to view and edit assignments. - Choose **All games** for global defaults or **This game** for an override. - Left/right or Cross cycles an assignment. - Each emulator shortcut has up to three button fields. **None** skips a field; all None disables that shortcut. - Settings save immediately and apply when the next game is started. - Save/load shortcuts trigger once per press and consume their bound game inputs. - Holding **L1 + R1 + touchpad click for two seconds** remains an emergency route back to the shelf. Saving a new state overwrites that ROM's previous state slot. Battery saves are written every five seconds and when returning to the menu. ## Library cache The first successful scan creates a local index. Internal and USB folders are scanned at every startup; later starts reuse the NFS index without rescanning the share. After adding, removing or renaming games, choose: **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → Rescan game library** Then restart PS5NES. Changing the NFS URL selects a separate cache automatically. The loading bar indicates activity while the total directory size is unknown. Live game and entry counts are shown. ## Covers Automatic box art uses the bundled 742-entry NES repository index, with [Libretro NES thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails/Nintendo_-_Nintendo_Entertainment_System) as a fallback. Matching handles title punctuation and region tags; No-Intro-style filenames work best. Press **R2 on the shelf** to refresh the selected cover. The previous cover is retained if downloading fails. For your own cover: ~~~text /data/PS5NES/covers/Game Name (USA).png ~~~ Match the game filename without its extension. PNG and JPEG are supported. Only nearby artwork is kept live; downloaded covers remain cached on disk. ## App data and logs | Content | Location | | --- | --- | | Games | /data/PS5NES/games/ | | Saves and states | /data/PS5NES/saves/ | | Global settings | /data/PS5NES/gs.ini | | Per-game settings | /data/PS5NES/settings/ | | Custom covers | /data/PS5NES/covers/ | | Library, cover and shader caches | /data/PS5NES/cache/ | | Boot log | /data/PS5NES/logs/boot.log | | Cover download errors | /data/PS5NES/logs/cover-download.log | | NFS URLs | /data/PS5NES/nfs.txt | If /data is unavailable, the app uses /download0/PS5NES as a fallback data folder. The QR settings page listens on **port 8844** and can provide logs. ## Build from source See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for the tested dependency layout, pinned versions and build command. The active app is in **nes/src/** and uses **ps5/frontend/** directly. The inherited PCSX2 source is retained as the original project scaffold; the NES build does not compile its PS2 emulator core. ## Current limits and testing - One active player in the current app integration. - FDS and Zapper/light-gun input are not exposed. - General firmware compatibility has not been established. - The NES/menu baseline and v5 memory fix were reported working on a user's PS5. The controller bindings passed host tests, and the v7 theme was rendered and visually checked; broader console testing is still needed. - No copyrighted ROMs, game images, BIOS files or console keys are included. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** — project customization and supplied logo. - **Spyros and PCSX2 contributors** — original PS5SX2 interface and project scaffold. - [FCEUmm / Libretro](https://github.com/libretro/libretro-fceumm) — NES emulation. - [mihawk-99 / PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) — native Vulkan driver and runtime work. - [BlackBearReloaded / ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) — native startup, packaging and elevation client. - [Lapy filesystem helper](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon) — restricted filesystem helper. - Libnfs, libcurl, OpenSSL, zlib, zstd, libpsl and the bundled font/library authors. PS5NES integration code is GPL-3.0-or-later. Upstream components retain their own licenses and notices. See [LICENSE](LICENSE), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and the included license files. ## Earlier library and cover improvements (AI-assisted) Local/USB directories are freshly scanned even with a warm NFS cache. Offline IPv4 NAS detection is bounded and local games are retained. Valid folders include /data/PS5NES/games and /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5NES/games (USB0 through USB7). Empty-library hints are shown only when no game is selected. R2 on the shelf refreshes the selected cover, preserving the previous image on failure. The 742-file NES repository index adds normalized title/region matching with libretro fallback and retries old failed cover lookups. FCEUmm and the NES theme are retained. Native build and host tests passed; latest changes still need PS5 testing. ## v1.0.0.9 by YAHBALLON (AI-assisted) Internal ROM discovery no longer requires successful path metadata for every file. Known directory-entry types and opened descriptors are used; header probing and bounded stream reads support mounts that also deny descriptor metadata. The library cache can be read without path metadata. Added internal aliases `/data/homebrew/PS5NES/games/`, `/data/homebrew/PS5NES/roms/` and `/data/homebrew/PPSA99204/roms/`. ROM source paths are displayed beneath the selected game title. Failed directory access and scan counts are reported in boot.log. USB and cached NFS regressions passed; internal detection under simulated metadata denial and the actual Vulkan path display were verified. Console retest remains required.

repos.name: PS5_Ghostship
repos.description: Super Mario 64 for PlayStation 5 homebrew: Ghostship (libultraship) on the PS5 Vulkan stack. No game data included.
repos.readme:
# Mario 64 for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_Ghostship?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_Ghostship)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [Ghostship](https://github.com/HarbourMasters/Ghostship)
(v3.0.0), HarbourMasters' native port of the 1996 Nintendo 64 game, compiled
from its decompilation on [libultraship](https://github.com/Kenix3/libultraship).
On the console it draws through libultraship's Vulkan renderer on RADV, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

The build reads no ROM and holds no game data. The player copies their own ROM
beside the title, and the title converts it once, on the console.

## Status

**Runs on the console.** First run on 2026-10-12 on a PS5 at 3840x2160: the title
screen, the file select, a new game and the castle grounds, at a measured 60
images a second (frame interpolation; the game's logic stays at 30).

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Game data | A US or JP `.z64` in the title's folder is found on the first start and converted to `sm64.o2r` in a few seconds. With neither file the title says what to copy where and closes |
| Picture | 3840x2160 on a 4K output, 16:9 |
| 60 fps | Measured at 3840x2160 on the title screen and the castle grounds |
| Menu | The touch pad's click opens Ghostship's settings menu. L1/R1 change tab, L2/R2 change section, the d-pad and Cross work the settings, Options asks to quit. The controls are listed along the bottom of the screen |
| HD textures | [SM64 Reloaded](#hd-textures-optional) seen working on the console |
| Saves, settings | `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/userdata/` |
| DevLoop | `devloop-shot` in the title's folder (registered as `ghostship`) |
| Art | The icon and background are the port's own, made with an image generator (`ps5/art/`) |

Controls are Ghostship's defaults for a pad: left stick to move, Cross A,
Circle B, L2 Z, R2 R, L1 L, Options START, the right stick for the C buttons.
They can be changed in the menu under Settings, Controls.

## Install

Download `Mario64-PS5-vX.Y.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99310`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
Build.) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Copy the whole folder `PPSA99310` to the console as
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/`, so that you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/ghostship.o2r
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/config.yml
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/assets/       (what the ROM's conversion reads)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon.
2. Copy your own Super Mario 64 ROM into the same folder, beside `eboot.bin`.
   It must be the Nintendo 64 game's US or JP release, in `.z64` format (big
   endian; convert a `.n64` or `.v64` dump first), under any name ending in
   `.z64`. The title checks the ROM against these hashes and takes no other:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/baserom.us.z64
   ```

   | Release | SHA-1 |
   | --- | --- |
   | US | `9bef1128717f958171a4afac3ed78ee2bb4e86ce` |
   | JP | `8a20a5c83d6ceb0f0506cfc9fa20d8f438cafe51` |

3. Wait a few seconds for "Mario 64" to appear on the home screen, and start it.
4. The first start says "ROM found" and asks whether to generate the game files:
   press **Cross**. It takes a few seconds, and the game starts. The ROM is not
   needed again and can be deleted from the console.

If you already have an `sm64.o2r` made by Ghostship 3.0.0 on a PC, copy that
into the folder in place of the ROM.

If "Mario 64" does not appear on the home screen, look in
`/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. "AppInstallAll hook is no longer installed" means
ShadowMountPlus has to be restarted before it will register a new title.

## HD textures (optional)

The port takes Ghostship texture packs unchanged. The one tried on the console is
**SM64 Reloaded** by GhostlyDark:

- Project: <https://github.com/GhostlyDark/SM64-Reloaded>
- Downloads: <https://github.com/GhostlyDark/SM64-Reloaded/releases/latest>

**1. Download the Ghostship version of the pack.** On the releases page, take the
file whose name contains `gs-o2r`:

| File | Size | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sm64-reloaded-v2.6.0-gs-o2r-hd.7z` | 99 MB | HD; the one used on the console |
| `sm64-reloaded-v2.6.0-gs-o2r-4k.7z` | 618 MB | 4K |

The other files on that page are for emulators and other ports and will not work.

**2. Unpack it.** It holds one `.o2r` file, for example
`SM64_Reloaded_v2.6.0_HD.o2r` (547 MB).

**3. Copy the `.o2r` to the console's `mods` folder:**

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/userdata/mods/SM64_Reloaded_v2.6.0_HD.o2r
```

The folder exists once the game has been started once.

**4. Switch the pack on in the menu.** Start the game, then:

1. Press the **touch pad** to open the menu.
2. Press **R1** once, to the **Enhancements** tab.
3. The **Graphics** section is the first one and is already selected (if another
   is, press **L2** until Graphics is).
4. Move down with the **d-pad** to **Use Alternate Assets**, under "Mods", and
   press **Cross** to tick it.
5. Press the **touch pad** to close the menu.

The setting is remembered. Untick the same box to go back to the original
textures. If the textures do not change when you tick the box, quit and start
the game again.

## Build

On Linux (on a Mac, in the Lima VM) with PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa and PS5_PayloadSDK
beside this folder.

```sh
ps5/tools/vm.sh build            # from macOS; ps5/tools/build.sh inside the VM
ps5/tools/vm.sh assets           # ghostship.o2r, Ghostship's own assets, into dist/
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy
ps5/tools/vm.sh run
```

`build.sh` runs `setup-source.sh` first, which applies the console's changes to
`vendor/ghostship` and its two submodules from `ps5/patches/` (every hunk behind
`__PROSPERO__` or `PS5`). While changing anything under `vendor/`, run
`ps5/tools/setup-source.sh --save` before a build.

`ps5/tools/vm.sh assets ROM.z64` also makes `sm64.o2r` on this machine, into the
ignored `game/` folder, and `ps5/tools/vm.sh console-files` uploads it: the
quicker loop while developing.

What the console needed:

- **SDL2.** libultraship is written for SDL2; `ps5/sdl/` holds SDL2 video, audio
  and pad drivers for the console (`ps5/patches/sdl.patch` registers them).
- **Vulkan with no loader.** RADV is linked into the title, so libultraship's
  Vulkan renderer and Dear ImGui's reach it through volk. OpenGL is compiled out.
- **shaderc**, built from source: the renderer writes its shaders as GLSL at run
  time.
- **No working directory.** A title cannot `chdir`, `getcwd` or `realpath`;
  `ps5/src/shims.c` answers the last two for `std::filesystem`.
- **The log.** A flush for every line made the ROM's conversion take twenty
  minutes; errors are flushed at once, the rest every two seconds.
- **The menu with a pad alone**: see Status.

`GHOSTSHIP_PS5_FPS=1` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/env.txt` writes the frame
rate to the console's log every ten seconds.

## Licence

GPL-3.0 for the repository as a whole and for a built title: see
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md). No game data is stored here or built in.
"Mario" and "Super Mario 64" are Nintendo's; this project is not affiliated with
Nintendo, HarbourMasters or Sony Interactive Entertainment.

latestRelease.body:
## Fixed

- The game no longer slows down the longer you play. The Vulkan renderer created new command buffers every frame and never freed them, so each frame took a little longer than the last, and after about ten minutes the slowdown was easy to see. It now reuses the same buffers, so the frame rate stays steady however long you play.

## Install

- Copy the folder `PPSA99310` from the zip over your existing `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/`. Your ROM, converted game data, saves, settings and texture packs stay where they are.
- New install: see the [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship#install). You need your own Super Mario 64 ROM (US or JP, `.z64`).

repos.description: The Wind Waker (GameCube) for PlayStation 5 homebrew: SwitchWaker on the PS5 Vulkan stack. No game data included.
repos.readme:
# Wind Waker (GameCube) for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [SwitchWaker](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker), the
native port of the 2002 GameCube game (USA disc `GZLE01`, revision 0) compiled
from its decompilation and drawn with [Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora).
It is laid out like [PS5_Dusklight](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight) and
uses the same console layer: Aurora on Dawn's WebGPU on RADV, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

The build reads no disc and holds no game data: SwitchWaker's runtime-assets
mode compiles against stub headers and fills them from the player's own disc
image when the title starts.

## Status

**Runs on the console.** First run on 2026-10-12 on a PS5 at 3840x2160: the
title screen, name entry, the prologue and Outset, at 60 images a second
(frame interpolation; the game's logic stays at 30), with the DualSense's
symbols on the HUD. Played on the console as far as the forest on Outset, the
scenes that follow it, and the boss room of Dragon Roost Cavern; nothing else
has been seen there.

**[Version 1.0.3](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.3)** fixes a crash in Dragon Roost Cavern, in the rooms with
the hanging platforms. [Version 1.0.2](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.2) fixed a crash when the boss of Dragon
Roost Cavern appears, and stopped the whole class of fault behind it (an
integer division by zero) from ending the game anywhere else. [Version 1.0.1](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.1)
fixed a stop on a black screen at the end of the forest scene. See
[Development](#development) for what
they were. Copy the [new release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest) over the old folder; saves carry on.

A release is the title's folder with no game in it: the player copies their own `GZLE01` disc image (`.iso`, `.gcm` or `.ciso`) into
`/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/` beside `eboot.bin`, and the title finds it (the
first one in its folder, then on a USB drive).

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Disc | Found in the title's folder; a `.iso` and a `.ciso` have both been run on the console; `.gcm` has not. A missing or wrong disc closes the title with a console notification (the close is seen working; the notification's text has not been read on a television yet) |
| Picture | 16:9. The output is 3840x2160 unless the options menu's "Output resolution" says 2560x1440 or 1920x1080 (applied at the next start); the console scales it to the television. "Internal resolution" follows it ("Window size") or is fixed, which dynamic resolution needs |
| 60 fps | Held at 3840x2160 in the scenes above, by the frame counter on screen. Not measured over a long session |
| Shaders | A first start with no cache compiled 3,056 render pipelines in about 12 minutes. The title now ships the caches a console produced (`ps5/shader-cache`) and copies them into place when the console has none: the same start then compiles nothing. They must be taken from a console again after a change to Dawn, the driver or the shaders |
| Button prompts | The HUD shows Cross (A), Square (B), Circle (X), Triangle (Y), R1 for Z, R2 for R and a right stick for the C stick (`ps5/art/make-glyphs.py`, [Kenney's CC0 Input Prompts](https://kenney.nl/assets/input-prompts)). The options menu's hints name the DualSense's buttons. Not done: the button pictures inside message text (they are in the game's font). With an HD texture pack the pack's buttons are drawn instead: see [Button symbols with a pack](#hd-textures-optional) |
| Options menu | The touch pad's click opens it |
| Saves, settings | `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/`; the first start asks to create a save file, as the game does on an empty memory card |
| HD textures | A Dolphin texture pack the player supplies replaces the game's textures (on when a pack is in `user/hd_textures`, off otherwise; see [HD textures](#hd-textures-optional)). Seen working on the console with Hypatia's pack on Outset and in its forest. The pack has an optional PlayStation button set for the HUD |
| Sound | Not checked by ear in this log |
| DevLoop | `devloop-shot` and `devloop-quit` in the title's folder (registered as `windwaker-gc`); the shot answers once the game's loop runs |
| Art | The icon and background are the port's own, cel-shaded, made with an image generator (`ps5/art/`) |

Controls: left stick to move, right stick for the camera (the C stick), Cross A,
Square B, Circle X, Triangle Y, R1 Z, L2 L, R2 R, Options START. The buttons are
mapped by position, where the GameCube pad has them around A, so the HUD's
symbols sit where the buttons do on the DualSense: the sword is on Square.
The symbol of an empty item slot sits in the middle of its bubble.

## Install

Download `WindWaker-PS5-vX.Y.Z.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99309`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
[Build](#build).) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Unpack the release (or build: the result is the folder `dist/PPSA99309/`).
2. Copy that whole folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/`, so that
   you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/initial_pipeline_cache.db
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/res/          (button symbols and shader caches)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon.
3. Copy your disc image into the same folder, under any name ending in `.iso`,
   `.gcm` or `.ciso`:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/your-disc.iso
   ```

   It has to be there or on a USB drive, not elsewhere in `/data`: a title can
   only see its own folder. The game takes the first image it finds.
4. Wait a few seconds for "Wind Waker" to appear on the home screen, and start
   it. The first start asks to create a save file.

With no disc image, or one that is not the supported disc, the title closes and
the console shows a notification that says why.

Saves and settings are written to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/`. Copying a new
build over the folder leaves them, and the disc image, alone.

**The disc image.** Dump your own copy of the game
([how](https://wiki.dolphin-emu.org/index.php?title=Ripping_Games)). Only the USA
disc, `GZLE01` revision 0, is supported. If your dump is RVZ or another compressed
format, convert it to `.iso` with [Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) first.

## HD textures (optional)

The game's textures are the GameCube's, made for a 480-line picture. A texture
pack replaces them with redrawn, larger ones as the game draws them; nothing in
the game itself changes, and the option can be turned on and off while playing.
The port reads packs made for the [Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) emulator
for the USA disc (`GZLE01`). No pack comes with the title: each is its author's
own work, and you download it yourself.

The pack tried here is **Hypatia's "WWHD Mod" v2.0001a**, about 5,700 textures
covering most of the game. Its downloads are in the first post of
[its thread on the Dolphin forum](https://forums.dolphin-emu.org/thread-55004.html).
Take **"PC DDS Half Size"** (a `.7z` of 850 MB, 2.5 GB unpacked), which is the
one used here:
[direct download from the author's Google Drive mirror](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qBK8YOeSAwLpNP3NUkwcXgvUnQPKlgj7/view?usp=sharing)
(`Hypatia WWHD Mod v2.0001a (DDS-Half).7z`). The port reads it as it is. The full-size one is four times larger for a picture that is hard
to tell apart, and the PNG one is not suitable.

1. Unpack the `.7z` on a computer. Inside is a folder `GZL`.
2. Copy what is **inside** `GZL` (the folders `Characters`, `Environments`,
   `HUD` and so on) to the console, into
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/hd_textures/`. Create that folder if it is
   not there. Over FTP the 5,700 files take about ten minutes.
3. Start the game. A pack found in that folder is used from the start; the
   options menu (the touch pad's click) has Graphics > "HD textures" to turn it
   off and on, and remembers what you chose.

With no pack in that folder the option does nothing.

Seen on the console on 2026-10-12 with that pack: Outset at 3840x2160 and 60
images a second with the textures replaced, and its forest. Not played further
than that.

**Button symbols with a pack.** The pack replaces the HUD's buttons as well, with
its own GameCube ones, so the DualSense's symbols this port draws are lost while
it is on. To have PlayStation buttons with the pack, also copy the `HUD` folder
from its `-[Optional Textures]-/[HUD] Controller Buttons - Playstation` over
the `HUD` folder in `hd_textures`, replacing files: those label the buttons by
position, as this port maps them (Cross where A is, Square for B, Circle for X,
Triangle for Y). The button pictures inside message text stay the GameCube's
either way.

## Development

To try a change without the console:

```sh
cmake -S vendor/switchwaker/native -B build/native-mac -G Ninja \
    -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_AURORA=$PWD/.deps/aurora -DCOS_AURORA_PREPATCHED=ON \
    -DCOS_RECOMPCORE_DIR=$PWD/.deps/recompcore \
    -DCOS_RUNTIME_ASSETS=ON -DCOS_ASSETS_DIR=$PWD/.deps/assets/GZLE01
ninja -C build/native-mac switchwaker
COS_BUILD_DIR=$PWD/build/native-mac COS_DISC=/path/to/GZLE01.iso COS_FPS60=1 \
    COS_BUTTON_GLYPHS=$PWD/ps5/art/glyphs vendor/switchwaker/native/tools/run.sh run \
    --preset sailing --aspect 16:9 --frames 700 --shot 690
```

**Finding a fault on the console.** The game's own `[cos]` lines go to the
console's log (klog, port 3232) with the driver's. A `[dev]` section at the end
of `user/settings.ini` sets developer variables at the next start, for example
`COS_TRACE=scene,res` for every scene created and every file opened. A scene
change that stays in one step logs `scene-req-watch` lines every 300 calls: the
step, and the processes still waiting to be deleted.

The stop that 1.0.1 fixes was found that way. Some actors declare their methods
as returning `bool` and the game's process framework calls them as returning
`int` and compares with `TRUE`. On x86-64 the rest of the register is undefined,
so a delete could be refused for ever and the next scene never came; on ARM (the
Mac, the Switch) it does not show. The framework now reads only the low byte
([`f_pc_method.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)). On the Mac, `COS_EVENT_SWEEP_FOLLOW=1` lets
`run.sh event-sweep` go on through a stage change an event asks for.

The crash that 1.0.3 fixes is a third one. A hanging platform of Dragon Roost
Cavern whose ropes were cut on an earlier visit is created with them cut, and
the rope points are simulated from values nothing has set. A NaN among them
reaches the arctangent table as an index: the conversion to an integer gives
0x80000000, which the GameCube's 32 bit address wraps back to the first entry
and x86-64 turns into a read 4 GB below the table. The lookup now gives the
first entry for a NaN or a ratio outside the table ([`c_math.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)).
It was found from a player's photograph of the console's error message: the
two addresses in it, less the load address 0x400000, name `cM_atan2s` and
`himo_move` in the release's ELF.

The crash that 1.0.2 fixes is the same kind of difference. The boss of Dragon
Roost Cavern turns towards the player with a step count that is still zero the
first time, an integer division by zero: the GameCube and ARM give a quotient
and go on, x86-64 raises SIGFPE. The three helpers involved now give 0
([`c_lib.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)), and so that the next one elsewhere is not a crash,
the title handles SIGFPE itself: it finishes the division as ARM does (quotient
0, remainder the dividend), logs `integer division fault` with the address, and
goes on. The console's code cannot be read at run time, so the build lists
every division instruction of the linked title in `res/div-table.bin`
([`make-div-table.py`](ps5/tools/make-div-table.py)) and the handler looks the address up; a fault
that is not in the list is still a crash with the console's record.
`COS_DIV_TEST=1` in `[dev]` divides by zero once at the start to check it. On
the Mac, `COS_SAVE_LOAD_WALK=<frames>` makes `run.sh save-load` walk forward
from a loaded save (`COS_CARD_DIR` names a card folder holding a player's
`.gci`).

`COS_TEXTURE_DUMPS=1` writes every texture drawn into the cache folder's
`texture_dumps`, named as a replacement for it must be named.

## Build

As PS5_Dusklight: on Linux (on a Mac, in the Lima VM) with PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa
and PS5_PayloadSDK beside this folder.

```sh
ps5/tools/vm.sh build     # from macOS; ps5/tools/build.sh inside the VM
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy
ps5/tools/vm.sh run
```

`build.sh` runs `setup-source.sh` first, which patches `vendor/switchwaker`
(`ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch`, every hunk behind `__PROSPERO__`) and fetches
into `.deps/` Aurora at SwitchWaker's pin with its patches, Dolphin's DSP HLE
sources and the stub asset headers. While changing `vendor/switchwaker`, run
`git -C vendor/switchwaker diff > ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch` before a build.

## Licence

GPL-3.0 for the repository as a whole and for a built title: see
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md). No game data is stored here or built in.

latestRelease.name: Wind Waker for PS5 v1.0.3
latestRelease.body:
## Fixed

- A crash in Dragon Roost Cavern, in the rooms with the hanging platforms. It showed as the game closing, or as an error message naming `SIGSEGV`, and was most likely to happen on coming back to a room after cutting a platform's ropes, including after loading a save. Thanks to the player who photographed the error message: the addresses in it were enough to find the cause.

This fix was made from that report and has not yet been confirmed on a console in that room. If the game still closes there, an issue with a photo of the error message is the quickest way to get it found.

## Updating

- Replace the folder `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/` with the one in this zip, or copy the new files over it. Your disc image, saves, settings and texture pack in that folder are kept if you copy over it.
- Copy the whole folder, not only `eboot.bin`.
- Saves from earlier versions carry on working.

## Install (new)

- Unpack the zip and copy the folder `PPSA99309` to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/`.
- Copy your own disc image (`.iso`, `.gcm` or `.ciso`) into that same folder, beside `eboot.bin`.
- Start "Wind Waker" from the home screen. The first start asks to create a save file.
- Full steps, controls and the HD texture pack: see the README.

## Known limits

- Played on a console only through Outset Island and into the boss room of Dragon Roost Cavern; other areas are untested there.
- Button pictures inside dialogue text still show the GameCube's buttons.
- With an HD texture pack on, the pack's own button pictures replace the DualSense symbols; Hypatia's pack has an optional PlayStation button set that matches this mapping (see the README).
- Only the USA disc is supported.

Unofficial; not affiliated with SwitchWaker, Nintendo or Sony Interactive Entertainment. No game data is included. Licence: GPL-3.0, sources in `SOURCE.txt` inside the zip.

repos.name: PS5MC
repos.description: PS5MC is a PS5 port of Kodi, the award-winning free and open source home theater/media center software and entertainment hub for digital media. With its beautiful interface and powerful skinning engine.
repos.readme:
![Kodi Logo](docs/resources/banner.png)

website • docs • community • add-ons

Welcome to Kodi Home Theater Software!

Kodi is an award-winning **free and open source** software media player and entertainment hub for digital media. Available as a native application for **Android, Linux, BSD, macOS, iOS, tvOS and Windows operating systems**, Kodi runs on most common processor architectures. Created in 2003 by a group of like minded programmers, Kodi is a non-profit project run by the XBMC Foundation and developed by volunteers located around the world. More than 500 software developers have contributed to Kodi to date, and 100-plus translators have worked to expand its reach, making it available in more than 70 languages. While Kodi functions very well as a standard media player application for your computer, it has been designed to be the perfect companion for your HTPC. With its **beautiful interface and powerful skinning engine**, Kodi feels very natural to use from the couch with a remote control and is the ideal solution for your home theater. ## Give your media the love it deserves Kodi can be used to play almost all popular audio and video formats around. It was designed for network playback, so you can stream your multimedia from anywhere in the house or directly from the internet using practically any protocol available. Point Kodi to your media and watch it **scan and automagically create a personalized library** complete with box covers, descriptions, and fanart. There are playlist and slideshow functions, a weather forecast feature and many audio visualizations. Once installed, your computer or HTPC will become a fully functional multimedia jukebox.

## Getting Started Kodi's developers work hard to make it support a large range of devices and operating systems. We provide final as well as development builds. To get started, head over to the **[downloads section](https://kodi.tv/download)** and simply select the platform that you want to install it on. A **[quick start guide](https://kodi.wiki/view/quick_start_guide)** to help you get acquainted with Kodi is available in our wiki. ## How to Contribute Kodi is created by users for users and **we welcome every contribution**. There are no highly paid developers or poorly paid support personnel on the phones ready to take your call. There are only users who have seen a problem and done their best to fix it. This means Kodi will always need the contributions of users like you. How can you get involved? * **Coding:** Developers can help Kodi by **[fixing a bug](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues)**, adding new features, making our technology smaller and faster and making development easier for others. Kodi's codebase consists mainly of C++ with small parts written in a variety of coding languages. Our add-ons mainly consist of python and XML. For more information, please have a look at our **[contributing guide](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)**. * **Helping users:** Our support process relies on enthusiastic contributors like you to help others get the most out of Kodi. The #1 priority is always answering questions in our **[support forums](https://forum.kodi.tv/)**. Everyday new people discover Kodi, and everyday they are virtually guaranteed to have questions. * **Localization:** Translate **[Kodi](https://kodi.weblate.cloud/projects/kodi-core/kodi-main/)**, **[add-ons, skins etc.](https://kodi.weblate.cloud/)** into your native language. * **Add-ons:** **[Add-ons](https://kodi.tv/addons)** are what make Kodi the most extensible and customizable entertainment hub available. **[Get started building an add-on](https://kodi.tv/create-an-addon)**. * **Documentation:** Kodi's **[wiki pages](https://kodi.wiki/)** are the hub for information about Kodi and surrounding ecosystem. Help make our documentation better by writing new content or correcting existing material. **Not enough free time?** No problem! There are other ways to help Kodi. * **Spread the word:** Share Kodi with the world! Tell your friends and family about how Kodi creates an amazing entertainment experience. Stay up to date on the latest stories about Kodi reading our **[news](https://kodi.tv/blog)** section, follow us on **[Twitter](https://twitter.com/koditv)** and **[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/XBMC/)**, or **star Kodi's repo** if you want to follow development. * **Donate:** We are always happy to receive a **[donation](https://kodi.tv/contribute/donate)**. Donations are typically used for travel to attend conferences, any necessary paperwork and legal fees, and the yearly XBMC Foundation Developers Conference, where a great deal of coding and planning for the following year occurs. Donations may also be used to purchase necessary hardware and licenses for developers, along with t-shirts, stickers, and other accessories for conferences. * **Buy Kodi merchandise:** Purchasing Kodi gear helps just as much as a donation, and you get something in return! Checkout our **[store](https://kodi.tv/store)** for Kodi branded gear. We regularly add new products so check back often. ## Building Kodi uses CMake as its building system but instructions are highly dependent on your operating system and target platform. Fortunately **[we've got you covered](docs/README.md)**. ## Acknowledgements Kodi couldn't exist without * All the **[contributors](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/graphs/contributors)**. Big or small a change, it does make a difference. * All the developers that write the fantastic **software and libraries** that Kodi uses. We stand on the shoulders of giants. * Our **[fantastic community](https://forum.kodi.tv/)** for the never ending support, inspiration, feedback, and for keeping us on our toes when we screw up! * **[Our sponsors](https://kodi.tv/sponsors)**. Without them, keeping a huge project like this alive would be next to impossible. ## License Kodi is **[GPLv2 licensed](LICENSE.md)**. You may use, distribute and copy it under the license terms.
